alt-01.name: Lake Teletskoye
alt-01.full: Lake Teletskoye (Altai: Altyn-Kol — “Golden Lake”), northeast of the Altai Republic
alt-01.near: North: Artybash village and Iogach village (at the source of the Biya); east shore: Yaylyu settlement (reserve headquarters); south: Balykcha village and the Kyrsay tract (mouth of the Chulyshman)
alt-01.short: The largest and deepest lake in Altai: 78 km long, up to 325 m deep, stretched in an “L” shape through the taiga; on the east shore the Altai Nature Reserve and waterfalls, in the south the mouth of the Chulyshman.
alt-01.desc: Lake Teletskoye lies at 434 m and stretches roughly 78–79 km with a width of up to 5.5 km; its area is about 223 km², and its maximum depth is 323–325 m (one of the deepest lakes in Russia and the world). According to different sources, anywhere from 19 large to more than 70 rivers and streams flow into the lake, the main tributary being the Chulyshman (about 70% of the inflow), and one river flows out — the Biya. The local name is Altyn-Kol (“Golden Lake”); the Russian name “Teletskoye” was given about 400 years ago after the Teleuts who lived on its shores. The water is cold: in the north in summer about +10…+12 °C, in the southern part up to +17…+22 °C (other sources say the water rarely warms above +16 °C); the south of the lake is 4–5 °C warmer than the north. The latitudinal (northern) part freezes in winter, while the deep meridional part only once every 7–12 years. The lake is known for sharp winds (nizovka/verkhovka) that quickly raise waves. The whole east shore and the southern part are in the Altai State Nature Biosphere Reserve (part of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”). The north shore is the tourist side: the villages of Artybash and Iogach with dozens of recreation bases, boat piers, a ferry to the south, and the Teletskiy ski resort on Mount Kokuya. The main sights on the water are the Korbu, Kishte, Estyuba and Choodor waterfalls, Kamenny Bay (Stone Bay), Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman, where the road into the valley to Uchar and the Stone Mushrooms begins.
alt-01.guide: The best part is seeing the lake from the water: take a motorboat at least to Korbu, or better the full-day “Golden Ring” to the south shore. Don't trust a calm: the nizovka wind arrives within half an hour, so bring a warm jacket even in the heat. Altaians call the lake Altyn-Kol, and there is a legend about a year of famine when a rich man threw a gold ingot into the water — hence the “Golden Lake”. For a panorama, ride the lift up Kokuya or hike up Tilan-Tuu (Wolf's Head) above Artybash. And be sure to try smoked Teletskoye whitefish or grayling.
alt-01.see: The source of the Biya and the bridge in Iogach/Artybash; Mount Kokuya (1385 m, lift) and the Tilan-Tuu viewpoint (740 m); the Korbu, Kishte, Estyuba, Choodor and Ayu-Kechpes waterfalls (from a boat); Kamenny Bay (Stone Bay); Yaylyu settlement — the reserve headquarters; Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman in the south; the Tayozhny zoo in Artybash; the Ortosh ethnographic museum near Kebezen
alt-01.skip: you aren't up for a long road (160 km from Gorno-Altaysk on a narrow road) and cold water for swimming, and boats and waterfalls don't appeal to you; at the end of the 2026 season, moreover, all the reserve's trails are closed because of bears
alt-01.diff: Easy (north, boat excursions); moderate to high for a trip to the south shore overland via Katu-Yaryk
alt-01.when: July–September (warm, boats run and the reserve's trails are open May–September); September — quieter and golden autumn; winter — ice, skiing, almost no frosts
alt-01.hours: The lake — around the clock, free access; the reserve's eco-educational routes are usually open May–September; in 2026 all the reserve's routes have been closed from late August to the end of the season
alt-01.daytime: Morning — calm and mirror-like water, boats leave at 7–9 am; sunset — from Tilan-Tuu or Kokuya
alt-01.how: North (Artybash/Iogach): Barnaul → Gorno-Altaysk 257 km (3.5–4 h), Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash ≈159–160 km (2–3 h by car) along the Teletskoye Trakt via Choya, Turochak/Kebezen; from Novosibirsk to Gorno-Altaysk ≈430 km (5–6 h). Buses from Gorno-Altaysk (≈4 h), Biysk and Barnaul. South (Balykcha/Kyrsay): car ferry from Artybash (5–6 h) or overland: Chuysky Trakt to Aktash → Ulagan road → Ulagan → Balyktuyul → Katu-Yaryk Pass → down the Chulyshman valley to the lake (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass + ≈75 km along the valley), only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV.
alt-01.needcar: To the north shore — bus or car; on the lake — motorboat; to the south — ferry, motorboat or 4×4 / SUV
alt-01.self: Yes: to the north by bus or car, with boats and excursions bought on the spot; to the south independently — by ferry with your car or in a 4×4 / SUV via Katu-Yaryk
alt-01.roadtype: To Artybash — paved road (a narrow two-lane road without shoulders); beyond Artybash along the west shore — dirt road; to the south overland — the Ulagan road (partly paved, then dirt), Katu-Yaryk Pass — a steep gravel serpentine
alt-01.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash 2.5–3 h by car, ≈4 h by bus; Barnaul → Artybash ≈6–7 h; Novosibirsk → Artybash ≈8–9 h; ferry Artybash → south 5–6 h
alt-01.stay: Dozens of bases in Artybash and Iogach: from 700 ₽/night (simple tourist bases, mirturbaz) and 2200 ₽ (the Teletskoye Zolotoye eco-hotel) to 15,000–46,000 ₽ (Urochishche Aktra, Altay Village Teletskoe); Altay Time cabins 5000 ₽ (2 people) — 15,000 ₽ (6 people); in the south — campsites and the Vyshe Gor glamping in Balykcha from 2200 ₽
alt-01.net: A stable mobile signal exists only in Artybash and Iogach (YouTravel, 2026); on the water and on the east shore — patchy; in the Chulyshman valley a signal has appeared but is unstable (T—Zh, 2025); specific operators — to be checked
alt-01.entry: The lake itself is free. Altai Nature Reserve trails (Korbu, Uchar, Yaylyu): 250 ₽/person (2025); from 31.08.2026 all routes are closed until the end of the season. There is no resort tax in the Altai Republic (under discussion); a tourist tax has been introduced only in the city of Gorno-Altaysk (2025–2026). Separate eco fees for private/local stops at waterfalls — 50–150 ₽ (KP, 2026); tour operators quote ≈750 ₽ for three waterfalls (Sputnik8, 2026). Free, per Turister, for children under 14 and school groups (to be confirmed).
alt-01.transfer: Taxi Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash ≈3000–4000 ₽ (2020–2023); car ferry to the south 15–17k ₽ (2026); private motorboat to the south ≈78,000 ₽ for 6 h (Extraguide)
alt-01.bring: A warm waterproof jacket even in summer (nizovka wind), repellent and tick protection, cash (signal and card terminals are not everywhere), sun protection, shoes for wet rocks
alt-01.warn: On 19.08.2026 a bear fatally attacked a tourist in a tent near Artybash; a curfew was imposed in Artybash and Yaylyu, and all the reserve's routes are closed until the end of the 2026 season — don't pitch a tent in the forest, store food airtight. Ticks (May–July). Sharp winds and waves — don't go out on the water in a boat without experience. The water is cold — dangerous for long swimming. The road to Artybash is narrow, without shoulders.
alt-01.food: Smoked and fried Teletskoye whitefish, grayling; cedar coffee and herbal tea (a cafe on the Korbu trail); the TsUP cafe at the foot of Kokuya and MKS at the first lift platform; tasting at the Ortosh ethnographic museum
alt-01.reviews: 2GIS: Lake Teletskoye — 4.6 (173 ratings). Excursions: “Legends of the Golden Lake” 4.9 (151 reviews, Sputnik8), “5 waterfalls and Tilan-Tuu” 4.8 (17), “Journey to the Stone Mushrooms” 4.6 (27). Pros: views, waterfalls, guides; cons: high prices, crowding in July–August, cancellations due to weather and bears, separate eco fees at waterfalls (up to 750 ₽ for three).

alt-01.p.sum: The base point is Artybash/Iogach on the north shore (≈160 km from Gorno-Altaysk on paved road, bus ≈4 h). You see the lake from a boat: from a 1-hour trip to Estyuba (≈2000 ₽) to the “Golden Ring” to the south (6000–7500 ₽). You can reach the south by car ferry from Artybash (5–6 h, with a car 15–17k ₽) or overland via Ulagan and Katu-Yaryk Pass — only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV. Lodging from 700 ₽ to 46,000 ₽ per night. At the end of the 2026 season the reserve's trails are closed because of bears.

alt-01.p.season: May–September for boats and trails; July–August is the peak (book lodging in advance); the ferry runs May to early October; winter — skiing on Kokuya, boats don't run.
alt-01.p.permits: No border-zone permit needed (Turochak district). Visiting the reserve's trails requires a route ticket (250 ₽, 2025) and registration on the route; organized groups need to apply to the reserve. Small boats need the reserve's seasonal permit. In 2026 the trails have been closed since 31.08. Since spring 2025 the reserve has issued permits for private small boats to sail on Lake Teletskoye to the eco trails: points in Artybash (Teletskaya St. 12) and Yaylyu (Tsentralnaya St. 14); you need a passport, a boat ticket and a boat operator's license; tel. +7 (388-22) 2-14-19, agpzmain@mail.ru (Altapress, 2025). Hiking groups register with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) online (forms.mchs.gov.ru/registration_tourist_groups); applications are processed within a day.
alt-01.p.access: With children — yes (motorboats, Korbu, the lift; children under 5 free on boats). For older people — boat trips and Kokuya. The Korbu trail is not adapted for people with limited mobility. Dogs in the reserve — not found (to be confirmed).

alt-02.name: Korbu Waterfall
alt-02.full: Korbu Waterfall at the mouth of the Bolshaya Korbu River, eastern shore of Lake Teletskoye, Altai Nature Reserve
alt-02.near: Yaylyu settlement (the reserve's estate, eastern shore); the starting villages for boats are Artybash and Iogach (≈25–30 km by water)
alt-02.elev: Lake level 434 m; height of the water drop 12.5–12.8 m
alt-02.short: The best-known and most accessible waterfall of Lake Teletskoye: a 12-meter stream drops from a slanting rock ledge right at the shore; it can be reached only by water.
alt-02.desc: Korbu is a waterfall on the Bolshaya Korbu River right where it flows into Lake Teletskoye, on the eastern shore, on the territory of the Altai Biosphere Reserve. The drop is 12.8 m according to the reserve (12–13 m in other sources). The stream falls from an inclined rock ledge, breaks on the stones and spreads in a wide fan. A natural monument since 1978. The waterfall can be visited only from the water: boats and motor ships go from Artybash and Iogach, ≈25 km one way. From the pier a short eco-trail (≈0.2 km, 30–40 minutes for the visit) with wooden decking and a viewing platform has been laid, and nearby are a visitor center, kiosks and a cafe. It is the reserve's most visited route: 47,640 people in 2012 and more than 40 thousand in 2014. The route is usually open from May to September and is included in almost all boat programs (“5 Wonders”, “7 Wonders”, “Golden Ring”). In 2005 the waterfall was temporarily closed because of the influx of tourists and unauthorized construction, and in 2026 the route is closed from the end of August to the end of the season because of the danger of bear encounters.
alt-02.guide: Korbu is not about scale but about the journey: the sail itself across the lake with mountains on both sides is the main impression. Step off the boat, walk along the decking to the platform and go up to the spray — in the heat it is the best shower in Altai. Don't spend all your time at the water: on the route there is a cafe with cedar coffee and chebureki with grayling. If you want photos without a crowd, take an early boat — by noon almost everyone moors at Korbu. On the way on the “5 Wonders” trip you will also see Kishte, Estyuba and the Stone Monkey.
alt-02.see: The waterfall itself from the viewing platform and from below at the rocks; the eco-trail with the reserve's flora and rock outcrops; on the way — the waterfalls Kishte, Estyuba, Choodor and Ayu-Kechpes (from the water), Love Island, the “Stone Monkey”, Stone Bay
alt-02.skip: you expect a grand waterfall — Korbu is only 12 m, and Lonely Planet honestly writes that the waterfall itself is “not memorable”, while the route across the lake is what impresses; or you dislike crowds and loud boat tours
alt-02.diff: Easy (a short 0.2 km trail; the rocks by the water are slippery)
alt-02.when: May–September; fullest in late spring and early summer; July–August is the crowd peak
alt-02.hours: The reserve route is usually open from May to September during the daytime boat services; in 2026 it was closed from 17–20 August (temporarily) and from 31 August to the end of the season
alt-02.daytime: Morning — the first boats and fewer people; after noon there are many vessels at the pier
alt-02.how: Only by water. Drive to Artybash or Iogach (≈160 km from Gorno-Altaysk), where you board a boat or motor ship. The sail is ≈25 km one way (reserve), about 2–2.5 h for the whole trip with the visit; Korbu is included in the programs “5 Wonders” (3 h), “7 Wonders” (3.5–4 h) and “Golden Ring” (7–8 h). One-day tours with transfer are sold from Gorno-Altaysk and Manzherok (≈7800–10,800 ₽, 10–12 h).
alt-02.needcar: Yes — a boat is mandatory (there is no access by land)
alt-02.self: Yes — drive to Artybash and buy a seat on a boat at the pier or from an operator; the reserve ticket is usually paid on the spot or included in the excursion
alt-02.roadtype: Paved road to Artybash; beyond that only water
alt-02.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash 2.5–4 h; boat Artybash → Korbu ≈40–60 min one way (estimated from the programs of 3-hour tours with several stops)
alt-02.stay: There is no overnight stay at the waterfall itself (reserve). Accommodation is in Artybash and Iogach: from 700–2200 ₽ (economy) to 6000–46,000 ₽ per night (see “Lake Teletskoye”)
alt-02.net: At the waterfall — no reliable data found; a reliable signal only in Artybash and Iogach
alt-02.entry: A ticket for the reserve's ecological-educational route costs 250 ₽/person (since 27.02.2025); reviews mention 150 ₽ (2020) and 750 ₽ in cash for several waterfalls on the route; KP gives 100 ₽ (2026) — contradictory. Often included in group tours. Children passed for free in 2012. Tour operators in 2026 list eco fees of ≈750 ₽ for the three waterfalls of the route (Sputnik8).
alt-02.transfer: A boat 2000–4000 ₽/person as part of a group (2026); an individual boat from 23,000–43,000 ₽
alt-02.bring: A windbreaker/warm jacket (it is cold on the water, the lower wind), shoes with a non-slip sole, cash (fees and cafe), sun protection
alt-02.warn: In 2026 the route is closed from 31.08 to the end of the season because of bears (after a tourist died near Artybash on 19.08.2026). Slippery rocks by the jets. In a storm the boats don't go out or turn back. Insist on life jackets — in reviews there were boats with no safety briefing.
alt-02.food: Cedar coffee and Altai herbal tea at the cafe on the route; the Altyn-Ay cafe at one of the route's waterfalls — chebureki with grayling, local tinctures (per a Tripster review)
alt-02.reviews: 2GIS: Korbu waterfall — 4.9 (80 ratings). Tours with Korbu: 4.9 (151 reviews) and 4.8 (17) on Sputnik8. Pros: views from the boat, convenient decking, a cafe, toilets; cons: crowds, “the waterfall is small” (Lonely Planet), a transfer on a bad road, loud commentary on the boat, unexpected extra charges (eco fees up to 750 ₽ for three waterfalls)

alt-03.name: Uchar Waterfall
alt-03.full: Uchar waterfall (cascade), also known as the Big Chulcha Waterfall — on the Chulcha River, a right tributary of the Chulyshman, in the Altai Nature Reserve
alt-03.near: Koo village and the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract in the Chulyshman valley; Balykcha village (south end of Lake Teletskoye)
alt-03.elev: Cascade drop ≈160 m over a stream length of ≈600 m; the rock jam the river forces its way through is 300–350 m high (nature reserve); ascent on the trail ≈240 m (KP, 2026); absolute elevation of the foot — not found
alt-03.short: The highest cascading waterfall in the Altai Republic (≈160 m): the Chulcha roars through a jam of giant boulders in a narrow canyon; you can get there only on foot — 8.5 km one way on a rocky trail with cables.
alt-03.desc: Uchar (“impregnable” or “flying” in Altai language) is a cascading waterfall on the Chulcha River a few kilometers from where it joins the Chulyshman, in the Altai State Biosphere Reserve. The water drops about 160 m, passing for about 600 m through a pile of huge boulders; it is more of a chute than a sheer waterfall. The cascade is thought to have formed from a collapse after the strong earthquakes of the late 19th and early 20th centuries; it was first described by V. Vereshchagin (1905 diary) and scientifically surveyed in 1982. Today it is the reserve's eco-educational route “Uchar Chute”: 8.5 km one way (≈3.5 h from the crossing), linear, of moderate difficulty for prepared hikers; the most dangerous rock section (a narrow ledge above the river) is equipped with railings, cables and metal staples (via ferrata, built in 2014). The start is on the right bank of the Chulyshman, where you are ferried across by boat; before setting out you must check in at the seasonal registration point. In 2011 Uchar was among Russia's five hardest-to-reach sights; in 2014 about 2000 people visited it (against 40,000 for Korbu). The route usually opens after the spring flood, in June (in 2016, after 20 June); in 2026 it was closed on 17–20 August and from 31 August to the end of the season because of bears.
alt-03.guide: Uchar is for those who find viewing platforms too little: you walk 3–4 hours through the taiga along the Chulyshman and the Chulcha, scramble over staples above the river, and at the end you hear a roar so loud you can't hear your neighbor. Set out at first light so you can get back to the boat before dark — the whole hike takes 7–8 hours. Locals joke about the “ground bunnies” — the chipmunks that steal food at rest stops — so don't leave your backpack open. Bring shoes with grippy soles: wet logs and rocks are the main enemy. On the way, look in at the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms — they are almost opposite.
alt-03.see: The cascade itself with the viewpoint at its foot; the Chulcha canyon; the cable-equipped ledge above the river; views of the Chulyshman valley; along the way, the taiga and the mouth of the Chulcha
alt-03.skip: you aren't ready for 17 km on foot there and back over rocks and staples, are afraid of heights, or are traveling with small children — in that case stick to the Stone Mushrooms and Katu-Yaryk
alt-03.diff: Moderate to high: 8.5 km one way, a rock ledge with cables and staples, fords/logs; good physical fitness required
alt-03.when: Late June to September (after the flood, when the reserve opens the route); May–June has the most water, but the trail is often closed because of floods and rockfalls
alt-03.hours: The reserve route is seasonal — June to September (English page of the reserve), in daylight; limit of up to 4 groups a day of 10–15 people, groups with an accompanying instructor, registration at the point at the start of the trail. In 2026: closed 17–20.08, then from 20.08 “until further notice” (bears on the trail), and from 31.08 all the reserve's routes are closed until the end of the season
alt-03.daytime: An early start (7–8 am), at the waterfall around noon, when the sun looks into the canyon
alt-03.how: First, get to the Chulyshman valley, to the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract / Koo village. Option 1 (overland): Chuysky Trakt to Aktash → Ulagan → Balyktuyul → Katu-Yaryk Pass → down the valley to about km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass + ≈30 km along the valley), 4×4 / SUV only. Option 2 (by water): a car ferry or motorboat from Artybash to the south end of Lake Teletskoye (5–6 h), then by car/UAZ up the valley. Then by boat across the Chulyshman to the right bank and 8.5 km on foot along the trail beside the Chulcha. From Artybash in one day — only on tours (12 h, but such tours usually include the Stone Mushrooms rather than Uchar).
alt-03.needcar: Yes — a 4×4 / SUV or a ferry/motorboat to the valley, plus a boat crossing over the Chulyshman; the trail itself is on foot only
alt-03.self: Getting to the valley and crossing — yes. But the reserve's rules (English version of the site) require groups to go with an accompanying instructor and limit the flow to 4 groups a day; in practice solo travelers join a guide's group from a tourist base (≈1000 ₽/person, KP 2026). Registration at the point by the trail is mandatory
alt-03.roadtype: To the valley — dirt/gravel and the Katu-Yaryk serpentine; the trail is a rocky mountain path with a rock ledge, cables and staples
alt-03.traveltime: Trail ≈3.5–4 h one way, 7–8 h for everything including sightseeing; Aktash → Ak-Kurum ≈4–5 h by 4×4 / SUV (estimate); ferry Artybash → south end 5–6 h
alt-03.stay: Tourist bases and campsites of the Ak-Kurum tract (km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road): Dolina Vodopadov (from 3000 ₽, 4.9/67 on 2GIS), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov (from 4500 ₽, 4.8/99), Kamennye Griby (from 2500 ₽, 4.3/79; yurt from 350 ₽ — mirturbaz); Zolotaya Dolina Chulyshmana (Koo, from 2500–3000 ₽); tents from 100 ₽/person (KP, 2026)
alt-03.net: There is no mobile signal in the valley according to KP (2026); according to T—Zh (2025) it has appeared but is unstable; on the trail — none. Some tourist bases have Wi-Fi (satellite/generators)
alt-03.entry: Altai Nature Reserve route ticket: 250 ₽/person (since 27.02.2025, all eco-educational routes); older sources say 100–180 ₽ (KP gives 100 ₽ for 2026 — contradictory). No border-zone permit needed.
alt-03.transfer: Boat across the Chulyshman 1000 ₽ per boat of up to 4 people round trip (2026) / 1500 ₽ at the campsite; previously ≈500 ₽/person (KP); transfer Ulagan → valley 16,000 ₽ for up to 8 people (2026); car ferry 15–17k ₽ (2026)
alt-03.bring: Trekking shoes with grippy soles, gloves for the cables, 1.5–2 L of water, a snack, a rain jacket, repellent and tick protection, a headlamp, a first-aid kit
alt-03.warn: In 2026 the trail has been closed since 20.08 “until further notice”: bears have appeared on it, and even inspectors are barred from access (reserve, Altapress 08.2026); from 31.08 all the reserve's routes are closed. The rock ledge above the river — hold on to the cables; setting out in rain is forbidden (mudflows). The most serious crossing is the Artyshtu stream. In spring (May–June) there are floods, mudflows and rockfalls, and the route is closed. Heat in the canyon above +30 °C. Ticks. No signal — guides carry satellite phones. No border-zone permit needed
alt-03.food: Meals at the Ak-Kurum tourist bases (dinner for two from 1300 ₽, KP 2026); a cafe at Chulyshmanskaya Berezka by the crossing; fish soup and fried grayling/roach caught in the Chulyshman
alt-03.reviews: No rating for the waterfall itself was found on 2GIS/Yandex. Tourist bases at the start of the trail: Dolina Vodopadov 4.9 (67), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov 4.8 (99) on 2GIS. Pros: the power of the cascade, wild taiga, few people; cons: a hard trail, slippery rocks, seasonal closures, the road over Katu-Yaryk.

alt-03.p.sum: Uchar is a day hike (≈17 km round trip, 7–8 h) from the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract in the Chulyshman valley: a boat across the river (≈500 ₽), registration, the reserve ticket (250 ₽, 2025). To reach the valley: over Katu-Yaryk by 4×4 / SUV, or by ferry/motorboat across Teletskoye. Stay overnight at the Ak-Kurum tourist bases (from 2500–4500 ₽ per cabin) or at a campsite (from 100 ₽/person). In 2026 the trail has been closed since 20 August because of bears.

alt-04.name: Chulyshman Valley and Katu-Yaryk Pass
alt-04.full: The Chulyshman River valley (the lower ≈75 km from the pass to Lake Teletskoye) and the Katu-Yaryk road descent/serpentine — the only overland entry into the valley, Ulagan district
alt-04.near: From above — Balyktuyul village (≈30 km to the pass) and Ulagan village (≈47 km); in the valley — Koo village and Balykcha village (by Lake Teletskoye)
alt-04.elev: Top of the pass / viewpoint ≈1200 m; bottom of the serpentine ≈670 m; drop ≈500–600 m (530 m according to some sources); valley floor at the lake 400–450 m
alt-04.short: A deep Chulyshman canyon with sheer walls, waterfalls and the Stone Mushrooms, reached via the famous Katu-Yaryk — 3.5–3.9 km of serpentine with nine hairpins and a gradient of up to 70%.
alt-04.desc: The Chulyshman is the main river feeding Lake Teletskoye (241 km). Tourists can reach the lower ≈75 km of the valley — from the foot of Katu-Yaryk Pass to the south shore of Lake Teletskoye. The valley is cut about a kilometer below the surrounding plateaus, so it has its own warm microclimate: in summer about +18 °C and higher, and apricots, pears and grapes were historically grown in the valley (by monks in the late 19th century). Telengits live here, and wooden churches stand in the villages of Koo and Balykcha. The Katu-Yaryk descent was built by bulldozer operators in 1987–1989 on the initiative of the state-farm director A. V. Sanaa; before that the valley could be reached only by the lake or on horse trails. The serpentine is 3.5–3.9 km long with 7–9 steep hairpins, single-lane, with passing pockets, and a slope of about 35° (70%). From the upper viewpoint you can see the canyon, the river and an almost 100 m waterfall on the opposite wall. In March 2026 construction of a new two-lane descent to the left of the current one was announced (≈4.9 billion ₽, due at the end of October 2027). The valley has the Kurkure (≈30 m), Uchar (≈160 m) and Achelman (near Balykcha) waterfalls, the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms, and dozens of tourist bases and campsites. There is no grid electricity or stable mobile signal: generators and solar panels, and in Balykcha the Kayru mini-hydropower plant.
alt-04.guide: Walk Katu-Yaryk on foot as far as the first hairpin first — from the top you will see the whole canyon and the waterfall on the opposite wall. If you're driving, descend in low gear and don't brake in the turns, and take a run-up for the climb in advance; if you can't make it, the tourist bases below will tow you out with a tractor for a fee. There are no cafes or shops in the valley, so stock up in Ulagan. And don't rush: Telengits live here, and in the evenings fishermen go out on the Chulyshman for grayling.
alt-04.see: The viewpoint on Katu-Yaryk (≈1200 m) and the serpentine itself; Kurkure waterfall (≈30 m, requires a crossing of the Chulyshman); Karasu waterfall (≈40 m); the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms; Uchar waterfall (17 km hike); Achelman waterfall near Balykcha; the wooden churches in Koo and Balykcha; Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman on Lake Teletskoye
alt-04.skip: you have a sedan or a rental car (rental companies fine you for driving Katu-Yaryk), you're afraid of heights behind the wheel, or you have less than two days — in that case the viewpoint at the top of the pass is enough
alt-04.diff: For the driver — high (a steep single-lane serpentine, rocks, 4WD and high ground clearance needed); for a passenger/walker — easy to moderate (walking up and down the serpentine ≈10 km, ascent ≈580 m)
alt-04.when: May to September; May — maralnik (Siberian rhododendron) in bloom, snow on the plateau; July–August — warm, but the bases are packed; September — colors (in mid-month there can be an invasion of stink bugs). In October most bases close. In winter entry is possible in a 4WD car, and winter is low on snow (January ≈ −7 °C)
alt-04.hours: Open around the clock, with no barriers. Base season is usually May–September (some from 15 April to 31 October)
alt-04.daytime: Morning — for the descent (fewer oncoming cars, soft light in the canyon); evening — a rainbow at Kurkure
alt-04.how: Overland: Novosibirsk/Barnaul → Biysk → Gorno-Altaysk → Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Aktash (≈310 km from Gorno-Altaysk, estimate) → Ulagan road: Krasnye Vorota (Red Gates, 8 km), Ulagan Pass 2080 m (26 km), Ulagan → Balyktuyul (74 km from Aktash) → ≈30 km of gravel to the pass (≈100 km from Aktash) → descent and ≈75 km along the valley to Lake Teletskoye. By water: from Artybash by ferry (5–6 h) or motorboat to the south shore, then up the valley by car/UAZ
alt-04.needcar: Yes: a prepared 4×4 / SUV, a tour with a jeep/UAZ, or a ferry with your car; there is no public transport into the valley
alt-04.self: Yes, in your own prepared 4×4 / SUV or by ferry with your car; without a car — only with a tour or a tourist base transfer
alt-04.roadtype: Ulagan road Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul: paved/gravel, under repair; Balyktuyul — pass ≈30 km of gravel with rocks; Katu-Yaryk — a single-lane rocky dirt serpentine; along the valley to Balykcha — dirt road
alt-04.traveltime: Aktash → pass ≈2.5–3 h; descent ≈20–30 min; pass → Ak-Kurum ≈1 h, → Balykcha ≈2–2.5 h (estimates). Gorno-Altaysk → pass — a full day
alt-04.stay: Dozens of bases (2GIS, 2026): Katu-Yaryk (km 34, from 4500 ₽, 4.6/80), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov (km 61, from 4500 ₽, 4.8/99), Dolina Vodopadov (km 61, from 3000 ₽, 4.9/67), Kamennye Griby campsite (km 61, from 2500 ₽, 4.3/79), Uchar (km 57, from 2000 ₽, 3.5/28), Zolotaya Dolina Chulyshmana (Koo, from 2500 ₽, 5.0/6), in Balykcha — Achelman (from 5000 ₽, 4.9/70), Start (from 7000 ₽, 4.4/57), Chulyshman (Cape Kyrsay, from 500 ₽, 3.9/53), the Vyshe Gor glamping (from 5000 ₽). Tents at campsites from 100 ₽/person (KP)
alt-04.net: Up top at Ulagan and Balyktuyul there is a signal; below the pass there was none for a long time (KP: none), since 2024–2025 it has appeared but is unstable (T—Zh, 2025); operators not specified. Some bases have Wi-Fi via satellite
alt-04.entry: Entry to the valley and the pass is free. Paid are the Altai Nature Reserve routes (Uchar; 100–250 ₽, data differ) and boat crossings. No border-zone permit needed
alt-04.transfer: Car ferry 15–17k ₽, pedestrian 3000 ₽ (2026); jeep tour from Aktash ≈23,000 ₽ per car (2022) / from 38,800 ₽ per group (Tripster, 2026); tour from Artybash 12,000 ₽/person
alt-04.bring: A full tank and a jerrycan (fuel stations only in Ulagan/Aktash), cash, food, a first-aid kit, a tow rope; repellent; warm clothes for the plateau and light ones for the valley
alt-04.warn: Katu-Yaryk is a steep single-lane serpentine without guardrails: only 4WD, high ground clearance and experience; rental companies fine you for the trip. After rains — rockfalls and fords. There are no shops, cafes or fuel stations in the valley. Bears: in August 2026 the reserve closed the Uchar trail. Ticks (May–July). No border-zone permit needed — Ulagan district is not in the border zone. From 2026 a new descent is being built nearby — construction machinery may be at work (no traffic restrictions found in the sources)
alt-04.food: Meals at the tourist bases (dinner for two from ≈1300 ₽, KP); grayling from the Chulyshman; at the top of the pass — a cafe by the viewpoint (Turister); in Ulagan and Aktash — cafes with Altai cuisine (kecheh-kasha, tutpash)
alt-04.reviews: Katu-Yaryk on 2GIS — 5.0 (6 ratings). Tourist bases in the valley on 2GIS: from 3.5 to 5.0 (Dolina Vodopadov 4.9/67, Achelman 4.9/70, Dolina Kamennykh Gribov 4.8/99). Pros: wild views, warmth, few people, “one of the most impressive descents in the world”; cons: a dangerous road, spartan conditions, prices high for the level, no signal
alt-04.photos.4.cap: The Chulyshman valley in late spring
alt-04.p.sum: There are two ways into the Chulyshman valley: overland via Aktash, Ulagan and the Katu-Yaryk descent (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass, then ≈75 km along the valley to the lake) — only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV; or by water from Artybash by ferry (with a car 15–17k ₽, 2026) or a tour. Entry is free, no permit needed. There are no shops or fuel stations in the valley, and the signal is unstable; stay overnight at dozens of tourist bases (from 500 to 7000 ₽, 2GIS 2026). A new two-lane descent is promised by the end of October 2027.

alt-05.name: Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms
alt-05.full: Ak-Kurum tract (valley) (Ak-Korum, Akkurum) — a slope on the right bank of the Chulyshman about 1.5 km from the mouth of the Chulcha, Chulyshman valley
alt-05.near: Koo village (≈5 km); tourist bases at km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (left bank, opposite the tract); Balykcha village (≈15 km, at Lake Teletskoye)
alt-05.elev: The pillar “mushrooms” are 1 to 7 m tall (up to 10 m per KP), the “caps” are boulders more than 2 m across; the gain from the river is ≈120 m (Turister). Absolute elevation — not found (the valley floor is ≈450–500 m)
alt-05.short: A field of “stone mushrooms” — clay-and-pebble pillars up to 7 m tall with heavy boulder caps on the slope above the Chulyshman. You cross by boat and climb on foot for about an hour.
alt-05.desc: Ak-Kurum is a tract (valley) on the slope of the Chulyshman’s right bank, about 15 km from Lake Teletskoye and ≈30 km below the Katu-Yaryk Pass. Dozens of “stone mushrooms” stand here — erosion pillars of clay and pebbles (former glacial deposits) topped with dense stone slabs, the “caps”. Rain and wind wash out the loose rock, while the stone on top protects the “stem” — so some mushrooms collapse and others slowly “grow”. The pillars are from 1 to 7 m tall, the caps more than 2 m. The tract has been declared a natural monument (since 1960 per Turister) and lies within the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. A large mushroom fell in the 1980s, and several more caps fell in the Chuya earthquake of 2003. Locals have a belief: when the last mushroom falls, the end of the world will come; and if you hold on to a “stem” and ask a question, the answer will come quickly. You can get there only from the left bank: the tourist bases at km 61 run a boat crossing, and then it is about an hour’s climb along a trail.
alt-05.guide: Take the first boat at 6:30–7:00: at 7–8 in the morning the sun lights up the mushrooms, and then the slope goes into the shadow of the mountains. The climb is steep and loose, but it takes about an hour — bring water and closed shoes. Don’t go under the caps or touch the pillars: they really do fall, the last time in the 2003 earthquake. According to the belief, if you hold the “stem” of a mushroom and ask a question, the answer will come soon; test it yourself. The trail to Uchar starts from the same place.
alt-05.see: The field of stone mushrooms itself and the viewpoint above it with a panorama of the Chulyshman valley; on the way — the “Shaman Rock” on the neighboring mountain (TripAdvisor); nearby — the start of the trail to Uchar, the Kurkure waterfall higher up the valley
alt-05.skip: you have already seen similar pillars (Cappadocia, Crimea, the Elbrus region) and are not ready to take the road over Katu-Yaryk or a 12-hour trip from Artybash for them
alt-05.diff: Easy–moderate: a boat crossing, then ≈1.5–2 km of a steep loose trail with a gain of ≈120 m, about an hour up; for the unprepared it is a “not very easy” climb

alt-05.daytime: Early morning (7:00–8:00) — the mushrooms are lit by the sun; in the daytime the slope is in shade most of the time

By water: from Artybash by ferry or motorboat to the southern shore of Lake Teletskoye, then ≈15 km along the valley. Then a boat across the Chulyshman and a climb of ≈1 h

Pros: unusual forms, a panorama of the valley, a mystical atmosphere; cons: a long road, a steep climb, “all the bases in the valley are alike” (TripAdvisor)

alt-05.p.sum: The stone mushrooms stand on the right bank of the Chulyshman, opposite the tourist bases at km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (≈30 km below Katu-Yaryk, ≈15 km from Lake Teletskoye). A boat across the river costs 1,000–1,500 ₽ per boat for up to 4 people round trip (2026), then ≈1 h of steep climbing (≈120 m). The best light is 7–8 in the morning. It is convenient to stay at the “Stone Mushrooms” campground (3,000–8,000 ₽ per cabin, 2026) or at the neighboring bases. From Artybash — a day tour for 12,000 ₽.

alt-06.name: Pazyryk Burial Mounds
alt-06.full: Pazyryk burial mounds — a Scythian-era burial ground in the Pazyryk tract (Bolshoy Ulagan valley), ≈4–4.5 km from Balyktuyul village, to the right of the road into the Chulyshman valley
alt-06.near: Balyktuyul village (≈4–4.5 km); Ulagan village (≈15–18 km)
alt-06.elev: ≈1,400 m above sea level (vdohaltay; not cross-checked). The mounds: diameter 24–47 m, height of the embankments 1.5–3.75 m, burial chambers at a depth of 4–5.2 m
alt-06.short: Five large stone burial mounds of the 5th–4th centuries BC that gave their name to the Pazyryk culture: from the permafrost here they extracted the world's oldest pile carpet, a chariot and tattooed mummies of chieftains. Today they are stone embankments by the road to Katu-Yaryk.
alt-06.desc: The Pazyryk tract lies in the Bolshoy Ulagan valley, a few kilometres from Balyktuyul, on the way from Ulagan to the Katu-Yaryk Pass. Five large mounds with stone embankments 24–47 m in diameter and 1.5–3.75 m high stand here in a chain, with smaller mounds next to them. They were excavated by M. P. Gryaznov (1929) and S. I. Rudenko (1947–1949; in 1948 L. N. Gumilev took part in the expedition). Under the embankments, at a depth of 4–5 m, log chambers with double walls and sarcophagus-logs were found; thanks to a lens of permafrost, organic material survived, along with mummified bodies of tattooed nobles, felt carpets and saddle cloths, 7–14 horses with trappings in each mound, a dismantled birch chariot, musical instruments and weapons. The most famous find is a pile carpet about 1.8×2 m in size (around 250,000 knots), the oldest known in the world. The finds are kept in the Hermitage (St. Petersburg), with some in museums in Gorno-Altaysk, Biysk and Novosibirsk. The mounds are part of a cluster of the Ak-Cholushpa nature park (since 2013), and the Pazyryk sites were added to UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List in 2018. Entry is free, and on site there is an information board and no museum buildings.
alt-06.guide: Don't expect a museum here: you'll see five stone “pancakes” in a steppe valley — all the magic is in what lay beneath them. Imagine: in this permafrost the world's oldest carpet lay for 2,500 years, along with a chieftain tattooed with fantastic beasts, and now they are in the Hermitage. Stop by on the way to Katu-Yaryk — it's 10–15 minutes from the road, and stand on top of the largest embankment for a panorama. If you want context, visit the museum in Ulagan or the National Museum in Gorno-Altaysk.
alt-06.see: Five large mounds and a chain of small ones; the information board by the road; a panorama of the Bolshoy Ulagan valley; on the way — the Ulagan Trakt (Red Gates, Dead Lake, Ulagan Pass); the history and ethnography museum in Ulagan
alt-06.skip: you want “wow views”: on site there are only grass-covered stone embankments, and all the treasures are in the Hermitage; but if you're heading to Katu-Yaryk it is worth stopping — it's almost on the way
alt-06.diff: Easy: you drive up, then walk across flat steppe for a few hundred metres

alt-06.p.sum: Five large stone burial mounds of the 5th–4th centuries BC in the Pazyryk tract — ≈4 km from Balyktuyul, to the right of the road to Katu-Yaryk (≈15–18 km from Ulagan, of which ≈15 km is dirt). Entry is free, and on site there is only an information board; the finds are in the Hermitage. It makes sense to stop on the way into the Chulyshman valley. Stay overnight in Ulagan (from 2,800 ₽) or Aktash (from 4,600 ₽), 2026.

alt-07.name: Chike-Taman Pass
alt-07.full: Chike-Taman Pass on the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), a spur of the Terekta Range, between the villages of Khabarovka (northern slope, Ursul valley) and Kupchegen (southern slope, Bolshoy Ilgumen valley)

alt-07.elev: 1295 m (Great Russian Encyclopedia; amic.ru; most sources); SibGid gives 1460 m — a discrepancy
alt-07.short: The second-highest pass on the Chuysky Trakt (1295 m, ≈km 659) with a steep serpentine road in granite cliffs, a viewing platform, a monument to road builders and a view of the abandoned old road.
alt-07.desc: Chike-Taman (“flat sole” in Altai) is a pass over a spur of the Terekta Range on the Chuysky Trakt, the watershed of the Ursul and the Bolshoy Ilgumen (according to other sources, the Maly and Bolshoy Ilgumen). The height is 1295 m, the pass is at km 659 of the highway (km 663 in the amic.ru article), and the climb and descent are about 4 km on each side (11 km of climb and descent combined per the Great Russian Encyclopedia). Traces of an ancient road here date from the 10th–12th centuries; by 1903 a pack trail with 34 sharp bends had been built, and cars first crossed the pass in 1924–1925. The modern paved road opened in 1984: more than 500,000 tonnes of earth were moved and about a dozen rocks blown up; the old narrow gravel road is still visible on the slope. Since 1996 the pass has been a natural monument of the Altai Republic (112.5 ha), valued also as a “monument of road construction of different eras”. The slopes are made of Cambrian-Ordovician sandstones and shales, and the pass has larch forests, rhododendron and edelweiss; in early spring yellow tulips bloom on the southern slopes. At the top there is a viewing platform with parking, vendor stalls (shashlik, chebureki, herbal tea, souvenirs), a cast-iron monument to road builders (2017), and a sacred larch with dyalama ribbons.
alt-07.guide: Don't just drive over the pass — park at the viewing platform and walk to the edge: below you can see the winding old road along which all the trucks to Mongolia drove until 1984. Drivers used to call the pass “Chert-Ataman” (“Devil Chieftain”) — look at the serpentine and you'll understand why. The ribbons on the larch are dyalama, an offering to the spirits of the pass: if you tie your own, take only a white or light one and don't touch other people's. Get herbal tea and a cheburek from the locals — it is a classic of the stop. The best light is in the morning on the northern side and at sunset on the southern valley.
alt-07.see: The viewing platform at the summit (the tour description mentions three viewpoints on the pass); a view of the old road of 1903–1984; the monument to the road worker (2017); the sacred larch with ribbons; a panorama of mountains of 2500–2600 m; the granite rock cuts of the serpentine; in spring — yellow tulips and rhododendron.
alt-07.skip: You are driving the highway in winter in icy conditions or in fog: a stop at the viewpoint will show nothing anyway, and the serpentine demands attention. If you are heading to Kalbak-Tash and the Chuya with children who get carsick on serpentines — get out to stretch your legs only at the top.
alt-07.diff: Easy: a paved approach, a few dozen meters from the parking area to the viewpoint
alt-07.when: Late spring to mid-autumn; autumn (September to early October) is the most colorful time (Bolshaya Strana). In winter the pass is passable, but ice is possible.

alt-07.daytime: Morning and evening — soft side light on the serpentine (editorial); on summer days the parking area is crowded
alt-07.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt R-256: from Gorno-Altaysk ≈220–230 km (Ongudai is 200 km from Gorno-Altaysk, then ≈25 km more), from Biysk ≈310–320 km, from Barnaul 8–9 h by car. By public transport — the Gorno-Altaysk–Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) goes over the pass, a stop at the summit by arrangement with the driver; catching a passing service back is hard. The most convenient way is your own car or an excursion.

alt-07.roadtype: Paved road of the federal highway R-256, a serpentine of ≈4 km of climb and ≈4 km of descent; the old road is dirt/gravel and abandoned
alt-07.traveltime: From Gorno-Altaysk ≈3–3.5 h by car (marshrutka (minibus) to Ongudai 2 h 50 min + ≈25 km); from Biysk ≈5 h; from Ongudai ≈30 min

alt-07.bring: A warm jacket/windbreaker (the weather changes sharply), cash for vendors, water and a snack, sun protection
alt-07.warn: A serpentine with sharp bends — don't stop on the roadside outside the platform. Ice and snow are possible from autumn to spring. A seismically active area (tremors of the 2003 Chuya earthquake were felt). Don't go along the old road to the edge of the rock cuts. R-256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; work continues until the end of 2026 at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — narrowing and reversing traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 an 18 km reconstruction near Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway without casualties was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys. There is no border zone here. Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Ongudai district is among the districts with bites). Payment terminals in villages work unreliably — bring cash (OneTwoTrip, 10.2024). Parking at the summit is small, and on the approach there is a “no stopping” sign and yellow markings: don't stop on the serpentine (2GIS reviews).
alt-07.food: The “Hello Chike-Taman” canteen in Khabarovka village (Severnaya St., 23; 4.8 from 122 ratings, bill ≈450 ₽, 2GIS 2026); chebureki, shashlik and herbal tea at the vendor stalls on the pass; in Ongudai — Leto na Altae (“Summer in Altai”) (bill ≈350 ₽), Nikitka (manty and pelmeni made from maral venison), Altyn (Altai cuisine)
alt-07.reviews: 2GIS: 5.0 (1828–1834 ratings, 242 reviews, 2026); Google: 4.9 (3532 reviews, per Wanderlog). Separately on 2GIS: “Chike Taman old road” — 4.0 (2), Chike-Taman souvenir markets — 3.5–5.0. Pros: views, the serpentine, the old road, a convenient platform. Cons: crowded in summer, trading and paid photos in costumes.

alt-08.name: Seminsky Pass
alt-08.full: Seminsky Pass on the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway, km 583), Seminsky Range, the watershed of the Sema and Ursul rivers
alt-08.near: Topuchaya village (western ascent), Tuekta village (eastern descent), the district centers Shebalino and Ongudai
alt-08.elev: 1717 m (most sources; 1700, 1719 and 1780 m also appear)
alt-08.short: The highest pass on the Chuysky Trakt (1717 m): cedar taiga, an obelisk marking 200 years since Altai joined Russia, a souvenir market, cafes and a ski base.
alt-08.desc: Seminsky Pass is the highest point of the Chuysky Trakt (km 583), the boundary between Northern and Central Altai and the watershed of the Sema and Ursul. Its elevation is 1717 m; the ascent from the west is ≈8 km (gaining ≈510 m), and the descent to the east is ≈11 km. The Altai name is Dyal-Menku (“Eternal Mane”); the Russian one is linked either to the Mongolian “sebi” (“fortress”) or to the Sema river. In the 19th century the pass was the hardest section of the road — mud in summer, snowdrifts in winter; it became easily passable only by the 1930s. In 1956 an obelisk was erected here in honor of the 200th anniversary of the voluntary entry of Gorny Altai into Russia (1756). Around it are cedar groves, subalpine meadows with globeflowers (zharki), dwarf-birch scrub; it is a natural monument with four endemics from the Red Data Book of the Altai Republic. Above the pass rise Mount Sarlyk (2507 m), the highest point of the Seminsky Range, and the more accessible Tyukhtya (1899 m). At the roadside area there is a souvenir market (honey, pine nuts, felt, herbs), several cafes and toilets; nearby are the Seminsky Pass training center (since 1986, ski runs up to 1000 m with a drop of up to 200 m) and the Dinamo tourist base. The weather is changeable: snow can fall even in summer, and already in mid-September (12.09.2024).
alt-08.guide: This is the highest point of the whole trakt — get out of the car and feel how much colder it is here than in Gorno-Altaysk. The obelisk was erected in 1956 for the 200th anniversary of Altai joining Russia — take a photo with the cedars behind it. At the market buy honey, pine nuts and herbal blends, but compare prices — reviews complain about markups. If you have a whole day and good weather, climb Sarlyk (2507 m): “wild yak” in Altai, and from there you can see the Tuyuk Lakes. The ribbons on the trees are dyalama, offerings to the spirits of the pass.
alt-08.see: The obelisk marking 200 years of Altai joining Russia (1956); a viewing platform with a view of snowy peaks; cedar forest; a souvenir market; Mount Sarlyk (2507 m) and Tyukhtya (1899 m); the Tuyuk Lakes (from Sarlyk); in winter — the ski runs of the training center.
alt-08.skip: You have already seen plenty of passes and are driving into fog — but the stop is still convenient for stretching your legs, eating and getting a coffee. If you don't like souvenir markets, just stand by the obelisk for 10 minutes.
alt-08.diff: Easy (the roadside area); Sarlyk — moderate, 8–10 h
alt-08.when: June–September for views and walks (globeflowers bloom in June); November to May — snow, skiing and snowmobiles; snow is possible in summer too
alt-08.hours: Around the clock, free; the cafes and market operate in daytime, year-round (per travelto), exact hours not found
alt-08.daytime: Morning — fewer tour buses and soft light; in the daytime in summer it is very crowded (editorial)
alt-08.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt R256: ≈150 km from Gorno-Altaysk (≈3 h), ≈140 km from Gorno-Altaysk airport, ≈370 km from Barnaul. All services to Ongudai, Kosh-Agach, Ulagan and back to Biysk/Barnaul go through the pass — Yandex.Schedules has a “Seminsky Pass” stop.

alt-08.warn: Snow and ice are possible from September to May; strong westerly wind, blizzards in winter, down to −20 °C and below. R256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; until the end of 2026 work continues at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — lane narrowing and reversible traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 an 18 km reconstruction near Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the road with no casualties was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The trakt is periodically closed for military convoys. For the Sarlyk hike clear weather is a must; it is 10–15 °C colder at the top, with wind up to 35 m/s. There is no border zone. Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3,600 reports of tick bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Ongudai District is among the districts with bites).
alt-08.food: Cafes at km 582 (2GIS, 2026): “Kedr Zolotoy” — home cooking, 4.8 (64), average bill ≈250 ₽; “Shugurat” — 4.9 (69), average bill ≈450 ₽; “Priroda” (km 582, 12, at Dinamo) — 4.8 (49), average bill ≈950 ₽; “Seminsky” — average bill ≈600 ₽; “U Mikhailovny” — fast food. At the market — Altai honey, pine nuts, herbal teas, fish
alt-08.reviews: Yandex Maps (viewpoint “Seminsky Pass”): 5.0, 13,140 ratings, 3,138 reviews (2026); TripAdvisor: 4.3 (24 reviews, No. 2 of 6 in Ongudai; in 2025 road repairs were noted). Pluses: views, cedars, the obelisk, toilets and cafes. Minuses: “prices are not always reasonable”, crowded, trading at the summit.

alt-09.name: Confluence of the Chuya and Katun
alt-09.full: Confluence of the Chuya and Katun rivers (Altai: Chuy-Oozy — “mouth of the Chuya”), km 712–714 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), between the villages of Inya and Iodro, at the turn-off to Inegen
alt-09.near: Inya village (≈7 km, km 703), Inegen village (beyond the bridge over the Katun), Iodro village
alt-09.elev: The exact elevation of the confluence was not found; a guide point is Inegen village ≈6 km upstream on the Katun: 750 m (Znanie); the viewing terrace is ≈120 m above the water (Great Russian Encyclopedia)
alt-09.short: The place where the muddy-white Chuya flows into the turquoise Katun: two colours of water run side by side against a backdrop of cliffs and river terraces; a sacred place of the Altai people right by the highway.
alt-09.desc: Chuy-Oozy is the mouth of the Chuya, where it flows into the Katun at km 712–714 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), about 7 km beyond the village of Inya. The Katun, flowing from the Belukha glaciers, is turquoise-green here, while the Chuya, which collects water from high-mountain steppes and clayey banks, is murky, milky-grey; at the line of the confluence the two streams run side by side for a while without mixing. The contrast is best seen from late July and especially in autumn, when the Katun finally clears of the silt from meltwater; in early summer both rivers may be muddy. The valley is formed by a system of up to 23 river terraces of different heights (210–230 m, 80–100 m, 3–8 m); the area was proposed as a geomorphological natural monument, “Mouth of the Chuya River” (110 ha). In 2002 the Chuy-Oozy nature park was created here (810 ha — the smallest in the republic, >400 species of flowering plants), and by 2011 it had lost its status. On the right bank of the Chuya there are the Ak-Uzyuk/“Chuy-Oozy” petroglyphs (8th–7th centuries BC), a tourist complex with a guesthouse and café, and 8–10 km upstream on the Chuya the Kalbak-Tash sanctuary. By the viewing area there is a gazebo where souvenirs are sold; opposite stands the Baatyr-Tash rock, in whose outline people see the head of a hero and a horse. For the Altai people this is a sacred place: people don't make noise or litter here.
alt-09.guide: Come here in August–September: in summer the Katun is still muddy, and instead of two colours you'll see “one dirty river and another a bit cleaner” — as disappointed bloggers honestly put it. Look opposite for the Baatyr-Tash rock — you can make out a hero's head and a horse in it. There is a legend about the “camel's neck” (Kyyo-Moyn): a man survived a deadly hailstorm by sheltering in a camel's carcass. For a better angle, cross the bridge towards Inegen — from the second viewpoint you can see how the Chuya “pours” into the Katun. This is a place of power for the Altai people: speak quietly and don't throw anything into the water.
alt-09.see: The two-colour confluence from the roadside viewing area; the second viewpoint by the road to Inegen (across the bridge over the Katun); the Baatyr-Tash rock; river terraces; the Ak-Uzyuk/Chuy-Oozy petroglyphs by the highway; the ovoo (cairn) and dyalama ribbons by the gazebo; the Inya (Tsaplin) suspension bridge of 1936 in Inya.
alt-09.skip: You're going in June or early July and have already seen the confluence in photos: during the flood both rivers are muddy and there is almost no effect. But the stop takes 15 minutes — on the way to Kalbak-Tash it is worth getting out anyway.
alt-09.diff: Very easy: a viewing area by the highway
alt-09.when: From late July to October (the Katun clears, turquoise colour); in autumn — yellow larches. June–July — flood, weaker contrast.
alt-09.daytime: The second half of the day and sunset — the best light according to 2GIS reviews; in the morning soft light (Inegen blog)

The Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) goes past — ask to be dropped off at the confluence; on the way back, catch a passing service/taxi from Inya.

alt-09.warn: Be careful at the edges of the terraces and by the water, especially after rain and in winter. Do not swim — strong current, icy water. The café of the Chuy-Oozy complex was previously closed by a court for sanitary violations (welcometoaltai) — check reviews. R-256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; until the end of 2026 work is under way at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — lane narrowing and alternating traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 — reconstruction of 18 km at Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway with no injuries was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys. There is no border zone (Ongudai district). Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3,600 reports of tick bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (the Ongudai district is among the districts with bites). Card terminals in the villages work unreliably — bring cash (OneTwoTrip, 10.2024).
alt-09.food: At the viewing area there are kiosks: cheese flatbreads, yak and maral (Altai red deer) chebureks (cheese cheburek ≈250 ₽), manty, belyashi; teas and halva (2GIS reviews, 2025). Chuy-Oozy café (Chuyozy village, 1 G. M. Toptygina St.; national cuisine, bill ≈600 ₽) — 3.2 from 111 ratings. In Inya: Kechu (4.9), Vkus Altaya (4.8)
alt-09.reviews: 2GIS: 4.9 (75 ratings, 42 reviews, 2026). Pros: colour contrast, a “place of power”, convenient from the highway. Cons: in summer the effect is weak (samokatus, 07.2025), crowded. Chuy-Oozy petroglyphs — 4.6 (34 ratings, 2GIS).

alt-10.name: Kalbak-Tash Petroglyphs
alt-10.full: Kalbak-Tash tract — a sanctuary with petroglyphs on the right bank of the Chuya, km 723 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), between the villages of Inya and Iodro
alt-10.near: Inya village (≈18–20 km to the west), Iodro village (≈12 km to the east, per Sayan Ring)
alt-10.short: The largest petroglyph complex in Gorny Altai, right by the Chuysky Trakt: 3,000–5,000 rock carvings from the Neolithic to the Old Turkic era and the largest Old Turkic runic inscription in Russia.
alt-10.desc: Kalbak-Tash (“flat/hanging stone”) is a tract on the right bank of the Chuya about 10 km from its confluence with the Katun, at km 723 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway). Rock outcrops with carvings stretch along the valley for ≈10 km (km 717–726), and the main exhibition is fenced off and developed by the highway. It was discovered in 1912 by the artists G. I. Choros-Gurkin and D. I. Kuznetsov and has been studied systematically since the 1980s. Estimates range from ≈3,000 to more than 5,000 images (figures differ), aged from 2,500 to 6,000–8,000 years: Neolithic animals, Bronze Age people, warriors, domestic animals, Scythian scenes of hunting ibex and big cats, and Old Turkic inscriptions of the 9th–10th centuries. Among the well-known images are the “Altai chimera”, the sanctuary of the goddess Umay, the “celestial ibex”, the only depiction of an ancient boat in Altai, and mysterious figures in “helmets” with “tails” (they are sometimes passed off as “aliens”; scholars see shamans or priestesses). The runic inscription — about 30 lines — is considered the largest Old Turkic one in Russia. On the site there are wooden railings and information signs; entry is paid, and local guides work here. The site lies within the boundaries of the former Chuy-Oozy nature park — people navigate by the sign for it.
alt-10.guide: Be sure to take a local guide at the entrance: without one you'll see only “scribbles” in the cracks of the rocks, and with one — deer, the chimera and hunting scenes. Look for the “aliens” in helmets — it's a popular riddle at Kalbak-Tash, and guides love to solve it. Come in the morning or toward evening: in side light the carvings are much easier to read than at noon. There are three “stones” on the site — a female one, a male one and a wish-granting one; touch only those, not the petroglyphs. Bring cash — there may be no card terminal.
alt-10.see: The main fenced-off exhibition with a trail; the Old Turkic runic inscription (~30 lines); the Umay sanctuary; the “Altai chimera”; the “celestial ibex”; the depiction of a boat; sun signs and a “star map”; figures in “helmets”; wish stones; a view of the Chuya valley.
alt-10.skip: You're not interested in archaeology and aren't ready to take a guide: without explanations the carvings are hard to make out, and the visit turns into a walk over rocks. It's hard on the open rocks in the hot midday.
alt-10.diff: Easy: a walk over rocks and a trail for 1–3 h, small climbs
alt-10.when: May–October (guides work); spring and autumn are more comfortable temperature-wise. In winter the site is accessible, but the carvings may be under snow (not confirmed).
alt-10.hours: According to 2GIS reviews: 9:00–17:00 (September 2024); in February 2025 — “closed on schedule” (the ticket office may be closed in winter); in April 2026 — open, entry paid, with a guided tour. Blogs give 8:00–21:00 (Turister, Sayan Ring, Snovatrip). Phone on 2GIS: +7 983 327-82-17 (the data has not been updated for a long time).
alt-10.daytime: Morning and early evening — slanting light makes the carvings stand out more (editorial note)
alt-10.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to km 723 — the sign of the Chuy-Oozy nature and economic park: ≈288–290 km from Gorno-Altaysk (≈4.5 h), ≈376 km from Biysk. The Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) goes past — ask to be stopped at Kalbak-Tash.
alt-10.self: Yes (entry is paid, the guide is optional; according to Sibalt-2023 a guide was mandatory — check)
alt-10.roadtype: Paved R-256, parking by the highway; on the site — a trail over rocks
alt-10.traveltime: ≈4.5 h from Gorno-Altaysk; ≈1.5 h from Ongudai; ≈15 min from the confluence
alt-10.stay: The nearest are the holiday camps in Inya (Chetyre Bogatyrya from 3,000 ₽, Alkyshtu from 4,000 ₽) and the Inegen agro-complex; further on — Aktash; Maly Yaloman — Baylyk, Ail (from 2,500 ₽), Baykan on the Katun bank (from 3,000 ₽) — 2GIS 2026

Rough figure for 2026: ≈300–350 ₽.
alt-10.transfer: Excursions 8,000–12,900 ₽/person (group tours along the highway), private ones 27,000–45,000 ₽ per vehicle (2026)
alt-10.bring: Cash (according to reviews, receipts aren't always issued), comfortable shoes, water, a hat, sun protection
alt-10.warn: Do not touch or trace the carvings, and don't climb the fenced-off rocks — it is a cultural heritage site. It is hot on the open rocks in summer; snakes and ticks are possible (common in Altai). Complaints in reviews: no receipts, litter. R-256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; until the end of 2026 work is under way at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — lane narrowing and alternating traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 — reconstruction of 18 km at Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway with no injuries was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys. There is no border zone (Ongudai district). Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3,600 reports of tick bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (the Ongudai district is among the districts with bites). Card terminals in the villages work unreliably — bring cash (OneTwoTrip, 10.2024).
alt-10.food: A café on site is mentioned (2GIS review, 10.2024); nearby — the Chuy-Oozy café in Chuyozy village (bill ≈600 ₽, 3.2 on 2GIS) and kiosks at the confluence (yak and maral (Altai red deer) chebureks); in Inya — Kechu, Vkus Altaya
alt-10.reviews: 2GIS: 4.5 (161–167 ratings, 92–95 reviews, 2024–2026). Pros: “the petroglyphs are simply fire”, strong guides, the energy of the place. Cons: payments without receipts, poor infrastructure, litter.

alt-11.name: Uch-Enmek Nature Park (Karakol Valley)
alt-11.full: Karakol (ethno)nature park “Uch Enmek” — the valley of the Karakol River (a tributary of the Ursul) and the northern slopes of the Terekta Range; the entrance is by the village of Karakol at km 618–620 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway)
alt-11.near: Karakol village (on the highway, km 620), the villages of the valley Bichiktu-Boom, Boochi, Kulada; Talda village; the district center Ongudai (≈15 km)
alt-11.elev: from ≈890–900 m (Ursul valley, Karakol 895 m) to 2,821 m (Mount Uch-Enmek; 2,792 m according to other data)
alt-11.short: The sacred Karakol Valley beneath the three-headed Mount Uch-Enmek: about 5,000 archaeological monuments — burial mounds, steles, petroglyphs, deer stones — and the “Eye of Tengri” eco-trail in a nature park of ≈60,500 ha.
alt-11.desc: The Uch Enmek nature park was established by a decree of the Government of the Altai Republic of 23 April 2001 (a municipal ethnopark had existed since 1998) on the initiative of local residents and Altai keepers of sacred places led by Danil Mamyev. The Karakol cluster is 60,551 ha (a strict-protection zone of 810.4 ha, a limited-use zone of ≈4,776 ha, a recreation zone of ≈54,965 ha); in 2011 the Argut cluster (20,572 ha) was added to the park, for a total area of 81,123 ha. The park is managed by the Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic. The Karakol valley holds the villages of Bichiktu-Boom, Boochi and Kulada; the Chuysky Trakt passes through the northern part. The name of Mount Uch-Enmek is translated as “three peaks/crowns” (or “three sources”); for the Altai people it is the “navel of the earth”, and climbing it is forbidden by tradition. More than 5,000 monuments of the Afanasievo (3rd millennium BC), Karakol, Scythian (Pazyryk) and Old Turkic cultures have been recorded here: burial mounds (the largest, at Kulada, are ≈40 m in diameter), stone steles, deer stones, the petroglyphs of Bichiktu-Boom, the Bashadar and Tuekta mounds, and a Paleolithic site near Karakol (50,000–40,000 years old). The high mountains hold cascades of glacial lakes, the largest and most visited being Aru-Kem (Arugem, ≈1,300–1,500 m). With the support of WWF the “Eye of Tengri” eco-trail has been set up (2.3 km, information boards, shelters, viewing platforms). The park receives about 1,000 organized tourists a year; 50–100 local residents work as guides and rent out horses and cars.
alt-11.guide: The Karakol Valley is not a museum behind glass: the burial mounds stand right in the fields, and without a local guide you will walk past them. Ask to be shown Mount Uch-Enmek from three points — the Altai people consider it the “navel of the earth”, and it must not be climbed. Walk the “Eye of Tengri” eco-trail (2.3 km) at dawn or in the evening, when the valley is in soft light. Do not climb the mounds or take stones — these are the graves of ancestors. If you have a day, go to Lake Aru-Kem: about 4.5 km on foot, and in summer the water warms up to +22 °C.
alt-11.see: The burial mounds and steles of the Karakol Valley (the cluster at Kulada — 57 mounds); the petroglyphs of Bichiktu-Boom; the Bashadar mounds; the Tuekta mounds; Mount Uch-Enmek (2,821 m) from viewpoints; the “Eye of Tengri” eco-trail; Lake Aru-Kem; the stone statue Kezer-Tash; Kulada — local history museum (200 ₽, 2026); the “Ail — Model of the World” program at the info center. The Bashadar mounds are at Kulada on the left bank of the Karakol (50.7094, 85.7756), Pazyryk culture of the 6th–3rd centuries BC, excavated by S. I. Rudenko in 1950, the largest mound is 58 m in diameter.
alt-11.skip: You have only a couple of hours and no guide — without the story the mounds look like piles of stones in a field. If you do not like “spiritual” tourism and ethno programs, limit yourself to a stop in Ongudai.
alt-11.diff: Easy (a car tour and the 2.3 km eco-trail); Aru-Kem — moderate (≈4.5 km, gain ≈250 m)
alt-11.when: May–September (excursions to Aru-Kem — from May); a geocacher does not recommend winter visits to remote points
alt-11.hours: The territory is open year-round; the info center/tourist complex “Uch-Enmek” in Karakol — 24 hours (2GIS). Visits to the strict-protection and buffer zones are only with a guide and with the consent of the park directorate.
alt-11.daytime: Morning and evening (editorial): soft light on the mounds and the mountain
alt-11.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to Karakol village (km 620): ≈180 km from Gorno-Altaysk (≈3 h by car, ≈2+ h by taxi per Khan-Altai’s estimate), via the Seminsky Pass. Scheduled buses Gorno-Altaysk – Ongudai (16:00) and the marshrutka (minibus) to Kosh-Agach (09:00) pass through Karakol. The villages of the valley (Kulada — 20 km from the highway, the end of road 84K-21) — by car.

alt-11.self: Partly: the eco-trail and the mounds by the road — yes; the buffer zone and sacred places — only with a guide and with the directorate’s permission

alt-11.entry: From 01.07.2026 the fee for visiting regional protected areas of the Altai Republic rose from 100 to 300 ₽ (Altai Republic residents pay the previous rate) — whether the rate applies to “Uch Enmek” and how it is collected on site is not confirmed. The museum in Kulada — 200 ₽ (children under 14 free). There is no resort fee.
alt-11.transfer: A private excursion from Gorno-Altaysk — 23,100 ₽ per car (2026); group tours 3,600–4,300 ₽ in the past (not currently run)
alt-11.bring: Comfortable shoes, a hat, water, a windbreaker; repellent and tick-bite insurance (not included in tours); cash
alt-11.warn: This is sacred land: do not climb Mount Uch-Enmek, do not touch the mounds, steles and ribbons, do not light fires near sanctuaries. Ticks (spring–early summer) — tick insurance is not included in tours. Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor (the consumer-protection agency) for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3,600 reports of tick bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (the Ongudai District is among the districts with bites). There is no border zone (Ongudai District). R256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; until the end of 2026 work continues on km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — lane narrowing and alternating traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 an 18 km section near Souzga–Manzherok is being reconstructed with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway was reported with no casualties (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys.
alt-11.food: Altai cuisine and dinners at the “Uch-Enmek” tourist complex (a demonstration of traditional life and cooking); cafés in Ongudai; in Ongudai (15 km): “Leto na Altae” (borscht, lagman, bill ≈350 ₽), “Nikitka” (manti and pelmeni made from maral deer meat, ≈230 ₽), “Altyn” (Altai cuisine, ≈800 ₽), “Derevenka” — 2GIS 2026
alt-11.reviews: 2GIS: the “Uch-Enmek” tourist complex — 4.8 (71–86 ratings); “Uch-Enmek Nature Park, Karakol cluster” — 5.0 (16 ratings); the park office in Ongudai — 4.3 (8). Pros: the atmosphere, the guides, the mounds, the views. Cons: few signposts, hard without a guide.
alt-11.p.sum: A valley-reserve of Altai holy sites 15 km from Ongudai. The base is the tourist complex/info center “Uch-Enmek” in Karakol on the highway; beyond it — mounds, petroglyphs and the eco-trail with a guide, and for a full day — Lake Aru-Kem.

alt-12.name: Taldy Caves
alt-12.full: Taldy (Tavda) Caves — a karst massif on the left bank of the Katun opposite the settlement of Izvestkovy (Altai Republic), in the Biryuzovaya Katun (Turquoise Katun) resort zone
alt-12.near: Izvestkovy settlement (Maima District of the Altai Republic, on the Chuysky Trakt, right bank, ≈2.3 km to the south); Aya village and the Biryuzovaya Katun resort zone (Altai Krai)
alt-12.elev: entrances 40–200 m above the Katun; the viewing platform ≈100 m above the river; the Arch of Wishes 80 m above the river (absolute elevation not found)
alt-12.short: About 30 karst caves in limestone cliffs above the Katun: the developed Big Taldy Cave, 1,107 steps, viewing platforms and an arch — the most visited cave site near Gorno-Altaysk.
alt-12.desc: The Taldy, or Tavda, caves are a complex of about 30 caves in Cambrian limestones of the Taldy karst massif, stretching ≈5 km along the left bank of the Katun. The name “Tavda” is linked with the word “tavda” (high bank), and “Taldy” with “tal” (willow). The site is a natural monument of regional significance in Altai Krai (per the Great Russian Encyclopedia it was declared in 2010, area 360 ha; by other data it has been protected since 1998), and is part of the tourist-recreation special economic zone Biryuzovaya Katun. The main one is Big Taldy (Tavda, “Maiden's Tears”): the main gallery is ≈140 m, the total length of passages ≈270 m, with electric lighting and stairs; nearby are Tavda-2 (≈250 m), Bear's Den and others. Excavations found traces of Bronze Age and early Iron Age camps; in the early 19th century Old Believer hermits lived here, and later people searched for “Kolchak's gold”. Visits are organized by the “Crossroads of Worlds” archaeological park: the main excursion “Taldy Caves” is 1.2 km, ≈1.5 h, 1,107 steps, a viewing platform 100 m above the Katun, the “Dragon's Nostrils” and the Arch of Wishes; there are also “Exciting Speleology” (4 h), the “Robinson Trail”, the “Ancestors' Trail” and “Place of Power”. Independent exploration of the caves is not allowed — groups with a guide.
alt-12.guide: This is not Ongudai and not even the Altai Republic: the caves stand on the left, “krai” bank of the Katun, 40 km from Gorno-Altaysk — easy to fit into the first day of a trip. Be ready for 1,107 steps — the climb is brisk, but from the viewing platform the whole Katun valley opens up. Find the “Dragon's Nostrils” and make a wish at the Arch — nature and legend hung it 80 m above the river. Bring a flashlight and a jacket: it is cool in the cave and in places you will have to stoop. In rain the caves may be closed — then guides lead you along the “Ancestors' Trail”.
alt-12.see: Big Taldy Cave with its lighting; the viewing platform 100 m above the Katun; the “Dragon's Nostrils”; the Arch of Wishes (a natural monument); Tavda-2 and Bear's Den (on the speleology route); an ancient human campsite; the Roerich monument; nearby — the Kamyshla Waterfall and the artificial lake of Biryuzovaya Katun.
alt-12.skip: Stairs are hard for you (1,107 steps) or you are traveling with a child under 7 — according to KP, small children are not taken on the route. If you want “wild” Altai without crowds — in summer this is a conveyor of groups.
alt-12.diff: Moderate: 1.2 km and 1,107 steps, stooping in places; the speleology route is hard (4 h, climbing)
alt-12.when: May–September; season: May — the beginning, July–August — the peak (queues of groups), September — a decline (Yandex reviews). Visits only in dry weather.
alt-12.hours: Daily 10:00–18:00 (KP, gorniy-altai.ru); in winter check with “Crossroads of Worlds” (+7 905 925-10-11)
alt-12.daytime: Morning — fewer groups and cooler on the stairs (editorial)
alt-12.how: By car: along the Chuysky Trakt from Gorno-Altaysk to Souzga, after it turn right onto the free bridge over the Katun at Aya, then ≈15–20 km along the Aya Trakt through Biryuzovaya Katun; the entrance is 200–250 m beyond the artificial lake on the right. Entry to Biryuzovaya Katun has been free since 2018. On foot/by public transport: by bus from Gorno-Altaysk to Izvestkovy (the buses to Chemal go along the trakt) and across the Katun by the bridge at the Arzhan-Suu spring (≈1 km to the caves; driving a car over this bridge is paid — 150–350 ₽ according to different reviews).
alt-12.needcar: Desirable (car/taxi/excursion); you can take a bus to Izvestkovy + walk across the bridge
alt-12.self: Getting there — yes; inside the caves — only as part of a group with a “Crossroads of Worlds” guide (per Yandex reviews of 2025–2026: a self-guided 40–45 min format is also sold)
alt-12.roadtype: Paved to the entrance (Aya Trakt / Biryuzovaya Katun); on the route — wooden stairs and trails
alt-12.traveltime: ≈40–60 min from Gorno-Altaysk by car; ≈3.5–4 h from Barnaul
alt-12.stay: Hotels and tourist bases of Biryuzovaya Katun: Domina Altai Shambhala (next to the caves, spa, pool), Altai Palace “Maralnik”, Grand Chalet Altay, “Podgoritsa” (economy, 3 km), “SrediGor”, “Kedrovy Bereg”, “Dom Katun” (per sibalt.ru, prices not found)
alt-12.net: not found (a resort zone near Gorno-Altaysk — coverage is expected but not confirmed)
alt-12.entry: Excursion “Taldy Caves”: 600 ₽ adult, 300 ₽ child (Yandex reviews, July 2026); 1,300 ₽ for 3 tickets — adult, child, pensioner (June 2026); independently 500 ₽ (September 2025). Earlier: 200/100 ₽ (2022); 900 ₽/person as part of a private tour (putevka). There is no resort fee.

alt-12.bring: Comfortable shoes with good tread, a jacket/sweater (it is cool in the cave), a flashlight, water; for children — spare clothes
alt-12.warn: The site is in Altai Krai, not in the Altai Republic (the krai's rules and the SEZ rules apply on this bank). Visit the caves only in dry weather; 1,107 steps are hard for people with heart conditions and limited mobility; dogs are not allowed into the caves (there are kennels); per KP, children under 7 are not admitted. Ticks in spring — early summer. Do not stray from the group and don't climb into unlit passages. The fee for driving over the bridge at Arzhan-Suu is 350 ₽ (Yandex review, 2026).
alt-12.food: Cafes and souvenir stalls at the entrance and in Biryuzovaya Katun; mountain honey from apiaries (included in some excursions)
alt-12.reviews: Yandex Maps: 5.0 (8,186 ratings, 2,711 reviews, 2026); 2GIS: “Tavda Caves” 4.9 (1,539 ratings). Pluses: views of the Katun, fun guides, a widened tunnel. Minuses: many steps, mandatory groups, no dogs, summer crowds.
alt-12.p.sum: A paid excursion site in the Biryuzovaya Katun resort zone (Altai Krai), 40 km from Gorno-Altaysk; the main excursion is 1.2 km / 1.5 h / 1,107 steps. It is not connected with Ongudai or the Karakol Valley.
