alt-13.name: Geyser Lake
alt-13.full: A small spring-fed lake in the swampy forested valley of the Mena stream (Chuya basin) by the Chuysky Trakt, 5–7 km south of the village of Aktash (towards Kurai/Kosh-Agach); the entrance is through a tourist base (called “Maly Rai” / “Mena” in different sources).
alt-13.near: Aktash village (5–7 km along the highway; per kp.ru ~1 km from the edge of the village to the path); Kurai village — ~25–30 km further along the highway (map estimate, not verified)
alt-13.elev: not found (Aktash is ~1,400 m; the exact elevation of the lake is not confirmed)
alt-13.short: A tiny (25–30 m, ~2 m deep) never-freezing lake with turquoise water, where springs on the bottom push up blue clay and draw changing concentric patterns; one of the most popular stops on the Chuysky Trakt.
alt-13.desc: Geyser Lake (also called Geyzerovoye, Blue or Silver Lake) is a small body of water 25–30 m across and about 2 m deep in a swampy larch-and-cedar forest by the Chuysky Trakt south of Aktash. There are no real geysers here: underground springs well up on the bottom and periodically (from seconds to minutes according to observers, roughly every half hour according to Altapress) push out grey-blue clay and sand, forming patterns on the bottom that look like a cross-section of malachite. The water is clear and cold (about 3 °C per altai.travel, about +7 °C per awd.is), and the lake does not freeze in winter. The lake became widely known in the 2000s; a popular version links its appearance/activation to the 2003 Chuya earthquake, but this is not scientifically confirmed (amic.ru 2012: “no explanation found”). The first tourist bases nearby appeared around 2010, and the wooden path was built around 2017 (kp.ru). Access is via a paid wooden boardwalk (~200–500 m, 5–10 minutes) across the marsh from the parking area by the highway; on site there are a cafe, souvenirs, toilets and viewing platforms. Swimming is prohibited. It is now a compulsory stop on most Chuysky Trakt tours, so it is crowded here in the daytime in summer.
alt-13.guide: Stand on the boardwalk and wait a couple of minutes: the springs on the bottom “switch on” unexpectedly, and the patterns of blue clay start moving right before your eyes. The turquoise is brightest in sunshine (although reviews say the colour is richer in overcast weather — check for yourself), and there are fewest people early in the morning, before the tour buses arrive. Locals also call it the Blue Lake and the Silver Lake, and a popular legend ties its birth to the 2003 earthquake. Do not touch the water or go into the lake — the silty bottom is slippery and the patterns get destroyed. Combine it with the Aktash relay station and the Kurai steppe — it makes one day along the highway.
alt-13.see: Patterns on the bottom made by the springs (look from the boardwalk and the raised spots); the wooden path through the marsh and the cedar-larch forest; figurines of fairy-tale characters for children along the path (tonkosti, gorniy-altai.ru — “Baba Yaga’s hut”); grayling live in the lake (altai.travel).
alt-13.skip: you expect real geysers or a big lake: it is a 30 m patch, the visit takes 15–40 minutes, and in summer daytime the boardwalk is crowded (Yandex reviews — “beautiful, but small and quick”). If you are driving past without a stop in Aktash, you lose little.
alt-13.diff: Very easy: 200–500 m on a wooden boardwalk, 5–10 minutes; suitable for children and older people; on uneven sections the boardwalk is incomplete (tonkosti).
alt-13.when: Year-round — the lake does not freeze; summer and September are the main season, September is recommended for smaller crowds and good light (tonkosti); in spring mud season the approach can turn soggy (kp.ru).
alt-13.hours: Open 24 hours per kp.ru; in practice the entrance is controlled by the tourist base during daylight — exact ticket office hours not found.
alt-13.daytime: Early morning or evening — before/after the tour groups (Altapress, awd.is); for the colour of the water, a sunny day.
alt-13.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt (R256) to Aktash (~km 786–788), then another 5–7 km towards Kosh-Agach to the banner/sign at about km 796 (Lonely Planet: km 796.5; Altapress 2018: km 797), turn right onto the gravel parking area, then along the boardwalk. It is ~350 km from Gorno-Altaysk (tonkosti) — 6–7 h; ~463 km from Biysk, ~629 km from Barnaul (Altapress). By public transport: the Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) with a drop-off at the turn-off or in Aktash.
alt-13.needcar: Yes, as far as Aktash/the turn-off — car, bus or tour; from Aktash you can walk (5–7 km) or take a taxi.
alt-13.self: Yes, fully: a sign on the highway, parking, a developed path; no guide needed.
alt-13.roadtype: Paved road (Chuysky Trakt R256) up to the turn-off; gravel parking; then a wooden boardwalk across the marsh.
alt-13.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → lake ~6–7 h (350–360 km; longer given the roadworks at km 455–495 in 2026); Biysk → ~7–8 h (463 km); from Aktash 5–10 min by car; the visit takes 40 min–1 h (altai.travel).
alt-13.stay: Aktash has 20+ options (101hotels, 2026): Legenda guesthouse from 1,440 ₽, Garmoniya from 1,400 ₽, Lebyodka from 2,300 ₽, Nayman from 2,850 ₽, Kak Doma from 4,600 ₽ (9.6/10), Gorny Oryol mini-hotel from 6,960 ₽, Zelyony Kolobok from 5,600 ₽, Aktash Village from 6,250 ₽, Krasnye Vorota from 7,000 ₽, AL'TAIr tourist base from 13,500 ₽; the “Altai Geyser Lake” base at km 796 — from 6,542 ₽ (mirturbaz; the phone number on the site is the aggregator’s booking line). An overnight at a tourist base by the lake — from 1,000 ₽ (kp.ru 2026).
alt-13.net: Aktash has mobile coverage and internet (Wi‑Fi at tourist bases — mirturbaz); specific operators at the lake are not confirmed — not found.
alt-13.entry: Paid; the tourist base charges for walking on the boardwalk: 150 ₽ for adults, children under 12–14 free, cash only (Yandex Maps reviews, altai.travel); kp.ru gives 100 ₽ “for 2026”; AiF 2023 — 100 ₽; Altapress 2018 — 50 ₽. The current price is probably 150 ₽ — check on site. There is no resort fee in the Altai Republic.
alt-13.transfer: Group tour from Gorno-Altaysk with Geyser Lake and Mars — 12,700 ₽ per person (Sputnik8, 2026); a private car for the day — 26,000–48,000 ₽ (Sputnik8, Tripster “Chuysky Trakt and Geyser Lake in 1 day” — 48,000 ₽). Taxi Aktash — lake: not found.
alt-13.bring: Cash for the entrance; insect repellent (marsh, mosquitoes — Altapress, kp.ru); comfortable shoes; warm clothes (Aktash is ~1,400 m, evenings are cold); polarizing glasses/filter for photographing the bottom.
alt-13.warn: Swimming and entering the water are prohibited (slippery clay bottom, the patterns get destroyed). The lake is in the Ulagan district — there is no border zone, no permit is needed for anyone. Chuysky Trakt 2026: roadworks at km 455–472 and 479–495 (Souzga—Barangol), delays possible. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured.
alt-13.food: Cafe by the lake: shashlik at a reasonable price (tonkosti), lunch from 500 ₽ (kp.ru 2026); in Aktash — cafe M52 (awd.is) and canteens; along the highway try herbal tea, chegen/kaima and mutton (Altai cuisine) — specific dishes at the lake are not confirmed.
alt-13.reviews: Yandex Maps: 5.0 (687 ratings, 370 reviews); 2GIS: 4.5 (641 ratings); the Sputnik8 tour with the lake — 4.8 (49). Pros: unusual colour and patterns, easy access, infrastructure. Cons: small, crowded in the daytime, “expectations higher than reality”, paid entrance in cash.

alt-14.name: Kyzyl-Chin Tract (“Mars”)
alt-14.full: A tract (valley) in the lower reaches of the Kyzylchin River (a left tributary of the Chuya) on the northern edge of the Chuya Steppe, 4–9 km from the village of Chagan-Uzun (the turn off the Chuysky Trakt at km 863–864). Several sites: Mars-1 (the main one, with infrastructure), Mars-2, Mars-3 and “Luna” (the Moon).
alt-14.near: Chagan-Uzun village (4–9 km by dirt road); Kurai village ~40 km; Kosh-Agach village ~50 km (estimate, not verified)
alt-14.short: “Altai Mars” — colorful clay hills and outliers in red, orange, yellow and white shades on the edge of the Chuya Steppe, one of the most photogenic spots on the Chuysky Trakt.
alt-14.desc: Kyzyl-Chin (from Turkic — “red”/“beautiful place”, or by other interpretations “red canyon”) is a tract (valley) in the valley of the Kyzylchin River near Chagan-Uzun. The multicolored slopes are made up of lake and marine sediments: according to Altapress, about 90 million years of geological history can be read here — a warm sea, then a huge freshwater paleolake of the Pliocene (5–6 million years ago) with more than 70 species of mollusks. The red and orange color comes from iron oxides (hematite, magnetite), other shades from compounds of manganese, chromium, titanium and copper; the white layers are calcareous (altai.travel, vpoxod). The myths about cinnabar and elevated radiation are not confirmed (Altapress). The sites: Mars-1 is the main tourist spot on the private grounds of a tourist complex: parking, a café, souvenirs, toilets, a playground, a pedestrian bridge over the Kyzylchin, costume rental for photos, paid entry (300 ₽, 2025); Mars-2 is brighter (purple and bluish tones), 3–6 km away, on foot or by SUV; Mars-3 (opened to tourists around 2019) and “Luna” are remote, accessible only by UAZs. Cinereous (black) vultures (Russian Red Data Book) nest in the cliffs, and the Pallas’s cat (manul) is found. In the vicinity is the Kyzyl-Chin polymetallic deposit (lead, zinc, silver; discovered in the 1950s).
alt-14.guide: Come before lunch on a sunny day — the colors glow and the clay is not yet baking; after rain it is better not to venture here, as the clay turns into an ice rink. Don’t limit yourself to Mars-1: the most otherworldly views are at Mars-2, 3–6 km on foot or a UAZ drop-off for 1,500–2,000 ₽. Look up — cinereous vultures with a wingspan of nearly three meters circle above the cliffs. Don’t believe the stories about “mercury cinnabar” and radiation — they are myths. Take water and a sun hat: there is no shade here at all.
alt-14.see: Mars-1 — viewing paths over the colored hills; Mars-2 — the brightest colors (purple/blue layers); Mars-3 and “Luna” — gray-white “lunar” landscapes; a panorama of the North Chuya Range beyond the Chuya Steppe; cinereous vultures.
alt-14.skip: You do not have 2–3 hours to spare and the weather is rainy — the dirt road turns to mud, and on an overcast day the colors are dull. If you have already seen colored mountains (for example, in Kyrgyzstan), crowded Mars-1 may disappoint — then only Mars-2.
alt-14.diff: Mars-1 — easy (short paths over the hills, with a gain of no more than ~50–100 m); Mars-2 — moderate (3–6 km one way over rough terrain, heat/wind); altitude ~1,900 m.
alt-14.when: June–September (T—Zh); May–June and September (Khalva); from May to late June the ford across the Kyzylchin may be impassable because of snowmelt (altai.travel). September — fewer tourists, dry.
alt-14.hours: Mars-1 operates in daylight during the tourist season (a ticket office at the lower site); exact hours not found.
alt-14.daytime: The first half of the day in sunny weather (T—Zh); the low evening light also gives contrast.
alt-14.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to km 863–864, the turn to Chagan-Uzun, across the bridge over the Chuya and through the village following the “Mars” signs, then a dirt road across the steppe ~8–9 km with a ford/dry bed of the Kyzylchin — 20–30 min (T—Zh, awd.is, vpoxod). From Gorno-Altaysk ~430–438 km, 6–8 h; from Barnaul ~680 km.
alt-14.needcar: Yes: a car to Mars-1; for Mars-2/3/“Luna” — an SUV or a UAZ drop-off.
alt-14.self: Yes — to Mars-1 there are signs and a packed dirt road; for Mars-2 it is better with a GPS track or a local driver.
alt-14.roadtype: Paved to Chagan-Uzun; then a dirt road with “washboard” and a ford across the Kyzylchin (altai.travel).
alt-14.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Chagan-Uzun 6–8 h; Chagan-Uzun → Mars-1 20–30 min (≈30 km/h, TripAdvisor 09.2025); a visit to Mars-1 — 1–1.5 h, with Mars-2 — half a day.
alt-14.stay: Chagan-Uzun: Sofiyskaya Polyana base from 2,200 ₽ (a cabin for 3), MADI from 3,700 ₽ (mirturbaz, 2026), Kuyaktanar from 1,980 ₽ (8.5/10, 101hotels); the glamping site “Svoy Altai” (altai.travel); guesthouses 1,500–3,000 ₽ (Khalva); also Kurai (ails — traditional dwellings) and Aktash.
alt-14.net: not found (per reviews the signal in the Chuya Steppe is patchy; at Mars-1 not confirmed)
alt-14.entry: Mars-1: 300 ₽/person (T—Zh, 08.2025; TripAdvisor 09.2025; Khalva); earlier locals charged 150 ₽ per car without receipts (awd.is, earlier years). The fee goes to a private tourist complex, not a protected area.
alt-14.transfer: A UAZ to Mars-2/3/“Luna” — 1,500–2,000 ₽ (2025); an excursion from Gorno-Altaysk — 12,700 ₽/person (2026).
alt-14.bring: Water (there is nothing at Mars-2), sun protection and a sun hat, a windbreaker (strong wind), trekking shoes, cash for the entrance, a flashlight if you stay until sunset (Altapress, Khalva).
alt-14.warn: After rain the clay is very slippery, and the dirt road and ford become impassable (T—Zh, altai.travel); in spring the ford can be deep. Altitude ~1,900 m, strong sun and wind, no shade. Border zone: the border zone in the Kosh-Agach District covers only part of the territory: under FSB Order No. 282 (2006) — the Jazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya rural settlements; by FSB Order No. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remained in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan District) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official answer from the Border Directorate for this specific point was found). General rules: for Russian citizens a passport is enough in the border zone, a permit is needed only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point in the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Saylyugem National Park website; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; the office in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 in the Altai Republic there were 3,600 reports of bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor, the consumer-protection agency) — vaccination/insurance.
alt-14.food: A café at Mars-1 (altai.travel, TripAdvisor) — menu/prices not found; in Kosh-Agach — Kazakh and Altai cuisine (baursaks, beshbarmak, kurut) — specific cafés not confirmed.
alt-14.reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.5 (24 reviews), No. 1 in Kosh-Agach; the Sputnik8 excursion — 4.8 (49). Pros: “otherworldly” views, easy access to Mars-1. Cons: a paid entrance, crowds at Mars-1, dust, a long road (excursions of up to 16–17 h), a dirt road that is impassable in the rain.

alt-15.name: Kurai Steppe
alt-15.full: An intermontane basin in the middle reaches of the Chuya between the Kurai (north) and North Chuya (south) ranges, along the Chuysky Trakt at roughly km 813–844; the main villages are Kurai and Kyzyl-Tash. The classic panorama is the North Chuya Range viewing platform at km 822.
alt-15.near: Kurai village (≈427 residents, 2016; 50°13′ N, 87°55′ E; ~66 km to Kosh-Agach), Kyzyl-Tash village; Aktash village is ~30–35 km to the northwest (estimate)
alt-15.elev: 1500–1600 m (basin floor; tonkosti, “Znanie”, amic.ru); vpoxod — ~1600 m
alt-15.short: A high-mountain steppe ~20 km across with a frontal panorama of the North Chuya Range glaciers (Maashey-Bash 4173 m, Aktru 4044 m) and giant current ripples — traces of catastrophic glacial lake outburst floods 15,000 years ago.
alt-15.desc: The Kurai Steppe is an intermontane basin in the middle reaches of the Chuya at an elevation of 1500–1600 m, about 20 km across, surrounded by mountains on all sides. To the south the glaciers of the North Chuya Range stand over it like a wall: Kurkurek, Kyzyl-Tash, Aktru (4044 m), and the highest point, Maashey-Bash (4173 m), with the largest glacier, Maashey (~10 km). The basin is famous for one of the most spectacular fields of giant current ripples in the world: ridges up to 20 m high (“frozen waves”, visible from space) were formed about 15,000 years ago, when the ice-dammed lakes of the Kurai and Chuya basins burst, with discharges of 1 to 18 million m³/s (amic.ru, vpoxod). The climate is sharply continental: the frost-free period is 55–60 days, precipitation is 150–200 mm a year, and in summer heat can suddenly give way to a snowstorm. The vegetation resembles the Mongolian desert steppes; along the Chuya there are poplar, willow, sea buckthorn and shrubby cinquefoil (Kuril tea). The steppe is rich in archaeology: ancient Turkic burial mounds, the Kezer stone statue (8th–9th centuries), rock drawings and ancient irrigation systems (the “Kurai culture”); since 2014 part of the monuments have been protected by the Mezhelik historical and cultural reserve (vpoxod). Drop-off trips to Aktru and to Lake Dzhangyskol start from Kurai; there are viewpoints nearby and lodging in ails and glamping sites.
alt-15.guide: Stop at the viewing platform at km 822 — from here you can see almost the whole wall of the North Chuya Range; find the highest snow dome: that is Maashey-Bash (4173 m). Take a good look at the steppe: those even rows of hills are not dunes but ripples left by the flood from a glacial lake 15,000 years ago, as tall as a six-storey building. The artist Yegor Meyer wrote in the 19th century that he had never seen a more grandiose picture. The mountains are clearest in the morning — by lunchtime clouds gather over the glaciers. Take a warm jacket even in July: here you can get all four seasons in one day.
alt-15.see: The panorama of the North Chuya Range from the viewing platform at km 822 (Kurkurek, Kyzyl-Tash, Aktru, Maashey-Bash); giant current ripples on the basin floor; the Kezer stone statue and burial mounds (Mezhelik reserve); the bridge over the Chuya; a view of the mouth of the Aktru valley.
alt-15.skip: the weather is overcast and the range is hidden by clouds — without the mountains the steppe looks flat and dusty. But if you're driving the trakt to Kosh-Agach/Mars, a 10–15 minute stop at km 822 costs you almost nothing.
alt-15.diff: Very easy: the viewing platform is right by the highway; walks across the steppe involve no climbing; dirt roads toward the mountains are for 4×4 / SUV only (dmitriytravel: attempts to reach Aktru end at water obstacles).
alt-15.when: June–September — snow on the mountains, dry roads; September — clear air and yellow larches; winter is very cold (the basin is one of the cold poles of Altai), but the panorama is accessible from the trakt.
alt-15.hours: Open terrain, open 24 hours and free.
alt-15.daytime: Morning — before clouds form over the range; sunset gives a pink light on the glaciers (editorial).
alt-15.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt: from Aktash to the southeast, the basin is at km 813–844 (tonkosti), the viewing platform is at km 822, Kurai village is near km 826 (the turn to Aktru — tonkosti “Aktru Glacier”). From Gorno-Altaysk ~380–390 km (estimate from the km markers), 6.5–8 h.

alt-15.self: Yes — the viewing platform is by the highway; for steppe dirt roads you need a 4×4 / SUV and a navigator.

alt-16.name: Aktru Glaciers
alt-16.full: The Aktru river valley on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range, 30–33 km south of the Chuysky Trakt at the village of Kurai (turn-off at about km 826). A glacier cluster of 7 glaciers (~16 km²): Left (Big) Aktru, Right Aktru, Maly Aktru and others; in the valley — the Aktru alpine camp (since 1938), the Altai-Aktru mountain centre, a Tomsk State University (TSU) research station and a rescue post.
alt-16.near: Kurai village (≈30–33 km along a dirt road/riverbed; 2 h by 4×4), Kyzyl-Tash village
alt-16.elev: Alpine camp ~2,150 m (Altai-Aktru site, trofey.ru; travel companies — 2,200 m); Blue Lake 2,840 m; snout of the Maly Aktru glacier ~2,246 m, top ~3,714 m (WGMS); Aktru peak 4,044 m (other data give Aktru-Bashi 4,075 m)
alt-16.short: The most accessible glacial valley in Altai: a UAZ drop from Kurai to the alpine camp at 2,150 m, from where in a day you can walk to the snouts of the Maly and Bolshoy Aktru glaciers and to Blue Lake at 2,840 m.
alt-16.desc: Aktru (South Altai for “white dwelling/white house” — because of the glaciers) is a glacial basin of the North Chuya Range with 7 glaciers of a total area of about 16 km² (tonkosti); Left Bolshoy Aktru is 5.51 km² (SummitX), Maly Aktru 2.72 km², from 2,246 to 3,714 m (WGMS). Maly Aktru is a reference glacier of the World Glacier Monitoring Service (WGMS ID 795): its mass balance has been measured since 1961/62 by the TSU glacioclimatology laboratory; it is called the fastest-melting glacier in Russia, and Left Aktru, according to a TSU forecast (2019), may melt completely in the second half of the 21st century. The ice thickness in the system is up to 360 m (Altapress). The Aktru alpine camp opened in 1938 — one of the first in the USSR; before 1970 more than 2,000 badge-holders were trained here; since 1993 a search-and-rescue unit of the Emergency Ministry (MChS) has been on duty in the valley, and a year-round TSU research station operates. Today there are two complexes in the valley: the Aktru alpine camp (the old lower part — 4-person modules with stoves, VIP cottages, a banya (sauna), tent sites) and the Altai-Aktru mountain centre (the upper part — two- and three-storey houses, banyas, the Akkem cafe). Routes range from a walk through the “Gnomes’ Valley” (dwarf forest) and a visit to the snout of Maly Aktru (30 min from the trail) to Blue Lake (2,840 m), the Uchitel pass (~3,050 m), the Three Lakes Dome (3,556 m, 1B) and peaks up to grade 6A; since 2019 there has been a via ferrata on the south-eastern slope of Kyzyl-Tash peak. In the valley you can get “all four seasons in a day”. Memorials: to the climber Galina Afanasyeva and to the snowboarders killed in the 2002 helicopter crash.
alt-16.guide: Leave Kurai early in the morning — clouds over the glaciers usually gather after lunch. The most rewarding day is the climb to Blue Lake at 2,840 m: the turquoise water by the Bolshoy Aktru moraine and the view of the icefall are worth it. If you have less energy, go to the snout of Maly Aktru: it is a reference glacier of the world, TSU scientists have been measuring it since 1961 and it melts faster than any in Russia, so you see it while it is still there. Find the memorial to Galina Afanasyeva — a local reminder that the mountains do not forgive mistakes. Bring a down jacket and a warm sleeping bag even in July: at night it is about +5 °C.
alt-16.see: The snout of the Maly Aktru glacier; Blue Lake (2,840 m) by the Left Aktru moraine and the TSU weather station at 2,850 m; the Bolshoy Aktru icefall; the Uchitel pass (~3,050 m) with a view over the valley; the “Gnomes’ Valley” (dwarf forest); waterfalls; memorials to climbers; the via ferrata on Kyzyl-Tash; the peaks Aktru (4,044) and the Three Lakes Dome (3,556).
alt-16.skip: you have only one day and no money for the vehicle drop (11–20 thousand ₽ per vehicle) — then the panorama of the range from the Kurai steppe will do. Without good footwear and readiness to walk 10–20 km a day there is little point.
alt-16.diff: The valley and the snout of Maly Aktru — easy/moderate; Blue Lake — moderate (≈5 km one way from the camp, ~700 m of gain, 2.5–4 h up, a full day round trip); the Uchitel pass — moderate (5 km, up to ~3,050 m); the Three Lakes Dome 1B and above — only with training and registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS)/KSS (control-and-rescue service).
alt-16.when: July–August is the main trekking season; May is best for climbers (trofey); January–March — ice camps; the camp operates year-round. June — flood, fords on the way up.
alt-16.hours: The Altai-Aktru mountain centre and the alpine camp operate year-round (sites, trofey).
alt-16.daytime: Start from the camp at dawn; by lunch clouds and a risk of thunderstorms; the drop from Kurai is usually 8:00 → 10:00, back by 18:00 (seven.travel).
alt-16.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to Kurai (turn-off at about km 826), then 30–33 km south across the Kurai steppe, forest and the bed of the Tete/Aktru river: the first ~25 km to the “perevalka” (transshipment point) are passable in a prepared 4×4, the last ~8 km and ~600 m of gain only by GAZ-66, ZIL-131, KamAZ, UAZ with an experienced driver or on foot (tonkosti, trofey, NGS forum). The Kurai — camp drop takes ~2 h.
alt-16.needcar: Yes: to Kurai — car/marshrutka (minibus); Kurai → Aktru — a drop in special vehicles (or on foot 8 km from the perevalka).
alt-16.self: Yes, with a drop: from the camp the trails to Maly Aktru and Blue Lake are well trodden; for passes and peaks — a guide/registration. In your own car — only as far as the perevalka (a prepared 4×4).
alt-16.roadtype: Paved to Kurai; then dirt across the steppe, forest, a rocky riverbed with fords (in spring the water level is high, vehicles have been swept away — NGS forum).
alt-16.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Kurai 6.5–8 h; Kurai → camp ~2 h (30 km) in special vehicles; camp → Blue Lake 2.5–4 h up; a side trip to Bolshoy Aktru and Blue Lake — 7–8 h (seven.travel).
alt-16.stay: Altai-Aktru mountain centre (2,150 m, +7 996 962-57-84, altay-aktru.ru): houses Karatash and Maashey from 6,200 ₽, Belukha and Karagem from 6,700 ₽, Aktru and Kyzyltash 9,200 ₽ per night (site, 2026); banya 6,000 ₽/h. A tent in the valley — a registration fee of 150 ₽ per person (drom, 2021). In Kurai/Kyzyl-Tash — guesthouses from ~1,000 ₽, glamping 5,000–12,500 ₽.

alt-16.transfer: Kurai ↔ Aktru: UAZ (4 seats) 11,000–20,000 ₽ per vehicle, “bukhanka” van (8) 16,000–32,000 ₽, ZIL/KamAZ (19–22) 30,000–51,000 ₽ — depending on the carrier and one way/round trip (2026). For comparison: in 2007 a GAZ-66 cost 2,500–4,500 ₽.
alt-16.bring: Waterproof trekking boots, gaiters, poles, a warm sleeping bag (+5 °C at night in July), a down jacket, hat, gloves, rain jacket, sun protection and glasses (glacier), a supply of food and water, cash.

alt-17.name: Shavla Lakes
alt-17.full: A chain of glacial lakes at the head of the Shavla river on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range (Lower, Middle/Upper and a nameless one at the source), 35–45 km on foot south of the village of Chibit (Chuysky Trakt, km 783). Above the lakes rise the peaks Mechta (Dream, ~3,600 m), Skazka (Fairy Tale, ~3,770 m) and Krasavitsa (Beauty, ~3,870 m).
alt-17.near: Chibit village (35–45 km along the trail; km 783 of the Chuysky Trakt, fuel station); Aktash village ~5 km from Chibit along the highway
alt-17.elev: Lower Lake 1,983 m; Upper Lake 2,164 m; nameless lake at the source 2,307 m (Bolshaya Strana); Oroy Pass ~2,045–2,290 m (sources differ: 2,045 / 2,220 / 2,229 / 2,290)
alt-17.short: Turquoise glacial lakes under three snowy peaks — Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa; a classic 4–10-day hiking or horse route from Chibit via the Oroy Pass and the Eshtykel plateau, the “champion of beauty” in the words of Boris Delone.
alt-17.desc: The Shavla Lakes lie at the head of the Shavla, a left tributary of the Argut, at the foot of the North Chuya Range. The Lower Lake (1,983 m) is the largest: about 1.5–1.7 km long and 370–500 m wide; the eastern shore is gentle, with larch forest and many campsites, the western one steep and rocky. The Upper Lake (2,164 m) is 610×110 m, up to 40 m deep, above the treeline, its shores strewn with boulders up to 5 m; higher up is a small lake at the source (2,307 m). Above the water rises a panorama of the peaks Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa with their glaciers; the mathematician and mountaineer Boris Delone called Lake Shavla the “champion of beauty”. The classic route is from Chibit: a vehicle drop to the Oroy Bridge, the climb to the Oroy Pass, the Eshtykel plateau (above 2,200 m), the descent into the Shavla valley; to the Lower Lake it is 35–45 km, 2–3 days, the whole round trip ~70 km (at least 5 days, comfortably 8–10). No phone coverage. An Altai family lives at the Lower Lake who run a banya (sauna), rent out horses, sell bread/groceries and offer guide services. Popular side trips go to the Upper Lake and to Mount Piramida (3,100–3,150 m). The place is very popular with tourists, and in summer there are many groups at the lake.
alt-17.guide: Pitch camp on the eastern shore of the Lower Lake and get up at dawn — in calm weather Skazka, Mechta and Krasavitsa are reflected in the turquoise water, and the peaks are best seen in the morning. Do not rush on on the first day: once you reach the lake you can stay for a week (even guidebooks say so). Go light to the Upper Lake and, if you have the energy, up Piramida (about 3,100 m) — from there you can see the whole chain of lakes. Boris Delone, who travelled the Caucasus and the Alps, called this lake the “champion of beauty”. A banya at the local family’s place on the shore after three days on the trail is the best thing that can happen.
alt-17.see: The Lower Shavla Lake with a view of Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa; the Upper Lake (up to 40 m deep) and the lake at the source; Mount Piramida (3,100–3,150 m) — a panorama; the Eshtykel plateau and the Oroy Pass; the “Idol Glade” with carved wooden figures at the Lower Lake (tonkosti); the glaciers of the North Chuya Range.
alt-17.skip: you have fewer than 5 free days, no multi-day hiking experience and do not want to pay for a horse tour — without that you will not see the lakes. Also if you seek solitude in July–August: dozens of groups camp at the Lower Lake.
alt-17.diff: Moderate (n/k, non-categorised): 35–45 km one way with ~900 m of gain on the first day (Chibit — Oroy Pass) and ~15 km of ascents, fords (Eshtykel 5–7 m wide, 0.3–0.5 m deep — skitalets 2020); days of 13–24 km; altitudes up to 2,300 m, a side trip up to 3,150 m. The horse option is easier, but part of the trail is impassable for horses (tonkosti).
alt-17.when: From the second half of June to the end of August (sport-marafon); best from late July to mid-August (T—Zh); September is golden autumn, but with frosts and snow; July: ~+25 °C down below, ~+10 °C at 2,000 m.
alt-17.hours: An open area; the hiking season is June–September.
alt-17.daytime: Early morning — calm water and clear peaks; ascents — in the first half of the day (T—Zh); towards evening the rivers run higher from glacial melt (they rise during the day and drop by ~20 cm overnight — LiveJournal 2015).
alt-17.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to the village of Chibit (km 783; the bridge over the Chuya at Chibit is km 780.4). Then a vehicle drop to the Oroy Bridge (~1,500 ₽ per car — Bolshaya Strana), crossing the paid bridge (100–150 ₽ per person one way), the climb to the Oroy Pass, the Eshtykel plateau, the descent to the Shavla and up to the Lower Lake: 35–45 km, 2–3 days on foot. Buses to Chibit: from Gorno-Altaysk daily at 9:00 (the Kosh-Agach route), from Barnaul on even days at 8:40 (sport-marafon, 2024).
alt-17.needcar: To Chibit — bus/car; beyond that — only on foot or by horse (or helicopter — mentioned by Altapress as an option, prices not found).
alt-17.self: Yes, if you have hiking experience: the trail is beaten and popular, but you need to register with the Emergency Ministry (MChS), a track/map, a tent and a food supply; no phone coverage.
alt-17.roadtype: Paved to Chibit; dirt road to the Oroy Bridge; then a mountain trail with fords and a boulder field (kurumnik) near the Upper Lake.
alt-17.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Chibit ~5.5–6.5 h (≈347 km — trekkingmania; by the highway km markers Biysk km 350 → Chibit km 783, i.e. ≈433 km from Biysk); Barnaul → Chibit 10–12 h; Chibit → Lower Lake 2–3 days (days of 13–20 km: skitalets — 13 km/+900 m on day 1, 20 km on day 2); Lower → Upper Lake side trip 8 km.
alt-17.stay: Only tents at the campsites by the lakes (Bolshaya Strana). In Chibit before the start: bases Start from 2,200 ₽, Altai Kabai from 2,200 ₽, Altai Eko Kedr and Krasnye Vorota 7,000–7,761 ₽, Agory from 19,800 ₽ (mirturbaz 2026); the Kochevnik ECO tourist complex at km 781.5 (vtourisme). Parking a car at the base — 150 ₽/day, storing belongings 50 ₽/day (sport-marafon 2024).
alt-17.net: No mobile coverage on the route and at the lakes — satellite only (Bolshaya Strana); in Chibit/Aktash there is coverage.
alt-17.entry: Bridges: 100 ₽ per person for crossing (T—Zh, skitalets 2020, LiveJournal 2015) / 150 ₽ each way for each of the two bridges (Bolshaya Strana) — the total differs. Tour operators include “recreation fees”/“protected-area fees” (altaitg, zovgor) — the amount and recipient not found. The banya at the lake: 1,200 ₽ per group (2020), from 1,800 ₽ (Adventure Club 2027).
alt-17.transfer: Chibit — Oroy Bridge ~1,500 ₽ per car; Gorno-Altaysk — Chibit transfer in tours +10,500 ₽ per person (Altai-Pokhod 2026); bus to Chibit — see above.
alt-17.bring: Waterproof boots + spare shoes for fords, gaiters, trekking poles, a 70–90 l backpack, a sleeping bag with comfort down to −5 °C, two rain jackets/a shell, sun protection, a mug, cash (cards are not accepted), insurance with helicopter evacuation.
alt-17.warn: Registering your group with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) is mandatory (T—Zh: 10 days in advance; MChS of the Altai Republic 8 388 23 9-99-99 per T—Zh — verify; online forms.mchs.gov.ru), check in before departure and after return. No phone coverage — evacuation only by helicopter, insurance is needed. Fords and rising water in the daytime; sudden rain and snow; rockfalls and boulder fields. Fishing: according to some data prohibited (Bolshaya Strana — “zakaznik”, a wildlife refuge), according to others grayling is caught (Altapress) — check. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured. Border zone: The border zone in the Kosh-Agach district covers only part of the territory: under FSB Order No. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB Order No. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remained in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan district) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official reply from the border directorate for this specific point was found). General rules: Russian citizens in the border zone need only a passport, a permit is required only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point of the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Sailyugem National Park site; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: FSB border directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; branch in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible.
alt-17.food: Fresh bread and milk from herders/the family on the route (Bolshaya Strana: bread 70–80 ₽ in 2015, LiveJournal); grayling fish soup (Altapress — if fishing is allowed); in Chibit/Aktash — cafes by the highway.
alt-17.reviews: No aggregator ratings for the place found; tours: Tripster (Andrey) — 4.82 (272 ratings, 233 reviews); “Alone with Nature” — 5.0 (2). Pros: “turquoise like the Maldives”, views of the peaks; cons: a hard route, rain, crowds in July–August.

alt-18.name: Maashey Glacier
alt-18.full: The Bolshoy Maashey glacier complex at the head of the Maashey River (a tributary of the Mazhoy → Chuya) on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range, below the range's highest point, Maashey-Bash (4173–4177 m). The approach is from the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) at km ~801–802 (the confluence of the Chuya and Mazhoy, a footbridge, the “Meny” tourist base), 13–20 km from Aktash/Chibit; below the glacier lies the bed of the former Lake Maashey (drained in 2012).
alt-18.near: The village of Aktash (~13–14 km along the highway to the start of the trail, km 788 → km 801–802); the village of Chibit (km 783; tours start from Chibit's bases, with a 14 km transfer to the bridge)
alt-18.elev: Glacier snout ~2280 m, top up to ~4100 m (Institute of Geography RAS); the former lake — 1984 m; the trailhead at the Chuya — 1461 m (Novosibirsk State University report 2015); the moraine pocket of the Left Maashey — 2621 m; Maashey-Bash — 4173/4177 m
alt-18.short: One of the largest glaciers of the North Chuya Range under the highest peak, Maashey-Bash (4173 m); a 3–6 day hike along a cedar valley past the bed of Lake Maashey, which burst in 2012 and left a “graveyard” of dead trees.
alt-18.desc: The Maashey valley is the right branch of the Mazhoy basin on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range. The catchment of the former Lake Maashey (96.1 km²) holds 27 glaciers with a total area of about 27 km² (28% glaciated); the main one is Bolshoy Maashey, about 10 km long (marshruting), descending from ~4100 to ~2280 m. The glacier is retreating fast: 3.2 m/year in 1962–1989, 7.1 m/year in 1989–2010 and about 14 m/year after 2010 (Institute of Geography RAS, “Ice and Snow”). Above it rises Maashey-Bash (4173–4177 m), the highest point of the range; the north face is a classic of Altai mountaineering. Further down the valley, at 1984 m, lay the famous Lake Maashey (1480×423 m, up to 7.5 m deep, volume 1.21 million m³), dammed by a rockfall-moraine dam in the first half of the 18th century (dendrochronology; the media wrote “about a century ago”). On 15–17 July 2012, after prolonged rains, a mudflow cut through the dam (a breach 10 m high, peak discharge 694 m³/s) and the lake drained; now a river flows in its place, and dead trees stand on the exposed bed. The trail starts at the Chuysky Trakt (km ~801–802) at a footbridge over the Chuya below its confluence with the Mazhoy (the bridge was rebuilt after the floods of 2010 and 2012, the current one dates from 2015 and is a toll bridge), goes up the Mazhoy to its confluence with the Karakabak (≈9 km), then along the Maashey valley to the former lake (≈9 km) and radially to the glacier (≈6–10 km). Nearby are the Karakabak lakes (~2300 m) and the Alyonka lakes; the valley is linked to the Shavla lakes via the Nizhne-Shavla Pass (grade 1B).
alt-18.guide: Come here if you want Shavla without the crowds: the Maashey valley is noticeably quieter. Be sure to stop at the site of the former lake — in 2012 a mudflow drained it in a couple of days, and now silvery dead trees stand among the pebbles, an eerie and beautiful sight. Start the radial hike to the glacier early: the snout retreats by almost 14 metres a year, and in front of it is a moraine lake with a view of the north face of Maashey-Bash, the highest point of the range. Camp at the “Kedrovaya” (Cedar) or “Solnechnaya” (Sunny) camp spots. Combine it with a rest day at the Karakabak lakes — another 12 km with a light pack.
alt-18.see: The bed of the former Lake Maashey with its dead forest (1984 m); the snout of the Bolshoy Maashey glacier and the moraine lake; the north face of Maashey-Bash (4173 m); the confluence of the Chuya and Mazhoy (the blue Mazhoy and the muddy Chuya); the Karakabak lakes (~2300 m); the Alyonka lakes.
alt-18.skip: you don't have 3–6 days for a hike and a tent — you can't drive up to the glacier. If you just want to look at Maashey-Bash, the North Chuya Range viewpoint on the Kurai steppe (km 822) is enough.
alt-18.diff: Moderate: from the bridge 8–9 km to the confluence with the Karakabak (+294 m to the fork, ~1844 m at the Karakabak), another ~8–9 km to the former lake (~2000 m), radially 6–10 km to the glacier (up to ~2600 m); a crossing of the Karakabak; walking days of 5–8 h. For beginners in good shape — on tours (altai-poxod, klubgidov 12+).
alt-18.when: July–August (tours run in the summer season); June — high water at the crossings; September — snow is possible.
alt-18.hours: An open area; the bridge over the Chuya and the parking at the tourist base are paid, in daylight (hours not found).
alt-18.daytime: Head to the glacier at dawn — before the clouds and before the streams rise (glacial melt during the day).
alt-18.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to km ~801–802 (after Aktash and Geyser Lake, by the Chuya hydropower plant — km 801 per vtourisme), turn off to the “Meny” tourist base/the bank of the Chuya, leave your car at the base (in 2015 — 300 ₽ for a round-trip crossing), the footbridge over the Chuya (toll, 150 ₽ in 2015), then on foot up the Mazhoy. Tours: from Chibit's bases (km 783) a 14 km transfer to the bridge (altai-poxod). From Gorno-Altaysk to the bridge ≈360 km, from Biysk ≈450 km (by the highway's kilometre markers: Biysk km 350, the bridge km ~802; Chibit — 347 km from Gorno-Altaysk per trekkingmania). The bridge at the mouth of the Maashey/Mazhoy is sometimes damaged by floods — check its condition with locals (trekkingmania).
alt-18.needcar: Yes, to the bridge — a car/bus (the Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach service passes by); beyond that only on foot or with horses.
alt-18.self: Yes, with hiking experience: the trail along the Mazhoy and Maashey is well worn; to the glacier and over the pass — navigation and caution; registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations.
alt-18.roadtype: Paved highway up to the turnoff; a dirt road to the base; a footbridge; then a mountain trail with a crossing of the Karakabak, moraines and kurums (boulder fields) near the glacier.
alt-18.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → bridge ~6–6.5 h (≈360 km); bridge → confluence with the Karakabak 3–4 h (8.6 km); → the former lake another 5–6 h (8–9 km); the radial hike to the glacier 4–6 h (6–10 km round trip depending on the programme).
alt-18.stay: On the route — tents (camp spots at the Karakabak, “Solnechnaya”, “Kedrovaya”). Before the start: bases in Aktash/on the Meny River — “Legenda” from 1,440 ₽, “V gorakh Altaya” (In the Altai Mountains) from 1,700 ₽, “Zelyony Kolobok” from 5,600 ₽, “Shepot Gor” (Whisper of the Mountains) from 7,200 ₽, “Krasnye Vorota” from 7,000 ₽ (101hotels 2026); Chibit bases from 2,200 ₽ (mirturbaz 2026).
alt-18.net: not found (probably no signal in the valley; there is signal near the highway around Aktash)
alt-18.entry: No protected-area fees were found. Paid: crossing the bridge over the Chuya — 150 ₽ (2015); parking/passage through the “Meny” tourist base — 300 ₽ round trip (2015). Current 2026 prices were not found.
alt-18.transfer: The Chibit — bridge transfer of 14 km is included in tours; no market price found. A tour with transfer: 24,000–78,300 ₽ (2026).
alt-18.bring: A tent and sleeping bag (about 0…+5 °C at night near the glacier), a waterproof shell, boots + shoes for crossings, poles, sunglasses, a GPS device/offline map, food for 4–6 days, cash (bridge, base), insurance with evacuation.
alt-18.warn: Mudflows and outburst floods: in 2012 a mudflow destroyed the lake and the bridges — don't go into the valley during prolonged rains. Crossings of the Karakabak/Maashey; crevasses and rockfalls on the glacier — don't step onto the ice without equipment. Registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Registration of tourist groups with the Ministry of Emergency Situations is online at forms.mchs.gov.ru (processed within a day); it is not mandatory for short outings to sites by the highway, but recommended for hikes. Ticks: by 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3600 bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured. Border zone: the border zone in Kosh-Agach District covers only part of the territory: under FSB order no. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB order no. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remain in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan District) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official reply from the Border Directorate on this specific point was found). General rules: for Russian citizens in the border zone a passport is enough, a permit is only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point of the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Sailyugem National Park website; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; the office in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible.
alt-18.food: A banya at the mouth of the Karakabak (arranged by tour operators, altai-poxod); on the route — trail food; in Aktash — cafes by the highway (see Geyser Lake).
alt-18.reviews: No ratings found; tours: Klub Gidov (Guides' Club) — no rating; Klub Priklyucheniy (Adventure Club) — describes it as “a harder, less popular but no less interesting” route. Pros: few people, the glacier and the dead forest; cons: a long approach, river crossings.

alt-19.name: Ukok Plateau
alt-19.full: A high-mountain plateau in the far south of Kosh-Agach District, at the junction of the borders of Russia, Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia; entry from the village of Kosh-Agach via the border post near the village of Belyashi and the Teply Klyuch Pass (Dzhumalinsky springs). Most of it is the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (part of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”).
alt-19.near: The village of Belyashi (the last village before the border post and the Teply Klyuch Pass); the district centre, the village of Kosh-Agach, is ~140–150 km from the plateau (Altapress 2018, pikabu 2020); the village of Dzhazator — on the northwest side of the Teply Klyuch Pass.
alt-19.elev: 2200–2500 m (plateau; bolshayastrana, geocaching.su); the main part of the park is above 2500 m (Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic); the Teply Klyuch Pass ~2400 m at the Dzhumalinsky springs (pikabu 2020) / 2600 m (make-trip) — the sources disagree; the highest point nearby is Kuyten-Uul (Nairamdal) 4374 m (welcometoaltai).
alt-19.short: A treeless high-mountain plateau on the border of four countries: hundreds of lakes, the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola glaciers, burial mounds of the Pazyryk culture (where the “Ukok Princess” was found in 1993), the radon Dzhumalinsky springs. SUV only, border zone, a season of about a month and a half.
alt-19.desc: Ukok is a cold high-mountain steppe-tundra at an altitude of 2200–2500 m in the southwest corner of Kosh-Agach District, where the borders of Russia, Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia meet. Since 1998 part of the plateau has been the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (252,904 ha, zones A/B/C; Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic), which is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. In the south the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola range (Tavan-Bogdo-Ula) rises above the plateau with its glaciers and the peak of Kuyten-Uul (4374 m). The plateau has more than 800 lakes (bolshayastrana), the sources of the Ak-Alakha and Kalguty rivers, the Bertek tract with dozens of archaeological sites, petroglyphs, deer stones and balbals (stone figures); 150–180 monuments in all. In 1993, in the Ak-Alakha-3 burial mound, N. Polosmak found the mummy of a woman of the Pazyryk culture (5th–3rd centuries BC) — the “Ukok Princess” (now in the Anokhin National Museum in Gorno-Altaysk). Snow leopards, Altai argali (mountain sheep), golden eagles and Pallas's cats live here. The climate is sharply continental: in summer up to +25…+30 °C by day, frosts at night, and snow is possible in any month. The tourist season is effectively from mid-July to late August. There is no infrastructure: overnight stays are in tents or in tour operators' yurts, and the nearest cabins are at the Dzhumalinsky springs by the Teply Klyuch Pass. The plateau is in the border zone, and the way leads through the border post near Belyashi.
alt-19.guide: Ukok is the end of the world in the literal sense: no trees, no people, only wind, lakes and the white wall of Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola on the horizon. For Altaians it is the “pasture of the heavens” and the land of the dead — after the “Ukok Princess” was taken to Novosibirsk in 1993, many linked earthquakes and misfortunes to it; don't take so much as a stone from here. Before the plateau, be sure to bathe in the radon Dzhumalinsky springs at Teply Klyuch (no longer than ~20 minutes). Look for deer stones and balbals in the Bertek tract on the plateau, and at Goose Lake (Gusinoye) watch the reflection of the glaciers. Travel only in a group of 2+ cars or with a local driver — help here is a hundred kilometres away.
alt-19.see: The Ak-Alakha-3 burial mound (“Ukok Princess”, 49.2997, 87.5625); the Bertek tract (63 monuments of various eras, sib-guide), the Bertek rock-art site (100+ petroglyphs, bolshayastrana); deer stones and balbals; the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola range with its glaciers and Kuyten-Uul peak 4374 m; Goose Lake (Gusinoye; Tashanta?) with a view of Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola; the Kaldzhin-Kul lakes and the Kaldzhinka waterfall (maral-travel); the “Gates of Ukok”; the Dzhumalinsky (Teply Klyuch) radon springs; on the way — the Tarkhata megalithic complex and the Kyzyl-Chin valley (“Mars”) near Chagan-Uzun.
alt-19.skip: You are travelling in an ordinary passenger car, you have fewer than 5–6 free days, you aren't ready for nights in a tent in frosts, for no signal and no medical help for 100+ km — or you are a foreigner without a border-zone permit arranged in advance.
alt-19.diff: High logistically: a prepared SUV, fords, rocky climbs to the Teply Klyuch Pass, altitude 2200–2600 m, no signal or services. Physically the hikes are easy to moderate (tour operators offer radial hikes to the glacier of up to ~20 km, vpoxod).
alt-19.when: Mid-July to late August (Altapress: a season of ~1 month, late July — late August; bolshayastrana — “the second half of summer”); from September to June roads wash out/drift over and passes close.
alt-19.hours: Round the clock; the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic) has no park checkpoint; passage through the border post near Belyashi (passport/permit check).
alt-19.daytime: Early morning and evening — soft light on Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola and the lakes, less wind; by day strong winds and the weather changes several times a day.
alt-19.how: The Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to the village of Kosh-Agach (≈890 km from Novosibirsk by the highway's kilometre markers; ~600 km from Gorno-Altaysk, ~700 km from Biysk — bolshayastrana). Then dirt road/steppe ~30 km to the border post near the village of Belyashi, another ~40 km to the fork (left — to the Teply Klyuch Pass and the Dzhumalinsky springs, right — Tarkhata), then a steep rocky climb to the pass and a descent onto the plateau. Kosh-Agach — Dzhumalinsky springs ~100–140 km, ~3–4 h (make-trip, pikabu 2020); Kosh-Agach — plateau ~150 km (Altapress). Only a prepared SUV/UAZ, preferably 2+ cars.
alt-19.needcar: Yes — only an SUV (a UAZ, a Land Cruiser, the Severtrak all-terrain vehicles of tour operators). There is no public transport beyond Kosh-Agach.
alt-19.self: Yes, for Russian citizens with a prepared SUV and off-road experience (passport; an FSB permit is for the 5-km border strip, and the Ak-Alakha-3 mound and the south of the plateau lie right by the Chinese border — better to get the permit in advance). For foreigners — only with a permit, processing ~30 days or more (tour operators close sales 3 weeks ahead — maral-travel; vpoxod — 2 months ahead for foreigners).
alt-19.roadtype: The paved road ends at Kosh-Agach; then dirt and steppe tracks across the Chuya steppe to the post, then rocky tracks, fords (the Dzhumaly River and others), a steep climb to the Teply Klyuch Pass; on the plateau — tracks across tundra and boggy sections, “there are no roads, only directions”.
alt-19.traveltime: Kosh-Agach — plateau ~2.5 h in a prepared SUV (akkem-tur.ru); Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach 1 day (~450–500 km, RussiaDiscovery: “450 km” along the highway on day 1); Kosh-Agach — Dzhumalinsky springs 3–4 h; the plateau — another 1–3 h depending on the spot. Tours: at least 5–6 days from Gorno-Altaysk.
alt-19.stay: On the plateau — only tents or tour operators' yurt camps (RussiaDiscovery: 3 nights in yurts). The Dzhumalinsky springs — simple unheated cabins with bunks: 200 ₽/person, firewood 250 ₽/bundle, bathing 200 ₽/day (make-trip, year not specified). Kosh-Agach — the Rasul hotel (72a Novochuyskaya St.) from 4200 ₽ (101hotels, 2026); the district's tourist bases from 3700 ₽/night (tropki.ru, 2026).
alt-19.net: There is no signal on the plateau (Altapress: “no signal or medical help within a 100 km radius”). The last reliable signal is Kosh-Agach/Belyashi; Dzhazator has gained mobile coverage (teletype 2022). You need a satellite tracker/phone.
alt-19.entry: The Ukok Quiet Zone nature park is a regional protected area: from 01.07.2026 the visit fee for the Altai Republic's regional protected areas is 300 ₽ (it was 100), with the previous rate for residents of the Altai Republic (Tolk/Altapress 2026); according to akkem-tur.ru “the park pass is issued on the spot” (no price or year). The border-zone permit is free.
alt-19.transfer: A private jeep trip — ~780,000 ₽ per car for 11 days (tomeet 2025); group tours 96,000–198,500 ₽/person for 6 days (2026). A one-off UAZ from Kosh-Agach to Ukok — price not found.
alt-19.bring: Your passport (and the FSB permit if travelling to the border), fuel for 300+ km, spare wheels and tools, a tow rope, a warm sleeping bag (down to −5…−10 °C at night even in August — teletype 2022), a down jacket, windproof and waterproof clothing, a gas stove/primus (no firewood), water/a filter, a first-aid kit, sun protection (altitude), satellite communication, a paper/offline map, a tracker.
alt-19.warn: Border zone (Kosh-Agach District; FSB order no. 282/2006 as amended by no. 512/2022): Russian citizens need a passport, with a check at the border post near Belyashi; in the 5-km strip along the border a permit is needed (Gosuslugi, the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic in Gorno-Altaysk or its office in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70); for foreigners a permit is mandatory everywhere. The fine for violating the regime is 500–1000 ₽ (Administrative Code, Altapress 2018). Solo trips are not recommended; fords, snow and frosts in summer; no medical help or signal for 100+ km; radon at the Dzhumalinsky springs — no more than ~20 min a day, consult a doctor if you have illnesses. Altitude 2200–2600 m. A sacred place for Altaians — don't touch the burial mounds and stones, excavations are prohibited. Ticks — lower down in the valleys (in the Altai Republic 3600 bites were reported by 25.08.2026).
alt-19.food: In Kosh-Agach — Kazakh and Altai cuisine: beshbarmak, baursaks, tea with milk and salt (talkan), kurut; on the plateau — only your own food. No specific cafes were found.
alt-19.reviews: No 2GIS/Yandex/Google ratings for the plateau were found. The Rasul hotel in Kosh-Agach is on TripAdvisor (reviews since 2014). Typical pros in the reports: “the end of the world”, solitude, glaciers, lakes, archaeology; cons: a hard road, cold, wind, no signal or infrastructure, high tour prices.

alt-19.p.sum: Ukok is an expedition destination: the Chuysky Trakt to Kosh-Agach (1 day), then 3–4 h of off-road driving through the border post near Belyashi and the Teply Klyuch Pass (Dzhumalinsky springs) onto the plateau. 4×4 only, season from mid-July to August, nights in tents/yurts. The easiest way is a 6-day tour from 96,000 ₽.

alt-21.name: Red Gates (Aktash)
alt-21.full: A narrow gorge with red cliffs in the Chibitka river valley on the Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul road (Ulagan Trakt), ~8 km from the village of Aktash, at the junction of the Kurai and Aygulak ranges.
alt-21.near: Aktash village (~8 km, welcometoaltai; altertravel gives 15 km — a discrepancy); Ulagan village is ~33 km further along the road (estimate: the whole Aktash — Ulagan road is ~41 km, TASS).
alt-21.elev: not found (Aktash ~1400 m; the exact elevation of the gorge is not confirmed)
alt-21.short: A natural monument: the road to Ulagan squeezes between sheer red-pink cliffs ~50 m high, coloured by cinnabar (mercury ore); a short but striking stop on the way to Ulagan Pass and Katu-Yaryk Pass.
alt-21.desc: The Red Gates are a narrow, winding passage between sheer cliffs about 50 m high in the Chibitka river valley, where the Ulagan Trakt (Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul) crosses the Kurai and Aygulak ranges. The cliffs are made of effusive (volcanic) rocks, and their pink-red colour comes from mercury compounds — cinnabar; near Aktash there is the Aktash mercury deposit (discovered in 1935, the plant started up in December 1942 — visit-altairepublic.ru), with the mine in the highlands at ~50.19, 87.43. The passage was originally almost impassable; the road was blasted through and a bridge was thrown across the Chibitka; an inscription dated 1945/1946 survives on the right-hand cliff (2GIS mentions inscriptions by soldiers from May 1945, welcometoaltai says 1946), and it is regularly touched up. The site is a natural monument of the Altai Republic. A decision on a bypass was made after public discussions: in 2020 (TASS, gorno-altaisk.info 07.09.2020), during repairs of the Aktash — Ulagan road, they planned to build an alternative route at km 8 so as not to blast the cliffs, and to eventually turn the old road through the gates into a pedestrian tourist route; as of 2024, 64 of the 71.7 km of the Ulagan Trakt had been repaired and paved (gorno-altaisk.info, 12.2024) — whether the bypass has been built is not confirmed. Further along the road are the Dead Lake (Cheybekkol), Lake Uzunkol, Ulagan Pass (2080 m), the Pazyryk burial mounds and Katu-Yaryk Pass into the Chulyshman valley.
alt-21.guide: Don't stop right in the narrows, but a little before or after them — that way you'll see how the cliffs “close” over the road. The red colour is cinnabar, mercury ore: don't lick the rocks or take them with you, even though they are harmless to the touch. Look for the old post-war inscription on the right-hand cliff — it has been touched up for almost 80 years. In the sun the cliffs glow scarlet, and on an overcast evening they turn gloomy — locals say the gates “let you in” to the Ulagan region. From here it is 4 km to the Dead Lake, Cheybekkol — stop by, it's on the way.
alt-21.see: The narrows between the red cliffs and the bridge over the Chibitka; the 1945/46 inscription on the right-hand cliff; the Dead Lake, Cheybekkol (~4 km further, welcometoaltai); Lake Uzunkol; Ulagan Pass (2080 m) with a gazebo and viewing platform (Tolk 2026); waterfalls on the Boka river (~19 km, altertravel); the Kurai steppe (~23 km).
alt-21.skip: If you aren't going to Ulagan/Chulyshman, a 16 km round-trip detour from Aktash just for 5–10 minutes at the cliffs is only worth it for photographers.
alt-21.diff: Very easy — a viewing stop by the road.
alt-21.when: June — September (dry road, Chulyshman season); passable in winter, but there is icing on the Ulagan Trakt (Tolk 08.2025).
alt-21.hours: Open 24 hours, free (a natural monument by the highway).
alt-21.daytime: A sunny day, midday — the cliffs are bright red (turistka, 2GIS); in the evening in overcast weather — a gloomy atmosphere.
alt-21.how: Take the Chuysky Trakt to the village of Aktash (km 788), at the junction at km ~790.7 turn toward Ulagan (Ulagan Trakt), ~8 km along the Chibitka valley to the gates. Biysk to the gates ~463 km (welcometoaltai). The Aktash — Ulagan road has been repaired and paved for most of its length (64 of 71.7 km by 12.2024; another 7.7 km under the national project in 2025).
alt-21.needcar: Yes — a car/taxi from Aktash; on foot it is ~8 km along the road from Aktash.
alt-21.self: Yes, easy — no permits needed (Ulagan district is outside the border zone).
alt-21.roadtype: Paved road (the Ulagan Trakt was repaired in 2022–2024, gorno-altaisk.info); some repair sections at km 29 (2025, temporary detour — Tolk 08.08.2025).
alt-21.traveltime: Aktash — gates ~10–15 min; Gorno-Altaysk — Aktash ~5 h by marshrutka (minibus) (avtovokzaly); Biysk — gates ~463 km, 7–8 h by car (estimate).
alt-21.stay: Aktash: the Krasnye Vorota (Red Gates) base (Leninskaya St. 63a, +7 961 893-52-42, kvorota.ru, from 6200 ₽, 2GIS 4.9/106); Gorny Orel, Kak Doma (101hotels, 9.6/10); Aktash has 20+ hotels from ~4600 ₽ (101hotels 2026); guesthouses 6–9 km from the gates from 200 ₽ (welcometoaltai, outdated).
alt-21.net: There is a signal in Aktash (a repeater); in the narrows — not found, check.
alt-21.entry: Free (a natural monument by the road; no information about a fee found).
alt-21.bring: A camera (wide-angle lens), a jacket — it's windy; if you're continuing on to Chulyshman — a full tank in Aktash/at the junction (fuel station at km 790.7).
alt-21.warn: Stopping in the narrow gorge on the roadway is dangerous — park in the wider spots before/after. Rockfalls from the cliffs are possible. In winter — icing on the Ulagan Trakt. Do not chip off cinnabar (mercury ore; the Aktash mercury mine is an environmentally problematic area). Ticks (season May–July).
alt-21.food: In Aktash (2GIS, 2026): Oasis (4.8, 935 ratings, home cooking), Karavan (4.4, 486, check ~400 ₽), M52 (4.5, 242, ~500 ₽), Myaso Khleb (4.9, 139, ~650 ₽), Teertpek (4.8, 232, Altai cuisine and game, ~1200 ₽).
alt-21.reviews: 2GIS: 4.8 out of 5 (68 ratings, 50 reviews, 202 photos) — 2026; TripAdvisor: 4.3/5 (27 reviews), No. 3 of 5 in Aktash. Pros: bright colour, unusual, on the way; cons: a short stop, narrow road, nowhere to pull over.
alt-21.p.sum: The Red Gates are 8 km from Aktash on the paved Ulagan Trakt; a free 10–20 minute stop on the way to Ulagan Pass, Pazyryk and Katu-Yaryk Pass. Lodging and food are in Aktash.

alt-22.name: Chuysky Trakt
alt-22.full: Federal highway R256 “Chuysky Trakt” Novosibirsk — Berdsk — Novoaltaysk (Barnaul) — Biysk — Maima (Gorno-Altaysk) — Seminsky Pass — Ongudai — Chike-Taman — Aktash — Kurai — Kosh-Agach — Tashanta (the border with Mongolia). The mountain section runs from the border of Altai Krai and the Altai Republic (km 428.7) to Tashanta (km 943).
alt-22.near: Key points: Biysk (km 350–364), Maima/Gorno-Altaysk (km ~440–453), Shebalino (~km 560–570), Ongudai (km 634), Inya (km 703), Aktash (km 788), Kurai (km 822), Kosh-Agach (km 889.7), Tashanta (km 943).
alt-22.elev: From ~200 m (Biysk/Maima) to 1717 m (Seminsky Pass, km 582–583, Wikivoyage); Chike-Taman 1295 m (amic.ru); on the Chuya steppe and near Tashanta — 1800–2000+ m (atlas.dcsr.ru: “up to 1900–2000 m”); the border at Durbet-Daba Pass (km 964).
alt-22.short: The main road of Gorno-Altai and one of the most beautiful highways in the world (National Geographic, per vpoxod): ~968 km of pavement from Novosibirsk to the Mongolian border through the Seminsky and Chike-Taman passes, the confluence of the Chuya and Katun, and the Kurai and Chuya steppes.
alt-22.desc: The Chuysky Trakt (R256, until 2018 M-52) is a historic route from Biysk to Mongolia along which merchant caravans traveled from the 18th–19th centuries; the motor road was built in 1914–1935 and opened on 01.01.1935 (vpoxod, atlas.dcsr.ru). Today it is a federal highway about 968 km long: a flat section Novosibirsk — Biysk (~350 km) and a mountain section of ~600 km from Biysk to the Mongolian border. Kilometer markers (vtourisme): Biysk 350.3; Srostki 384.9 (Shukshin museum); the Altai Republic border 428.7; Maima/the junction to Gorno-Altaysk ~453; Seminsky Pass 582.4 (1717 m, a stele for the 200th anniversary of Altai joining Russia); Ongudai 634; Chike-Taman 662.9 (1295 m, a serpentine road from 1984); Inya ~703 (suspension bridge); the confluence of the Chuya and Katun 712.4; Kalbak-Tash 723; the monument to Kolka Snegiryov 744; Chibit 783; Aktash 788; the fork to Ulagan 790.7; Geyser Lake ~797; Kurai 822; Kyzyl-Tash 830; the turn to Chagan-Uzun/Kyzyl-Chin 865; Kosh-Agach 889.7; Tashanta 943 (international road checkpoint); Durbet-Daba Pass and the border — 964. The surface is asphalt throughout. The road is open year-round, but in winter closures are possible because of snow and rockfalls (on 19.01.2024 a rockfall at km 764 closed traffic Yodro — Aktash, km 737–790). In 2026 repairs are under way: km 455–472 (Souzga — Cheremshanka — Manzherok) and km 479–495 (Izvestkovy — Ust-Muny — Barangol); km 439–444 and 560–570 have been repaired (Tolk 06.10.2026); the reconstruction of km 454–475 into four lanes (18 km: 14.4 km of new road bypassing Souzga, Cheremshanka and Manzherok + 3.6 km of reconstruction, two interchanges, a pedestrian overpass) started on 10.08.2026 (amic.ru), with completion by the end of 2028 (amic) / the second half of 2029 (promrazvedka, 19.36 billion ₽, TSM LLC).
alt-22.guide: The trakt is not a road “to a destination” but the journey itself: allow at least 2 days from Gorno-Altaysk to Kosh-Agach, otherwise you will fly past all the best parts. Stop at Seminsky (that is where real Altai begins), at the Chike-Taman viewpoint and at the confluence of the Chuya and Katun — the turquoise Katun and the muddy gray Chuya flow side by side without mixing. At km 744 find the monument to Kolka Snegiryov — the driver from the song “There Is a Road Along the Chuysky Trakt”. After Aktash services thin out — fill up at every opportunity and don't speed: there are cows, horses and rockfalls on the road. Buy pies in Srostki — it's a ritual for everyone heading to Altai.
alt-22.see: Srostki (Shukshin museum, Mount Piket); Seminsky Pass (1717 m, stele); Chike-Taman Pass (viewpoint, serpentine road); Inya (suspension bridge, stelae); the confluence of the Chuya and Katun (km 712, near Inya; a viewpoint with a gazebo, a cafe, the Chuy-Oozy nature and recreation park — seven.travel); the Kalbak-Tash petroglyphs (km 723; entry 250–300 ₽, excursion 300 ₽, children free, ~9:00–19:00 — 2GIS 4.5/167, 2026); the monument to Kolka Snegiryov (km 744); Bely Bom; Aktash and the Red Gates (the turn to Ulagan); Geyser Lake (~km 797); the Kurai steppe with a view of the North Chuya Range and the Kurai Pass; Kyzyl-Chin (“Mars”, the turn at km 865); the Chuya steppe and Kosh-Agach; Tashanta (petroglyphs, the border).
alt-22.skip: You are flying to Gorno-Altaysk for Lake Teletskoye or Chemal and are not ready to spend 2+ days behind the wheel — the northern part Novosibirsk — Biysk is boring and can be replaced by a train/plane.
alt-22.diff: Easy for a driver — paved road, passes without extreme gradients; allow for livestock on the road, rockfall sections and winter conditions.
alt-22.when: June — September (better late August — September: fewer cars, “golden autumn”); in winter it is passable, but closures are possible, especially of the passes and the Yodro — Aktash section.
alt-22.hours: The road — around the clock; the Tashanta border checkpoint — 09:00–18:00, closed on Sundays and holidays (Rosgranstroy); closed 10–15.07.2026 (Naadam, alta.ru).
alt-22.daytime: In the daytime — the passes and viewpoints in good light; morning — less traffic on the Maima — Manzherok section (repairs and weekend traffic jams); avoid driving at night beyond Aktash (livestock, rocks).
alt-22.how: Start: Novosibirsk (km 0) — by car ~4.5–5 h to Biysk, or train 306N Novosibirsk — Biysk (~9 h 25 min, from 1,025 ₽, tutu.ru 2026), buses Novosibirsk — Gorno-Altaysk (4,026–6,300 ₽, ros-bilet 2026); Barnaul — the junction onto the trakt is near Novoaltaysk (km 217); Gorno-Altaysk airport (GRV) is near Maima, 2 km from the trakt (not checked).
alt-22.needcar: Yes — a car (own/rented), marshrutka (minibus) or a tour. Any regular car is fine for the main road.
alt-22.self: Yes — this is the most accessible way to see Gorno-Altai. For Russian citizens no permit is needed up to and including Kosh-Agach; Tashanta is a border zone (passport; a permit for foreigners).
alt-22.roadtype: Paved throughout; mountain serpentines at Seminsky and Chike-Taman; repair sections with reversible traffic (km 455–472, 479–495 in 2026); reconstruction Maima — Manzherok until 2029 (detours).
alt-22.traveltime: Novosibirsk — Biysk ~350 km (4.5–5 h); Biysk — Gorno-Altaysk ~100 km (1.5 h); Gorno-Altaysk — Aktash ~5 h (marshrutka); Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach ~450–500 km, 7–8 h; Novosibirsk — Kosh-Agach with a transfer 15–17 h (ros-bilet). A comfortable road trip — 6–10 days (sport-marafon).
alt-22.stay: Campsites 300–400 ₽/tent (sport-marafon); tourist bases near Aktash 500–2,500 ₽/day (Wikivoyage, outdated); hotels in Aktash from ~4,600 ₽ (101hotels 2026); Kosh-Agach: Rasul from 4,200 ₽ (101hotels 2026), bases from 3,700 ₽ (tropki 2026). It is convenient to plan overnight stops in Ongudai/Inya, Aktash and Kosh-Agach.
alt-22.net: There is signal along the main road, but it drops out in mountain sections (sport-marafon); specific gaps by operator were not found.
alt-22.entry: Travel is free (no toll sections found); the tourist tax applies only in Gorno-Altaysk; individual sights by the road (Geyser Lake, Kalbak-Tash and others) are paid at different rates.
alt-22.transfer: Marshrutka Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach ≈4,772–7,977 ₽ (2026, sources differ); a tour/transfer in a Land Cruiser — on request.
alt-22.bring: A full tank after Aktash, a spare wheel, a first-aid kit, cash (not all villages have card terminals — not checked), water and a snack, warm clothes (it is cold on the Chuya steppe and passes even in summer), offline maps.
alt-22.warn: 2026 repairs: km 455–472 and 479–495 (Souzga — Barangol), reconstruction near Maima/Manzherok until 2029 — traffic jams. Rockfalls: on 19.01.2024 a lane at km 764 was destroyed and traffic Yodro — Aktash was closed (RG). Livestock on the road, especially at night. In winter — snow and ice on the passes. Kosh-Agach District is a border zone (Tashanta and others). The Tashanta border checkpoint is closed on Sundays and holidays. Ticks in season (in the Altai Republic by 25.08.2026 — 3,600 reports).
alt-22.food: “Srostki pies” (Srostki, pies from 130 ₽, lunch ~500 ₽); “Arzhan-Suu” (km 478, shashlik, plov — after Shukshin's film); “Traktir Nika” (km 292, 24/7, pelmeni) and “Prival” (km 214) — on the flat section (Altapress 05.06.2026); “Na Obochine” (Ongudai, km 656, buuzy, lagman); “Traktir” (Aktash); “Sailyugem” (Kurai, Altai cuisine); “U Katuni” (Inegen) — altaihelicopters.com; in Aktash — “Oasis” (2GIS 4.8/935), “Karavan” (4.4/486).
alt-22.reviews: No ratings were found for the road as a sight. Seminsky Pass is on TripAdvisor. Fuel stations: Lukoil in Souzga (km 455) 4.9/290, Gazpromneft in Maima 4.9/502, Rosneft Ust-Sema/Shebalino 4.7–4.8 (2GIS 2026). Pluses — views, asphalt quality; minuses — repairs, traffic jams near Maima, slow trucks.

alt-22.p.sum: The Chuysky Trakt is a paved road ~968 km long from Novosibirsk to Mongolia; the mountain section begins beyond Biysk (km 350) and the Altai Republic border (km 428.7). From Gorno-Altaysk to Kosh-Agach it is ~7–8 h of pure driving, but plan 2–3 days with stops. In 2026 — repairs near Maima/Manzherok and Barangol.

alt-23.name: Chemal Hydropower Plant and Patmos Island
alt-23.full: Two neighbouring sights in the village of Chemal at the confluence of the Chemal and Katun: the historic Chemal hydropower plant (1935, 16A Kedrovaya St.) and the rocky island of Patmos on the Katun with the Church of St. John the Theologian, linked to the shore by a suspension bridge; between them runs the pedestrian “Goat Trail” (~1 km).
alt-23.near: The village of Chemal (the sights are within the village); Gorno-Altaysk ~95–98 km (bolshayastrana).
alt-23.short: Chemal's most popular pair of sights: the first hydropower plant in the Altai Mountains (1935), now a museum with a dam, viewpoints and attractions, and Patmos Island with its wooden Church of St. John the Theologian, reached by a swaying suspension bridge over the turquoise Katun.
alt-23.desc: The Chemal hydropower plant was built in 1935 by prisoners (~700 people, trekkingmania) — the first hydropower plant in the Altai Republic; construction ran 1931–1935 (privet-altai), with a capacity of ~400 kW (privet-altai), <460 kW (220+240 kW, trekkingmania) or 500 kW (welcometoaltai), depending on the source; it survived the floods of 1959 and 1969 and supplied nearby villages and sanatoriums. In 2011, after an accident/flooding of the machine hall, the plant was shut down, in 2013 the reservoir was drained, and the 2014 flood damaged the earthen part of the dam and the bridge (sibalt). Now it is a monument of local significance and a museum: in summer — tours of the plant building, a paid walk onto the dam, and all around a souvenir market, an extreme-entertainment park (a bungee swing, the “Krutoe Pike” (Steep Dive), a zip line, a Ferris wheel), and ATV and catamaran rentals. About 300 m away is the confluence of the Chemal and Katun. Patmos Island is a rock in the Katun in the centre of Chemal, consecrated in 1855 in honour of the Apostle John the Theologian (by analogy with the Greek Patmos). The church built on the island in 1915 burned down in the 1920s–30s; in the 1990s the Muscovite Viktor Pavlov restored the shrine, in 1998 a suspension bridge was built (about 15 m above the water), and in 2000 a new cedar church of about 20 m², consecrated on 10.01.2001 (kp.ru, bolshayastrana). Today the island holds the women's skete of the Apostle John the Theologian of the Barnaul Znamensky Monastery (altaitur.com); on the rock is a carved image of the Mother of God. Entry to the island is free, donations are welcome; since 2020 vehicle access to the island has been closed by a barrier. Between the hydropower plant and the island, the “Goat Trail” runs along the Katun (~1 km, partly with wooden stairs).
alt-23.guide: Come before 9 a.m. — after that there is a queue on the suspension bridge to Patmos, and the bridge sways noticeably (you may feel dizzy if you're not used to it). Speak quietly on the island: it is a working women's skete, and women are better off bringing a scarf and a skirt. Find the image of the Mother of God carved into the rock by the nuns, and watch from the island as the Katun changes colour from turquoise to milky. Then walk the “Goat Trail” over the rocks along the Katun to the old hydropower plant — the 1935 dam, built by prisoners, is now overgrown with attractions, but the plant itself is a piece of history. If you want quiet — come in September.
alt-23.see: The suspension bridge and Patmos Island; the Church of St. John the Theologian (cedar, a myrrh-streaming icon — kp.ru); the image of the Mother of God on the rock; viewpoints over the Katun; the “Goat Trail” Patmos — hydropower plant (~1 km); the dam and machine hall of the hydropower plant (a museum, tours in summer); the confluence of the Chemal and Katun (~300 m from the hydropower plant, free; ~200 m for the entrance — gorniy-altai 2020); nearby — the trail to the Tekelyu waterfall, the Chemal highway along the Katun.
alt-23.skip: You don't like crowds and souvenir stalls — in summer by day this is one of the most crowded corners of the Altai; or you're afraid of heights and wobbly bridges.
alt-23.diff: Easy: the bridge and island — 30–40 min (vsesvoitravel); the “Goat Trail” — moderate, with narrow spots above a drop, but passable with children (sibalt).
