alt-24.name: Tekelyu Waterfall
alt-24.full: Tekelyu Waterfall (Tekelyu), ~60 m high, on the Tekelyu River — a right tributary of the Akkem, ~8 km below Lake Akkem, in the Belukha area (Katun Range). NOTE: this is Ust-Koksa District, not Chemal District — no waterfall of this name near Chemal was found in the sources. It is visible from the Akkem trail (Tyungur — Lake Akkem) from the left bank of the Akkem; the approach to its foot is from the right bank (forded in autumn) or via the Oroktoy trail.
alt-24.near: The village of Tyungur (the start of the Akkem trail; ~30–34 km along the trail — a calculation: the lake is 37.5–42 km from Tyungur, the waterfall ~8 km below the lake); the village of Kucherla (the start of the Oroktoy trail).
alt-24.elev: Drop height ~60 m (all sources); elevation above sea level — not found (camps on the Oroktoy route ~2150 m, Tyungur ~850 m — mountainstories).
alt-24.short: The second-highest waterfall in the Altai Republic (~60 m, after Rassypnoy): the Tekelyu River (“of the goats”) plunges almost vertically, without cascades, into the Akkem valley on the way to Belukha. A natural monument since 1996; reachable only on foot or on horseback, 2+ days.
alt-24.desc: Tekelyu is a waterfall on the river of the same name, ~13 km long, a right tributary of the Akkem, about 8 km below Lake Akkem under Belukha (Katun Range, Ust-Koksa District). It is ~60 m high; unlike many Altai waterfalls, the water falls in almost a single vertical stream, which gives a sense of power. The name comes from the Altai “teke” (mountain goat), of which there are many here. It is a natural monument of republican significance (since 1996 — turistka, altai-poxod; sibalt gives 1980), within the territory of the Belukha nature park; species from the Altai Republic Red Data Book live here — the saker falcon, Altai snowcock, great rosefinch and great snipe. The waterfall is clearly visible from the Akkem trail from the left bank of the Akkem; opposite is a popular camp spot with flat places for tents and water. You can reach the foot by crossing the Akkem's channels (realistic in autumn at low water), then 30–40 min to the upper cascade; in summer the approach is possible via the Oroktoy trail from Kucherla through the headwaters of the Tukhman (a radial hike to the waterfall ~4 km, +130 m — mountainstories). Many tourists confuse it with sights near Chemal — there is no Tekelyu waterfall in Chemal District (there you have Che-Chkysh, Belter-Tuyuk and Kamyshlinsky).
alt-24.guide: Tekelyu is visible right from the Akkem trail — look at the right bank of the Akkem about half a day before Lake Akkem: a white 60-metre string against dark rock. Stop at the camp opposite — it's one of the best overnight spots on the way to Belukha. If you go in September, you can wade across the Akkem's channels and climb to the upper cascade in 30–40 minutes; in July the water is high — don't take risks. Watch for mountain goats — “teke”, from which the waterfall got its name. Combine it with Lake Akkem, the Seven Lakes Valley and the view of Belukha.
alt-24.see: The waterfall itself (from the left bank of the Akkem and at its foot); the upper cascade (30–40 min from the ford); the Akkem valley; further — Lake Akkem and the view of Belukha, the Akkem weather station, the Seven Lakes Valley (a radial hike of 12 km, +600 m — mountainstories); on the Oroktoy variant — Lake Kyuldyuayry, the Kuzuyak pass.
alt-24.skip: You're looking for a waterfall near Chemal for a couple of hours — Tekelyu is in a completely different district, part of a multi-day hike to Belukha (2–3 days one way). You aren't ready for a ford and tents — look from the trail.
alt-24.diff: Moderate: the Akkem trail is 37.5–42 km to the lake with a gain of ~1000–1977 m (activelife / sport-marafon — the sources differ), 2–3 days; fords. The Oroktoy trail is higher and harder (a day with +1050 m).
alt-24.when: July — September; to the foot — in autumn (low water, the Akkem can be crossed — turistka, sibalt). The trekking season to Belukha runs from mid-June to September.
alt-24.hours: Round the clock (a natural feature on the trail).
alt-24.daytime: Morning — the slope is lit and there are fewer clouds; in the evening from the camp opposite — a silhouette at sunset (not confirmed).
alt-24.how: To Tyungur: a bus Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur 10:00 → 17:50, Tue–Sun, from 3677 ₽, sole proprietor Maimanov I.Ya. (unitiki 2026); or to Ust-Koksa + a taxi of 50–60 min (belukha.ru); a group transfer from the airport 6000 ₽/person (June–August 2025, belukha.ru). Tyungur is 60 km from Ust-Koksa and 894 km from Novosibirsk (turistka). Then on foot along the Akkem trail: over the Kuzuyak pass to “Three Birches” (~17 km, can be done with a GAZ-66 transfer) and up the Akkem ~13–17 km to the camp opposite Tekelyu (calculation), and to the lake another ~8 km.
alt-24.needcar: To Tyungur — yes; beyond that on foot/horseback; a GAZ-66 transfer to “Three Birches” shortens the route (turistka, sport-marafon).
alt-24.self: Yes — the trail is popular and well worn (trekkingmania); Russian citizens need a passport (Ust-Koksa District is a border zone; an FSB permit is needed only in the 5-km strip, e.g. the Tomsk camps); foreigners need an FSB permit, processing 60+ days (sport-marafon). Register your group with the Ministry of Emergency Situations.
alt-24.roadtype: To Tyungur — paved/dirt; Tyungur — “Three Birches” — a battered dirt road over the Kuzuyak pass (GAZ-66); then a footpath along the Akkem (forest, rocks, streams).
alt-24.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur ~8 h; Tyungur — the camp opposite Tekelyu 1.5–2 days on foot (estimate; to the lake 2–3 days, sport-marafon); with a transfer to “Three Birches” — 1 day.
alt-24.stay: A tent camp opposite the waterfall (flat places, water — altai-poxod); at Lake Akkem — the “Ak-Kem” weather station (since 1932, they bake flatbread for tourists; at the “Akkem” tourist base a banya costs 4000 ₽ for 3 h, no shower — varandej 2017), the “Akkem” mountain hut, the Active Life campsite (activelife.bz); in Tyungur — the “Vysotnik” tourist base (7 Zarechnaya St., +7 913 698-19-06, belukha.ru, 2GIS 4.6/70), the “Tyungur” base (turbazy.ru) — prices not found.
alt-24.net: There is no signal on the trail or at the lake; the nearest is Tyungur/Kucherla (activelife, trekkingmania). You need a radio/satellite phone.
alt-24.entry: The Belukha nature park is a regional protected area: since 01.07.2026 the fee is 300 ₽ (it was 100), unchanged for residents of the Altai Republic (Tolk 30.06.2026); how to pay — not found (possibly via the “Green Button”/checkpoints).
alt-24.transfer: A bus to Tyungur from 3677 ₽ (2026); a group transfer 6000 ₽ (2025); a transfer to “Three Birches” — not found.
alt-24.bring: Your passport, a tent and sleeping bag (frosts at night by the Akkem), trekking boots and sandals for fords, a rain jacket, gas (campfires are restricted), a first-aid kit, a filter, repellent, tick insurance, a radio/satellite communication.
alt-24.warn: The Akkem fords are dangerous in July at high water; to the foot — only at low water. The border zone of Ust-Koksa District (passport; a permit for foreigners). In summer a border post at Lake Akkem checks documents and logs everyone; Russian citizens can go freely up to the glacier, beyond that is a strict border zone with a permit (guide-altai; varandej 2017). Ticks (in the Altai Republic by 25.08.2026 — 3600 bite reports, 22 cases of encephalitis). No signal. Bears in the Belukha area — store your food properly. Don't confuse it with Chemal District!
alt-24.food: In Tyungur — local mountain honey and dairy from residents (turistka); at Lake Akkem — meals at the weather station/at the Active Life campsite (by order). No cafes with ratings were found.
alt-24.reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.7/5 (3 reviews), no. 2 in Ust-Koksa — “a real gift on the route”, a rainbow on a sunny day; no 2GIS/Yandex entries for the waterfall were found. The “Vysotnik” tourist base — 2GIS 4.6/70. Pros: a powerful vertical stream, the view from the trail, the camp opposite; cons: hard to reach the foot in summer.

alt-25.name: Kamyshlinsky Waterfall
alt-25.full: Kamyshlinsky Waterfall (Kamysh-La) — a two-tier waterfall on the Kamyshla River where it flows into the Katun, on the right bank of the Katun (opposite the highway) between Barangol and Ust-Sema, landmark — km 490–496 of the Chuysky Trakt
alt-25.near: Barangol (the Tsarskaya Okhota (Royal Hunt) tourist base, km ~492 of the highway) and Ust-Sema (km ~496); Chemal ~40 km, Gorno-Altaysk ~60 km
alt-25.elev: ≈390 m above sea level; the waterfall is 12 m high (two tiers)
alt-25.short: A low (12 m) but powerful two-tier waterfall on the Kamyshla River, 2.5–3 km from the Chuysky Trakt — one of the most accessible and popular natural sites in Gorny Altai.
alt-25.desc: Before flowing into the Katun, the Kamyshla River drops over two ledges with a total height of about 12 m: the upper tier is almost sheer, the lower one breaks against the rocks like a “tent”. The waterfall is a natural monument of republican significance (status since 1978, confirmed in 1996, area 0.0313 km²). It is on the right bank of the Katun, so from the Chuysky Trakt you reach it by crossing the suspension bridge of the Tsarskaya Okhota (Royal Hunt) resort complex (Barangol) or the bridge at Ust-Sema, then ~2.5–3 km along the forest “Shamans' Trail” by the Katun; in summer motorboats also run along the Katun right to its foot. At the waterfall there is a viewing platform above the upper tier and a railed boardwalk by the lower one, gazebos, souvenir stalls, a cafe, and nearby trout ponds and a rope swing. According to a claim common in guidebooks, the cascade is partly linked to a mill dam of 1930 (data from a single source — tonkosti.ru).
alt-25.guide: Go through the Tsarskaya Okhota suspension bridge — the bridge over the Katun is an attraction in itself, and after it comes a pleasant 40 minutes through pine forest. Climb to the viewing platform above the upper tier: from above you can see the Kamyshla literally “fall” into the Katun. Locals say that washing your face with the waterfall's water washes away grief and tears, and a legend tells of the lovers Kamysh and La, at the place of whose death the waterfall appeared. In autumn, in golden foliage, the best shots are here; in spring after the snow melts, the stream is at its most powerful.
alt-25.see: Two tiers and a viewing platform above the upper one; the boardwalk by the lower tier; the suspension bridge across the Katun at Tsarskaya Okhota; the “Shamans' Trail” through the pine forest; trout ponds (fishing with rod rental); a motorboat trip along the Katun.
alt-25.skip: You have already seen Altai's big waterfalls (Uchar, Korbu, Chulcha) and dislike crowded tourist spots with paid bridges and souvenir rows — Kamyshlinsky is small and very crowded in summer.
alt-25.diff: Easy: ~2.5–3 km one way along a forest trail with small climbs (≈40 min); a short steep section of 300–500 m; slippery after rain. Unofficial trails are muddy and dangerous.
alt-25.when: Year-round. Spring (May–June) has the most water and the maralnik (Siberian rhododendron) in bloom; autumn (September to early October) is the most photogenic season; in winter the waterfall freezes into ice formations.
alt-25.hours: A natural site with no time restrictions; the paid bridge and boats work in daylight (exact hours not found).
alt-25.daytime: Morning — before the tour groups arrive (editorial data).
alt-25.how: Along the Chuysky Trakt (R-256) from Gorno-Altaysk ~60 km to Barangol (km ~492) or Ust-Sema (km ~496). Option 1: the Tsarskaya Okhota suspension bridge (paid) → ~2.5–2.8 km along the trail. Option 2: the free road bridge at Ust-Sema → ~4 km along the trail by the bank. Option 3: a motorboat along the Katun to the foot. Public transport: Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal buses (06:25, 13:35, 14:05, 16:25, 18:30, from 720 ₽) pass Barangol and Ust-Sema. Note: on the Souzga — Barangol section (km 455–495) the highway is under repair in 2026.
alt-25.needcar: Yes — as far as Barangol/Ust-Sema (car, Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal bus, taxi, excursion); then on foot or by boat.
alt-25.self: Yes, fully: the trail is obvious, it takes 40–60 minutes to walk.
alt-25.roadtype: Paved road (the Chuysky Trakt, in 2026 under repair with detours at km 455–495) to the parking area; then a forest dirt trail with roots and stones, wooden boardwalks.
alt-25.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Barangol ~1 h by car (60 km, longer allowing for the highway repair); the trail 40–60 min one way; by boat — a few minutes.
alt-25.stay: Tsarskaya Okhota (Royal Hunt) resort complex (Barangol, Chuyskaya St. 2): an eco-house from 16,000 ₽/night, a VIP house with a pool from 18,000 ₽ (putevka.com, 2026); numerous tourist bases and guesthouses in Barangol, Ust-Sema, Manzherok, Chemal.
alt-25.net: There is a mobile signal by the highway in Barangol/Ust-Sema (Wi-Fi at Tsarskaya Okhota); coverage by operator on the trail — not found.
alt-25.entry: There is no separate ticket for the waterfall in recent sources; the paid crossing of the Tsarskaya Okhota suspension bridge costs 350 ₽ (Sputnik8) / 450 ₽ (2GIS), the sources differ; the route via the bridge at Ust-Sema is free. Whether the natural monument is on the list of paid protected areas of the Altai Republic (300 ₽ from 01.07.2026) — not found. There is no resort fee in the Altai Republic.
alt-25.transfer: Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal bus (via Barangol) from 720 ₽; group excursions from 2850 ₽ (Manzherok) to 5200–6700 ₽ (combined from Gorno-Altaysk), individual 18,000–26,000 ₽ (Sputnik8, 2026).
alt-25.bring: Closed shoes with a thick non-slip sole, a rain jacket/windbreaker (spray and wind), camera protection, tick repellent, cash for the bridge and boat.
alt-25.warn: The rocks and boardwalks at the waterfall are wet and slippery; unofficial bypass trails are dangerous after rain (windfalls, steep mud). Ticks: in 2026 the Altai Republic had 3600 reports and 22 cases of encephalitis — vaccination/insurance. Repair of the Chuysky Trakt at km 455–495 in 2026 — allow extra time. Swimming in the Katun is dangerous — a strong current.
alt-25.food: Trout from the local trout ponds by the waterfall; a cafe on the grounds and in Barangol (names not specified); in Chemal/Manzherok — Altai dishes (keche, talkan, kai-chai).
alt-25.reviews: 2GIS: 4.7/5, 1587 ratings, 513 reviews (10.2026). Pros: beautiful, well-kept trails and viewing platforms, the bridge across the Katun, a cafe and gazebos. Cons: the paid bridge, many people, “commercialization”, dangerous unofficial trails.

alt-25.p.sum: The most accessible waterfall by the Chuysky Trakt: drive to Barangol or Ust-Sema (~60 km from Gorno-Altaysk), cross the Katun by the suspension bridge (paid) or by the road bridge in Ust-Sema (free) and walk 40–60 minutes through the forest. You can go by boat. It combines well with Manzherok and Chemal.

alt-26.name: Karakol Lakes (Iolgo)
alt-26.full: Karakol Lakes — a cascade of 7 cirque lakes on the western slope of the Iolgo Range (the watershed of the Katun and Biya) at the foot of Bagatash Pass, in the upper reaches of the Elekmonar river (Sorgat tract)
alt-26.elev: Sources differ: 1630–1840 m (iskatel) or from ~1820 m (lowest) to ~2097 m (highest) (Bolshaya Strana); a tour operator says 1620–2000 m
alt-26.short: A chain of seven cold, clear lakes below Bagatash Pass on the Iolgo Range, connected by streams and small waterfalls — a classic one-day “all-terrain truck” outing from Elekmonar and Chemal.
alt-26.desc: Seven lakes lie in steps in the cirques of the western slope of the Iolgo Range at an elevation of about 1600–2100 m, 300–800 m apart. The largest is the 5th lake (~435×350 m), where the only tourist base stands, with cedar cabins and a canteen; the smallest is the 7th (~78×30 m). The water is icy and very clean; in winter the small lakes freeze through, and there is almost no fish; on the upper lakes snow lies even in July. Higher up are Bagatash Pass with its panorama, the “Valley of Turs” (cairns) and the rock outliers called the “Castles of the Mountain Spirits”. The lakes are a natural monument of regional significance (since 1987, confirmed in 1996, IUCN category III). Access is from Elekmonar up the Elekmonar river valley with dozens of fords to the Sorgat tract (~3 h on a GAZ-66 “shishiga” or a UAZ), then 8–12 km on foot, on horseback or by the same all-terrain truck. The season runs from late May to October; in winter — snowmobile tours.
alt-26.guide: You will ride in a “shishiga” along the bed of the Elekmonar — hold on tight, it is part of the adventure, not an inconvenience. Don't stop at the fifth lake with the tourist base: walk up the chain to the seventh and to Bagatash Pass — from there you can see all the lakes at once and half of Altai. According to legend, the lakes are beads of a pearl necklace of an evil spirit's daughter, and the spirits of the second lake help those who ask for health. Take a down jacket even in July: at night it can be zero here, and hail can come in the daytime.
alt-26.see: All 7 lakes in the chain; Bagatash Pass (panorama); the “Valley of Turs” (cairns); the “Castles of the Mountain Spirits” outliers; small waterfalls between the lakes; the starry sky (Milky Way) if you stay overnight.
alt-26.skip: You get carsick and are not ready for 3–4 hours of shaking in an all-terrain truck each way for a few hours at the lakes, or you have only one day and want more views for less travel — then choose Chemal and the Katun.
alt-26.diff: Moderate. A one-day trip by all-terrain truck is physically not hard, but the road is exhausting (up to 4 h each way). On foot from Sorgat it is 8 km, a 3–4 h climb; the climb to Bagatash Pass is extra. Altitude ~2000 m.
alt-26.when: Season — late May / from 25 May to October; optimal mid-June to mid-August, especially July; in August there are night frosts. In winter — only snowmobile tours.
alt-26.hours: A natural site; tours depart from Elekmonar at 07:00 (a group on a GAZ-66) or 08:00 (jeep tour), returning in the evening (Karakol-Tur, 2026).
alt-26.daytime: Midday — the sun is above the cirques and the lakes glow (editorial); for stars — an overnight stay at the tourist base.
alt-26.how: Gorno-Altaysk — Elekmonar via the Chuysky and Chemal trakts (~99 km, by bus ~2 h, the buses to Chemal pass through Elekmonar). From Elekmonar — only all-terrain trucks (GAZ-66, ZIL-130, UAZ) for about 30–33 km along the bed and valley of the Elekmonar (20+ fords) to the Sorgat tract (~3 h), then 8–12 km uphill: on foot (3–4 h), on horseback or by GAZ-66 (1.5–3 h). In your own regular car — not possible. Approaches from the Beshpeltir/Kuyum side are not described in the sources found.
alt-26.needcar: Yes — an organized all-terrain truck (GAZ-66/UAZ) from Elekmonar or Chemal; or on foot/horseback over several days.
alt-26.self: On foot — yes (for experienced hikers, over several days, with fords across the Elekmonar). By car — only in your own serious 4×4; most people go with local all-terrain trucks.
alt-26.roadtype: Paved to Elekmonar; Elekmonar — Sorgat is heavy off-road along the riverbed, 20+ fords, bridges get washed away; higher up — a rocky track/trail.
alt-26.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Elekmonar ~2 h; Elekmonar — lakes 3–4 h by all-terrain truck each way; the whole tour 12–14 h.
alt-26.stay: The only tourist base is at the 5th lake (cedar cabins, a canteen, no mains power): a 2-day/1-night tour is 14,000 ₽ (Karakol-Tur, 2026); per tonkosti — 4,000–8,000 ₽/night, banya 1,500 ₽/h, a tent pitch 500 ₽, firewood 500 ₽ (year not stated). Bases in Elekmonar and Chemal.
alt-26.net: not found (according to reviews there is no signal; check)
alt-26.entry: No separate ticket found. The lakes are a regional natural monument; from 01.07.2026 the fee for visiting regional protected areas of the Altai Republic is 300 ₽ (residents of the Altai Republic keep the previous rate), but whether the Karakol Lakes are on the paid list was not found.
alt-26.transfer: 4,000–6,000 ₽ per person (all-terrain truck/jeep from Elekmonar, 2026); 7,000 ₽ from Gorno-Altaysk (Sputnik8).
alt-26.bring: A warm jacket/down jacket, a hat, a rain jacket (hail, downpours), trekking shoes, dry rations and water (food at the base is expensive; lunch ~1,000 ₽), tick repellent, motion-sickness pills, a headlamp if staying overnight.
alt-26.warn: Fords across the Elekmonar — after rain and during floods the road may be impassable; the “shishiga” shakes you a lot. Altitude ~2000 m: down to 0 °C at night, snow on the upper lakes in July, hail. Ticks (in 2026, 22 cases of encephalitis in the Altai Republic). Children — from 5 years old (tour operators).
alt-26.food: Lunch at the tourist base at the 5th lake — porridges, soups, dishes cooked in cauldrons over a fire (~1,000 ₽ per Karakol-Tur); in Chemal and Elekmonar — cafes with Altai cuisine (names not specified).
alt-26.reviews: Sputnik8 (excursion from Gorno-Altaysk): 4.6/5, 11 reviews. Pluses — beauty, “like another world”, the starry sky. Minuses — a very hard road (4 h each way), cold, expensive food. 2GIS/Yandex ratings were not found.

alt-28.name: Manzherok
alt-28.full: Manzherok is a village on the Katun by the Chuysky Trakt (Maima district) and the year-round resort of the same name at the foot of Mount Malaya Sinyukha (resort address: Ozernoye village, Kurort Manzherok, bldg 1), with Lake Manzherok nearby
alt-28.near: Manzherok, Ozernoye; Gorno-Altaysk ~20–30 km, Gorno-Altaysk airport (GRV) ~26 km
alt-28.elev: Lake 373 m; upper station of the Chuysky Trakt gondola ~1020 m (drop of 633 m); summit of Malaya Sinyukha ~1200–1240 m
alt-28.short: The biggest year-round resort in the Altai Mountains: Siberia's longest gondola up Malaya Sinyukha, ski runs, a spa and 3–5* hotels, and below it the warm Lake Manzherok with water chestnut and a beach.
alt-28.desc: The village of Manzherok has been known since Soviet times (the song “Manzherok” and the friendship festival of the 1960s), and since the 2010s the year-round Manzherok resort has been growing on the slopes of Mount Malaya Sinyukha. Five lifts run all year; the main one is the Chuysky Trakt gondola, 2516 m long with a 633 m drop (8–12 min ride up), plus the Voskhod, Sofia, Lednik and Karusel chairlifts and a travelator. In winter (≈mid-November to mid-April) there are about 50 km of runs; in summer there are sightseeing lift rides, eco trails of the Keeper of the Great Altai theme park, viewpoints, paragliding, a bike park and restaurants on the mountain. The resort has the Manzherok 5* and Manzherok 3* hotels and a spa complex with pools. 2 km from the village is Lake Manzherok (1.1×0.4 km, up to 3 m deep), a former oxbow of the Katun; in summer it warms up to +21…22 °C, and it has a free beach and catamaran and SUP rental. The lake is a natural monument because of the Red Data Book water chestnut (chilim, Trapa natans), and it has been cleared of silt since 2018. In 2026 a bypass of the Chuysky Trakt (km 454–475, with an interchange at the turn to Ozernoye) is under construction near Manzherok, due to finish at the end of 2028.
alt-28.guide: Take the Chuysky Trakt gondola up Malaya Sinyukha on a clear day: from the top you can see the Katun winding between the ridges, and Lake Manzherok looks like a green drop. Down below, be sure to visit the lake — in summer it is one of the few mountain lakes in Altai where you can swim without an icy shock; look for rosettes of water chestnut, a Red Data Book plant, near the shore. If you're on a budget, stay at a guesthouse in the village of Manzherok or Ozernoye and buy food there, coming to the resort only for the cable car. Everyone here knows the 1960s song “Manzherok” — ask the locals where the name comes from.
alt-28.see: The gondola ride up Malaya Sinyukha and the viewpoints; the eco trails of the Keeper of the Great Altai park; Lake Manzherok (beach, water chestnut, catamarans, SUPs); the Katun by the village; nearby: Cheremshanka Waterfall (~9 km), Emurla Waterfall, Patmos Island in Chemal, Kamyshla Waterfall.
alt-28.skip: You are going to Altai for wild nature and quiet: Manzherok is a developed resort with hotels, construction and crowds, and the Chuysky Trakt next to it is under reconstruction in 2026–2028.
alt-28.diff: Easy: the cable car is accessible to everyone; the eco trails on the mountain are easy/moderate; the runs range from green to black.
alt-28.when: Skiing: mid-November to mid-April (best January–March); summer: July–August (swimming in the lake); autumn: September (colors). The cable cars run all year.
alt-28.hours: Cable cars 9:00–18:00, last boarding 17:00; they do not run in wind over 15 m/s, thunderstorms, or frost below −25 °C (kp.ru, 2026). Lake beach 10:00–21:00 (kp.ru).
alt-28.daytime: Morning: be first on the gondola, before the clouds and queues arrive (editorial); sunset: at the lake.
alt-28.how: Fly to Gorno-Altaysk (GRV), then 26 km/30–40 min along the Chuysky Trakt (transfer ~8500 ₽ per car via Sputnik8). From Novosibirsk by bus 8–9.5 h; or by train to Biysk and then along the trakt. From Gorno-Altaysk ~35–40 min by car; according to kp.ru, bus No. 132 (≈1 h). To the resort, turn off to Ozernoye, 4 km from Manzherok; free parking. In 2026–2028 the bypass of the trakt (km 454–475, Souzga — Manzherok) is under construction.
alt-28.needcar: Yes, to reach the resort (taxi/transfer/car/bus); inside the resort everything is on foot.
alt-28.roadtype: Paved road (Chuysky Trakt R256 + the access road to Ozernoye); in 2026 there are construction sections with detours.
alt-28.traveltime: GRV airport — resort 30–40 min; Gorno-Altaysk — 35–40 min; Novosibirsk — 8–9.5 h by bus; gondola ride up 8–12 min.
alt-28.stay: At the resort: Manzherok 5* — from ~29,800–32,000 ₽/night, Manzherok 3* — from ~24,000 ₽ (travelto/kp, 2025–2026); the resort's overall range is 4800–126,000 ₽ (Altapress, 06.2026). In the villages of Manzherok/Ozernoye — guesthouses and bases 2500–7000 ₽ (kp.ru, travelto, 2026).
alt-28.net: Resort and villages by the trakt — mobile signal and Wi-Fi in hotels (operators not specified).
alt-28.entry: Entry to the resort grounds and the lake beach is free (kp.ru). Cable cars are paid (sightseeing ride from 1500 ₽). There is no resort tax in the Altai Republic.
alt-28.transfer: Airport — Manzherok 8500 ₽ per car (Sputnik8); excursions from Manzherok from 2200 ₽ (kp.ru).
alt-28.bring: A windbreaker/warm sweater for the summit (it is cooler 600 m higher), sun protection, a swimsuit in summer, tick repellent for the eco trails.
alt-28.warn: Construction of the Chuysky Trakt bypass (km 454–475) until the end of 2028 — traffic jams and detours; repairs at km 455–472 and 479–495 in 2026. Cable cars close in strong wind/thunderstorms. Eco trails are sometimes closed because of bears (Yandex reviews). Ticks: April to August.
alt-28.food: Resort restaurants (including a restaurant on the mountain; average bill ~700–1500 ₽, Gornaya ~1500 ₽ per person — Altapress 2026), dishes from local farm produce; groceries are cheaper in the shops in Ozernoye.
alt-28.reviews: Yandex Maps (resort): 5.0, 20,047 ratings, 6592 reviews (10.2026). Pros: modern infrastructure, spa, cable cars, eco trails, breakfasts. Cons: high prices, uneven service, construction, overcrowded spa at peak times.

alt-29.name: A. V. Anokhin National Museum
alt-29.full: A. V. Anokhin National Museum of the Altai Republic — Gorno-Altaysk, 46 Grigory Choros-Gurkin St.
alt-29.near: Gorno-Altaysk (city centre; 5–7 min on foot from the bus station, ~15 min from Lenin Square)
alt-29.short: The main museum of the Altai Mountains: archaeology from the Stone Age to the ancient Turks, the “Ukok Princess” — the mummy of a Pazyryk woman about 2,500 years old — Altai ethnography and paintings by G. I. Choros-Gurkin.
alt-29.desc: The museum is named after the Turkologist and ethnographer Andrey Viktorovich Anokhin. The new building opened in 2012 after a major reconstruction funded with help from Gazprom. The collection holds more than 60,000 items; the permanent exhibitions are ancient history (7 halls), ethnography (3), nature (4, including mammoth bones), the “Ukok Plateau” complex with a reconstructed burial, fine art (3 halls, including works by Choros-Gurkin) and modern history (6 halls). The centrepiece is the mummy of the “Ukok Princess” (Pazyryk culture, 6th–2nd centuries BC), found on Ukok in 1993. She is displayed only on certain days according to a lunar calendar agreed with Altai traditions (waxing moon), from 09:30 to 13:00 under strict climate control; flash photography and video are prohibited. There is an audio guide (Russian, Altai, English), themed tours, a museum shop, a cafe and a research library; the Pushkin Card is accepted. In 2026 the entrance is at the end of the building because the main staircase is under repair.
alt-29.guide: Check the dates: the “Ukok Princess” is shown only 9–10 days a month and only until 13:00 — on other days you will see the reconstructed burial but not the mummy itself. Look at the tattoos on her shoulder (mythical griffin-deer) — they are often compared to modern tattoos. Many Altai people believe that removing the princess from Ukok brought earthquakes to the republic, which is why the showings are timed to a “favourable” moon. Do not skip the hall with Choros-Gurkin’s paintings — after them you see Belukha and the Katun differently.
alt-29.see: The “Ukok Plateau” complex and the mummy of the “Ukok Princess” (on display days); the ancient history halls (Pazyryk burial mounds, ancient Turkic stone statues); Altai ethnography (ail, costumes, shamanic items); the nature section (mammoth, fauna); paintings by G. I. Choros-Gurkin.
alt-29.skip: You have only one day in Altai and the weather is great — nature matters more; or you will not be there on a mummy display day and are not interested in archaeology.
alt-29.diff: None (city museum; 2–3 h to see it).
alt-29.when: Year-round; ideally on mummy display days (2026: 14–18, 21–25 October; 11–15, 18–22 November; 11–12, 16–20, 23–24 December; September — 16–20, 23–26).
alt-29.hours: Wed–Sat 9:30–17:30, Sun 9:30–16:30, closed Mon–Tue (2GIS, 10.2026); per snovatrip/karoaltai — Wed–Sat until 18:00, Sun until 17:00, ticket offices close 30 min earlier. The mummy is shown only on display days, 09:30–13:00.
alt-29.daytime: Morning (9:30–13:00) is the only time the mummy is shown.
alt-29.how: The museum is in the centre of Gorno-Altaysk: 5–7 min on foot from the bus station, ~15 min from Lenin Square. From Gorno-Altaysk airport — taxi across the city. From Belokurikha it is 122 km (bus/taxi); from Manzherok ~38 km, from Chemal ~100 km (karoaltai).

alt-29.traveltime: From the bus station 5–7 min on foot; from Manzherok ~40 min; from Chemal ~2 h.

alt-29.entry: Adult 350 ₽, full-time students 200 ₽, pensioners and schoolchildren 150 ₽, family ticket 750 ₽ (2 adults + 1–3 children aged 7–16), children under 7 free (2GIS, updated 27.03.2026; snovatrip 2026). Audio guide 350 ₽. There is a separate ticket for viewing the mummy (official website; price not found). The Pushkin Card is accepted. Tourist tax applies only when staying overnight in Gorno-Altaysk.

alt-29.bring: Passport/Pushkin Card for discounts, cash/card; a warm sweater — the mummy hall is +16…18 °C.
alt-29.warn: The mummy is shown only on schedule and until 13:00; flash photography and video are prohibited in its hall. The museum is closed Mon–Tue. In 2026 the entrance is at the end of the building (staircase repairs).
alt-29.food: The museum cafe serves regional dishes, including yak and maral (Altai deer) meat (snovatrip); in town there are cafes with Altai cuisine (kyoche, talkan, kai-chai).
alt-29.reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 1,834 ratings, 598 reviews (10.2026). Pros — rich archaeology, the Ukok princess, modern exhibition. Cons — the mummy is not visible every day, entrance under repair.

alt-30.name: Multa Lakes
alt-30.full: Multa Lakes — a cascade of glacial lakes in the Multa river valley on the northern slope of the Katun Range: Lower (1,710 m), Middle (1,740–1,860 m), Upper (1,920 m), as well as Poperechnoye, Kuiguk, Akchan and others; start points — the villages of Multa/Zamulta and Maralnik-1
alt-30.near: Maralnik-1 (≈12–13 km to the Lower Lake), Multa and Zamulta (≈20–22 km); the district centre Ust-Koksa ≈30–43 km
alt-30.elev: Lower 1,710 m; Middle 1,740 m (1,860 m per tonkosti); Upper 1,920 m (zapovedtravel ~1,860 m); the whole cascade 1,700–2,030 m
alt-30.short: A necklace of turquoise glacial lakes under the Katun Range, linked by the roaring “Shumy” rapids — one of the most beautiful and most visited places in the Ust-Koksa district.
alt-30.desc: The Multa river flows out of a cascade of glacial lakes on the northern slope of the Katun Range. Lower Multa Lake (1,710 m) is the largest: ~2.37×0.7–1 km, up to 20–21 m deep, warming up to +15 °C in summer, with huge moraine boulders along the southern shore and pebble beaches along the northern one. Between the Lower and Middle lakes is the “Shumy” rapids-waterfall (a drop of ~30 m). The Middle Lake (~2×0.6 km, up to 20 m) is already on the edge of the Katun Biosphere Reserve. The Upper Lake (1,920 m, 1.4×0.4 km, 47.7 m deep, water up to +10 °C) lies in a cirque with waterfalls of 47–60 m, entirely inside the reserve, and requires a permit. In the neighbouring valleys are Poperechnoye, Kuiguk and Akchan; through the Kuiguk Pass (1A, 2,520 m) loop routes lead to Kyrgyz Lake and Tyungur. To the Lower Lake from Maralnik-1 it is 12–13 km along a rutted forest road: 4–6 h on foot or 1.5–3 h in a GAZ-66; passenger cars cannot go beyond Maralnik. At the Lower Lake the mountain complex of the “Multa Lakes” tourist complex operates (cabins, glamping), with boats on the Lower and Middle lakes. The season is late June to mid-September; in winter there are snowmobile tours. There is no phone coverage at the lakes.
alt-30.guide: Do not stop at the Lower Lake, where the bases are: walk or take a boat to the “Shumy” and the Middle Lake — there the scene is completely different and wild. If you have the energy for a second day, arrange a permit and climb to the Upper Lake: the deepest (almost 48 m) and coldest lake of the cascade, with waterfalls in the cirque. Locals call the road from Maralnik “mud porridge” — if you walk, wet feet are guaranteed, and in a GAZ-66 hold on tight. Be sure to download offline maps: navigation apps suggest a non-existent road via Inegen and Tyungur.
alt-30.see: The Lower Multa Lake (beaches, boulders, boat); the “Shumy” waterfall-rapids; the Middle Multa Lake; the Upper Multa Lake with waterfalls of 47–60 m (reserve); Poperechnoye Lake; Kuiguk and the Kuiguk Pass; forest and berry patches along the Multa valley.
alt-30.skip: you do not have 2–3 days for this area alone: the road from Gorno-Altaysk is 6–8 h one way plus 1.5–6 h of transfer — too much for a couple of hours at the lake; and if you are not ready for mud, cold and no phone coverage.
alt-30.diff: Moderate: 12–13 km on foot to the Lower Lake with constant climbing (4–6 h, mud); to the Upper Lake — another ~7 km from the Middle Lake (~2 h one way). With a GAZ-66 transfer — easy but bumpy. The loop via Kuiguk is difficult (1A pass).
alt-30.when: Late June to early/mid-September (best from July to mid-August); in June — flowers and full waterfalls, but snow at the upper lakes; frosts from September; in winter — snowmobile tours.
alt-30.hours: A natural area; the permit for the Katun Reserve (for the Upper Lake) is available at the office in Ust-Koksa (Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00) or at the ranger post by the Middle Lake; entry to the reserve is only in daylight (tonkosti/zapovedtravel data).
alt-30.daytime: Morning — calm water and reflections on the Lower Lake (editorial).
alt-30.how: Gorno-Altaysk — Ust-Koksa via the Chuysky Trakt and through Ust-Kan/Tuekta: ~320–424 km, 6–8 h (paved, mostly gravel after Ust-Koksa). Then Ust-Koksa — Multa/Zamulta — Maralnik-1 (~43 km from Ust-Koksa to Maralnik per Wikipedia). From Maralnik-1 (or Multa) to the Lower Lake it is 12–22 km only on foot, on horseback or by GAZ-66/UAZ. Navigation apps suggest a non-existent road via Inegen and Tyungur. From Novosibirsk ~830 km, Barnaul ~550, Biysk ~380 km. Buses run daily from Gorno-Altaysk and Barnaul to Ust-Koksa (8–10 h), then a taxi/base transfer.
alt-30.needcar: Yes: to Multa/Maralnik — your own car, or a bus to Ust-Koksa + taxi; to the lakes — GAZ-66/UAZ, horse or on foot.
alt-30.self: Yes: on foot along the beaten road/path from Maralnik-1 (there are forks — an offline map is needed) or with a transfer by locals. For the Upper Lake — get a reserve permit.
alt-30.roadtype: Paved up to Ust-Koksa; Ust-Koksa — Multa — Maralnik: gravel/dirt, a passenger car can reach Maralnik-1; beyond that — a rutted muddy forest road only for GAZ-66/UAZ, with stretches of wooden decking towards the Upper Lake.
alt-30.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Multa 6–8 h (1–2 days from Novosibirsk); transfer 1.5–3 h; on foot 4–6 h to the Lower Lake; Middle — Upper ~2 h.
alt-30.stay: “Multa Lakes” tourist complex (Zamulta, 4 Novaya St., +7 909 508-10-77): rooms 3,500–8,000 ₽, economy 3,500–5,500 ₽, tent 500 ₽; the mountain complex at the Lower Lake — cabins 4,000 ₽ per person, glamping sphere 12,000 ₽, chalets 12,000–15,000 ₽ (2026). Kedrovaya Opushka base (Maralnik-1, 9 Gornaya St., +7 909 508-25-38): cabins from 1,200 ₽, tent from 400 ₽ (year not stated). At the reserve ranger post by the Upper Lake there is a hut for up to 10 people. All campsites at the Multa Lakes are paid (sport-marafon).
alt-30.net: There is no phone coverage or internet at the lakes (zapovedtravel, kp.ru); in Multa/Ust-Koksa there is (operators not specified).
alt-30.entry: Permit for the Katun Reserve (Upper Lake) — 200 ₽ per person per day (turistka.ru 2026, seven.travel); campsites by the lakes are paid (tent 400–500 ₽). Whether the Lower/Middle Lake falls under the paid regional protected areas (300 ₽ from 01.07.2026) — not found. No resort fee.
alt-30.transfer: GAZ-66 to the Lower Lake 3,000–4,000 ₽ per person (2026); older sources say 2,500 ₽ (kp.ru).
alt-30.bring: Warm waterproof clothing, trekking boots (mud), sun protection, offline maps (the “Karta RU” app), passport for the permit, cash (ATM — Ust-Koksa), tick and mosquito repellent, a gas stove.
alt-30.warn: No phone coverage. The road from Maralnik is mud and ruts. To the Upper Lake — only with a Katun Reserve permit and in daylight. Navigation apps lead you along the non-existent Inegen — Tyungur road. Border zone: the Ust-Koksa district is partly in the border zone (the Karagaiskoye, Amurskoye, Ust-Koksinskoye, Ognevskoye, Katandinskoye, Taldinskoye and Verkh-Uimonskoye settlements); the Multa Lakes are not on the list — Russian citizens need only a passport; foreigners should check with the FSB border directorate (on the way through Ust-Koksa). Ticks and bears (in 2026 — attacks in Altai). Night frosts at the lakes are possible even in summer.
alt-30.food: Meals at the tourist complex and the mountain complex; in the Uimon valley — Old Believer dishes (honey, mead, pelmeni), Altai kai-chai (cafe names not found).
alt-30.reviews: Aggregated 2GIS/Yandex ratings not found. Typical pros — “one of the 10 most beautiful places in Russia”, turquoise water, Shumy; cons — a hard muddy road, paid campsites, crowded at the Lower Lake in July–August.

alt-31.name: Mount Belukha and Lake Akkem
alt-31.full: Mount Belukha (4,506 m, the highest point of Siberia) and Lake Akkem at the foot of its northern (Akkem) face
alt-31.near: Tyungur village (start of the Akkem trail, ~40 km to the lake); Kucherla settlement (start of the Kucherla trail, 4 km from Tyungur by road)
alt-31.elev: Belukha — 4,506 m (East Summit; PeakVisor gives 4,509 m), West Summit — 4,440 m; Lake Akkem — 2,050 m; Akkem mountain hut — 1,980 m; Karatyurek Pass — 3,060 m
alt-31.short: Three-headed Belukha is the highest point of Altai and Siberia; Lake Akkem is a glacial lake of milky turquoise colour right beneath its 3-kilometre northern face, the end point of Altai's most popular trek.
alt-31.desc: Belukha (Altai: Uch-Sumer — “three-headed”, Kadyn-Bazhy — “summit of the Katun”) is the highest point of the Altai Mountains: East Summit 4,506 m, West Summit 4,440 m, with a saddle between them. The border between Russia and Kazakhstan runs over the summit. The Akkem, Katun, Gebler and Berel glaciers flow down from Belukha; the Katun begins at the Gebler. The mountain is part of Belukha Nature Park (≈131,000 ha, zones: nature reserve 11,012 ha, specially protected 37,000 ha, recreational 83,258 ha) and of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. Lake Akkem lies at 2,050 m at the foot of the Akkem face: length ≈1,350 m, width ≈610 m, depth up to 14–15 m, area ≈54 ha. The water is grey-turquoise from glacial silt, with visibility up to 1 m, a temperature of no more than +4.5 °C, and no fish. 2.6 km higher up is the Upper Akkem Lake (≈2,100 m). On the northwest shore there has been an Akkem weather station since 1932, on the west shore an Emergency Ministry base with a helipad, and 1.5 km below the lake the Akkem mountain hut. Above the lake stands the Chapel of the Archangel Michael. Three main trails lead to the lake: the Akkem trail (from Tyungur, ≈40–42 km, 2 days), the Kucherla trail (via Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass, 3,060 m) and the difficult Oroktoy trail. From the lake there are day trips to the Akkem Glacier (6 km), the Valley of the Seven Lakes (6 km, +600 m) and the Yarlu valley. Climbing Belukha is category 4A, only for trained mountaineers.
alt-31.guide: Stand on the western shore of Akkem at dawn — the first rays tint the Akkem face pink, and the lake reflects it if there is no wind. The Altai people consider Belukha a sacred mountain where the spirit of the Katun lives, and the Old Believers sought Belovodye (the legendary land of the righteous) nearby — so don't make noise and don't climb the mountain “just because”. Make a day trip to the Valley of the Seven Lakes: 6 km up, and you're above the clouds with a view of the whole Akkem face. Check in with the border guards at the lake — keep your passport in a waterproof bag. And buy flatbreads at the weather station — it's a local tradition.
alt-31.see: The Akkem (northern) face of Belukha; Lake Akkem and the Upper Akkem Lake (2.6 km higher); the Akkem Glacier (6 km from the lake); the Valley of the Seven Lakes (6 km, +600 m); the Yarlu valley (“White Stone”); the Chapel of the Archangel Michael; the Akkem weather station (since 1932); Karatyurek Pass (3,060 m) with a panorama of Belukha; along the way — Kuzuyak Pass and the “Three Birches” tract
alt-31.skip: If you have 1–2 free days and aren't fit enough for 40 km of trail with 1,000 m of gain — you can only see Belukha from a helicopter or after 2 days on foot/horseback. If you aren't ready for cold nights (snow is possible even in August) and for having no mobile coverage.
alt-31.diff: The trek to Lake Akkem is medium-hard: ≈40–42 km one way, ≈1,000 m of gain from “Three Birches”, 2 days. Via Karatyurek it is hard (climb ≈1,400 m, descent ≈1,100 m). Climbing Belukha is 4A and requires mountaineering training.
alt-31.when: July–August (the most stable weather; up to +15…+23 °C in the valleys by day, around 0…+5 °C at the lake at night, snow possible); June and September — snow on the passes, cold; in winter down to −30 °C, the Akkem hut takes guests from January to mid-March
alt-31.hours: Natural area — open 24 hours. The Akkem hut — summer season and January to mid-March (2026). The weather station works year-round.
alt-31.daytime: Dawn and early morning — Belukha is most often visible without clouds; by lunchtime the summit is usually covered
alt-31.how: To Tyungur: from Gorno-Altaysk ≈450–490 km (6–8 h) along the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Shebalino/Cherga, then via Ust-Kan and Ust-Koksa; from Barnaul ≈600 km, ≈13 h (via Cherga, Besh-Ozek, Ust-Kan, 2019). Bus Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur (sole trader Maymanov) at 10:00, Tue–Sun, from 3,677 ₽; to Ust-Koksa — 10:00, 12:05, 12:10 (from 2,530 ₽, 6.5–8.5 h). From Tyungur: on foot/by horse over Kuzuyak Pass to the “Three Birches” tract (17 km, you can get a GAZ-66 lift), then 25 km up the Akkem to the lake; or via Kucherla, Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass; or by helicopter (departure from the Chemal district, landing at the lake).
alt-31.needcar: Yes: to Tyungur — bus/car; on the trail — your feet, horses, a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, a helicopter
alt-31.self: Yes, the trail is well trodden and popular; independently — with group registration with the Emergency Ministry (online at forms.mchs.gov.ru), a passport and multi-day hiking experience. Climbing Belukha — only with mountaineering training/a guide.
alt-31.roadtype: Paved road to Ust-Koksa with stretches of crushed stone (part of the way via Cherga/Ust-Kan is graded road); Ust-Koksa — Tyungur ≈30 km of crushed stone (2019); then a dirt road for a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, then only a horse-and-foot trail (rocks, roots, streams)
alt-31.traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur 6.5–8 h; Tyungur — Lake Akkem 2 days on foot (1 day if you're fit or with a lift to “Three Birches”); via Kucherla and Karatyurek 3–4 days; helicopter ≈3 h (round trip with a landing)
alt-31.stay: Tyungur: Vysotnik tourist complex (7 Zarechnaya St.; tents 500 ₽/person/night, cottages; 2GIS 4.9 from 79), Altai u Beryoz (8 Zarechnaya St.; beds 1,300 ₽/night, camping 250 ₽/person). Kucherla: Yelovaya Opushka (2,500 ₽/room, 2024). At the lake: Akkem mountain hut (1,980 m; economy 12,000 ₽/8-bed room, comfort 18,000 ₽/4-bed room, 2026), Active Life campsite (tents on platforms, banya, canteen), free tent sites by the Emergency Ministry base on the west shore, overnight stays at the weather station.
alt-31.net: MTS and Beeline — in Tyungur and Kucherla; there is no mobile coverage on the trail or at the lake (you only get a signal on Karatyurek Pass). The weather station has satellite communication and charging; the Akkem hut has paid communication/Wi-Fi.
alt-31.entry: Tourists do not need a separate ticket/permit for Belukha Nature Park (T—Zh, 2024). From 01.07.2026 the fee for visiting regional protected areas of the Altai Republic is 300 ₽ (the previous rate for Altai Republic residents); its applicability to Belukha Park has not been confirmed. There is no resort fee. A boat across the lake — 300 ₽ (2024).
alt-31.transfer: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur: bus from 3,677 ₽ (2026), minibus ≈2,400 ₽ (2024); GAZ-66 Tyungur — “Three Birches” from 3,000 ₽/person or 15,000 ₽/vehicle (2026); horse 4,000 ₽/day (2026); helicopter from 770,000 ₽ per aircraft (2026)
alt-31.bring: Passport (original; for foreigners — an FSB permit), compulsory health insurance policy and tick-bite insurance, a warm sleeping bag (comfort rating around 0 °C), a down jacket, hat and gloves, a waterproof shell, trekking poles, sandals for fords, gas/stove, a food supply (there are no shops on the trail), sunscreen and sunglasses, repellent, a first-aid kit, a power bank, cash (flatbreads, boat, banya)
alt-31.warn: Border zone: the Katanda rural settlement (Tyungur, Kucherla) is in the border zone — for Russian citizens a passport is enough, and at the lake you must check in with the border guards; foreigners need a permit from the FSB Border Directorate (up to 30 working days), and for the 5-km strip along the border everyone needs a permit. The summit of Belukha is the border with Kazakhstan; crossing to the Kazakh side is prohibited (fines). Cold and snow even in August, sudden weather changes, fords of mountain streams, a steep climb to Karatyurek. Glaciers and avalanches — only with experience. Ticks (encephalitis) in the forest belt. There is no mobile coverage — register your group with the Emergency Ministry.
alt-31.food: Flatbreads and herbal tea at the Akkem weather station; dinners at the tourist bases in Tyungur (manty, home cooking); in Ust-Koksa — Smak café (4.9, 207 ratings, bill ~500 ₽), the vegetarian Ganga (4.9, 399 ratings, ~750 ₽); local honey and maral (Altai red deer) products from the Uimon valley
alt-31.reviews: 2GIS: “Lake Akkem” 4.7 (10 ratings); Vysotnik tourist complex in Tyungur 4.9 (79 ratings) — people praise the staff, food and guides, and criticize the prices and extra charges (banya 2,500–3,500 ₽/h). Typical pros of the route: the most spectacular view of Belukha, a good trail, infrastructure at the lake; cons: the long road to Tyungur, cold, crowds in July–August, expensive lifts.

alt-31.p.sum: Lake Akkem is the base for admiring Belukha; 2 days on foot/by horse from Tyungur (≈40–42 km) or 3–4 days on a loop via Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass. Logistics: bus/car to Tyungur (6.5–8 h from Gorno-Altaysk), a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, pack horses for your luggage, overnight stays in the Akkem hut or in a tent. Russian citizens need a passport (border zone); foreigners need an FSB permit in advance.

kg-0002.name: Kara-Bulak Gorge
kg-0002.near: The villages of Arashan and Koi-Tash (the approach is via the Tatyr tract); Bishkek is 25–27 km away (sxodim, triptokyrgyzstan).
kg-0002.elev: About 1800 m at the Kara Bulak eco-resort (sxodim, karabulak.kg); the gorge slopes are higher. The neighboring mountain Tysha is 2300 m (hiking.kg).
kg-0002.short: A small gorge in the Kyrgyz Ala-Too 25–27 km from Bishkek, above the Tatyr tract: colorful rocks, springs, a waterfall and panoramas of the Chuy Valley; the Kara Bulak eco-resort is in the gorge.
kg-0002.desc: Kara-Bulak (“black spring”) is a gorge in the foothills of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too between the Alamedin Gorge and Chunkurchak. Triptokyrgyzstan describes colorful rocks, green hills, a waterfall, many springs and streams, and panoramas of Bishkek, the Chuy Valley and snowy peaks. The approach is along the road through Tatyr toward Chunkurchak (it is being paved in 2026) and then up a steep serpentine over a small pass. Most of the gorge is occupied by the private Kara Bulak eco-resort (2GIS 4.8/5, 903 ratings): cottages, a national-cuisine cafe, a bathhouse, horse rides. The surroundings suit hiking and horse riding; nearby are Mount Tysha, the “Sky Bridge” and the Pigeon Waterfall on the road to Altyn-Ter.
kg-0002.guide: Kara-Bulak is the “mountain weekend” closest to Bishkek: just an hour by car, and the view of the Chuy Valley from above is like from a plane. The most picturesque part is the serpentine after Tatyr: stop at the small pass before the descent into the gorge. The gorge is largely occupied by a private eco-resort, so for a walk on its territory and a horse ride (700 som/hour per 2022 data) arrange it with the reception. If you just want a walk, climb the neighboring mountain Tysha (6 km, ~2.5 hours, +540 m).
kg-0002.see: The colorful rocks and springs of the gorge, a waterfall (triptokyrgyzstan); panoramas of Bishkek and the Chuy Valley from the serpentine; on the way — the “Sky Bridge” and the Pigeon Waterfall (hiking.kg); Mount Tysha (2300 m) with a view of the city and the range.
kg-0002.skip: You are looking for a wild gorge without infrastructure — a private resort dominates here. You have no car: there is no public transport to the gorge. You want high mountains and glaciers — Ala-Archa or Alamedin is better.
kg-0002.diff: Easy: walks in the gorge and around the resort; the ascent of Tysha is 2/5 on hiking.kg (6 km from the parking area, 2 h 25 min, +540 m). The walking approach from Kara-Kiya to the resort takes 5–6 h (karabulak.kg).
kg-0002.when: May to October: green slopes in spring and early summer, golden in autumn; the resort works year-round (2GIS), but in winter the serpentine may be snowed over (editorial).
kg-0002.hours: The gorge is a natural area with no regime. Kara Bulak eco-resort: daily 08:00–24:00 per 2GIS (as of 10.2026), around the clock per sxodim (2022). Entry to the resort's territory is by arrangement.
kg-0002.daytime: Morning — clean air and the best visibility of the Chuy Valley before the daytime haze; sunset — from the serpentine above Tatyr (editorial).
kg-0002.how: Bishkek → Koi-Tash → Arashan → Tatyr tract on the road to Chunkurchak (paved, works in 2026), then the turn to Kara-Bulak and a steep serpentine over a small pass (triptokyrgyzstan; hiking.kg). About 1 h by car (sxodim). On foot — 5–6 h from Kara-Kiya (karabulak.kg).
kg-0002.needcar: Yes: your own car, a taxi or a resort transfer; there is no public transport to the gorge (sxodim: “a private car, about 1 hour”).
kg-0002.self: Yes, by car — no permits needed. Walks on the private eco-resort's territory should be arranged with it; check the walking route from Kara-Kiya against karabulak.kg.
kg-0002.roadtype: Paved road to Tatyr (the 21.7 km Arashan–Chunkurchak road is being paved in 2026: the first layer was laid on 20.7 km by the end of July, economist.kg 11.08.2026); the turn to Kara-Bulak is a steep dirt serpentine, unsuitable for a low city car (hiking.kg).
kg-0002.traveltime: About 1 h from Bishkek by car (sxodim; hiking.kg — 1 h 5 min to the Tysha trailhead, 32 km). The walking approach from Kara-Kiya takes 5–6 h one way (karabulak.kg).
kg-0002.stay: Kara Bulak Eco Resort (karabulak.kg): a cottage for 2 adults with breakfast — 7400 som (sxodim, 2022), from 8700 som (2GIS, 2026); capacity up to 40 guests, bathhouse, spa, Wi-Fi, cafe. Booking is also possible through Ostrovok and Google Hotels.
kg-0002.net: The eco-resort's territory has Wi-Fi for guests (2GIS). Operator coverage in the gorge itself is not confirmed.
kg-0002.entry: No separate entrance ticket to the gorge was found. On the resort's territory services are paid: a horse ride 700 som/h, archery 150 som/3 shots, the “Ishtyk Moncho” bathhouse 22,000–25,000 som (sxodim, 2022). A fee for visiting the territory without staying is not confirmed.
kg-0002.transfer: Not confirmed: the resort's transfer prices are not published. A benchmark — a taxi at the city rate of Yandex Go/inDrive for ~30 km (price not checked).
kg-0002.bring: Comfortable walking shoes, a windbreaker (1800 m and higher), water and a snack for the hike up Tysha, sun protection.
kg-0002.warn: The serpentine after Tatyr is steep and unpaved — slippery in rain and snow, not recommended for low cars. A significant part of the gorge is the eco-resort's private territory. In 2026 roadworks are under way on the Arashan–Chunkurchak road.
kg-0002.food: The Kara Bulak eco-resort cafe with national cuisine (triptokyrgyzstan), kumys (karabulak.kg), herbal teas in the bathhouse (sxodim: 1200–1800 som). Check the menu when booking.
kg-0002.reviews: 2GIS (Kara Bulak eco-resort): 4.8/5, 903 ratings, 269 reviews (as of 07.10.2026). TripAdvisor: a page “Gorge Kara Bulak (Tatyr)” exists, the rating was not read from the environment. Ostrovok: 18 reviews of the hotel. Pros — views, clean air, closeness to Bishkek, the bathhouse; cons — prices, the steep approach.
kg-0002.p.sum: Kara-Bulak is the “mountain weekend” closest to Bishkek: about an hour by car through Koi-Tash, Arashan and the Tatyr tract (the road to Chunkurchak is being paved in 2026), and the last climb is a steep dirt serpentine, a low car had better not try it. There is no public transport: your own car, a taxi or a jeep tour (Tripster “Above the clouds near Bishkek” — €173 per car, 7 h). The gorge is mostly occupied by the Kara Bulak eco-resort: horse rides 700 som/h, a cottage from 7400–8700 som for two; for a free walk, climb the neighboring Mount Tysha (6 km, +540 m).

kg-0003.name: Ala-Archa National Park
kg-0003.elev: From ~1500 m in the lower part of the gorge to 4895 m (Semenov-Tyan-Shansky Peak) — asiamixtravel 2026. Route landmarks: Ak-Sai waterfall ~2860 m, Ratsek hut ~3380 m (adventuresoflilnicki, 16.09.2026); the starting zone at the alpine camp is about 2150 m (calculated: waterfall 2860 m minus a 700 m ascent per hiking.kg).
kg-0003.short: Ala-Archa is a state nature park in a gorge of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too ~40 km south of Bishkek: spruce and juniper (archa) forests, glaciers and peaks up to 4895 m, and the country's most popular day treks.
kg-0003.desc: Ala-Archa is a mountain nature park in Alamudun district of Chuy region, in the gorge of the Ala-Archa River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too. Elevations range from ~1500 m to 4895 m; in the upper reaches are the Ak-Sai, Adygene and other glaciers, and on the slopes Schrenk spruce and the archa (juniper) that gave the gorge its name. Since 1 May 2025, by presidential order, cars with internal combustion engines have been banned from the park: guests leave their cars at the parking lot by the checkpoint (≈700 spaces), and from there ~80 electric buses carry them free of charge (about 12 km to the alpine camp and the start of the trails). On site are a restaurant, a cafe, cottages, a yurt village and gas grills (campfires and wood-fired barbecues are banned). The classic routes are the Ak-Sai waterfall (4.3 km, +700 m), the Ratsek hut (~3380 m) by the Ak-Sai glacier, and the Adygene gorge; in winter a ski base operates nearby.
kg-0003.guide: Ala-Archa is the best way to get into real high mountains in a single day from Bishkek: take bus No. 1 from Usubaliev Square and in an hour you're at the checkpoint. From there a free electric bus takes you to the alpine camp, where all the trails start. For a first visit the Ak-Sai waterfall is enough: 4.3 km and +700 m, about 2.5 hours up, with a view of the glacial cirque. If you're well acclimatized, continue to the Ratsek hut (~3380 m), but set out early: in the afternoon the weather in the mountains often turns bad. Campfires are banned, so bring a thermos and a snack or eat at the cafe by the alpine camp.
kg-0003.see: Walking sections along the Ala-Archa, the alpine camp, the Ak-Sai waterfall; the Ratsek hut is a separate, harder hike.
kg-0003.skip: You've already hiked similar gorges (Alamedin, Kegety) and are looking for solitude — it's crowded here on weekends. You want to drive your own car to the trails — since May 2025 only electric cars are allowed inside. You aren't ready for a 700+ m climb even for the “easy” waterfall.
kg-0003.diff: The park has no single difficulty level: a walk along the river, the trail to the waterfall and the climb to the Ratsek hut require different levels of preparation.
kg-0003.when: May to October is the main hiking season (asiamixtravel 2026); July to September is the best time for the Ratsek hut. In winter the park is open (electric buses run around the clock per hiking.kg), the trails are under snow and avalanche-prone, and there is skiing nearby.
kg-0003.hours: The park is open daily; electric buses run around the clock (hiking.kg), and Google and 2GIS give “24 hours”. The administration office is open 09:00–17:30, closed Sat–Sun (park website) — don't confuse this with the checkpoint's hours. Bus No. 1 runs 08:00–19:00. Checkpoint: +996 312 883 205.
kg-0003.daytime: Early morning: fewer people on the electric buses and on the trail, stable weather; in the mountains after noon there are more often clouds and thunderstorms. On weekends arrive at opening — there are queues for the electric bus (editorial).
kg-0003.how: Bus No. 1 (semi-express): old Usubaliev Square (corner of Abdymomunov and Erkindik) → park checkpoint, 08:00–19:00, every 20–30 min, 45–60 min on the way, 50 som cash / 40 som by card (economist.kg 05.2025; adventuresoflilnicki 09.2026; the route through the city was changed 02.09.2025). Taxi 40–60 min. Cars with internal combustion engines are left in the parking lot at the checkpoint, and from there a free electric bus runs ~12 km to the alpine camp.
kg-0003.needcar: To get there — yes, but the city bus No. 1 or a taxi is enough. Inside the park a private vehicle isn't needed: free electric buses run to the alpine camp and the start of the trails.
kg-0003.self: Yes: bus No. 1, a ticket at the checkpoint (by QR code), the free electric bus and the marked popular trails. For the Ratsek hut and the glaciers you need mountain experience; overnight stays in the hut are booked through Ak-Sai Travel.
kg-0003.roadtype: Paved road from Bishkek to the checkpoint (a mountain serpentine at the end); inside the park, a paved road for electric buses to the alpine camp; above that, mountain trails.
kg-0003.traveltime: From central Bishkek: bus No. 1 — 45–60 min, taxi — 40–60 min (~40 km; hiking.kg — 43 km, 1 h 10 min). From the alpine camp: Ak-Sai waterfall — 4.3 km, ~2.5 h up, +700 m (hiking.kg); Ratsek hut — 5.7 km one way (asiamixtravel), usually 3.5–4.5 h up (editorial).
kg-0003.stay: In the park: a hotel/cottages at the alpine camp, a yurt village, a restaurant (banks.kg 2025); the Ratsek hut (~3380 m, book via Ak-Sai Travel); nearby — ALTO Cabins, Manzara A-Frames, the Kashka-Suu ski base (adventuresoflilnicki 2026). 2026 prices are not given in the sources.
kg-0003.net: A mobile signal is usually available at the checkpoint and the alpine camp, but unstable higher up the trails; “don't count on reliable coverage in the mountains” (asiamixtravel 2026). The operator by section is not confirmed.
kg-0003.entry: Since 11.06.2026: adults 250 som, children 7–14 years 180 som, under 7 free; entry of a private electric car 880 som (24.kg 11.06.2026; asiamixtravel 2026; Reporter.kg). Before that (from 01.05.2025): 200/150 som, electric car 800 som (banks.kg, economist.kg). Ticket by QR code at the checkpoint. Parking at the checkpoint — 50 som (hiking.kg, undated). The tariff on the park's website (free on foot, cars 700 som) is outdated.
kg-0003.transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50 som cash / 40 som by card (2025–2026); taxi Bishkek — Ala-Archa 800–1500 som one way (vc.ru 2026); tours $30–80 per person; the electric bus inside the park — free.
kg-0003.bring: Trekking shoes, a windbreaker and a warm layer (elevations 2150–3400 m), 1.5–2 L of water and a snack (campfires are banned), sun protection, cash for the checkpoint (card terminals are unreliable — vc.ru), poles for the descent; for Ratsek — a headlamp and a down jacket.
kg-0003.warn: Since 1 May 2025 cars with internal combustion engines are banned — parking at the checkpoint and the electric bus. Campfires and wood-fired barbecues are banned (only gas grills in designated zones). Above the alpine camp the elevation is 2800–3400 m: altitude sickness, sudden changes of weather, avalanches and rockfalls out of season; turn back if visibility worsens (asiamixtravel). Tariffs change — check at the checkpoint +996 312 883 205.
kg-0003.food: A restaurant and a cafe with drinks and pastries at the alpine camp, a yurt village (banks.kg, 2025); mountain tea from a thermos and a picnic at the gas grills in designated zones are popular. Specific menus and prices are not confirmed.
kg-0003.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 3871 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). Yandex Maps and TripAdvisor (page d735790) have many reviews, the rating could not be captured in this environment; Tripster excursions to Ala-Archa have their own reviews. Pros: closeness to Bishkek, views, the electric buses and the cleanliness after the 2025 reform; cons: queues and crowds on weekends, rising entry prices, the ban on private cars.
kg-0003.p.sum: Easiest is bus No. 1 from the old Usubaliev Square (50 som cash / 40 by card, 08:00–19:00, every 20–30 min) or a taxi ≈1000 som to the checkpoint; cars with internal combustion engines are left in the large lot at the entrance. At the checkpoint a ticket is 250 som (children 7–14 — 180), then a free electric bus ~12 km to the alpine camp (every 10–15 min in the daytime). Since 19.02.2026 a Doppelmayr gondola has operated at the alpine camp (1 km, 2166→2494 m, 600 som round trip, cashless only, closed on Tuesdays). The classic day hike is the Ak-Sai waterfall (≈4 km, +450–700 m); for the prepared, the Ratsek hut (6.4 km, +1100 m, 3380 m; bunk 700–1400 som, book via Ak-Sai Travel). Set out early: on weekends there are queues for the electric bus.

kg-0004.name: Lake Tulpar-Kul
kg-0004.near: Sary-Mogol — about 25 km to the northwest (Visit Alay, Backpack Adventures); the base for transfers, horses and CBT. It can also be reached on horseback from Kashka-Suu (too.kg).
kg-0004.elev: About 3500 m (too.kg; at the yurt camp — sarymogol.com). Visit Alay's claim of “the same altitude as the base camp” is not accepted as an exact figure.
kg-0004.short: Tulpar-Kul is a high-mountain lake (~3500 m) in the Alay Valley, within easy reach of Lenin Peak base camp (7134 m), with yurt camps on its shore.
kg-0004.desc: Tulpar-Kul (Tulpar-Kol) is a fairly large, clear lake at about 3500 m at the foot of the Trans-Alay range, within easy reach of Achyk-Tash, the base camp of Lenin Peak (too.kg). In calm weather Lenin Peak (7134 m) is reflected in it. The lake is 25 km from the village of Sary-Mogol: about 45 min by car, 4–5 h on horseback or 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay). In summer, yurt camps run by CBT and private owners operate on the shore (from 1000 som a night with breakfast and dinner — Visit Alay). Day treks start from the lake to Travellers Pass (~4100 m) and to the tongue of the Lenin glacier, and multi-day ones to Yukhin Peak and Razdelnaya (Visit Alay, CBT). The area is in the border zone — a permit is needed (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.guide: Come to the lake early in the morning: in calm conditions Lenin Peak is reflected in the water, and after lunch the weather in the Trans-Alay often turns bad (TripAdvisor reviews). Spend the night in a yurt on the shore — from 1000 som with dinner and breakfast (Visit Alay) — and the next day climb Travellers Pass (~4100 m): 3 h up, 2 h down and a panorama of the entire Lenin wall. Don't forget your border permit — processing takes 10–20 days (Visit Alay). If you happen to be there on the third weekend of July, Sary-Mogol holds a festival of horse and yak games.
kg-0004.see: The reflection of Lenin Peak (7134 m) in the lake; the wall of the Trans-Alay range; Achyk-Tash base camp nearby; the trek to Travellers Pass (~4100 m) and to the Lenin glacier; marmots in the meadows (too.kg, Visit Alay, TripAdvisor).
kg-0004.skip: You can't get the border permit in time (10–20 days). You tolerate altitude poorly — spending a night at ~3500 m without acclimatization is hard. A view of Lenin Peak from the highway near Sary-Tash is enough for you.
kg-0004.diff: The lake itself is easy: you can drive right to the shore. Treks: Travellers Pass — 3 h up/2 h down to ~4100 m (Visit Alay); the trek to the glacier is ~14 km, with passes up to 3820 m, moderate (CBT); Yukhin Peak 2–3 days, Razdelnaya 4–5 days with equipment (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.when: June — September (CBT); the yurt camps operate only in summer, the trekking season runs from late May — June; from October the risk of snow grows (Backpack Adventures). The festival of horse and yak games is on the third weekend of July (Visit Alay). I Love KG: best time June–August, the yurt camps close in September.
kg-0004.hours: A natural area, accessible round the clock (TripAdvisor: 00:00–23:59); the yurt camps operate in the summer season (Backpack Adventures). A border permit is needed (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.daytime: Early morning — calm air and the reflection of Lenin Peak; the weather becomes unpredictable toward evening (TripAdvisor reviews).
kg-0004.how: From Osh to Sary-Mogol (~4 h, CBT): a marshrutka (minibus) from the Osh bus station at 14:00, arriving around 18:00, 300 som; a shared taxi from the new bus station 400 som/seat; a private car 3000 som (Backpack Adventures; the 14:00 departure is confirmed by the schedule of 27.08.2026 — I Love KG). The distance Osh — Sary-Mogol is ~220 km, about 4 h of pure driving (I Love KG). From Sary-Mogol it is 25 km to the yurt camp by the lake: ~45 min–1 h by car (Visit Alay, CBT), 4–5 h on horseback or 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.needcar: Yes: to Sary-Mogol — marshrutka (minibus)/taxi; from Sary-Mogol to the lake — a CBT/private car (1500 som per car), a horse, or an 8–9 h walk.
kg-0004.self: Yes, with a border permit: marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to Sary-Mogol, then a CBT car or on foot; you can pitch a tent for free in designated places (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.roadtype: Osh — Sary-Tash — Sary-Mogol — paved (the highway via Taldyk); from Sary-Mogol to the lake it is 25 km of dirt road across the Alay Valley with fords, passable for cars/SUVs in ~45 min (Visit Alay; surface type — editorial, based on descriptions).
kg-0004.traveltime: Osh → Sary-Mogol ~4 h (CBT; marshrutka 14:00–18:00); Sary-Mogol → lake ~45 min–1 h by car (Visit Alay, CBT), 4–5 h on horseback, 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
kg-0004.stay: Yurt camps on the shore: from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay; Backpack Adventures); the CBT Sary-Mogol yurt camp “Tulpor-Kul” — warm yurts by the shore, a stove, lighting, a shared toilet and shower outside the yurts (CBT, sarymogol.com); one TripAdvisor review advises choosing an alternative to the CBT camp. Tents — free in designated places. In Sary-Mogol — guesthouses at $15–20 with breakfast (Backpack Adventures). Prices according to reports: CBT camp 1000 som ($15) per bed with dinner and breakfast (Nature's Off Grid Treasures) / $30 with three meals (The Gone Goat); a tent pitch on the camp grounds $8–10; dinner 300 som, breakfast 250 som.
kg-0004.net: Specific Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage at the lake is not confirmed in 2025–2026 sources. The Lenin Peak base camps (Achyk-Tash, ~10 km) have “3G WiFi” (The Gone Goat); in Sary-Mogol Wi-Fi is unreliable, and a local SIM is advised (Backpack Adventures). Expect no signal at the lake itself.
kg-0004.entry: There is no entrance ticket. Border permit: ≈$35–40 via Visit Alay (FAQ 07.2026) or 2054 som (Nature's Off Grid Treasures), 1–3 weeks to process; for the lake itself it may formally not be required (see the warning).
kg-0004.transfer: Osh → Sary-Mogol: marshrutka (minibus) 300 som, shared taxi 400 som/seat, private car 3000 som; Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul 1500 som per car one way (Backpack Adventures, Visit Alay; 2023–2025 data, check). An alternative from The Gone Goat's report: a shared taxi Osh → Sary-Mogol 500 som/seat (3 h), a driver to Tulpar-Kul 500–800 som.
kg-0004.bring: Warm clothes and a down jacket (nights at 3500 m are cold even in summer), sun protection and sunglasses, your passport and border permit, cash in som (an ATM in Sary-Mogol was open in 2023 — economist.kg), trekking shoes, a first-aid kit including altitude-sickness remedies.
kg-0004.warn: Border permit: Visit Alay (FAQ, updated 12.07.2026) — a permit is mandatory for Lenin Peak base camp; people often go to Tulpar-Kul without it, but Visit Alay strongly advises getting one (≈$35–40, 1–2 weeks) because of military patrols. Nature's Off Grid Treasures — no permit is needed for Tulpar-Kul and Travellers Pass, but military checks are possible (permit 2054 som, 10–20 days); The Gone Goat — no checks were encountered. I Love KG (2026) — not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, needed for Achyk-Tash. Conclusion: formally the lake is on the edge of the border zone — it is safer to get a permit. Altitude ~3500 m: risk of altitude sickness. The weather changes toward evening (TripAdvisor). Fords on the way from Sary-Mogol can be deep after rain (editorial).
kg-0004.food: Dinner and breakfast at the yurt camp (included in the 1000 som — Visit Alay): Kyrgyz home cooking, kumis from shepherds in summer; in Sary-Mogol — meals at guesthouses (editorial).
kg-0004.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 38 ratings (03.10.2026); TripAdvisor: 4.7/5, 9 reviews, no. 1 of 3 in Sary-Mogol (reviews 07.2018–07.2025). Pros: views of Lenin Peak, treks of varying difficulty, yurts on the shore, marmots; cons: unpredictable weather after lunch, uneven quality of the camps (one review against the CBT camp).
kg-0004.p.sum: From Osh take a marshrutka (minibus) or shared taxi to Sary-Mogol (220 km, 4–5 h; marshrutka at 14:00 from the New Bus Station, 300 som), spend the night in a guesthouse, and in the morning take a CBT car to the lake (23–25 km, ~45 min–1 h, 1500–2000 som per car) or ride on horseback for 4–5 h. On the shore are yurt camps run by CBT, Buaisha and others (1000–2000 som with dinner and breakfast; $30 with three meals), season ~late June — early September. The main walk is Travellers Pass (4150 m, 16 km round trip, 5–8 h). A permit is formally needed for Achyk-Tash; people often go to the lake without one, but it is safer to get it.

People often go to Tulpar-Kul itself without a permit, and there is no checkpoint (The Gone Goat 2024, Beyond Wild Places), but military checks are possible — it is safer to get one. kg-0007.name: Chychkan Gorge
kg-0007.near: There are no villages inside the gorge — only roadside cafés, trout farms and a tourist base. The nearest town is Toktogul (where the gorge opens to the reservoir, ~30–50 km along the highway — not specified); according to OSM, Mazar-Suu is ~23 km in a straight line from the catalogue point.
kg-0007.elev: The gorge's average elevation is about 2,200 m; small lakes on the slopes are at about 3,000 m (too.kg). The cliffs rise roughly 1,000 m above the river (central-asia.live).
kg-0007.short: Chychkan is about 30 km of a picturesque wooded gorge of the river of the same name on the Bishkek — Osh highway between the Ala-Bel Pass and the Toktogul Reservoir: spruce trees, meadows, honey, trout farms and roadside cafés.
kg-0007.desc: Chychkan Gorge stretches for about 30 km along the Chychkan River in the northern part of the Fergana Range (central-asia.live) — from the Ala-Bel Pass south to the Toktogul Reservoir, into which the turbulent river flows (too.kg). The average elevation is about 2,200 m; the slopes are covered with Tian Shan spruce, flowers and berry bushes, and higher up there are small lakes at ~3,000 m. The name translates as “mouse” — because of the many field mice in burrows on the slopes (too.kg). The gorge is known for fragrant honey and medicinal herbs; along the highway there are cafés, trout farms, guesthouses and the Chychkan tourist base (~km 240 of the Bishkek — Osh highway). Part of the territory is the Chychkan state nature reserve (zakaznik). There is almost no mobile coverage in the gorge (too.kg).
kg-0007.guide: Chychkan is the best stop on the long Bishkek — Osh drive: after the bare slopes of Suusamyr and Ala-Bel the road plunges into a spruce forest alongside a turbulent river. Stop for a trout lunch at one of the roadside farms and buy local honey — the gorge is famous for it. If you have a couple of hours, climb up the side valleys — small lakes hide at around 3,000 m. Don't drink water from the river — take it from springs or at a café. There is no mobile coverage, so tell your family you'll be out of touch for a couple of hours.
kg-0007.see: The Chychkan River and spruce slopes along the highway; side valleys (for example, the Itagar River) and high-mountain lakes (~3,000 m); apiaries and honey sales; trout farms; waterfalls, caves and petroglyphs in the surrounding area (central-asia.live — no specific locations); the Ala-Bel Pass to the north and the Toktogul Reservoir to the south.
kg-0007.skip: You're flying Bishkek — Osh and not driving the highway — there's no point in coming here specifically for 5–6 hours. You're looking for secluded places — the highway has heavy traffic. You need mobile coverage — there is almost none here.
kg-0007.diff: Easy: stops by the highway, short walks. Hikes along the side valleys to lakes at ~3,000 m are medium (editorial; too.kg).
kg-0007.when: May–October: the gorge is green and the roadside spots are open (avtoprokat.kg). In winter the highway is passable, but the neighbouring passes (Ala-Bel, Too-Ashuu) are slippery and avalanche-prone.
kg-0007.hours: Open 24 hours (a stretch of state highway); cafés and trout farms mostly operate in the warm season (avtoprokat.kg). The nature reserve regime follows protected-area rules.
kg-0007.daytime: By day — for lunch and a walk; plan to cross the highway's mountain passes in daylight (editorial).
kg-0007.how: Along the Bishkek — Osh highway (EM-02): from Bishkek via the Too-Ashuu tunnel, Suusamyr and the Ala-Bel Pass — about 5–6 h (avtoprokat.kg); the Chychkan tourist base is at ~km 240 of the highway (TripAdvisor). Fee for passing through the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels: 50 som for cars with Kyrgyz plates / 200 som for foreign ones (since 01.01.2024). From Osh/Jalal-Abad — north via Tash-Kumyr and Toktogul.
kg-0007.needcar: Yes: the gorge is a stretch of the intercity highway. Your own car, a taxi or a seat in a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi Bishkek — Toktogul/Osh (ask to be dropped off in the gorge).
kg-0007.self: Yes: the stops are right by the highway, no permits needed. For hikes into the side valleys — an offline map and a supply of water.
kg-0007.roadtype: A paved intercity Bishkek — Osh highway along the bottom of the gorge; a 4WD car is not required on the main highway in good weather (avtoprokat.kg). Side turn-offs are dirt.
kg-0007.traveltime: From Bishkek — 5–6 h by car (avtoprokat.kg); to Toktogul by marshrutka — longer, with stops. From Osh — roughly 6–7 h (editorial, not confirmed).
kg-0007.stay:
• Chychkan tourist base/hotel (~km 240 of the Bishkek — Osh highway): $51–58 for a standard room, breakfast; TripAdvisor 3.1/5, 10 reviews (2019–05.2026) — people praise the nature and the staff, and criticize the plumbing, dampness and restaurant prices.
• Oson motel — standard rooms and suites, hot water, meals (C.A.T. catalogue, +996 704 663 664; price not confirmed).
• Several guesthouses and many places to camp (too.kg).
kg-0007.net: There is no mobile coverage in the gorge or it is limited (too.kg; avtoprokat.kg). Wi-Fi — in some hotels (not confirmed).
kg-0007.entry: Free: a stretch of highway. You only pay the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnel fee (50/200 som since 01.01.2024), which is unrelated to the gorge.
kg-0007.transfer: Bishkek → Toktogul: marshrutka 400 som, shared taxi 600–800 som/person, private taxi 3,200–5,600 som (toktogulvisit; publication year not given).
kg-0007.bring: Cash for honey and trout; a warm sweater (2,200 m, cool in the evening); water (drinking river water is not recommended — too.kg); mosquito/tick repellent for walks in the forest (editorial).
kg-0007.warn: Do not drink water from the Chychkan River — only from springs or bought. No mobile coverage. Heavy truck traffic — park only on shoulders and pull-outs. In winter and spring avalanches are possible on the Bishkek — Osh highway (video “An avalanche came down on the Bishkek-Osh road”), and the passes are slippery. Trout prices in restaurants can be high (TripAdvisor review: 2,200 som/kg).
kg-0007.food: Fresh trout from local farms; mountain honey and herbal tea from the gorge's herbs (too.kg, avtoprokat.kg). The Oson motel café and the Chychkan tourist base restaurant.
kg-0007.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 36 ratings (03.10.2026, the gorge listing). TripAdvisor (Chychkan hotel): 3.1/5, 10 reviews. Pros: nature, forest, river, trout. Cons: service in the hotels, no mobile coverage.
kg-0007.p.sum: Chychkan is a picturesque stretch of the Bishkek — Osh highway between the Ala-Bel Pass and Toktogul: people pass through on the way south and stop for a trout lunch, honey and kumys, and if they wish stay overnight at the Chychkan tourist base (km 240, ~$40–58). By car from Bishkek it is 5–6 h (tunnel fee 50/200 som); without a car — a marshrutka/shared taxi Bishkek — Toktogul or Bishkek — Osh with a stop by arrangement. There is almost no mobile coverage in the gorge.
