kg-0009.name: Lake Sary-Chelek
kg-0009.near: Arkyt is a village at the foot of the nature reserve (~200 families) and the lodging base; the shore of the main lake is ~15 km away along the reserve road (central-asia.guide, journalofnomads, govori.tv).
kg-0009.elev: 1878 m is the lake level (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, central-asia.guide). Conifer forests start at ~2100 m (govori.tv).
kg-0009.short: Sary-Chelek is a turquoise mountain lake at 1878 m with a depth of up to 234 m, in the UNESCO Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve in the Chatkal Range, surrounded by spruce and walnut forests; the reserve has seven lakes in all.
kg-0009.desc: Sary-Chelek is the largest lake of the state biosphere reserve of the same name (part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves) in the Chatkal Range of the Western Tian Shan. The lake is about 6.2 km long, up to 2.6 km wide and up to 234 m deep, at an elevation of 1878 m (central-asia.guide). The reserve covers 23,868 ha and has seven lakes: Sary-Chelek, Kyla-Kol, Choichok-Kol, Bakaly-Kol, Aram-Kol, Iyri-Kol and Tuyuk-Kol (govori.tv). The shores are covered with spruce, fir, walnut and apple forests. The entrance is from the village of Arkyt through the reserve checkpoint, then ~15 km along a serpentine road to the parking lot at the main lake; at the shore there is a toilet, bins, covered gazebos and tent areas (central-asia.guide). From here a trail leads to the system of small lakes and a panoramic viewpoint (7.1 km, ~3 h 15 min, 760 m of ascent — hiking.kg). An automated checkpoint is planned for installation in 2026 (time.kg, 08.06.2026).
kg-0009.guide: Sary-Chelek is the main jewel of western Kyrgyzstan: turquoise water up to 234 m deep framed by spruces and walnut groves. Spend the night in Arkyt and drive to the lake early in the morning, while the surface is mirror-calm and there are few tourists. Don't stop at the parking lot: the trail to the small lakes and the panorama (about 7 km and 3 hours) opens up a view of the chain of lakes from above. Swimming, campfires and picking plants are not allowed in the reserve — it is a strictly protected area. Bring cash in som: the fee is taken at the barrier, and the rates on the spot may differ from what blogs say.
kg-0009.see: The main lake Sary-Chelek (turquoise water, 234 m deep); the chain of small lakes (Iyri-Kol, Kyla-Kol, Choichok-Kol, Bakaly-Kol, Aram-Kol, Tuyuk-Kol); the panorama above the lakes (7.1 km trail); spruce and walnut forests; wild apple trees (govori.tv, hiking.kg).
kg-0009.skip: You have less than 3–4 days for the west of the country: from Bishkek it is ~540 km and ~11 h one way (hiking.kg). You want to swim and grill shashlik by the water — this is forbidden in the reserve. You are going before mid-May — the road may be closed by snow.
kg-0009.diff: Visiting the main lake is easy (drive to the parking lot at the shore). The trail to the small lakes and the panorama is 7.1 km, 3 h 15 min, 760 m of ascent, difficulty 4/5 according to hiking.kg. On foot from the gate to the lake it is 15 km with ~600 m of ascent (zewanderingfrogs).
kg-0009.when: Mid-May to September/early October; until mid-May the road may be closed by snow (central-asia.guide). May to October is suitable for hiking and horse riding (journalofnomads). In October nights are below freezing (TripAdvisor).
kg-0009.hours: Entry is through the reserve checkpoint (barrier) at the northern exit of Arkyt; the checkpoint's opening hours are not officially published. An automated checkpoint is planned for 2026 (time.kg, 08.06.2026). Out of season, entry is limited by the weather.
kg-0009.daytime: Early morning means a mirror-calm surface, soft light and fewer people; leave on the serpentine road back while it is still light (editorial).
kg-0009.how: From Bishkek, take the Bishkek–Osh highway to Tash-Kumyr, then via Kara-Jygach/Aksy to Arkyt (~540 km, ~11 h — hiking.kg; TripAdvisor — ~600 km, 8–9 h). From Jalal-Abad it is ~210 km, ~4.5 h (govori.tv); from Osh ~300 km. From Arkyt, go through the northern checkpoint ~15 km along the serpentine road to the parking lot at the main lake. Tunnel toll on the Bishkek–Osh highway: 50 som (KG plates) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024. From Tashkent it is ~400 km via the Uchkurgan checkpoint (weproject, 2026).
kg-0009.needcar: Yes: a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to Arkyt and a car (taxi) from Arkyt to the lake, or 15 km on foot.
kg-0009.self: Yes: no permits are needed — the fee is taken at the barrier (eurasia.travel forum, 09.2025). Independently: marshrutka (minibus) to Arkyt + taxi/on foot; the trails to the small lakes are easy to follow (hiking.kg).
kg-0009.roadtype: Paved road to Tash-Kumyr; then regional roads to Arkyt (unpaved in the village, govori.tv); from the checkpoint, a dirt service road with serpentines ~15 km long leads to the parking lot (zewanderingfrogs, hiking.kg). In August 2025 the hiking.kg author noted road repairs — current passability is not confirmed. On YouTube there is a video “the road to Sary-Chelek, driving a sedan” — an ordinary car can get through in dry weather.
kg-0009.traveltime: Bishkek to Sary-Chelek: ~540 km / 11 h (hiking.kg); Jalal-Abad to Arkyt: 210 km / ~4.5 h (govori.tv) or ~6 h by marshrutka (minibus); Osh to Arkyt: 7–8 h by marshrutka (minibus). Arkyt to the lake: 15 km, ~40–60 min by car (editorial). The trail to the small lakes takes 3 h 15 min.
kg-0009.stay: Guesthouses and CBT homestays in Arkyt: 500–1000 som per person per night, meals ~300 som (journalofnomads, 2026); Kamilla Homestay — 400 som for two + 100 som per meal (zewanderingfrogs, 2018 — outdated). Camping by the lake — 500 som per tent per night (journalofnomads 2026; adventuresoflilnicki 2025). In July–August book in advance.
kg-0009.net: According to hiking.kg (2025), there is no coverage across much of the area; Arkyt has one shop and minimal services (zewanderingfrogs). Coverage by specific operators is not confirmed.
kg-0009.entry: Sources disagree: 400 som for foreigners and 100 som for Kyrgyz citizens + 150 som per car (journalofnomads, updated 03.04.2026; central-asia.guide — 400 som); 200 som per person (adventuresoflilnicki, late 2025); 150 som per passenger + 150 som per car (eurasia.travel forum, 29.09.2025); older data — car 100, minibus 150, bus 200 som (govori.tv). Camping — 500 som per tent. Pay in cash at the checkpoint barrier at the northern exit of Arkyt; the official 2026 rate was not found.
kg-0009.transfer: Arkyt to the lake: 150 som per person shared, or 1500 som per car round trip (journalofnomads 2026); marshrutka (minibus) Jalal-Abad to Arkyt 450 som, Osh to Arkyt ~600 som; Bishkek to Tash-Kumyr ~800 som per seat.
kg-0009.bring: Cash in som (entry, taxi, guesthouse); warm clothes (autumn nights are below freezing); trekking shoes; food and water for the day (there are no cafes in the reserve — editorial); a rain jacket; a bag for rubbish; a tent if camping (500 som/night).
kg-0009.warn: Strict nature reserve: hunting, picking plants, flowers and fruit, swimming and littering are prohibited; problems with campfires and trampling have been noted (govori.tv; Kaktus). Entry rates differ between sources — check at the checkpoint and ask for a receipt. The road may be closed by snow until mid-May; road repairs were recorded in August 2025 (hiking.kg). There is almost no mobile signal.
kg-0009.food: Home-cooked Kyrgyz food in Arkyt guesthouses (~300 som per meal, journalofnomads 2026); buy local nuts and apples from residents outside the reserve (picking is forbidden inside the reserve).
kg-0009.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 476 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Sary Chelek Biosphere Reserve”: 4.8/5, 29 reviews, No. 1 of 17 in Jalal-Abad Region. Pros: crystal-clear water, forests, seven lakes, few crowds. Cons: remoteness and a long road, little accommodation, cold autumn nights; one negative review (07.2025) about service and lack of amenities.
kg-0009.p.sum: The base for Sary-Chelek is the village of Arkyt: one daily marshrutka (minibus) goes there from Osh (07:30, 600 som) and Jalal-Abad (09:00, 450 som); from Bishkek take a shared taxi to Tash-Kumyr (~800 som) and change to the midday marshrutka (minibus) to Arkyt (250 som). Stay 2–3 nights in an Arkyt guesthouse (500–1000 som per person; Booking: Sabira, Kyzyl Alma, Aida — $24–40); the main lake is 15–17 km away by service road — a taxi costs 1500 som round trip or 150 som per seat. Entry for foreigners is 400 som (other sources say 150–200), car 150 som, in cash at the checkpoint. The main day route is the trail past 6 of the 7 lakes (11 km, ~4 h); swimming is not allowed.

kg-0009.p.season: May–June: greenery, rain, mud on the dirt road. July–September: warm, up to +25 °C, peak visitor season (book accommodation in advance in July–August), mosquitoes by the water. October: autumn colors of the walnut and fruit forests. November–April: access is limited by the weather, check with CBT Jalal-Abad.
kg-0009.p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Osh–Arkyt 600×2 + taxi to the lake ~300–750 + entry 400 + 2 nights in a guesthouse with dinner ~2600 ≈ 5000–5500 som/person for 3 days
kg-0009.p.budget.comfort: Private taxi Osh–Arkyt 5000–6000 som/car one way + guesthouse $30–40 + boat 1000 som/h, or a 6-day horse tour $372–779
kg-0009.p.permits: No border-zone permit is needed. At the checkpoint barrier at the northern exit of Arkyt you pay in cash (ask for a receipt): foreigners 400 som, Kyrgyz citizens 100 som, car 150 som (journalofnomads 04.2026); other reports say 150–200 som per person (forum 09.2025, adventuresoflilnicki 2025). Camping 500 som/tent. On foot through the checkpoint — only 07:00–14:00. Since 10.02.2026 unified payment rules for protected areas apply (students/schoolchildren −50%); an automated checkpoint is declared in the 2026 program, and as of 28.07.2026 it has been installed in other parks. A real-life example: on 31.05.2026 a couple in their own car paid 525 som for two people and the vehicle; there are two registration points at the entrance (travelwithkevinandruth, 06.2026).
kg-0009.p.access: With children — yes (short walks near the parking lot, but the serpentine road is hard on those prone to motion sickness). For older people — at the lake and at the viewpoint. Strollers — only near the parking lot. Dogs — it is a nature reserve, not advisable.

kg-0010.name: Cholpon-Ata Rock Gallery
kg-0010.near: Cholpon-Ata: ≈3 km from the town center, in the foothills above the airfield (runway); up to an hour on foot from the center.
kg-0010.elev: ≈1700–1750 m (estimate: Cholpon-Ata by the lake is ≈1620 m, the petroglyph field is on a gentle foothill slope above the town; the exact elevation of the entrance is not published in the sources)
kg-0010.short: A field of boulders of ≈42 ha on the slope above Cholpon-Ata with hundreds of petroglyphs from the Bronze Age to the Middle Ages (2nd millennium BC to the 4th century AD and later): ibexes, deer, snow leopards, hunting scenes. Three marked routes from 800 m to 3 km.
kg-0010.desc: The open-air petroglyph museum occupies about 42 hectares of stony foothills between the Kungey Ala-Too range and the lake. Thousands of boulders brought by a glacier are carved with images of mountain ibexes (the majority: in one sample of 409 petroglyphs there were 285 ibexes), deer, camels, snow leopards, and scenes of hunting, battles and festivals. The oldest date to the 1st–2nd millennium BC (Saka-Wusun period), some to the Turkic era and the Middle Ages; the site has no single date. Besides the drawings, the area has stone circles, burial mounds, balbals and remains of walls. Three routes have been laid out: 800 m (30–40 min, with blue markers — the best developed), 1.5 km (≈1.5 h) and 3 km (≈2 h); at the entrance is the main stone with the most striking drawings. There are signs in three languages, but few; you have to look for some of the petroglyphs yourself. There is no shade or water on the site, and cattle roam the field. A UNESCO nomination was being prepared; the site is not on the list. From the upper part of the field there is a panorama of Issyk-Kul and Terskey Ala-Too.
kg-0010.guide: Start with the big stone by the ticket window — it has the clearest snow leopards and ibexes — and then follow the blue flags of the short loop: in 40 minutes you will see the main things, and the rest of the field is for those who like hunting for drawings like treasure. Look at the boulders from the south, sun-baked side: the ancient masters chose the dark “desert varnish”, on which light lines show best, which is why the drawings often face the lake. Come in the morning or toward evening — slanting light pulls shadows out of the carved lines, while at noon the petroglyphs “disappear”. You can pay the caretaker for a tour: without the story the field looks like a scatter of stones, with it — like a gallery. Don't step on the stones with drawings and don't trace them — they are protected by nothing but your care.
kg-0010.see: The main stone at the entrance with snow leopards and ibexes; petroglyphs with hunting scenes, deer, camels; stone circles and burial mounds, balbals; a panorama of Issyk-Kul from the upper part of the field; routes of 800 m / 1.5 km / 3 km.
kg-0010.skip: If you expect a museum with display cases and air conditioning — this is a bare field of stones with no shade. If you have already seen Saimaluu-Tash or Cholpon-Ata — it is not the main interest: there are not many drawings relative to the area, and many people don't find them without a guide. If the heat is above 30° and you have no hat — better to postpone until evening.
kg-0010.diff: Easy: a walk on an uneven stony slope, routes of 0.8–3 km, small ascent. Closed shoes are needed.
kg-0010.when: April to October; in summer only in the morning/evening because of the heat with no shade; accessible in winter, but the stones are slippery after snow/rain. Crowds peak in July–August and on the days of the Nomad Games.
kg-0010.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): daily 08:00–20:00; 2GIS: daily with no days off; eurasia.travel: from 8:00. In practice — daylight hours; out of season the ticket booth may be closed, the field is open.
kg-0010.daytime: Early morning or 2 hours before sunset — slanting light brings out the lines of the petroglyphs, and there is no heat. Midday is the worst time (flat light, scorching).
kg-0010.how: From Bishkek: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek → Cholpon-Ata from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1; the Western station has been closed since 10.2024), 400–450 som, ≈3–3.5 h (24.kg, 2024); GoBus 580 som (2024); a taxi 700–1000 som/person. In Cholpon-Ata: from the center 3 km north, toward the airfield — by taxi (Yandex Go/local) or on foot up to 1 h; there are no signs, ask for directions. There is parking at the entrance.
kg-0010.needcar: No: from the center of Cholpon-Ata you can walk (3 km, up to an hour) or take a taxi in a few minutes. You only need a car if you are not in Cholpon-Ata.
kg-0010.self: Yes, fully: the short route is marked with blue signs; to “read” the drawings, a guide or the I Love KG description is useful.
kg-0010.roadtype: Paved road through the town to the outskirts, the last few hundred meters are dirt/gravel to the parking area (I Love KG); inside — trails on a stony slope, uneven ground.
kg-0010.traveltime: From the center of Cholpon-Ata 5–10 min by taxi, 40–60 min on foot; from Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h. A visit takes: 30–40 min (short loop) to 2–3 h (full), up to midday per reviews.
kg-0010.stay: In Cholpon-Ata: private rooms 600–1500 som/night, guesthouses up to 3000 som at peak (July–August), mid-range hotels $15–20/person, premium resorts $184–528/night (24.kg, 2024). Names: Ak Bermet, Karven Four Seasons, Tri Korony (Three Crowns), Akun, Goluboy Issyk-Kul (Blue Issyk-Kul) (weproject 2024).
kg-0010.net: Cholpon-Ata is a town, with Beeline/O!/MegaCom 4G coverage; in April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Cholpon-Ata (economist.kg). On the field itself, 3 km from the center, a signal is expected, but there are no separate measurements.
kg-0010.entry: According to Yandex Maps reviews (2024–2026): 80 som, in some reviews 100 som per person; 2GIS — “entry is paid”; in 2015 — 40–50 som (ZigZag on Earth). The caretaker's tour is separate, by arrangement. The museum's official rate is not published.
kg-0010.transfer: A taxi within Cholpon-Ata to the museum — roughly 100–200 som (estimated from city rates, not confirmed by a price list); marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek 400–450 som, GoBus 580 (2024). Sightseeing excursions with a stop here — see Tripster/Sputnik8, prices on request.
kg-0010.bring: Water, a hat, sunscreen, closed shoes for uneven stones, cash in som (ticket booth and guide), a camera with a zoom — the drawings are small.
kg-0010.warn: There is no shade or water — scorching in summer. The petroglyphs are protected by nothing: don't step on the stones, trace or “refresh” the lines. Cattle roam the field — watch your step. There is construction nearby, and some signs are damaged (reviews 2025–2026). The ticket booth is partly informal: ask for a receipt.
kg-0010.food: There is nothing on site. In Cholpon-Ata there are cafes and canteens: a canteen from ≈1000 som for three meals, an average bill in a cafe of ≈1400 som for a snack, 2700 for dinner (24.kg 2024); local fish (chebak, farmed trout), lagman, samsa, ashlan-fu.
kg-0010.reviews: Google Maps: 4.2/5, 886 ratings (03.10.2026). Yandex Maps: 4.6/5, 104 reviews, 81% positive (07.10.2026). 2GIS: 4.7/5, 23 ratings (07.10.2026). Pros: views of the lake and mountains, the antiquity, the large area, a friendly caretaker, souvenirs. Cons: few signs and little information, “lots of stones — few drawings”, heat, cattle and dirt, construction nearby, poor upkeep.
kg-0010.p.sum: The site is within the town limits of Cholpon-Ata: from the center 20–40 minutes on foot uphill (north, toward the airfield) or 5–10 minutes by taxi/Yandex Go; there is parking at the entrance. To Cholpon-Ata itself from Bishkek — a marshrutka (minibus) from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1, 400–600 som, 3.5–5 h) or the summer train to Balykchy + a marshrutka (minibus). Come early in the morning or 2 hours before sunset, take water and a hat; it is convenient to combine with Rukh Ordo in one day.

kg-0011.name: Manas Gumbez
kg-0011.full: Manas Gumbez (mausoleum in the Manas Ordo historical and cultural complex)
kg-0011.near: Tash-Aryk — ~1 km (OSM); the village has guesthouses, shops and cafés (too.kg). The town of Talas is 13–15 km to the west (Nomad's Land, too.kg; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com gives 22 km).
kg-0011.short: A 14th-century brick mausoleum (around 1334) near Tash-Aryk village outside Talas — the main monument of the Manas Ordo complex, linked to the epic about the hero Manas; after a two-year reconstruction the complex reopened on 11.09.2026.
kg-0011.desc: Manas Gumbez is a medieval mausoleum of fired brick with carved clay cladding, Karakhanid ornaments and an Arabic inscription; it dates from the 14th century, around 1334 (Nomad's Land, 2GIS). According to the inscription the tomb belonged to the daughter of a ruler of the Chagatai ulus (Kenizek Khatun), but popular tradition regards it as the grave of Manas: allegedly the hero's wife Kanykey ordered a woman's name to be written so that enemies would not desecrate the burial (Nomad's Land). In Soviet times the Manas Ordo complex (about 225 ha) was created around the mausoleum: an epic museum, a lapidarium with petroglyphs, balbals and stones with Yenisei runic writing, an avenue of sculptures of the epic's heroes, a yurt for performances of the epic by manaschi (epic reciters), and Karool-Debe hill with a view of the valley (too.kg; visitsilkroad.org; economist.kg). From 01.08.2025 the complex was closed for its first reconstruction in 30 years (24.kg); on 11.09.2026 the president opened the renovated Manas Ordo: a new congress hall, an administrative building, a pilgrims' house, and the museum expanded from 700 to 1,090 m²; the cost of the work was 1.4 billion som (economist.kg, for.kg).
kg-0011.guide: The main intrigue of the Gumbez is the inscription: the wall says that the daughter of a Chagatai emir is buried here, while legend insists this is a ruse by Kanykey, who hid Manas's grave from his enemies. Take a close look at the carved terracotta of the facade — it is one of the best examples of medieval brick architecture in the country. After the mausoleum, look into the renovated epic museum and the lapidarium with balbals and runic stones, and then climb Karool-Debe hill — from there you can see the whole Talas Valley. The complex has only just reopened after reconstruction, so check opening hours and ticket prices by phone or in Talas before you go.
kg-0011.see: The Manas Gumbez mausoleum (14th century) with carved terracotta and an inscription; the renovated Manas epic museum (1,090 m²); the lapidarium — petroglyphs, stone tools, balbals, 13 stones with Yenisei runic writing; an avenue of sculptures of the epic's heroes; a yurt for performances of the epic; Karool-Debe hill with a view of the valley; Saka and Wusun burial mounds (too.kg; visitsilkroad.org; economist.kg 2026).
kg-0011.skip: You aren't interested in history and the epic — there is not much natural scenery here, it is above all a memorial. You aren't going to the Talas region — from Bishkek it is 5–6 hours one way.
kg-0011.diff: Easy: a paved road to the complex, a walk through the park; the climb up Karool-Debe is a short walk (editorial).
kg-0011.when: April–October; the complex operates year-round (before the reconstruction). On national holidays and event days (the congress hall, Independence Day on 31 August) restrictions and crowds are possible (editorial).
kg-0011.hours: The complex reopened after reconstruction on 11.09.2026 (economist.kg, for.kg). On Google Maps as of 03.10.2026 it still showed “temporarily closed” — probably not updated. Opening hours after the reopening have not been published — check before you go.
kg-0011.daytime: Morning or the second half of the day: soft light on the brickwork and views from Karool-Debe; in summer it is hot in the Talas Valley by day (editorial).
kg-0011.how: From Bishkek to Talas: marshrutkas (minibuses) from the Ak-Kula hippodrome in western Bishkek (the Western bus station has been closed since 10.2024) (~350 som, 5.5–6 h) or a shared taxi from ~650 som/seat (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com; Wikivoyage — data up to 2025), via the Otmok Pass. From Talas — 15 km east to Tash-Aryk on a good paved road; taxis and marshrutkas run daily from Talas bus station/bazaar (visitsilkroad.org; Wikivoyage — 20 som, an outdated price). By your own car: Bishkek — Sosnovka — Too-Ashuu tunnel — Suusamyr — Otmok Pass — Talas (~300 km); at the Sosnovka post a fee for the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels is charged: 50 som (Kyrgyz plates) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024.
kg-0011.needcar: Yes: to Talas and from Talas to the complex (marshrutka, taxi). On site — on foot.
kg-0011.self: Yes: the complex is accessible without a guide; museum tours are with the complex's guide (digital equipment for tours was installed during the reconstruction, economist.kg).
kg-0011.roadtype: Paved: a good road from Talas to the complex (too.kg); Bishkek — Talas — paved through the Too-Ashuu and Otmok passes.
kg-0011.traveltime: Bishkek — Talas ~5.5–6 h (marshrutka); Talas — Manas Ordo ~20 min by car (15 km, estimate).
kg-0011.stay: Guesthouses in Tash-Aryk (too.kg; names not found); in Talas — guesthouses $10–30/night, 2–3* hotels from $30 (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com); Hotel Talant — 300–400 som/person (Wikivoyage, an outdated price). A pilgrims' house and guest houses have been built on the complex's grounds (24.kg, economist.kg) — the arrangements for accommodating tourists are not confirmed.
kg-0011.net: There is mobile coverage (visitsilkroad.org); operators not specified.
kg-0011.entry: Not confirmed after the reconstruction (reopened 11.09.2026). Before the reconstruction: foreigners 200 som, Kyrgyz citizens 30 som (Wikivoyage, data up to 2025). The new rate for the Manas Ordo complex has not been published in official announcements — check on site.
kg-0011.transfer: GoBus Bishkek — Talas 500 som (06.2025, via Kazakhstan); marshrutka Bishkek — Talas ~350 som; shared taxi from ~650 som/seat (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com, year not given); Talas — Manas Ordo — marshrutka 20 som (Wikivoyage up to 2025, outdated), taxi — by arrangement.
kg-0011.bring: A hat and water (open area, hot in summer), modest clothing for visiting the mausoleum (a holy place for pilgrims), cash for tickets.
kg-0011.warn: The complex reopened after reconstruction on 11.09.2026, but opening hours and rates after the reopening have not been published; on Google Maps (03.10.2026) it still shows “temporarily closed” — call ahead. This is a place of pilgrimage — behave respectfully and dress modestly. During state events access may be restricted.
kg-0011.food: Talas beans are the valley's main product; beshbarmak and boorsoki in the cafés of Tash-Aryk and Talas (typical of the region; specific eateries have not been verified).
kg-0011.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8 from 867 ratings (listed as “Kumbez Manasa”, catalogue check 10.2026). 2GIS: 3.3 from 21 ratings (07.10.2026). Pros — history, the museum, the atmosphere; cons in older reviews — the condition of the complex before the reconstruction (per 2GIS, details not disclosed).
kg-0011.p.sum: The Manas Ordo complex with the Manas Gumbez reopened after reconstruction on 12.09.2026 (a new 1,500 m² museum, cottages, canteens); it is 12–15 km east of Talas by the village of Tash-Aryk — city marshrutkas and taxis go there. Base yourself in Talas: from Bishkek take a marshrutka/shared taxi via Otmok (5.5–6 h) or GoBus via Kazakhstan. The rate and hours after the reopening have not been published — check on site; dress modestly.

kg-0012.name: Alay Valley
kg-0012.near: For different parts of the valley — Sary-Tash (~3200 m, the fork of the Pamir Highway), Sary-Mogol (~2980 m, the base for Lenin Peak and Tulpar-Kul), Daroot-Korgon in the west (I Love KG). The catalog point lies between Sary-Mogol and Kashka-Suu.
kg-0012.elev: On average about 3000 m (too.kg); Sary-Tash ~3200 m, Sary-Mogol ~2980 m, Tulpar-Kul ~3500 m, Taldyk Pass at the entrance — 3615 m (I Love KG).
kg-0012.short: The Alay Valley is a wide high-mountain (~3000 m) intermontane basin between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges with a view of Lenin Peak (7134 m); the Pamir Highway runs through it.
kg-0012.desc: The Alay Valley is an intermontane basin in southern Kyrgyzstan between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges, about 120 km in a straight line from Osh (too.kg); the average elevation is about 3000 m, and the width ranges from 8–10 to 25 km (too.kg). The relief was leveled by ancient glaciation. Above the valley stands the wall of the Trans-Alay Range with Lenin Peak (7134 m), whose base camp is reached by roads from the valley (too.kg). The Pamir Highway Osh — Khorog runs through the valley, popular with cyclists and motorcyclists, and in ancient times a branch of the Great Silk Road ran here (too.kg). The valley remains a center of nomadic herding: in summer the slopes are dotted with yurts and camps (too.kg). The main villages are Sary-Tash, Sary-Mogol and Daroot-Korgon (I Love KG).
kg-0012.guide: The best way to meet the Alay is from Taldyk Pass (3615 m): after the last bend the whole valley opens up, with the wall of the Trans-Alay and Lenin Peak. Base yourself in Sary-Mogol — from here it is 25 km to Lake Tulpar-Kul and the yurt camps at the foot of Lenin. Don't rush: Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol sit at 3000–3200 m, and a headache on the first evening is a signal to stop, not to climb higher (I Love KG). A border permit is not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, but it is needed for Achyk-Tash and the base camp (I Love KG). If you catch the third weekend of July, Sary-Mogol hosts a festival of horse and yak games (Visit Alay).
kg-0012.see: The panorama of the Trans-Alay Range and Lenin Peak (7134 m); Taldyk Pass (3615 m); Lake Tulpar-Kul and the Achyk-Tash base camp; yurts and nomads' herds; the Pamir Highway (too.kg, I Love KG).
kg-0012.skip: You tolerate altitude poorly and cannot set aside a day for acclimatization (I Love KG). You are going in the off-season — the yurt camps close in September, and in spring there is snow on Taldyk (I Love KG). You have one day from Osh — that is 4+ hours each way.
kg-0012.diff: Driving through the valley is easy (the paved highway); the main difficulty is the altitude of 3000–3600 m (I Love KG). Treks from Sary-Mogol and Tulpar-Kul: Travellers' Pass ~4100 m (5 h round trip — Visit Alay), the multi-day “Best of Alay” 123 km with passes up to 4306 m (Visit Alay).
kg-0012.when: June — August (I Love KG); the yurt camps operate in summer and close in September; in spring there may be snow on Taldyk, in summer thunderstorms, and the nights are cold (I Love KG). Trekking — June to early September (Visit Alay).
kg-0012.hours: Open territory; the Osh — Sary-Tash road is open year-round (in winter Taldyk may be closed because of snow — editorial). Achyk-Tash and the Lenin Peak base camp — with a border permit (I Love KG).
kg-0012.daytime: Morning — clear visibility of Lenin Peak and the Trans-Alay; by evening clouds and thunderstorms (I Love KG, TripAdvisor on Tulpar-Kul).
kg-0012.how: From Osh along the Pamir Highway via Gulcha and Taldyk Pass (3615 m) to Sary-Tash, then west to Sary-Mogol (~220 km, ~4 h of pure driving — I Love KG) or to Daroot-Korgon. Marshrutka (minibus) Osh → Sary-Mogol — one trip at 14:00 (schedule for 27.08.2026 — I Love KG), arriving ~18:00, 300 som (Backpack Adventures).
kg-0012.needcar: Yes: marshrutka/shared taxi to the villages of the valley, then local cars to the lakes and camps (transfer to Tulpar-Kul ~1 h — I Love KG).
kg-0012.self: Yes: marshrutka/taxi to Sary-Mogol or Sary-Tash, accommodation in guesthouses, a transfer to the lake on the spot; no permit is needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, but it is needed for Achyk-Tash/the base camp (I Love KG).
kg-0012.roadtype: The main approach from Osh via Taldyk is the paved Pamir Highway (too.kg); turn-offs to pastures, Tulpar-Kul and the camps are dirt roads (Visit Alay; editorial).
kg-0012.traveltime: Osh → Sary-Mogol: ~220 km, ~4 h of pure driving, longer with stops (I Love KG); marshrutka 14:00 → ~18:00 (Backpack Adventures); Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul ~45 min–1 h.
kg-0012.stay: Guesthouses in Sary-Mogol with meals — $15–20 with breakfast (Backpack Adventures; year not stated); yurt camps at Tulpar-Kul in summer — from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay); CBT Sary-Mogol (sarymogol.com, +996 556 092627) books accommodation.
kg-0012.net: Not confirmed by operator: in Sary-Mogol the Wi-Fi is unreliable and a local SIM is recommended (Backpack Adventures); I Love KG advises an offline map and a power bank.
kg-0012.entry: There is no entrance fee for the valley. A border permit costs ≈$35–40 (Visit Alay FAQ, 07.2026), takes 1–2 weeks, and is needed for the Lenin Peak base camp (I Love KG, Visit Alay); it is not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol (I Love KG).
kg-0012.transfer: Osh → Sary-Mogol: marshrutka 300 som, shared taxi 400 som/seat, private car ~3000 som (Backpack Adventures); Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul 1500 som/car (Visit Alay). The year of the Backpack Adventures data is not stated — check for 2026.
kg-0012.bring: Cash, an offline map, warm clothes, sun protection, a power bank, a flashlight (I Love KG); passport and permit if you are going to Achyk-Tash.
kg-0012.warn: Altitude 3000–3600 m: a headache and nausea are a reason to stop and not climb higher (I Love KG). Snow on Taldyk in spring, thunderstorms in summer, cold nights (I Love KG). The border zone at Achyk-Tash/the base camp and along the border with Tajikistan — a permit is needed.
kg-0012.food: Home-style Kyrgyz cooking in the guesthouses of Sary-Mogol and in yurts (dinner and breakfast are included in the 1000 som — Visit Alay); kymyz and ayran from nomads in summer (too.kg: nomadic herding; editorial).
kg-0012.reviews: Google Maps “Alay Valley”: 4.5/5, 8 ratings (03.10.2026). For related places: TripAdvisor Tulpar-Kol 4.7/5 (9 reviews, until 07.2025). Pluses: views of Lenin Peak, nomadic culture, treks; minuses: altitude, changeable weather, the long road. TripAdvisor “Base Camp For Peak Lenin” (in the valley): 4.7/5, 58 reviews, No. 2 of 23 in Osh; 2025 reviews: yurt camps from basic to “hotel-like”.
kg-0012.p.sum: The Alay Valley is a high-mountain (about 3000 m) steppe between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges; the gateways are Sary-Tash (the fork of the Pamir Highway) and Sary-Mogol (the base for Tulpar-Kul and Lenin Peak). From Osh it is 4–5 h on paved road via Taldyk: the 14:00 marshrutka from the New Bus Station (300 som) or a shared taxi 400–500 som/seat, a private car ~3000–4500 som. For overnight stays — guesthouses in Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol ($10–20) and yurt camps on the jailoo (summer pasture) in summer; there are no ATMs — withdraw cash in Osh. A permit is needed only for Achyk-Tash and the border area.

kg-0013.name: Ruh Ordo Cultural Center
kg-0013.full: Ruh Ordo Cultural Center named after Chingiz Aitmatov
kg-0013.near: Cholpon-Ata; the complex is on the lakeshore in the southern part of the town, Sovetskaya St.
kg-0013.elev: ≈1610 m (estimate: the complex is on the shore of Issyk-Kul, and the lake level is ≈1607 m)
kg-0013.short: A park-museum on the shore of Issyk-Kul in Cholpon-Ata: five identical white chapels of the world's religions, the Chingiz Aitmatov house-museum, sculptures, a yurt museum, a concert hall and a pier with pavilions. A visit takes 1–3 hours, entry 350 som (2024).
kg-0013.desc: Ruh Ordo (“spiritual headquarters”) was built in 2002 as a private complex, opened to everyone in 2007, and in 2024 was transferred to state management. On the grounds by the water stand five identical white chapels — Orthodox, Catholic, Muslim, Jewish and Buddhist — as a symbol of the unity of religions; between them are avenues of sculptures of historical figures and Aitmatov's characters, the writer's house-museum, galleries with copies of petroglyphs, a yurt with traditional furnishings, an exhibition of headwear (kalpak, elechek, tebetei), a concert hall with special acoustics and a pier into the lake with four pavilions representing the cardinal points/seasons. The exhibits are decorative rather than historical-museum in character: there are few authentic artifacts and few explanatory signs, so a guided tour (in Russian/Kyrgyz/English, ≈1.5–2 h) adds noticeably more meaning. The main trump card is the view: white chapels against the blue lake and the snow-capped Terskey Ala-Too.
kg-0013.guide: Take a guided tour or an audio guide at the entrance: without the story Ruh Ordo is a pretty park with statues, and with it, a story about how Kyrgyz people see the unity of religions and Aitmatov's legacy. Walk to the end of the pier and turn around: five white chapels in a row against the mountains — the complex's main shot, best in the pre-sunset hour. Look into Aitmatov's house even if you haven't read “The White Ship” — here hangs the story of how Issyk-Kul became his “sea”. Plan 1.5–2 hours; in season there are concerts in the hall — ask for the program at the ticket office. If you are going with children, bring hats: there is little shade on the grounds.
kg-0013.see: Five chapels of the world's religions; the Chingiz Aitmatov house-museum; an avenue of sculptures (historical figures, Aitmatov's characters, Buddha); the yurt museum and the headwear exhibition; a gallery of petroglyph copies; the concert hall; a pier with four pavilions and a view of the lake and mountains.
kg-0013.skip: If you expect a real museum with artifacts — here there are decorations and copies, and the price of 350–500 som seems inflated to many for a 20-minute look. If you have half a day in Cholpon-Ata and a choice between this and the mountains — the gorges will give you more. If you don't like “new-builds” and symbolic complexes.
kg-0013.diff: Easy: level paths through the park, 1–3 h of walking. Accessible for children and older people.
kg-0013.when: May–September (summer hours until 19:00, concerts, the swimming season nearby); in autumn — golden trees and snow on the mountains, few people; in winter it is open on reduced hours (9:00–17:00).
kg-0013.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): daily 09:00–17:00 (winter schedule); TripAdvisor: winter 9:00–17:00, summer 9:00–19:00; Trip.com (2026): 09:00–17:00; Motohorek (2021): 9:00–20:00. Open every day.
kg-0013.daytime: The second half of the day and the hour before sunset — light on the chapels and mountains from the pier; fewer people in the morning.
kg-0013.how: From Bishkek: a marshrutka (minibus) from the Bishkek bus station (1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St; the Western station has been closed since 10.2024) to Cholpon-Ata 400–450 som, ≈3–3.5 h; GoBus 580 som; taxi 700–1000 som/person (2024). In Cholpon-Ata — on foot from the center/bus station 10–20 min to the shore (Sovetskaya St) or a taxi. Parking at the entrance.
kg-0013.needcar: No: the site is in town, within walking distance of the center of Cholpon-Ata and the hotels.
kg-0013.self: Yes: a ticket at the entrance, a free walk around the park; a guided tour is optional and separate.
kg-0013.roadtype: Paved city streets of Cholpon-Ata up to the entrance; inside — paved park paths.
kg-0013.traveltime: From the center of Cholpon-Ata 10–20 min on foot; from Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h. The visit takes 1–2 h, with a tour 2–3 h.
kg-0013.stay: Cholpon-Ata, 2024: private rooms 600–1,500 som/day, guesthouses up to 3,000 som at peak, mid-range hotels $15–20/person, premium pansionats (Soviet-style resort hotels) $184–528/night with meals (24.kg). Hotels nearby: Karven Four Seasons, Ak Bermet, Tri Korony (Three Crowns), Akun, Goluboy Issyk-Kul (weproject 2024).
kg-0013.net: Urban area, 4G from all operators; in April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Cholpon-Ata (economist.kg). There are no signal problems in the reviews.
kg-0013.entry: 350 som per person — since 19.06.2024 by the president's order after the center passed to the state (24.kg, Kaktus, AKIpress); before that 500 som (2024), under private management 400 som (2021: adult 400, students/pensioners 200, children under 7 free — Motohorek). TripAdvisor reviews of 2024–2025 mention “500 som” — probably before the reduction; Trip.com (2026): “the price is low, changes every year”. The guided tour is separate, “available for a group”.
kg-0013.transfer: From Bishkek marshrutka 400–450 som, GoBus 580, taxi 700–1000 som/person (24.kg, 2024). A city taxi to the entrance — roughly 100–200 som (an estimate, not confirmed by a price list).
kg-0013.bring: A hat and water in summer, cash/card for the ticket and tour, a camera; clothing appropriate for chapels (covered shoulders/knees are not strictly required, but respectful).
kg-0013.warn: The entry price changed four times in 2021–2024 (400 → 500 → 350) — check at the ticket office. Quiet rules apply in the chapels; these are symbolic buildings, not working places of worship. In the summer peak — queues and tour groups. The pier has no railings on the water side — watch children.
kg-0013.food: On the grounds a cafe/buffet seasonally (not described in detail in reviews). Nearby on the embankment and Sovetskaya St — Cholpon-Ata cafes: Issyk-Kul fish, lagman, shashlik; average cafe bill 1,400–2,700 som (24.kg 2024).
kg-0013.reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 2,359 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.4/5, 144 reviews, No. 1 of 14 in Cholpon-Ata (07.10.2026). Trip.com: 5.0/2 (2026). Pluses: the view of the lake and mountains, a well-kept park, the idea of the unity of religions, Aitmatov, the pier. Minuses: exhibits “piled together”, few originals and signs, the price is high relative to 20–40 minutes of actual viewing.
kg-0013.p.sum: Ruh Ordo is within the limits of Cholpon-Ata on the shore (Sovetskaya St), 10–20 minutes on foot from the center and bus station; you don't need your own car, and there is parking at the entrance. From Bishkek — a marshrutka from the Bishkek bus station (1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St, 400–600 som) or the summer train to Balykchy + a marshrutka. A ticket is 350 som (since 06.2024); allow 1.5–2 h, it is better to take a guided tour at the ticket office and go to the pier in the pre-sunset hour; it is convenient to combine with the petroglyphs (3.2 km) in one day.

kg-0014.name: Burana Tower
kg-0014.dist: Chuy District, Chuy Region, about 12 km south of Tokmok
kg-0014.near: The town of Tokmok (~12 km, 15 min by taxi — asiaodysseytravel); next to the complex is the village of Burana. Bishkek is ~80 km away.
kg-0014.elev: About 750 m above sea level — the Chuy Valley (not confirmed by a source, a guideline from topographic maps; verify manually). The height of the tower itself is 21–25 m (too.kg — 21 m; danroundtheworld — 25 m), originally 40–45 m.
kg-0014.short: Burana is an 11th-century minaret about 21–25 m high on the Balasagun ancient town site (the Karakhanid capital) near Tokmok, part of the UNESCO site “Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang’an-Tianshan Corridor” (2014).
kg-0014.desc: The Burana Tower is the surviving minaret of an ancient town site identified with medieval Balasagun, the capital of the Karakhanid state in the 10th–12th centuries. Originally its height reached about 40–45 m; the top collapsed in earthquakes, and now the tower is 21–25 m (too.kg; danroundtheworld). The lower part was restored in the 1970s, and in 2021–2023, with the support of the U.S. Embassy (Ambassador's Fund for Cultural Preservation, World Monuments Fund), the top of the tower was rebuilt, a ceramic rain shield was laid and cameras were installed (Kaktus, 30.06.2023). On the grounds there is a “stone garden” of balbals (ancient Turkic stone statues), burial mounds, remains of fortifications, the foundations of mausoleums and a small museum with finds. You can climb to the top by a narrow steep staircase inside. The Balasagun ancient town site is part of the serial UNESCO “Silk Roads” property (2014).
kg-0014.guide: Climb inside the tower by the narrow and very steep staircase — from the top you can see the whole Chuy Valley and the snowy wall of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too. Then stroll through the “stone garden”: dozens of balbals — stone statues with faces, some holding cups at their chests. Notice the fresh masonry and the ceramic “cap” at the top — that is the 2021–2023 restoration. In the small museum look at the finds from the Balasagun ancient town — once the capital of the Karakhanids was here. There is no food on site and little shade — come in the morning and bring water.
kg-0014.see: The Burana minaret with a climb to the top by the inner staircase; the “stone garden” with balbals; the burial mounds and remains of the fortress walls and mausoleums of the Balasagun ancient town; a museum with archaeological finds and photos (in a yurt/small building — ummigoeswhere, danroundtheworld); a view of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too range.
kg-0014.skip: You are not interested in archaeology and history — the complex itself is small (1–1.5 h). You are afraid of tight steep staircases — the climb up the tower is narrow and dark. You are short on time and heading to Issyk-Kul — the detour from Tokmok adds about an hour to an hour and a half.
kg-0014.diff: Easy: level grounds by the parking lot; the only difficulty is the narrow steep staircase inside the tower (danroundtheworld).
kg-0014.when: April–June and September–October: warm, but without the summer scorching heat (there is little shade on the grounds — ummigoeswhere); in summer at midday it is hot. Open year-round (editorial).
kg-0014.hours: Daily 09:00–17:00 (Google Maps as of 03.10.2026; danroundtheworld 08.2025; atlasrambler 2025; asiaodysseytravel 2026). Ummigoeswhere gives 09:00–19:00 — probably summer hours/old data.
kg-0014.daytime: Morning right after opening (09:00): soft light on the brickwork, fewer groups and less heat; evening light — until closing at 17:00 (editorial).
kg-0014.how: Marshrutka (minibus) No. 353 (or 352) from the Eastern Bus Station in Bishkek to Tokmok — ~100 som, 1–1.5 h, every 15–20 min 06:00–20:00 (danroundtheworld 08.2025; asiaodysseytravel 2026). From Tokmok — local marshrutka No. 212 to Burana (50 som, 25–30 min, danroundtheworld) or a taxi ~15 min. Also the commuter train Bishkek-2 → Tokmok (18:35, 60 som — evening only, inconvenient). By car — the Bishkek–Balykchy highway to Tokmok, then south.
kg-0014.needcar: Yes, but public transport is enough: a marshrutka to Tokmok + marshrutka No. 212 or a taxi. There is little regular transport back from the tower — it is better to arrange waiting with a taxi driver (atlasrambler).
kg-0014.self: Yes: free access during opening hours, no permits needed; payment in cash at the entrance.
kg-0014.roadtype: Paved: the Bishkek–Tokmok highway and a local paved road to the complex’s parking lot (editorial; there are no complaints about the road in the sources).
kg-0014.traveltime: From Bishkek: by car about 1–1.5 h (~80 km), by marshrutka with a change at Tokmok 1.5–2.5 h; from Tokmok — 15 min by taxi. For the visit — 1–1.5 h.
kg-0014.stay: There are no hotels at the complex (too.kg). People usually make a day trip from Bishkek; for a night — hotels in Tokmok or guesthouses on the way to Issyk-Kul (specific options have not been checked).
kg-0014.net: There is mobile coverage at the complex, “full” (too.kg); the operator and speed are not specified.
kg-0014.entry: No official tariff was found. According to travelers’ reports: 220 som for everyone, including the museum and the climb up the tower (danroundtheworld, visit 08.2025, article updated 02.2026; asiaodysseytravel 2026 — “about 220 or 150 som”); 150 som (atlasrambler, 04.2025); 60 som tower + 50 som museum (ummigoeswhere, earlier; too.kg — 60 som). A guideline for 2026 — ~220 som, in cash.
kg-0014.transfer: Marshrutka Bishkek – Tokmok ~100 som; Tokmok – Burana marshrutka No. 212 50 som or a round-trip taxi 500–1,000 som; taxi Bishkek – Burana 1,500–2,200 som one way (danroundtheworld 2025; asiaodysseytravel 2026). For reference: Tokmok – Kant 70 som (Kaktus, 09.02.2026).
kg-0014.bring: Water and sun protection — there is little shade and no places to buy supplies on the grounds (too.kg, danroundtheworld); cash for the entrance; comfortable shoes for the steep staircase; a phone flashlight for the dark climb.
kg-0014.warn: The staircase inside the tower is very narrow, steep and dark — not for people with claustrophobia or small children without supervision. There is no food or water on site, and the toilet is primitive (danroundtheworld). Taxi drivers from Tokmok sometimes overcharge (up to 1,300 som — ummigoeswhere) — agree on the price in advance. Yandex Go may take you to the wrong spot — check the pin.
kg-0014.food: There is no café on the grounds (too.kg, danroundtheworld). For a bite — in Tokmok (canteens and cafés with lagman, samsa and Dungan cuisine — editorial) or on the way to Issyk-Kul.
kg-0014.reviews: Google Maps: 4.5/5, 2,900 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: the Burana Tower (Tokmok, d4176350) page with a large number of reviews, the rating could not be read from the research environment. Pros — history, balbals, the view from the tower, easy logistics from Bishkek; cons — a small and simple museum, heat without shade, a primitive toilet, no food.
kg-0014.p.sum: Burana is easy to do as a day trip from Bishkek by public transport: marshrutka No. 353 from the Eastern Bus Station to Tokmok (≈100 som, 06:00–20:00, every 15–20 min), then marshrutka No. 212 to the tower (50 som) or a taxi from Tokmok with waiting (500–1,500 som round trip — agree in advance). Yandex Go directly from Bishkek — ≈1,500–2,200 som one way. The complex is open 09:00–17:00, entry ≈220 som in cash; there is no food, water or shade on site — eat in Tokmok and arrive at opening, before the groups (10–11 am).

kg-0016.name: Lake Kol-Tor
kg-0016.near: Kegety dachas and the tourist bases/guesthouses in the gorge (trailhead); Kegety village — ~11 km below the trailhead (asia-hikes); Bishkek — 82–90 km.
kg-0016.elev: About 2700–2735 m: 2725 m (thegonegoat), 2733 m (asia-hikes), ~2700 m (pinyourfootsteps, the previous entry).
kg-0016.short: Kol-Tor is a turquoise glacial-moraine lake at ~2730 m in a side valley of the Kegety gorge, 82–90 km from Bishkek; one of the most popular day hikes from the capital.
kg-0016.desc: Kol-Tor (Kyol-Tyor, Kel-Tor) is a lake of glacial-moraine origin above the tree line (bookit.kg) in the valley of the same name, a side valley of the Kegety gorge on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too. The water is bright turquoise and very cold all year round. From the parking in the gorge, a 7–8 km trail climbs 800–1000 m through spruce forest, along a stream and up steep switchbacks (hiking.kg: 7.5 km, 3.5 h, +1000 m). At the start there are guesthouses and a Trekking Union hut; you can pitch a tent beyond the lake. In summer, organized day groups come here from Bishkek (Trekking Union, Kyrgyz Concept, ticket.kg).
kg-0016.guide: Kol-Tor is a classic day hike from Bishkek: set out at 6–7 am so you start the climb before the heat. The hardest stretch is the steep switchbacks after the forest; after that the trail reaches the moraine, and the lake suddenly opens up in bright turquoise. We don't recommend swimming — the water is icy all year, and the wind at the lake is often strong. If you want some quiet, stay overnight in a guesthouse at the trailhead or camp beyond the lake. It's best to head back with time to spare: finding transport out of the gorge in the evening is almost impossible.
kg-0016.see: The turquoise moraine lake and the glacial slopes above it; spruce forests and the stream in the Kol-Tor valley along the way; panoramas of the Kegety gorge; in the gorge itself, Kegety Waterfall (separate entry, 4.9 km).
kg-0016.skip: You aren't ready for a climb of 800–1000 m in one day (7–8 km each way, 6–8 h in total). You have no car or tour — it's hard to get out of the gorge by public transport. You're looking for solitude on a summer weekend — the trail has many groups from Bishkek.
kg-0016.diff: A physically demanding hike: 7.5 km one way, about 1000 m of ascent, 3.5 h up (hiking.kg — difficulty 4/5); other sources say 800–900 m of ascent and 3–5 h (pinyourfootsteps, thegonegoat). Steep switchbacks, stream fords; slippery in wet weather, ice in winter — you need crampons (asia-hikes).
kg-0016.when: July–August is optimal (hiking.kg); the season overall is May to October, outside it the trail is under snow, hard and dangerous (pinyourfootsteps). In winter people hike with crampons (asia-hikes); in mid-October there may be deep snow.
kg-0016.hours: A natural site with no schedule. The post/barrier at the entrance to the Kegety gorge (eco fee) operates in daylight — hours not confirmed.
kg-0016.daytime: Start the climb early in the morning (7–9 am): it's cool on the ascent, in the morning the lake is usually calm and brighter in color, while in the afternoon there is more often wind and cloud (editorial; wind — asia-hikes).
kg-0016.how: By car: Bishkek → Krasnaya Rechka → Yuryevka → Syn-Tash → Rot-Front → Kegety gorge, after the first bridge at the fork go straight on toward the Kol-Tor valley, then on foot (hiking.kg). Public transport: a marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek's Eastern Bus Station to Kegety village (about 2 h; 50 som per thegonegoat 2024 — the price is probably outdated), then ~11 km by hitching/on foot to the trailhead (asia-hikes).
kg-0016.needcar: Yes: your own car, a taxi or an organized tour. The marshrutka goes only as far as the village; the remaining ~11 km up the gorge are on foot or by hitching; finding transport back is very hard (thegonegoat).
kg-0016.self: Yes: no permits needed, the trail is popular and well trodden. At the entrance to the gorge an eco fee is charged per car. Without mountain hiking experience it's better to go with a group.
kg-0016.roadtype: Paved road gives way to a dirt road at Kegety; the last driveable section is rough. A trail leads to the lake.
kg-0016.traveltime: Hiking.kg reference: from Bishkek to the trailhead 82 km / 2 h 10 min; from the parking to the lake 7.5 km / 3.5 h, ascent about 1000 m. On foot there and back 7–8 h.
kg-0016.stay: At the trailhead: Kegety Tour guesthouse (~1 km to the start, 1500 som/person with three meals a day — asia-hikes), the Kol-Tor guesthouse (Booking, 25 reviews), the Trekking Union hut (book via TUK — thegonegoat), Malinka (pinyourfootsteps); tent spots at the trailhead and beyond the lake.
kg-0016.net: The source notes a rare signal at the guesthouse and no stable coverage at the lake; operators are not specified.
kg-0016.entry: The eco fee at the post in the Kegety gorge is about 200 som per car (hiking.kg, 2024); the current amount for 2026 is not confirmed. There is no separate fee for the lake.
kg-0016.transfer: Trekking Union tour ~450 som/person with transport (thegonegoat, 2024); marshrutka to Kegety 50 som (2024, probably outdated — for comparison: Tokmok — Krasnaya Rechka 60 som, Kaktus 02.2026). A taxi price Bishkek — Kol-Tor for 2025–2026 was not found.
kg-0016.bring: Trekking shoes, 1.5–2 L of water and food for the whole day (there are no shops on the trail or at the start — stock up at a supermarket on the way), a warm windproof jacket, sun protection, an offline map; in winter — crampons; for an overnight stay — a warm sleeping bag (cold nights — thegonegoat).
kg-0016.warn: 800–1000 m of ascent in a day to an elevation of ~2730 m — gauge your strength and time, and turn back if the weather worsens. Outside May to October the trail is under snow and dangerous, and in winter crampons are needed on icy sections (pinyourfootsteps, asia-hikes). The lake water is icy all year — swimming is dangerous. The wind at the lake is strong — secure your tent. In the evening it is almost impossible to find transport out of the gorge — arrange a return car in advance. No signal at the lake.
kg-0016.food: At the start — guesthouses with meals (Kegety Tour — 1500 som/person with a bed and three meals a day, asia-hikes; the guesthouse has instant coffee and simple dishes, pinyourfootsteps). There is no food on the trail or at the lake — stock up at a supermarket on the way.
kg-0016.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 88 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). Booking: Kol-Tor guesthouse — 25 reviews. Pros: the color of the lake, closeness to Bishkek, views; cons: the steep climb, cold and wind at the lake, difficult return transport.
kg-0016.p.sum: Kol-Tor is a classic day hike from Bishkek: by car via Krasnaya Rechka — Yuryevka — Rot-Front into the Kegety gorge (≈82–90 km, ≈2 h), after the first bridge straight on into the Kol-Tor valley to the guesthouse/yurts at the start, where you leave the car; then 7.5 km and +800–1000 m on a well-trodden trail (3–3.5 h up, 2–2.5 h down). Without a car the easiest options are a group tour (Trekking Union and others), a taxi to the start ≈1500 som, or marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the Eastern Bus Station to Kegety village (09:30 and 15:30, ≈80 som) + 11 km by hitching. Set out before 8–9 am and arrange a return car in advance; bring water and food — there is nothing at the lake.

kg-0017.name: Lake Merzbacher
kg-0017.full: Lake Merzbacher — an ice-dammed glacial lake on the Inylchek Glacier
kg-0017.near: Inylchek (Enylchek) — a half-abandoned settlement at the start of the valley, ≈40 km as the crow flies; Sary-Jaz — ≈38 km as the crow flies (OSM). The nearest inhabited points are the seasonal camps At-Jailoo (2500–2600 m) and Maida-Adyr (helipad), 30–40 km down the valley; ≈150 km by road to Karakol.
kg-0017.elev: 3304 m (MasterTour, ru-Wikipedia “3304 m a.s.l.”); the “Merzbacher meadow” camp is at 3400–3600 m (karakol.kg 3400, Ecotour/Horizon 3600); Advantour and Kyrgyzstan Travel give 3500 m — overstated compared with map data.
kg-0017.short: A “vanishing” lake between the North and South Inylchek glaciers, discovered by Gottfried Merzbacher in 1903: it fills with meltwater and once a year (usually in July–August) drains under the glacier within a few hours, causing a flood on the Inylchek and Sary-Jaz rivers. Access is only by a multi-day trek along the South Inylchek moraine from the border zone, or by helicopter flyover.
kg-0017.desc: Lake Merzbacher forms where the North Inylchek glacier butts against the South Inylchek: the glacier tongue blocks the valley, and meltwater accumulates behind the ice dam. The lower part (≈3.5–6 km long, ≈1 km wide) breaks through under the glacier every year, usually from mid-July to late August, and empties within hours to a day; the upper part, separated by an ice bridge, remains. The outburst raises the level of the Inylchek and Sary-Jaz rivers, which is why hydrologists monitor the lake. In 1903 the German geographer Gottfried Merzbacher saw the lake full on his way to Khan Tengri, and three days later empty, and the following year he confirmed that the phenomenon recurs regularly; the exact breakout mechanism is still debated. The lake lies in the border zone with China and Kazakhstan: a border service permit is required. The standard route: Karakol → Chon-Ashuu Pass (3822–3830 m) → Inylchek valley → At-Jailoo camp (2500–2600 m) → Iva camp (≈18 km) → Glina/Chon-Tash camp along the moraine → Merzbacher meadow (3400–3600 m) → side trip to the lake; ≈78–80 km over 5–6 days with climbs of up to 2000 m, walking on moraine and ice, river crossings and sections washed out by mudflows. Operators' seasonal camps run roughly from 5 July to 30 August. The alternative is a helicopter from Karkyra to South Inylchek with a flyover of the lake (Ak-Sai Travel), or combined programs with helicopter drop-off/pick-up.
kg-0017.guide: What is most interesting here is not the view but the timing: come in early July and you will see a turquoise lake with floating icebergs, in late August an empty basin with blocks of ice on the bottom, and both pictures are rare in their own way. At the Merzbacher meadow listen at night: the rumbling and cracking is the glacier “breathing”, and on the day of the outburst the glacier “comes alive with frightening sounds”, as the first eyewitnesses wrote. Set aside a spare day — weather and the state of the moraine dictate the schedule, and the camps work only in July–August. Arrange the border-zone permit at least a week ahead (through an operator, ≈3000 som in 2025) — without it you will be turned back at the second checkpoint in the valley. If you lack the legs or days, the helicopter tour from Karkyra shows both the lake and Khan Tengri in three days — expensive, but the only “quick” way.
kg-0017.see: The lower lake with icebergs (before the outburst) or its empty basin (after); the ice dam and the ice bridge between the upper and lower lake; the Merzbacher meadow; the South Inylchek glacier (≈60 km — one of the largest outside the polar regions) with multicolored glacial lakes along the way; views of Nansen Peak (5697 m), Khan Tengri (7010 m) and, in good visibility, Pobeda Peak (7439 m); a side trip to Panorama Peak (≈4500 m).
kg-0017.skip: If you don't have 6–13 free days, experience of high-altitude hikes and a budget from $1,500 — this is an expedition, not an excursion. If you are afraid of glaciers, crevasses and river crossings — the route goes over moraine and ice without a marked trail. If you want to be sure of seeing the “lake” — it may already be gone: the outburst happens as early as mid-July.
kg-0017.diff: Hard: 5–6 days of trekking over moraine and glacier, 78–80 km, total ascent ≈2000 m, elevations 2500–3600 m (4500 for Panorama Peak), river crossings, crevasses, sections washed out by mudflows; you need high-altitude hiking experience, good fitness and a guide. The alternative without trekking is a helicopter.
kg-0017.when: Late June to late August (operator camps: 5 July — 30 August). To catch the lake full — the first half of July; to see the empty basin — late August. In recent years the outburst has shifted to July, and sometimes there are two (July and late August). A winter outburst also exists, but access is closed in winter.
kg-0017.hours: Around the clock, but in practice only in the camps' working season (July–August) and with a border permit; the second border checkpoint is at the entrance to the Inylchek valley.
kg-0017.daytime: Morning — clear sky and views of Khan Tengri before the afternoon clouds; head out to the lake early so you can return to camp in daylight.
kg-0017.how: Only with a tour operator or your own logistics: Karakol → Inylchek village over Chon-Ashuu Pass (3822 m) by truck/4×4 → At-Jailoo camp (2500–2600 m; 1 day) → 3-day trek along South Inylchek to the Merzbacher meadow → side trip to the lake → 2 days back (or helicopter South Inylchek → Karkyra). Ak-Sai variant: Bishkek → Karkyra → helicopter to the Inylchek valley → trek to the meadow (day 6 of the program) → South Inylchek base camp → helicopter back. A border-zone permit is mandatory (takes ≈7 days to process).
kg-0017.needcar: Yes: a 4×4/truck drop-off from Karakol to At-Jailoo (≈150 km, 6–8 h) or a helicopter; beyond that, only on foot. Getting there on your own in a regular car is impossible.
kg-0017.self: Formally yes (with a permit and glacier-hiking experience), in practice most people go with an operator: the moraine route is not marked, the camps and food belong to the operators, and rescue is only through them. Asia Hikes describes an independent option with nights in camps for ≈$60/day.
kg-0017.roadtype: Karakol → Inylchek: paved to Ak-Suu/Ottuk, then a gravel mountain road over Chon-Ashuu Pass (3822–3830 m) and the Sary-Jaz valley — truck/4×4, 6–8 h; At-Jailoo → lake: a footpath along the lateral moraine and the ice of South Inylchek, river crossings, sections without a trail. There is no road access to the lake itself.
kg-0017.traveltime: Karakol → At-Jailoo ≈1 day by car; At-Jailoo → Iva camp ≈18 km (6–7 h) → Glina/Chon-Tash camp (3–5 h) → Merzbacher meadow ≈15 km (5–6 h) → lake and back (3–4 h); in total 78–80 km over 5–6 days of trekking. In the Ak-Sai program the lake is on day 6 of 13, allowing for the helicopter and acclimatization. The helicopter tour takes 3 days from Bishkek.
kg-0017.stay: Operators' tent camps: At-Jailoo (2500–2600 m), Iva, Glina/Chon-Tash (2900 m), Merzbacher meadow (3400–3600 m), South Inylchek base camp (4000 m); ≈$60/day with meals for independent travelers (Asia Hikes 2024), and Ak-Sai has permanent tents included in the tour. Before departure — guesthouses in Karakol or the Karkyra yurt camp.
kg-0017.net: There is no mobile signal in the Inylchek valley or on the glacier; operators have satellite phones/radios in the base camps. The last signal is at Karakol/Ak-Suu. There are no operator measurements; this comes from tour descriptions and trip reports.
kg-0017.entry: Khan Tengri Nature Park: 300 som per foreign tourist + 150 som per tent per night (Asia Hikes, updated 05.2024); with Ak-Sai the eco fees are included in the tour. Border permit: 3000 som/person via too.kg (2025, 50% prepayment, ≈7 days); Asia Hikes — $15–50 via operators. The park's official 2026 tariff was not found.
kg-0017.transfer: Trek with an operator: from $1,590/person (Ecotour, 6 days, 2025) to $3,200/person (Ak-Sai, 13 days with a helicopter, 2027); Ak-Sai helicopter tour — $1,050/person (3 days). A separate transfer Karakol → At-Jailoo by truck/4×4 is only on request from operators (Neofit, Karakol.kg); there is no public price list.
kg-0017.bring: Waterproof trekking boots, a sleeping bag rated to −5…−10 °C, a down jacket and warm layers, a rain jacket, poles, crampons/ice axe as required by the guide, sun protection (category 4 glasses, sunscreen), a first-aid kit with altitude sickness pills, a headlamp, a power bank, passport and permit, cash in som. The porter limit at Ak-Sai is 12 kg.
kg-0017.warn: It is a border zone — without a border service permit you will not be let in. At 3300–4000 m there is a risk of altitude sickness and you need to acclimatize. On the glacier: crevasses, moving moraines, river crossings; parts of the route are washed out by mudflows. On the day the lake breaks out the Inylchek and Sary-Jaz rivers rise sharply — do not pitch a camp by the water and follow your guide's instructions. The weather changes within an hour; snow in August is normal. Outside the camps there is no signal and no rescue infrastructure; insurance with helicopter evacuation is mandatory.
kg-0017.food: Only the operators' camp cooking (three meals a day are included in the tours, ≈$60/day for independent travelers): soups, porridges, tea; in Karkyra and Karakol before departure — kumys, boorsoks, beshbarmak. There are no cafes on the route.
kg-0017.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 19 ratings (03.10.2026). No TripAdvisor/2GIS cards. Trip reports (LiveJournal e_kaspersky, olly_ru; Skitalets) describe the lake as the main attraction of the trek to Inylchek; typical minuses are the hard moraine, the weather, and the cost of logistics.

kg-0017.p.sum: This is an expedition-level destination in the border zone: you cannot simply “drive” there on your own. The realistic options are (1) a 5–6 day trek from Karakol: a 4×4/truck over Chon-Ashuu Pass (5–6 h) to At-Jailoo camp, then 3 days along the South Inylchek moraine (≈78 km round trip) — with an operator from $1,590; (2) an Ak-Sai helicopter tour from Bishkek via the Karkyra base with a flyover of the lake (3 days, $1,050). Arrange the border permit 2–6 weeks ahead (too.kg 3000 som, 5–7 days); insurance with helicopter evacuation is mandatory. The window is mid-July to late August.

kg-0018.name: Chon-Ak-Suu Gorge
kg-0018.near: Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu) on the north shore, at the mouth of the gorge; ≈30–35 km east of Cholpon-Ata, ≈60 km west of Karakol on the Balykchy — Karakol road.
kg-0018.elev: Mouth at Grigorievka ≈1700 m; the lower part of the gorge with camps ≈1900–2100 m (Nomad's Land: 2000 m); alpine meadows and lakes 2200–2500 m, upper pastures up to 3000–3500 m; the peaks Kum-Bel 4200 m and Eshenbulak 4647 m. The exact elevation of the catalog point has not been published.
kg-0018.short: A narrow, forested gorge of the Chon-Ak-Suu river on the slope of Kungey Ala-Too above Grigorievka: Tian Shan spruces up to 50 m tall, a rushing river, and three mountain lakes (Lower, Middle, Upper) farther up the valley. The most visited “wild” spot on the north shore: yurt camps, horses, eagle hunters (berkutchi), and trout grilled over charcoal.
kg-0018.desc: Chon-Ak-Suu (“big white water”) is a gorge 22–35 km long (depending on the source) on the northern slope of Issyk-Kul, parallel to the neighboring Semyonovka (Kyrchyn) gorge; Kok-Bel Pass and dirt roads connect them, so they are often done as a loop. The lower part is a tight rocky canyon with sheer cliffs and spruce forest, which people compare to the Krasnoyarsk Stolby (Pillars); higher up the gorge opens into alpine meadows (2200–2500 m) with three lakes, of which the Upper one at the treeline is considered the most beautiful, and nearby is the bright blue Jasyl-Kol. On the jailoo (summer pasture) there are shepherds' and tourist yurts where they serve trout grilled over charcoal, sell honey, offer horse rides and show eagles. In season (July–August) the lower part is full of cars, vendors and day groups from the pansionats (Soviet-style resort hotels) of Cholpon-Ata; above the lakes there is sometimes an army post that restricts access to the Kazakhstan border. Entry is paid (according to 2025–2026 reviews, with different rates for foreigners); the amount is not officially published.
kg-0018.guide: Don't stop at the first yurts with shashlik and eagles — drive or walk on to where the gorge opens into meadows: that is where the Upper Lake is, with quiet and views of the four-thousanders Kum-Bel and Eshenbulak. Negotiate for the horse in advance and count by the minute: according to reviews, prices are quoted as “from 300–500 som an hour”, and then they charge 20 som per minute. The trout here really is local — it is grilled by the river, but the average bill in a yurt for a group is about 1000 som per person, so ask the price before ordering. If you have a 4×4 and a day, do the loop: up the Grigorievka gorge, over the pass and down the Semyonovka gorge; in a regular car it is better not to go beyond the first kilometers. Spring comes late in the gorge — in May the lakes are still under ice, and in June the meadows bloom.
kg-0018.see: A tight canyon with sheer cliffs and spruce forest; the Chon-Ak-Suu river in a turquoise glacial color; a small waterfall; three lakes (Lower, Middle, Upper) and Jasyl-Kol; alpine meadows with yurts; views of Kum-Bel (4200) and Eshenbulak (4647); eagle hunters and horses at the yurt camps; the loop route over the pass into the Semyonovka gorge.
kg-0018.skip: If you are looking for solitude — in July–August the lower part is jammed with cars, yurts and vendors. If you are in a low-slung car — beyond the first few kilometers the road is “awful”, especially during repairs. If you are already going to the Semyonovka gorge — the landscape is similar; choose one unless you have a day for the loop.
kg-0018.diff: Easy for seeing the lower part (walks from the parking spots, 1–3 h); moderate for the hike to the lakes (ascent to 2500 m, 10–15 km one way) or the loop over the pass; the road higher up needs a 4×4.
kg-0018.when: June — early October. Spring comes late and summer is short; late May — June — the meadows bloom, September — golden autumn and fewer people. Peak crowds — July–August. In winter the road is limited by snow.
kg-0018.hours: The gorge is open around the clock; the barrier/fee at the entrance operates in daytime in season; yurt camps — May–September. There is no Google card (ambiguous result); 2GIS lists no hours.
kg-0018.daytime: Morning (leave Cholpon-Ata by 9:00): fewer cars, and the river water is clearer; by lunchtime there are traffic jams of tour jeeps in the lower part.
kg-0018.how: From the Balykchy — Karakol road, in Grigorievka turn north (signpost); the first kilometers are dirt road/paved in places, then a mountain road. From Cholpon-Ata: marshrutka (minibus) No. 501 or bus No. 401 to Grigorievka ≈200 som (40 min), then a 30 min walk to the entrance of the gorge; taxi 700–800 som (Tonkosti Turizma, 2024–2025). From Bishkek: marshrutka to Grigorievka — 700 som for two (T—Zh, 2022). Jeep tours from Cholpon-Ata 900–1300 som/person (basic) or €32–35/person including Semyonovka and the Holy Lake (2026).
kg-0018.needcar: For the lower part — any car in dry weather (Too.kg); for the lakes and the loop with Semyonovka — a 4×4, or on foot/horseback. Without a car it is realistic: marshrutka to Grigorievka + on foot.
kg-0018.self: Yes: entry is free for pedestrians after paying the fee, and the trail along the river is obvious; for the lakes and over the pass, use navigation and allow extra time; for the upper reaches a guide or a horse is better.
kg-0018.roadtype: Too.kg: a dirt road of decent quality, passable by a regular car; 2GIS reviews 2025–2026: even asphalt in places, narrow sheer sections in others, and broken during repairs; TripAdvisor: “awful roads, better not to go in a regular car”, but people drove a Corolla slowly; beyond the first kilometers — only a jeep (LJ uritsk). Above the lakes there is an army post.
kg-0018.traveltime: Cholpon-Ata → Grigorievka 40 min (marshrutka) / 30 min (taxi); Bishkek → Grigorievka ≈4 h; Karakol → Grigorievka ≈1–1.5 h. In the gorge: to the yurts 15–30 min by car, to the lakes 1–1.5 h by 4×4 or 3–5 h on foot. The jeep loop with Semyonovka takes 8 h.
kg-0018.stay: Yurts in the gorge: ≈2000 som per yurt for 5 people/night, meals ≈400 som (tonkosti.ru); seasonal yurt camps and a campsite by the river (Too.kg). In Grigorievka/Chon-Sary-Oi and Bosteri — guesthouses and pansionats at 2000–3000 som/day (tonkosti.ru); hotels in Cholpon-Ata — see 24.kg 2024.
kg-0018.net: In Grigorievka and at the mouth, all operators have signal; higher up the gorge the signal disappears in the narrow part and appears in places on the meadows. There are no direct measurements; in 2026 Beeline strengthened the neighboring Chon-Sary-Oi/Ananyevo without naming Grigorievka. An offline map is a must.
kg-0018.entry: Barrier of the Issyk-Kul forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): per person — Kyrgyz citizens 20 som, citizens of former USSR countries 100, foreigners 220 som; per vehicle — car 80, large vehicles 170, buses/trucks 300 som. This matches the 2GIS reviews of 2025–2026 (“paid entry, more for foreigners”). The same rates apply in the neighboring Semyonovka (Kichi-Ak-Suu).
kg-0018.transfer: From Cholpon-Ata: marshrutka 200 som, taxi 700–800 som (2024–2025); group jeep tour €35/person or €215 per vehicle (2026); basic excursions 900–1300 som/person (tonkosti.ru). From Bishkek, marshrutka to Grigorievka ≈350 som/person (2022).
kg-0018.bring: A windbreaker/fleece (it is cool in the gorge even in July), shoes for rocks and fords, cash in som (entry, horses, food — no cards), water (higher up, water is scarce), repellent, sun protection, an offline map.
kg-0018.warn: The road above the lower part is narrow, with drop-offs, and broken; do not drive a low car after rain. Horse handlers at the yurts often inflate the price and count “by the minute” — agree on the amount before mounting. Above the lakes there is an army post, and you won't be let through to the Kazakh border. Swimming in the lakes — the water is icy and the shores are boggy. In season there are lots of livestock and dogs near the yurts. The entrance fee is the forestry enterprise's official tariff since 2025 (foreigners 220 som/person + 80 for a car); ask for a receipt.
kg-0018.food: Trout grilled over charcoal by the river in the yurt camps (a guide of ≈1000 som/person for lunch in a yurt on jeep tours, 2026; reviews note inflated prices), mountain honey, kumys and ayran from shepherds, flatbreads, shashlik. The river water is glacial — drink it only after boiling.
kg-0018.reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 350 ratings, ≈100 reviews (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Grigorevskoye Canyon): 4.8/5, 36 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: no unambiguous card. Pluses: the scenery, the air, the river, trout, honey. Minuses: roads during repairs, pushy and dishonest horse handlers, inflated yurt prices, crowds in season, the post higher up the valley.
kg-0018.p.sum: There is one way in — from the village of Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu) on the north-shore road, 35 km east of Cholpon-Ata. A regular car can slowly reach the lower part of the gorge (the first ≈10 km to the meadows); to the upper lakes only by jeep or on foot/horseback. The most convenient option is a jeep tour from Cholpon-Ata combining the Grigorievka and Semyonovka gorges (from €35/person in a group, €215–250 per vehicle). On a budget — bus No. 401 or marshrutka No. 501 from Cholpon-Ata (≈200 som) and on foot; there is a forestry barrier at the entrance (foreigners 220 som + 80 for a car), and agree on the horse price before mounting.
