kg-0019.name: Kara-Keche Pass
kg-0019.near: The Kara-Keche coal miners’ settlement (open pit, ~3.6 km as the crow flies, ~2,800 m); the nearest village in the valley is Bash-Kuugandy (Bashkaingdy) at the mouth of the gorge: from there it is 75 km of dirt road to Song-Kol (dangerousroads, Too.kg). The district centre is Chayek.
kg-0019.elev: 3,384 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, OunTravela, dangerousroads, quad-offroad); other sources: 3,364 m (Nomad's Land), 3,348 m (Too.kg), ~3,350 m (Baibol).
kg-0019.short: The south-western road pass (about 3,384 m) from the Jumgal valley to Lake Song-Kol — through a gorge with red cliffs and the country’s largest coal open pit.
kg-0019.desc: Kara-Keche is a pass in the Moldo-Too mountains separating the Jumgal valley from the Song-Kol basin. The road climbs through the 50-km Kara-Keche gorge, where reddish rock slopes contrast with spruce groves; at about 2,800 m there is an open coal pit, the largest coal deposit in Kyrgyzstan, with a small blue lake in the spoil heap. Thanks to the pit the dirt road is kept passable, but heavy coal trucks use it constantly. From the saddle you get a view of Song-Kol and of the gorge. The pass is popular with cyclists and off-road drivers; Nomad's Land calls it the most car-accessible pass to Song-Kol, and OunTravela calls it stony but well kept.
kg-0019.guide: Use Kara-Keche if you are heading to Song-Kol from the west — from Suusamyr, Chayek or the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons: it is the most logical route and ties the lake and the Jumgal valley into one loop. On the climb, stop at the viewpoint above the coal pit — the little blue lake among the black spoil heaps looks unexpected. From the saddle Song-Kol is the first thing to open up — the best shot is in clear weather before noon. Let the coal “Shacman” trucks pass at narrow spots and do not stand in the cloud of dust behind them. Do not drink river water below the pit — take it from springs.
kg-0019.see: The panorama of Song-Kol from the saddle; the Kara-Keche gorge with red cliffs and spruce groves; the open coal pit with the blue lake on the spoil heap; the jailoo (summer pasture) on the south-western shore of Song-Kol; in the valley — Jumgal and the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons.
kg-0019.skip: You are going to Song-Kol from Kochkor — Kalmak-Ashuu is much closer. You dislike dust and heavy truck traffic on a narrow dirt road. You want a beautiful serpentine for its own sake — Moldo-Ashuu is more spectacular.
kg-0019.diff: Moderate for a driver: a stony but maintained dirt road (OunTravela), a climb to ~3,384 m, heavy truck traffic. TripAdvisor: “quite a normal road”, but a 4×4 is needed. For cyclists — a long climb (used on bike tours).
kg-0019.when: Late June — September. All passes to Song-Kol are blocked by snow until June (OunTravela); TripAdvisor notes Kara-Keche as one of the last passes to open. Safe from June to September (dangerousroads); snow lies at Song-Kol for 180–200 days a year.
kg-0019.hours: An open road with no barriers; the coal miners use it year-round up to the pit (~2,800 m), but the section over the saddle to Song-Kol is closed by snow in winter and spring. There is no official schedule — ask drivers in Chayek/Kochkor.
kg-0019.daytime: Morning until noon: clear weather and a view of Song-Kol, fewer clouds; towards evening — thunderstorms and fog at altitude.
kg-0019.how: From the Jumgal valley (the Kochkor — Chayek — Suusamyr/Kazarman road): from the village of Bash-Kuugandy go south through the Kara-Keche gorge past the coal pit to the pass and on to the south-western shore of Song-Kol — about 75 km of dirt road in all (dangerousroads). Nomad's Land offers a Song-Kol — Kara-Keche — Kyzyl-Korgon route. The drive to Song-Kol over the pass takes 4–4.5 h (TripAdvisor review).
kg-0019.needcar: Yes: a 4×4 or a high-clearance crossover (OunTravela/TripAdvisor recommend a 4×4); there is no public transport over the pass. Alternatives are a bicycle or a horse route.
kg-0019.self: Yes, in your own 4×4; no permits. The road is easy to find — it follows the coal trucks up to the pit. Above the pit there are few people; at Song-Kol itself there are yurts in summer.
kg-0019.roadtype: Dirt/gravel from Bash-Kuugandy to Song-Kol (~75 km), stony but maintained because of the coal pit; coal grit and stones on the surface; heavy trucks. Above the pit to the saddle — a mountain dirt road with steep gradients (OunTravela).
kg-0019.traveltime: Bash-Kuugandy — Song-Kol over the pass: 4–4.5 h (TripAdvisor). From Bishkek to Chayek ~5–6 h (estimate); Bishkek — Song-Kol via Kara-Keche is a long day.
kg-0019.stay: There are no cafes, shops or hotels in the gorge (Too.kg); plenty of spots for a tent, and springs. The nearest overnights are yurt camps on the south-western and southern shores of Song-Kol (budget $10–25 with meals, 2025–2026) and guesthouses in Chayek/the Jumgal valley (prices not confirmed).
kg-0019.net: There is mobile coverage in the Kara-Keche gorge (Too.kg, 2023 — probably from the coal pit’s towers); the operator is not stated. On the saddle and at Song-Kol the signal is unstable or absent.
kg-0019.entry: Free: no fees for driving over the pass are mentioned in any source.
kg-0019.transfer: No published prices for a 4×4 specifically via Kara-Keche were found. A guide for Song-Kol: 2,500–3,500 som per car from Kochkor (visitkyrgyzstan.org); the Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka (minibus) 350 som (May 2026).
kg-0019.bring: A warm jacket and hat (snow is possible at 3,384 m in summer), a spare tyre, spring water or a supply (river water below the pit is unfit — Too.kg), a mask/buff against coal dust, cash, offline maps.
kg-0019.warn: Heavy coal-truck traffic: dust, narrow spots, stones on the road. Do not drink river water below the pit. The pass is one of the last to open (snow until June). Weather at altitude changes fast — fog and snow are possible in summer.
kg-0019.food: There are no eateries on the pass. In Song-Kol yurts — kumys, beshbarmak, boorsok, kaymak; in Chayek — roadside cafes (lagman, manty). Dishes at specific places were not checked.
kg-0019.reviews: Google Maps: 4/5, 12 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Kara-Keche Pass): 4.4/5, 7 reviews (2015 — February 2020; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: stunning views in clear weather, an alternative route to Song-Kol from Jumgal. Cons: the coal pit and trucks, the pass opens late, little public transport.
kg-0019.p.sum: Kara-Keche is the north-western “gateway” to Song-Kol from the Jumgal valley: from the village of Bash-Kuugandy (Chayek area) ≈75 km of gravel past the coal pit to the south-western shore, 4–4.5 h, best in a 4×4. Open from late June to September. IMPORTANT: on 3 July 2026 a mudflow destroyed a bridge at km 30–32 of the Dyikan — Kara-Keche — Moldo-Ashuu road, and passage was fully closed with no restoration date — check the status before the trip (Kyrgyzkomur, local drivers). It makes the most sense to use the pass on the way out from Song-Kol to the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons and Suusamyr.

kg-0020.name: Ak-Sai Canyons
kg-0020.near: The village of Ak-Sai on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, ≈16 km west of Bokonbaevo; the canyons begin 5 km from the Balykchy–Karakol highway (or from the village itself) and stretch toward the lake, ending ≈1 km from the shore.
kg-0020.elev: ≈1750 m (average height of the canyons per smapse/LJ 2024); a range of ≈1650 m near the lake to ≈1900 m in the foothills (estimated from the lake level of 1607 m).
kg-0020.short: A system of dry erosion channels and light sandstone canyons between the village of Ak-Sai and the south shore of Issyk-Kul, covering more than 15 km². The “Valley of Forgotten Rivers” bears traces of streams that fill only in snowy springs. A wild, empty place with a view of the lake from the ridges; access by gravel road/channels in an SUV.
kg-0020.desc: The Ak-Sai canyons lie on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, 200 km from Bishkek and 130 km from Karakol, 16 km from Bokonbaevo. This is not one canyon but a network of branching channels in layered deposits — red, yellow, orange and white — carved by spring floods that have become rarer in recent years: hence the local name “Valley of Forgotten Rivers”. The main channel, about 11 km long, runs from the highway to the lake and ends a kilometer from the water; the track runs along it too — sand and gravel with many dry side channels, impassable after rain. From the ridges there are panoramas of the lake and Terskey Ala-Too; there are no marked trails, but there is a short route, “Ak-Sai Panorama”, of ≈2 km with an 80 m ascent. There is no infrastructure — no shade, water or shops; the nearest place to stay is the Remote. Forgotten Rivers lodge (the Ak-Sai Travel team) next to the canyons, and guesthouses and yurts in Bokonbaevo. The landscapes have been filmed for series and movies as an “alien planet”. Names like “Sun Peak”, “Bridge Through Time” and “Ancient Trail” from old descriptions are not confirmed on the map.
kg-0020.guide: Come here for the silence: unlike Skazka, there are no buses and no barrier with a cashier, only wind and the rustle of sand under the wheels. The main channel is like a road in a movie: 11 km between white walls, where the car drives right along the bed of a dried-up river, so take an SUV and watch the sky over the mountains — a downpour in Terskey turns the channel into a torrent. Climb any ridge — the blue strip of Issyk-Kul against the sun-bleached canyons is exactly that “Martian” shot. The best light is in the evening: the white and yellow layers glow orange, while by day the landscape fades. Combine it with Salt Lake Tuz-Kol 13 km away — after the dust of the canyons, floating on the water as in the Dead Sea feels especially good.
kg-0020.see: The main dry channel (≈11 km) with white and red walls; branching side canyons; layered colored deposits; ridges with a panorama of Issyk-Kul; the “Ak-Sai Panorama” route (2 km, +80 m); sunset over the lake; the neighboring salt lake Tuz-Kol (13 km).
kg-0020.skip: If you have an ordinary passenger car and it has rained — the channels turn soft, and there is no tow truck here. If you have already been to Skazka and the “Mars” canyons and expect brighter colors — Ak-Sai is paler, its strength lies in scale and solitude. If you don't have 4–5 hours for the road from Bishkek one way.
kg-0020.diff: Easy for a walk along the channel and ridges (1–3 h, ascent up to 100 m), but with no trails or shade; moderate for the driver: 5–13 km of gravel and sandy channels, an SUV at minimum, 4×4 is better.
kg-0020.when: May to October; spring and autumn are optimal (mild temperatures after the dry period); in summer only morning/evening. Don't go after rain or during snowmelt (soft clay, mudflows). In winter — ice and sticky clay.
kg-0020.hours: Open around the clock, a free territory without fences or ticket booths (Trip.com 2026: “24/7”).
kg-0020.daytime: Evening 1–2 hours before sunset — warm light on the light-colored layers and a sunset over the lake; morning — for coolness. Midday — faded colors and heat.
kg-0020.how: From Bishkek along the highway through Balykchy and the south shore to the village of Ak-Sai (≈200 km, 4–5 h), turn off the highway to the south/toward the canyons; then 5–13 km of gravel and channels. From Karakol ≈130 km (1.5–2 h to the turnoff). Without a car: a marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek → Bokonbaevo or Ak-Sai, then a local taxi (Trip.com 2026). Navigation is unreliable — use an offline map and the “Ak-Sai Canyons” point in Google Maps; agree on the turnoff with the lodge/driver.
kg-0020.needcar: Yes: an SUV at minimum, 4×4 recommended (I Love KG); according to a 2026 review an ordinary car can manage 5–7 km of dry dirt road, but not the channels after rain. On foot 5 km from the highway is possible, but without shade and water.
kg-0020.self: Yes, if you have an SUV, an offline map and dry weather; there are no trails or signs — navigate by the channels and ridges, and tell someone your route (I Love KG).
kg-0020.roadtype: The Bishkek–Balykchy–south shore highway is paved road of excellent quality; from the highway/village there are 5–13 km of gravel and sandy dry channels (“heavy gravel”, I Love KG; “the last 5–7 km is dirt road”, Trip.com 2026). Impassable after rain, dangerous in a thunderstorm.
kg-0020.traveltime: From Bishkek 4–5 h to the village of Ak-Sai; from Karakol 1.5–2 h; from Bokonbaevo ≈30 min; along the channel to the viewpoints 20–40 min in a 4×4. A visit takes 1–3 h.
kg-0020.stay: Remote. Forgotten Rivers is a lodge by the canyons from the Ak-Sai Travel team (booking.com; prices on request, not confirmed); Bokonbaevo: CBT guesthouses, Bel-Tam Yurt Camp on the shore, private rooms; yurt camps on the south shore (Tosor, Kaji-Sai). A 2024 benchmark for south-shore prices — from 1600 ₽/person in yurt camps.
kg-0020.net: There is a signal in the village of Ak-Sai and in Bokonbaevo (Beeline strengthened Bokonbaevo in 04.2026, economist.kg); in the canyon channels reception is unstable — I Love KG advises saving an offline map and telling someone your route. There are no operator measurements.
kg-0020.entry: Sources conflict: Trip.com (May, no year) — “entry is free”; the 2026 Trip.com guide — “eco fee 50–100 som, parking free”; Putevye istorii 2022, smapse 2024, Kabar 2024 do not mention fees; Sputnik8 includes “all fees” in its tour. Not confirmed: the current fee and who collects it. Most likely free or an irregular local fee.
kg-0020.transfer: From Bishkek: a taxi/transfer 6000–10,000 som round trip, a group tour 1500–3500 som/person (Trip.com 2026); Sputnik8 excursions $330 / Tripster €345 per car (2026). A local taxi from Bokonbaevo — price not confirmed (south-shore benchmark 2024: 1500 som per car with a wait to Skazka).
kg-0020.bring: 2 L of water per person, closed shoes, a hat, sunscreen, a windbreaker, cash in som, an offline map/GPS, a first-aid kit, a reserve of fuel (fuel stations in Balykchy and Bokonbaevo), and for a 4×4 — a shovel and tow rope.
kg-0020.warn: Dry channels turn into mudflows when it rains in the mountains — don't enter or park in narrow canyons in a thunderstorm. The walls are unstable — don't stand under overhangs. There is no shade, water, signal or help; navigators lead the wrong way — agree on the turnoff with locals. “Sun Peak” and “Bridge Through Time” from old descriptions are unconfirmed landmarks. Soft clay in winter and spring bogs down even SUVs.
kg-0020.food: There is nothing in the canyons. The nearest food is the cafes and canteens of Bokonbaevo (lagman, manty, Issyk-Kul fish), home-cooked lunches in CBT guesthouses; at the Remote. Forgotten Rivers lodge — meals for guests (not confirmed). Bring food and water with you.
kg-0020.reviews: Google Maps: there is no separate listing with a rating in the data export (ambiguous result). Reports 2022–2026 (Putevye istorii, smapse/LJ, Trip.com, Tripster 4.9 for the tour organizer): pros — solitude, “Martian” scale, views of the lake, sunsets; cons — a hard road, no infrastructure or signs, paler in color than Skazka.
kg-0020.p.sum: The canyons lie by the village of Ak-Sai on the south shore, ≈16 km west of Bokonbaevo: from the highway, following signs, 5–13 km of gravel and sandy dry channels to a spot at the edge of the canyons, then 30 minutes on foot to the panorama (the “Ak Sai Panorama” route ≈2 km, +80 m). You need a car with ground clearance, preferably a 4×4 (let air out of the tires in sand); don't go during or after rain. Without your own car — a taxi from Bokonbaevo through CBT or a tour from Bishkek ($330 / €345 per car for 10 h). It is convenient to stay in Bokonbaevo or on the beach at Ton (Bel-Tam, from $17–23).

kg-0021.name: Kok-Jaiyk Valley
kg-0021.full: Kok-Jaiyk Valley (“Valley of Flowers”, Kok-Jaiyk jailoo (summer pasture) in the Jeti-Oguz gorge)
kg-0021.near: The Jeti-Oguz resort (a sanatorium, ≈4 km in a straight line, 6–8 km by road up the gorge); the village of Jeti-Oguz is at the mouth of the gorge; Karakol is 25–28 km away.
kg-0021.elev: ≈2,300 m at the Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp (Destination Jeti-Oguz); Nomad's Land gives 2,540 m for the meadows higher up; the valley rises from ≈2,200 m (the sanatorium) to ≈2,600 m.
kg-0021.short: A wide high-mountain meadow at the head of the Jeti-Oguz gorge above the red “Seven Bulls” cliffs: summer pastures with yurts, flowering meadows in June, birch and spruce groves, and the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (≈40 m) in a side gorge. Accessible by car (6–8 km of dirt road with bridges) or on foot in 3 h from the resort.
kg-0021.desc: Kok-Jaiyk (“green meadow”, which tourists call the “Valley of Flowers”) begins where the narrow Jeti-Oguz gorge, after the fifth wooden bridge, suddenly opens into a spacious valley with boulders, hayfields and yurts on the slopes. It is one of the main summer pastures of the southern shore: in May–June the meadows are covered with flowers, and in winter with snow. From the Jeti-Oguz resort (with its hydrogen sulfide springs at 2,200 m) 6–8 km of bumpy dirt road with five bridges over the river lead here — an SUV can drive it, and in summer ordinary cars can too at low speed; the entrance to the gorge is paid, through a barrier of the Jeti-Oguz forestry enterprise. In the valley there are family yurt camps with meals and horses; from them trails start to the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (Maiden’s Tears; ≈300 m through spruce forest from the upper yurts, and according to reviews the trail disappears among the branches) and farther on — to Oguz-Bashi Peak (5,181 m), to Teleti and to Lake Ala-Kul. Above the valley there are views of the snow-capped peaks of the Terskey Ala-Too.
kg-0021.guide: Go in June: Kok-Jaiyk is not called the “Valley of Flowers” for nothing — the slopes are then blue and yellow with lupine and buttercups, and by August they are mown. Count the bridges: after the fifth the road comes out onto the meadow — stop there, because farther on cars only get in the way. To the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall go from the yurts along the path through the spruce forest, without turning onto the livestock tracks — travelers regularly add an extra 1.5 km; it is easier with a horse and a local guide. Ask your yurt hosts for kumis and flatbreads, not just a photo with a golden eagle: shepherds still live here, it is not only an “attraction”. If you want more, a trek starts here through Teleti to Ala-Kul and the Karakol gorge, 2–3 days.
kg-0021.see: The meadow with yurts and boulders; flowering meadows (May–June); the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (~40 m); birch and spruce groves; views of Oguz-Bashi (5,181 m); on the way — the red “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” cliffs; the Jeti-Oguz sanatorium with hot springs.
kg-0021.skip: If you have already seen the Seven Bulls and do not have 2–3 hours for the dirt road and a walk — the meadow is beautiful, but it is “one more jailoo”. If you go in August after the haymaking and expect a “valley of flowers” — the flowers are gone. If you are in a low-clearance car after rain — the bridges and ruts will be a problem.
kg-0021.diff: Easy for the drive and a stroll on the meadow; to the waterfall — a short but choppy climb through the forest (30–60 min); on foot from the resort — 3 h, 6–8 km, gain ≈300–400 m. Further treks — moderate/high.
kg-0021.when: Late May–June (flowering), July–August (yurts, the season), September (gold, few people). In winter the valley is accessible with snow, the yurts do not operate (Nomad's Land: year-round). In spring after the thaw — mud and high water at the bridges.
kg-0021.hours: Open 24 hours; the forestry barrier at the gorge entrance — paid passage in the daytime in season (Kaktus, 06.2025); the yurt camps — roughly June–September.
kg-0021.daytime: Morning (leave Karakol at 8:00–9:00 per Destination Karakol’s recommendation) — light on the red cliffs on the way and coolness on the climb to the waterfall; return by 16:00 on a marshrutka (minibus) from the resort.
kg-0021.how: From Karakol: marshrutka No. 372 or a shared taxi from the Ak-Tilek bazaar to the Jeti-Oguz resort — 100 som/person (in summer some trips may end in the village — ask for “Jeti-Oguz kurort”); a taxi ≈1,800 som per car one way (Destination Karakol). From the resort — 6–8 km up the gorge by car (5 bridges) or 3 h on foot. From Bishkek — ≈5 h by car to Jeti-Oguz.
kg-0021.needcar: Not necessarily: a marshrutka to the resort + 3 h on foot. By car an SUV/crossover is advisable (bumps, bridges); in summer in dry weather ordinary cars get through.
kg-0021.self: Yes: the road is obvious (up the gorge across the bridges), the meadow is open; for the waterfall it is better to ask the yurt hosts for directions or take a guide.
kg-0021.roadtype: Karakol → resort — paved; above the resort 6–8 km of dirt road with bumps, climbs and five wooden bridges (ZigZag on Earth; varandej); in 2018 — 7 km of gravel to the yurts (frantsouzov). Passable for an SUV; after rain — only 4×4. Inside the valley — trails.
kg-0021.traveltime: Karakol → Jeti-Oguz resort 30–40 min; resort → meadow 20–30 min by car or ≈3 h on foot; meadow → waterfall 30–60 min on foot. A full day from Karakol — 8–9 h with lunch.
kg-0021.stay: Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp (Destination Jeti-Oguz, jetioguz.travel) — yurts at 2,300 m, national cuisine, horseback outings; prices on request via a form. Family yurt camps in the valley — through CBT Karakol (ZigZag on Earth: mattresses, Western toilets, a shower in one of the camps). The Jeti-Oguz sanatorium below. 2026 prices are not published.
kg-0021.net: Beeline strengthened its network in Jeti-Oguz in April 2026 (economist.kg) — there is a signal at the village and the resort; in the Kok-Jaiyk valley beyond the bridges the reception is weak/absent according to reports, there are no measurements. Offline map.
kg-0021.entry: Passage through the barrier of the Jeti-Oguz forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): car 50–80 som, large vehicles 100–250, buses 200–300 som per entry; pedestrians in Jeti-Oguz do not pay (the fee is charged only on vehicles). Earlier (2018) ≈200 rubles were charged per car. The waterfall and the meadow — no separate fee.
kg-0021.transfer: Marshrutka 100 som/person; taxi 1,800 som per car one way (Destination Karakol); MYWAY 8,000 som round trip with waiting (2026); a Tripster excursion €240 per group (2026).
kg-0021.bring: Shoes for forest and rocks, a windbreaker/fleece (it is cool at 2,300–2,500 m), a rain jacket, cash som (barrier, yurts, horses), water, repellent, sun protection.
kg-0021.warn:
Since 21.07.2025 there has been an eco-post at the Kok-Jaiyk entrance: private cars are not allowed onto the pasture (24.kg). Go up on foot, on horseback or by permitted transport.

Do not swim in the river — icy water and a strong current; do not approach horses and cows from behind (ZigZag). The trail to the waterfall disappears in the spruce forest — it is easy to wander onto livestock tracks. The bridges are wooden — check their condition after a flood. Drones lose their compass in the narrow gorge (2018 report). The entry is paid through the forestry enterprise, demand a receipt.
kg-0021.food: In the valley’s yurts: kumis, kaymak and flatbreads, lagman, manti, soups, pancakes (ZigZag); lunch in a yurt is included in the Tripster excursions. At the Jeti-Oguz resort — the sanatorium canteen; in Karakol — ashlyan-fu and Dungan cuisine.
kg-0021.reviews: The site has no Google listing (ambiguous result). According to reports from 2013–2026 (varandej, frantsouzov, ZigZag on Earth, 24.kg readers, a Tripster organizer 4.9): pros — space, flowers, yurts with living everyday life, the waterfall; cons — the bumpy road, the trail to the waterfall that gets lost, and in summer many local picnickers.
kg-0021.p.sum: Kok-Jaiyk is a meadow valley above the Jeti-Oguz resort, 25–28 km from Karakol. From Karakol: marshrutka No. 355/372 to the resort (≈100 som) or a taxi (1,000–1,800 som one way), then 6–8 km of dirt road with five wooden bridges — by crossover/jeep (after rain only 4×4) or 2.5–3 h on foot. It is worth staying overnight in a yurt camp at 2,300 m (from $13 at Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp to $50 with breakfast at Ecotrek), and in the morning going to the waterfall (2.5 km, +161 m) and riding across the meadows. Vehicle entry through the forestry barrier is paid (50–80 som), pedestrians do not pay.

kg-0022.name: Shamsi Gorge
kg-0022.near: The villages of Koshoy and Shamshy where the gorge opens into the Chu Valley; the city of Tokmok is further down the valley. From Bishkek it is about 100–105 km (too.kg, hiking.kg). The earlier value “Karagul ~6.2 km” was calculated from an erroneous catalogue point.
kg-0022.elev: Shamsi Pass — 3570 m (eurasia.travel); the lower part of the gorge where it opens into the Chu Valley — about 1000–1500 m (estimate, not confirmed). The elevation gain on walking routes from the parking lot is up to 300 m (hiking.kg).
kg-0022.short: Shamsi is a little-known wooded gorge of the Shamshy River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range ~100 km east of Bishkek, with the side gorge of Tuyuk, spruce forests and a pass into the Kochkor valley.
kg-0022.desc: Shamsi Gorge (Shamshy) stretches from the Chu Valley near the villages of Koshoy and Shamshy south to Shamsi Pass (3570 m), which historically linked the Chu and Kochkor valleys. The slopes are covered with dense coniferous forests, with subalpine meadows higher up; the side river Tuyuk, with a cascade of waterfalls and a lake at its head, flows into the gorge (24.kg, 2017). Wild boar, lynx, hares and ermine live here (eurasia.travel). The gorge is associated with the Shamshy hoard: in 1958 a gold mask from a woman's burial was found in a burial mound at its mouth — according to local legend, the mask of “Princess Shamsi” (24.kg). Too.kg mentions the “Shah's house”, built in 1968 for a visit by the Shah of Iran. There is no infrastructure: no shops, cafes or guesthouses — only places for tents and picnics.
kg-0022.guide: Shamsi is for those who want forest and quiet two hours from Bishkek without the crowds of Ala-Archa. Leave your car at the parking lot in the gorge and walk along the Shamsi or turn into the Tuyuk valley: 2–8 km, up to 300 m of gain, easy trails. Ask locals about the 1968 “Shah's house” — it was built for a visit by the Shah of Iran. Remember that a gold mask was found in a burial mound at the mouth of the gorge in 1958 — according to legend, that of “Princess Shamsi”. There's no signal and no shops, so bring everything with you and don't forget to take your litter out.
kg-0022.see: Coniferous forests and the Shamsi river valley; the side gorge of Tuyuk with a cascade of waterfalls (24.kg); viewpoints and picnic spots (hiking.kg); the 1968 “Shah's house” (too.kg); for the experienced — Shamsi Pass (3570 m) and treks toward Song-Kol (silkroadexplore).
kg-0022.skip: You need infrastructure — cafes, guesthouses and mobile signal are absent here. You have no car: there is no public transport into the gorge. You're looking for “wow” views of glaciers — Shamsi is more of a calm forest gorge.
kg-0022.diff: A walk in the lower valley is relatively easy; crossings of high passes are separate, demanding routes.
kg-0022.when: May — October: the dirt road is passable, the meadows are green (May — June) or golden (September — October). In winter and in the muddy season the road in the upper reaches and the fords become hard to pass (editorial, based on hiking.kg on fords).
kg-0022.hours: A natural area with no regime and no barrier with a fee (too.kg: free entry). The sources mention no access restrictions.
kg-0022.daytime: Morning — fewer cars on the dirt road and soft light in the forest; for a night in a tent — the evening by the river (editorial).
kg-0022.how: Via Tokmok, Koshoy and Shamshy; then along the river. Choose where to park according to the condition of the dirt road and your car's capabilities.
kg-0022.needcar: To get there — a private car or a booked car; Too.kg doesn't mention any regular transport into the gorge.
kg-0022.self: Yes: free entry, no permits needed (too.kg). You need your own or a booked car, preferably with good ground clearance.
kg-0022.roadtype: A dirt road along the Shamsi and Tuyuk, deteriorating in the upper reaches; there are fords.
kg-0022.traveltime: Hiking.kg guideline: 105 km / 2 hours from Bishkek; walks from the parking lot — up to 7.8 km and 2 h 20 min for the chosen option, gain up to 300 m.
kg-0022.stay: The source describes tent camps; it doesn't confirm any operating hotels or bookings in the gorge itself.
kg-0022.net: Too.kg's description says there is no signal; the date of the check and the operator are not given.
kg-0022.entry: Too.kg calls entry free but gives no effective date. There is no confirmed rate for 2026.
kg-0022.transfer: Not confirmed: no 2025–2026 prices for a taxi/transfer to Shamsi were found. Guidelines: a taxi Bishkek — Burana 1500–2200 som one way (asiaodysseytravel 2026, a nearby destination); Sputnik8 tours “Tuyuk Gorge and the Burana Tower” — $210 per group.
kg-0022.bring: All your food and water (no shops; boil river water — too.kg), a tent and warm clothes for a night out, an offline map (no signal), shoes you don't mind getting wet at the fords, litter bags.
kg-0022.warn: There is no mobile signal (too.kg) — tell someone your route. Fords and a deteriorating dirt road in the upper reaches; after rain the road turns soggy (hiking.kg). Drink river water only after boiling — livestock graze here. Shamsi Pass (3570 m) is a serious mountain route, not a stroll.
kg-0022.food: There are no cafes in the gorge (too.kg). Bring food with you; the nearest eateries are in Tokmok and roadside cafes on the Bishkek — Balykchy highway (editorial). In summer you can ask shepherds for kumis.
kg-0022.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 20 ratings/reviews per the card's counter as of 03.10.2026. The review texts were not used to confirm prices, roads or safety.
kg-0022.p.sum: Shamsi is a forest gorge with no infrastructure ≈100–110 km (≈2 h) from Bishkek via Tokmok and the villages of Koshoy/Shamshy: there is no public transport into the gorge, so you need your own car with good clearance (further up the gorge it is dirt road and fords) or a jeep tour (Sputnik8/Tripster $210–235, €206 per car). The most interesting format is a horse ride to Shamsi Pass with lunch with a family (Eurasia Travel, $130–315/person). There is no signal, shops or cafes — bring food, water and a gas stove; the best time is May — October.

kg-0023.name: Tuz-Kol, Dead Lake
kg-0023.near: Kyzyl-Tuu and Kara-Koo on the Balykchy–Karakol highway (south shore), km 56–73 from Balykchy; from the highway to the lake there are 12–14 km of gravel road. The lake lies 400 m to 1 km from the shore of Issyk-Kul.
kg-0023.elev: ≈1609–1611 m (geocaching 1609 m, Nomad's Land 1611 m, Baibol 1600 m) — practically at the level of Issyk-Kul (1607 m).
kg-0023.short: A small hypersaline lake near the south shore of Issyk-Kul, separated from the big lake by a narrow strip of land: salinity up to 236 g/L seasonally (as in the Dead Sea), the water holds you afloat, and on the bottom there are healing muds of three colors. A paid fenced area with yurts, a cafe and a shower; 12–14 km of gravel road from the highway.
kg-0023.desc: Tuz-Kol (“salt lake”) is a separate body of water with a shoreline of ≈1.5 km and a depth of up to 11 m, a kilometer from Issyk-Kul, between the villages of Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu. Salinity changes with the season from ≈62 to 236 g/L, so in summer people lie in the water as if on a mattress, and in winter the lake does not freeze. On the bottom and shores there are black, blue and green muds, which people smear on “for psoriasis and joints”; there is no fresh water nearby, and you have to rinse off the salt in a paid shower. Until the 2000s the place was little known, and since the 2010s it has become popular: the farmers' cooperative “Gulistan” fenced off the territory (since 2014 a per-person and per-car fee has been charged by decision of the local kenesh), and yurts, a cafe, changing cabins, toilets and a shower appeared. The approach is 12–14 km of gravel road with bends and bumps from the highway after Kesken-Bel Pass; it is better not to drive down to the sandy shore without 4WD. In 2021 tourists complained of charges without receipts and poor sanitation (24.kg), in 2018 of litter, after which “order was restored” with separate waste collection. The Ak-Sai canyons are 13 km away, so the two are often combined in one day.
kg-0023.guide: Enter the water slowly and don't dive: at 200+ g/L of salt a drop in the eye means a minute of tears, and any scratch will immediately remind you of itself. Lie on your back and lift your feet — here it happens by itself, as in the Dead Sea, and the “reading a newspaper in the water” photo is a must. Take mud from the bottom near the shore, smear it on and let it dry in the sun, then wash it off — only in the paid shower, there is no fresh water at the lake at all. It is better to come in July–August: the water is warmed, and salinity is higher by the end of summer, so it “holds” you more. Bring water shoes, drinking water and cash: entry, the shower and the toilet are paid here, and a receipt is not always given.
kg-0023.see: Floating “lying down” on hypersaline water; healing muds of three colors; a view of Issyk-Kul and Terskey Ala-Too across the isthmus; a salt crust on the shores; yurts; sunset over the lake; nearby — the Ak-Sai canyons and Kesken-Bel Pass.
kg-0023.skip: If you have wounds, acute eczema or you are with small children — concentrated salt burns. If you expect the cleanliness of the Dead Sea with infrastructure — here there are simple yurts, two toilets and a 50 som shower, and reviews say it can be dirty. If you aren't ready for 12–14 km of bumpy gravel road for an hour of swimming.
kg-0023.diff: Easy: a drive to the site, swimming and a walk along the shore; the only difficulty is the road (gravel, sand) and the lack of shade/fresh water.
kg-0023.when: June to September for swimming (the water is warm, salinity rises toward the end of summer); the lake doesn't freeze — it is accessible year-round, but the infrastructure works in season. Peak is July–August, weekends are crowded.
kg-0023.hours: A fenced area of the cooperative; the ticket booth/barrier works in daylight in season; there are no official hours. Google Maps: no hours given (meta).
kg-0023.daytime: Midday to early evening for swimming (water and air are warmed); sunset for photos. The water is cooler in the morning.
kg-0023.how: Along the Balykchy–Karakol highway on the south shore to km 56–73 (between Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu), after Kesken-Bel Pass turn onto the gravel road toward the lake — 12–14 km to the parking area. From Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h, from Karakol ≈3 h. By public transport — a marshrutka (minibus) to Kara-Koo/Kyzyl-Tuu and then a taxi/12 km on foot (inconvenient).
kg-0023.needcar: Yes: 12–14 km of gravel road; in dry weather an ordinary car can manage with careful driving, but to the sandy shore only with 4WD (cars get stuck). On foot from the highway is unrealistic with luggage in the heat.
kg-0023.self: Yes: paid entry, the site is obvious, no guide needed. You can arrange a tent with the owners of the territory (Too.kg).
kg-0023.roadtype: Paved highway; 12–14 km of gravel road with frequent bends and bumps (geocaching: 12.2 km by odometer); the last stretch at the shore is sand, where cars get stuck without 4×4. Too.kg: “poor quality of the last section, an off-road vehicle is needed”.
kg-0023.traveltime: From the highway to the lake 20–30 min; from Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h; from Bokonbaevo ≈40 min; from Karakol ≈3 h. On site — 1–3 h.
kg-0023.stay: Yurts at the lake ≈1000 som/night, beds in cabins 150–250 som (2014, geocaching — outdated); Too.kg: yurts, a cafe, a shower and a toilet on the fenced territory, a tent by arrangement and for a fee. Vera guesthouse at the Salt Lake (video/veratravel.ru, not confirmed). Current 2025–2026 prices are not published; alternatives are guesthouses in Bokonbaevo and Tosor, and south-shore yurt camps.
kg-0023.net: Too.kg: there is a signal, but weak (no date or operator). In April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Bokonbaevo; Kara-Koo/Kyzyl-Tuu are not named. There is a signal by the highway.
kg-0023.entry: History: 2014 — 50 som/adult + 150 per car (geocaching); since 2014 by decision of the ail kenesh (village council) — 100 som/person + 150 per car (24.kg 08.2018, Too.kg); 2021 — 150 som/person, toilet 5, shower 50 som, no receipts (24.kg 07.2021). Not confirmed: the 2025–2026 rate (expected 150–200 som/person + a car fee). The fee is private (the Gulistan cooperative).
kg-0023.transfer: No public price lists from carriers to Tuz-Kol were found. South-shore benchmarks 2024: a taxi with a wait ≈1500 som per car (Tosor–Skazka), a car Karakol–Tosor 5000 som; Sputnik8 excursions along the south shore — from $330–430 per group (2026).
kg-0023.bring: Drinking water (there is no fresh water), water shoes, a towel, cash in small som notes (entry, shower 50, toilet 5), sun protection and a hat, goggles/don't rub your eyes, a bag for salty clothes, a sun umbrella.
kg-0023.warn: Salt of 100–236 g/L: don't dive, don't swallow the water, protect your eyes and cuts; be sure to rinse off the salt after swimming. There is no fresh water. The fee at the barrier is private, and receipts are not always issued (24.kg 2021); sanitation is basic. The sandy shore is a trap for cars without 4×4. Mud therapy for skin and heart conditions — with caution.
kg-0023.food: The cafe and yurts on the territory serve simple food (shashlik, lagman, tea) in season; the menu and prices are not published. The nearest cafes are in Kyzyl-Tuu, Kara-Koo and Bokonbaevo; on the south shore — smoked Issyk-Kul fish by the highway.
kg-0023.reviews: Google Maps: 4.3/5, 234 ratings (03.10.2026). Yandex/2GIS/TripAdvisor — listings not checked. Pros: “like the Dead Sea”, muds, views, an unusual experience. Cons (24.kg 2018, 2021; reports): charges without receipts, litter and poor sanitation at peak season, a bad road, no fresh water or shade.
kg-0023.p.sum: A salt lake on the south shore ≈60–73 km from Balykchy: from the highway between Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu (after Kesken-Bel Pass) 12–14 km of “washboard” gravel (≈30 min), the last stretch is sand. In dry weather ordinary cars get there too, but a crossover/4×4 is better; after rain it is impassable. Without a car — a taxi from Bokonbaevo/Balykchy (≈1500–1800 som) or south-shore tours. Entry ≈150 som/person (2025), shower 80–100, toilet 30 — bring plenty of fresh water, sandals and cash; it is convenient to combine with the Ak-Sai canyons (20–30 km east).

kg-0027.name: Holy Trinity Orthodox Church
kg-0027.full: Holy Trinity Orthodox Cathedral (Church of the Life-Giving Trinity), Karakol
kg-0027.near: Karakol, town center: Gagarin St., 16, at the intersection of Gagarin and Lenin streets, near the central square.
kg-0027.elev: ≈1760 m (Nomad's Land); the center of Karakol lies at 1690–1770 m.
kg-0027.short: A wooden five-domed Orthodox cathedral of 1895 in the center of Karakol — the tallest (26 m) and most photogenic building in town: a log frame of Tian Shan spruce on a granite base, carving, gilded onion domes, a bell tower. Inside is the Tikhvin Icon of the Mother of God (1897). Entry is free.
kg-0027.desc: The first church in Karakol (then Przhevalsk) was built in 1869 for the Cossacks and the garrison; an earthquake destroyed it (sources differ: 1876, 1887 or 1889). The new church was built from 1895 by craftsmen from Verny (Almaty) on an “earthquake-resistant” plan: a wooden log frame on granite blocks, three naves with a rectangular apse, five domes and a bell tower on the west side; the dimensions are ≈35.5 × 18 m, wall height 5.1 m, total height ≈26 m. A local legend says it was “built without a single nail”. After the revolution the church was closed: it housed a school, a gym, a theater and a coal warehouse; in 1961 it was finally closed to worshippers, in 1986 a three-year restoration began, in 1991–1992 the building was returned to the church, and in 1995 the restoration was completed. Today it is an active cathedral of the Bishkek and Kyrgyzstan Diocese of the Russian Orthodox Church: services follow the Julian calendar, and at Easter and Christmas there are big gatherings. Inside are carved walls, paintings, the Tikhvin Icon (1897) and a copy of Rublev's icon. It is part of a walking route around old Karakol together with the Dungan Mosque and the Przhevalsky Museum.
kg-0027.guide: Walk around the cathedral before going in: the carved window frames, the five domes and the bell tower read best from the corner of Gagarin and Lenin in morning light. Inside, find the Tikhvin Icon of 1897 — one of the few things that survived both the earthquake and the Soviet gym the church was turned into for half a century. Women are given a headscarf at the entrance; it is best to photograph inside with permission — according to reviews, the staff can be strict with tourists, especially during a service. Look in on a weekday morning or right after lunch: on weekends the gates are sometimes closed and services are held when “just looking” won't work. Combine the cathedral with the Dungan Mosque (1 km) — two wooden shrines of the late 19th century built without nails by different communities, and you get the best hour of a walk around old Karakol.
kg-0027.see: A five-domed wooden log building with carving and gilded domes; the bell tower; the Tikhvin Icon of the Mother of God (1897); paintings and carved walls of the interior; the granite base; a garden with flower beds; the neighboring Dungan Mosque (1910) and the Przhevalsky Museum on the route.
kg-0027.skip: If you have 20 minutes in Karakol and have to choose between the cathedral and the Dungan Mosque — the mosque is more unusual for the region, while the cathedral resembles the wooden churches of Siberia. If you come on Sunday morning during the liturgy and don't want to disturb the service. If the gates are closed — don't insist, the staff sometimes turn tourists away (reviews).
kg-0027.diff: Minimal: a city walk, 20–40 minutes to look around, accessible to all.
kg-0027.when: Year-round. Summer — a green garden and blue domes against the mountains; winter — snow on the domes. Orthodox Easter and Christmas (7 January) bring processions and crowds of parishioners; Trinity is the patronal feast.
kg-0027.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): Mon–Sat 08:00–17:00, Sun 07:00–17:00. Nomad's Land: 8:00–17:00, “closed on Saturdays and Sundays” — probably meaning that services are held on weekends and there is no free sightseeing. The service schedule is with the parish (no official website with a schedule was found).
kg-0027.daytime: Morning 9:00–11:00 on weekdays — soft light on the eastern facade and open gates; closed in the evening.
kg-0027.how: On foot from the center of Karakol (Gagarin St., 16, corner of Lenin) — 5–15 minutes from the bus station/bazaar; city marshrutkas (minibuses) No. 109, No. 111 and others — 20 som (2024); a taxi in town — 100–150 som. From Bishkek to Karakol a marshrutka (minibus) costs 500–550 som, 6–6.5 h; the GoBus night bus 700 som (2025).
kg-0027.needcar: No: the site is in the town center, within walking distance.
kg-0027.self: Yes: entry is free during opening hours; a headscarf for women is provided at the entrance; no guide needed, there is an izi.Travel audio guide.
kg-0027.roadtype: Paved streets in the center of Karakol; the cathedral grounds have paths, and steps at the church entrance.
kg-0027.traveltime: 5–15 minutes on foot from the center/bus station of Karakol; a visit takes 20–40 minutes. From Bishkek 6–6.5 h by marshrutka (minibus), 5 h by car.
kg-0027.stay: Karakol is the region's main tourist hub: guesthouses and hostels (Snow Leopard Hostel, Karakol Guesthouse — from ≈$10 per bed), CBT Karakol guesthouses, mid-range hotels; prices 2024–2026: hostels $10–25/bed, guesthouses $50–80/room in season (freedom-travel 2026, benchmark for Issyk-Kul). Specific prices near the cathedral were not collected.
kg-0027.net: Town: 4G from all operators (Beeline, O!, MegaCom); in April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Karakol (economist.kg). No signal problems.
kg-0027.entry: Free (Too.kg: “entry is free, open to tourists”); donations and candles are optional. There are no paid tickets.
kg-0027.transfer: Not required; a city taxi 100–150 som (estimate based on Karakol rates, not confirmed by a price list); marshrutka (minibus) 20 som (2024).
kg-0027.bring: A headscarf for women (available at the entrance), clothing that covers shoulders and knees, cash for candles/donation, a camera (agree on photography inside).
kg-0027.warn: An active church: during services keep quiet, don't walk in front of the altar, photos inside only with permission; according to reviews, the staff sometimes close the gates to tourist groups. Dress code: women a headscarf, men remove their hats. The dates of the earthquake and of the church's return differ across sources (1876/1887/1889; 1991/1992).
kg-0027.food: Nearby in the center of Karakol: ashlan-fu (cold Dungan noodles) at the Ak-Tilek bazaar and in cafes near the central square, Dungan cuisine (lagman, manty, “ganfan”), Uyghur samsas; coffee shops in the center (Giraffe Coffee — the transfer meeting point). A specific establishment by the cathedral is not confirmed.
kg-0027.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 1111 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 231 reviews (103 “excellent”, 87 “very good”, 39 “good”, 2 negative), No. 3 of 40 in Karakol (07.10.2026). Pros: a beautiful wooden building, carving, domes, a quiet garden, the “without nails” story. Cons: closed gates/unfriendly staff (2017), little information for tourists, a short visit.
kg-0027.p.sum: The wooden Holy Trinity Cathedral stands in the center of Karakol (Gagarin St., 16, corner of Lenin) — 5–15 minutes on foot from the bus station and most hostels, entry is free. The easiest way to reach Karakol is a marshrutka (minibus) from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1, ≈500–600 som, 6–7 h), the GoBus night bus (700 som) or an Asman Airlines flight (from ≈4000 som). Come outside service times; women need a headscarf (provided at the entrance); in the same hour it is easy to continue to the Dungan Mosque and the Przhevalsky Museum by marshrutka (minibus)/taxi.

kg-0028.name: Kegety Waterfall
kg-0028.near: Kegety dachas (~4.5 km as the crow flies) and Kegety village at the mouth of the gorge; Tokmok — ~20 km to the gorge, Bishkek — 70–85 km (too.kg, hiking.kg).
kg-0028.elev: Drop height — about 30 m (too.kg). The absolute elevation above sea level is not confirmed: the gorge starts at ~1250 m and rises to a pass at ~4000 m (too.kg); the waterfall is in the lower-middle part, roughly 1800–2000 m (estimate, to be verified).
kg-0028.short: The first (big) waterfall of the Kegety gorge — a full-flowing stream about 30 m high, 200 m from the road, 2 hours' drive from Bishkek.
kg-0028.desc: Kegety Waterfall is the most accessible and best-known of several waterfalls in the Kegety gorge on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range. Too.kg describes it as a “small but full-flowing” stream about 30 m high with cold, clean water. It falls from a sheer rock face 200 m from the dirt road through the gorge — about 5 minutes on foot, ~30 m of ascent (hiking.kg). Opposite the waterfall in summer there are yurts serving food; further up the gorge is the branch to Lake Kol-Tor and trails to the upper waterfalls. The gorge stretches for ~27 km (too.kg); it is popular for day trips and picnics from Bishkek.
kg-0028.guide: Kegety Waterfall is an easy half-day target: the car stops almost at the foot, and 5 minutes on foot puts you in the spray of a 30 m stream. Come in the first half of the day: the sun lights up the jet and a rainbow sometimes forms above it. If you have more energy, climb the steep path above the waterfall to the viewpoints, or combine it with a hike to Kol-Tor (the fork is lower down the gorge). In summer there are yurts opposite the waterfall where you can have lunch. The rocks by the water are wet and slippery — shoes with good soles are a must.
kg-0028.see: The waterfall itself (~30 m) and the basin beneath it; viewpoints above the waterfall along the steep path; in winter, a partly frozen waterfall (video); in the gorge, the upper waterfalls, the Kol-Tor valley and yurts on the meadows.
kg-0028.skip: You're looking for a big, powerful waterfall — this one is modest (about 30 m), and hiking.kg rates the place 6/10. You don't want to drive 2+ hours for a 5-minute walk — then combine it with Kol-Tor or Burana. You have no car — public transport goes only as far as the village.
kg-0028.diff: Easy: 200 m from the road, ~5 min, ~30 m of ascent (hiking.kg). The climb above the waterfall is a separate steep section.
kg-0028.when: May to September: the road is dry, the water is fullest in late spring to early summer (snowmelt), and the yurts are open (too.kg). In winter the waterfall partly freezes and is photogenic too, but the dirt road may be covered in snow and ice (video of a winter visit; editorial).
kg-0028.hours: Google Maps, viewed 03.10.2026: Daily: open 24 hours. Check separately the ticket office hours and access to the routes.
kg-0028.daytime: Hiking.kg recommends the first half of the day for the light on the waterfall.
kg-0028.how: Via Krasnaya Rechka, Yuryevka, Syn-Tash and Rot-Front to Kegety. After the first bridge, at the fork, go right to the next bridge, then left, and about 5 km along the gorge.
kg-0028.needcar: Yes: a car or a tour. The marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek's Eastern Bus Station goes only as far as Kegety village (thegonegoat, asia-hikes); from there it's ~5 km up the gorge on foot or by hitching a ride.
kg-0028.self: Yes: no permits needed, the waterfall is by the road. At the entrance to the gorge there is a post charging an eco fee per car.
kg-0028.roadtype: Paved road on the approach gives way to a dirt road; a short path leads to the waterfall.
kg-0028.traveltime: Hiking.kg: 85 km / 2 h 15 min from Bishkek; from the road about 200 m / 5 minutes on foot, ascent about 30 m.
kg-0028.stay: Yurts opposite the first waterfall with meals; a small hotel beyond the first barrier; a guesthouse in the Kol-Tor tract with full board (too.kg); Kegety Tour guesthouse — 1500 som/person with three meals a day (asia-hikes). Names of the yurt camps and 2026 prices are not confirmed.
kg-0028.net: Too.kg describes a signal in the lower part of Kegety up to the first waterfall; above that it becomes unstable. The operator and date of measurement are not stated.
kg-0028.entry: About 200 som per car at the Kegety post according to Hiking.kg for 2024; the current fee as of 04.10.2026 is not confirmed.
kg-0028.transfer: Not confirmed: no current taxi/transfer prices from Bishkek were found. For reference: the Trekking Union tour to Kol-Tor ~450 som/person (2024), marshrutka to Kegety 50 som (2024, probably outdated).
kg-0028.bring: Shoes with non-slip soles; poles for the steep path above the waterfall.
kg-0028.warn: Wet, slippery rocks at the base of the waterfall — don't go close to the jet and don't climb the rocks. After rains and during floods the road through the gorge turns to mud; on the upper sections you need a 4×4 / SUV (too.kg). Don't drink river water untreated — livestock graze above (too.kg). The signal disappears above the waterfall.
kg-0028.food: In summer — yurts with food opposite the first waterfall (too.kg): usually Kyrgyz home cooking, tea, kumys (editorial; menu not confirmed). There are practically no shops in the gorge — it's better to buy food in Tokmok or Ivanovka.
kg-0028.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 682 ratings/reviews according to the listing counter on 03.10.2026. Review texts were not used to confirm prices, roads or safety.
kg-0028.p.sum: The waterfall is an easy half-day target: the car drives almost to the foot, ≈200 m (5 min) from the road. Route from Bishkek (≈85 km, 2 h 15 min): Krasnaya Rechka — Yuryevka — Syn-Tash — Rot-Front — Kegety village, after the first bridge go right, after the next bridge left, and ≈5 km along the gorge; the first ~10 km of the gorge are passable by an ordinary car. Without a car — marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the Eastern Bus Station to Kegety (09:30/15:30, ≈80 som) and 5 km on foot/by hitching, or a tour (Sputnik8 $200–300 per car together with Burana). In summer there are yurts with food opposite the waterfall; it's best combined with Kol-Tor or Burana.

kg-0029.name: Moldo-Ashuu Pass
kg-0029.near: There are no permanent villages by the pass. From the south the road runs through the canyon of the Kurtka River from Ak-Talaa District (the district centre is Baetov); per Asia for Adventure and Kyrgyz Guide, the stretch from Kara-Oy to Song-Kol over the pass is 45.6 km. From the north — the summer yurt camps on the south shore of Song-Kol.
kg-0029.elev: 3346 m (quad-offroad.com, OunTravela, Asia for Adventure, TripAdvisor). Other values: 3243 m (Baibol Travel), 3201 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan) — probably intermediate points of the switchbacks.
kg-0029.short: The most “switchbacked” pass to Song-Kol (3346 m): 9 hairpins above the Kurtka River canyon and a height difference of about 800 m over 11 km.
kg-0029.desc: Moldo-Ashuu is a pass in the Moldo-Too range on the southern approach to Lake Song-Kol from Ak-Talaa District. The gravel road climbs out of the Kurtka River canyon in nine hairpin switchbacks (Baibol describes a “seven-level serpentine”) — about 800 m of elevation difference over 11 km from the first bend (OunTravela). On the sides are slopes with tall Tian Shan spruces, flowering valleys, and snowy peaks in the distance. The pass is often shrouded in cloud and thick fog. Of the four road passes to Song-Kol it is considered the most picturesque and the most winding; the road is well kept, but slippery on the steep sections. From November to March it is almost impassable because of snow and fog.
kg-0029.guide: Drive Moldo-Ashuu in at least one direction — it is the most photogenic switchback on the way to Song-Kol. The best shot is from above, from the viewing area by the saddle, when all the hairpins above the Kurtka canyon are visible; climb before noon, while the fog hasn't covered the slopes. Descend in a low gear: the gravel on the steep bends is loose, and trucks and flocks may be coming the other way. Combine it with Kara-Keche or Kalmak-Ashuu to make a loop through the lake. On the descent to Song-Kol, yurts stand by the road in summer — you can have some kumis.
kg-0029.see: The switchback of 9 hairpins above the Kurtka River canyon (a view from above); spruce slopes and the snowy peaks of the Moldo-Too; on the north side — a panorama of the Song-Kol basin and the yurt camps of the south shore.
kg-0029.skip: You're afraid of heights and sharp bends without guardrails. You're driving to Song-Kol from Kochkor and aren't planning a loop — Kalmak-Ashuu is simpler and closer. It's November — March or the forecast is for fog — you won't see anything, and the road is dangerous.
kg-0029.diff: Moderate for a driver: a well-kept gravel road suitable for almost all cars in dry weather (OunTravela), but 9 steep hairpins, a ~800 m height difference over 11 km, fog; Asia for Adventure and Kyrgyz Guide recommend only a 4×4. For cyclists — a hard, slippery climb.
kg-0029.when: June — September. Until June the passes to Song-Kol are blocked by snow (OunTravela); from November to March it is almost impassable (Asia for Adventure, quad-offroad). Snow is possible in summer too (TripAdvisor).
kg-0029.hours: An open road with no barriers or fees; there is no official schedule, winter closure depends on actual snow (November — March, sometimes until late May).
kg-0029.daytime: Morning — before noon: fewer clouds and less fog, good side lighting on the switchback; in the afternoon there is often fog and thunderstorms.
kg-0029.how: From the south — from Ak-Talaa District (Baetov) through the valley and canyon of the Kurtka River, then up the switchbacks to the pass and down to the south shore of Song-Kol; the Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch is about 45.6 km (Asia for Adventure, 2024). From Naryn — through Ak-Talaa District; from Kochkor it makes more sense to take Kalmak-Ashuu and use Moldo-Ashuu for the exit toward Naryn/Kazarman. Specific distances from Naryn/Bishkek are not confirmed in the sources.
kg-0029.needcar: Yes: an SUV/crossover with high ground clearance (a 4×4 is recommended); there is no public transport over the pass. A bicycle is possible (Baibol cycling tours).
kg-0029.self: Yes, in your own car with high clearance in dry weather; no permits. For those new to mountain driving, better with a local driver (steep hairpins without guardrails, fog).
kg-0029.roadtype: Gravel dirt road, “well maintained” (OunTravela, quad-offroad), with no asphalt; 9 steep hairpins along the Kurtka canyon; loose gravel on the bends, slippery in rain.
kg-0029.traveltime: The Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch (45.6 km) — roughly 1.5–2 h (a calculation from the length and character of the road). The 11 km climb up the switchbacks — 30–40 min. Full times from Naryn/Bishkek were not found in the sources.
kg-0029.stay: There is no lodging at the pass. The nearest is the yurt camps on the south shore of Song-Kol (budget $10–25/person with meals, Caravanistan/visitkyrgyzstan 2025–2026); yurts by the road on the descent in summer (TripAdvisor). In Ak-Talaa District and Naryn — guesthouses (via CBT Naryn). Specific names near the pass are not confirmed.
kg-0029.net: There is mobile signal at the saddle (TripAdvisor, a 2019–2020 review; operator not specified). In the Kurtka canyon and on the shore of Song-Kol — unstable or none.
kg-0029.entry: Free: no source mentions any toll.
kg-0029.transfer: No published transfer prices over Moldo-Ashuu were found. A guideline: a jeep Kochkor — Song-Kol 2500–3500 som per car; a marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (May 2026).
kg-0029.bring: Warm clothes and a rain jacket (fog, snow in summer), a spare wheel and a full tank, water and a snack, cash, offline maps; a camera/drone for the view of the switchback.
kg-0029.warn: Steep hairpins without guardrails; thick fog can suddenly cut visibility to almost zero (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). November — March almost impassable; snow is possible in summer too. Altitude 3346 m. Oncoming trucks and flocks on narrow bends.
kg-0029.food: In the summer yurts by the road on the descent to Song-Kol — kumis, tea with boorsok (TripAdvisor); in the Song-Kol camps — beshbarmak, kaimak. Specific places not checked.
kg-0029.reviews: Google Maps: 5/5, 61 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Moldo-Ashu Pass): 4.3/5, 10 reviews (July 2015 — February 2020; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: one of the most beautiful passes in the country, views of the switchback, many viewpoints. Cons: altitude, weather (snow even in summer), poor signage.
kg-0029.p.sum: Moldo-Ashuu (3346 m) is the southern exit from Song-Kol toward Naryn, Baetov and Kazarman: 9 hairpins above the Kurtka canyon, a good gravel road, the Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch ≈46 km. Drive a crossover/4×4 from June (it is sometimes closed in the first half of June) to September. It makes the most sense to enter Song-Kol via Kalmak-Ashuu from Kochkor and leave via Moldo-Ashuu to the south — to Naryn (Salkyn-Tor, Tash-Rabat) or to Kazarman (≈8 h). There is no lodging at the pass — spend the night in the camps on the south shore.

kg-0030.name: Ratsek Hut
kg-0030.near: Kashka-Suu — about 18 km as the crow flies (OSM marker); the Ala-Archa park's address on 2GIS is Kashka-Suu. The real starting point is the Ala-Archa alplager (mountaineering camp) (~12 km above the park checkpoint), from where it is 5.7–6 km on foot to the hut.
kg-0030.elev: About 3300–3400 m; sources disagree: 3240 m (kgnomad, 05.2026), 3300 m (travelbar.kg), 3360 m (asiamixtravel), ~3380 m (adventuresoflilnicki, 09.2026); in 2026 the Ministry of Emergencies wrote “about 3200 m”. Ascent from the alplager is ~1100–1350 m (asia-hikes: +1341 m).
kg-0030.short: Ratsek Hut is a legendary mountaineers' shelter on a moraine in the Ak-Sai gorge (Ala-Archa) at ~3300–3400 m, at the tongue of the Ak-Sai glacier; the most popular goal of a long day hike from Bishkek.
kg-0030.desc: Ratsek Hut stands on moraines in the side gorge of Ak-Sai in Ala-Archa Nature Park, at about 3300–3400 m, below the Ak-Sai glacier and the peaks Korona (4860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (Free Korea) (4740 m) and Uchitel (Teacher) (4530 m). It is named after Vladimir Iosifovich Ratsek (1918–1980) — a Master of Sport, 1950 USSR high-altitude mountaineering champion and one of the pioneers of Kyrgyz mountaineering. At first a canvas tent stood here; the permanent shelter was built in 1969 and rebuilt by 2008. The hut is now run by Ak-Sai Travel: up to 35 beds in two shared rooms and a VIP room, a kitchen, a bathhouse/sauna, solar-panel electricity, open year-round. It is the base camp for climbs of Uchitel (1B) and other peaks of the Ak-Sai spur; for ordinary tourists it is the goal of a hard day hike past the Ak-Sai waterfall.
kg-0030.guide: Ratsek Hut is your first real “high-mountain” trophy near Bishkek: from the alplager it is about 6 km and +1300 m, usually 4–5 hours uphill. Set off from the alplager no later than 8 a.m. — the first electric bus from the checkpoint and an early start will save you from the afternoon thunderstorm. Landmarks along the way: the “Broken Heart” rock, the Tepshi plateau, the Ak-Sai waterfall (the last reliable stream before the steep scree climb) and finally the moraine with a view of the Ak-Sai glacier and Korona peak. If you are staying overnight, book a place with Ak-Sai Travel ($15 per bunk) and climb to the lake and the Uchitel glacier in the morning. The hut is named after the mountaineer Vladimir Ratsek — memorial plaques hang on the wall inside.
kg-0030.see: The Ak-Sai glacier and icefall from the moraine at the hut; the panorama of the peaks Korona (4860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (Free Korea) (4740 m) and Uchitel (4530 m); the Ak-Sai waterfall on the way; a radial side trip (~4 km round trip) to the glacier and Lake Uchitel (asia-hikes); memorial plaques to mountaineers at the hut.
kg-0030.skip: You are not ready for ~1300 m of ascent in a day and steep scree on the last section — the Ak-Sai waterfall is enough for an easy walk. You don't tolerate altitude above 3300 m well: every season the Ministry of Emergencies evacuates tourists with altitude sickness from here. You arrive at Ala-Archa after lunch — you won't manage a round trip before dark.
kg-0030.diff: Moderate to hard for an unprepared tourist: 12–16 km round trip, ~1100–1350 m of ascent, maximum altitude ~3350 m (kgnomad: moderate, 14 km, +1500 m; asia-hikes: 6 km and +1341 m one way). The last section above the waterfall is steep scree and moraine. No technical skills are needed in summer; above the hut (glacier, peaks) is a mountaineering zone.
kg-0030.when: Late June to September: the trail has no deep snow and the weather is more stable (asiamixtravel); kgnomad says June to October. The hut is open year-round (Ak-Sai Travel), but in winter and spring the approach is avalanche-prone and requires winter gear.
kg-0030.hours: The hut receives guests year-round (Ak-Sai Travel); book via WhatsApp/e-mail on the site ak-sai.com. Ala-Archa park is open daily; electric buses run from the checkpoint to the alplager all day (hiking.kg says around the clock), bus No. 1 from Bishkek runs 08:00–19:00.
kg-0030.daytime: Start from the alplager before 8:00 (kgnomad) so you reach the top by noon: afternoons often bring clouds and thunderstorms, and you need to finish the scree descent in daylight (asiamixtravel). Morning has the best light on the glacier and Korona peak.
kg-0030.how: Bishkek → Ala-Archa park checkpoint: bus No. 1 from the old Usubaliev Square (50 som cash/40 som by card, 45–60 min) or a taxi. Since 01.05.2025 combustion-engine cars are left at the checkpoint; from there a free electric bus runs ~12 km to the alplager. From the alplager on foot up the Ak-Sai gorge: the “Broken Heart” rock → the Tepshi plateau → the Ak-Sai waterfall → a steep scree climb to the moraine and the hut (ilovekg). There is no road access to the hut.
kg-0030.needcar: Only as far as the park checkpoint (bus No. 1 or taxi); inside there is a free electric bus to the alplager, and beyond that only on foot. You don't need your own car.
kg-0030.self: Yes, in summer the trail is popular and easy to follow: bus No. 1 → electric bus → on foot. You need good physical shape, an offline map (there is no signal on the route) and an early start. Book an overnight stay in the hut in advance with Ak-Sai Travel. Going onto the glacier and peaks is only for experienced people or with a guide.
kg-0030.roadtype: Paved road to the checkpoint; inside the park, a paved road for electric buses to the alplager. Above that is a mountain trail; above the Ak-Sai waterfall it is a steep rocky climb and a moraine section with slippery scree.
kg-0030.traveltime: Bishkek → checkpoint: 45–60 min by bus No. 1; checkpoint → alplager: electric bus ~12 km. Alplager → hut: 5.7–6 km, 4–6 h up, 3–4 h down (ilovekg; asia-hikes: 4 h walking, 5–7 h with stops); the whole day takes 8–11 h.
kg-0030.stay: Ratsek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel, up to 35 beds): shared room $15/person, VIP $25/person, RedFox tent rental $15, your own tent — $3/person/day; heating $30 for 4 h, sauna $45/h, sleeping bag $10/night, kitchen rental $25/day (ak-sai.com, 2026). Nearby is the Light House hut in the Ratsek clearing (booking at the same place). Lower down are cottages and yurts at the Ala-Archa alplager.
kg-0030.net: There is no mobile network on the route or at the hut — download offline maps (asiamixtravel). The last reliable signal is around the checkpoint/alplager (group 6 data, operator not confirmed). The hut has solar-panel electricity (Ak-Sai Travel).
kg-0030.entry: Entry to Ala-Archa Nature Park from 11.06.2026: adults 250 som, children 7–14 years 180 som, under 7 free (24.kg; group 6 data). There is no separate fee for the climb to the hut; overnight stay and camping are paid to Ak-Sai Travel ($15 bunk, $3 own tent). The old figures (80 som per person, 500 som per bunk — asia-hikes) are out of date.
kg-0030.transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50 som cash/40 som by card (2025–2026); the electric bus inside the park is free; taxi Bishkek → checkpoint ~$12–18 one way, private transfer $40–90 (kgnomad, 2026); the travelbar.kg group hike — 350 som per person including transport.
kg-0030.bring: Trekking boots with stiff soles and poles (slippery scree), a waterproof shell, fleece, hat and gloves (at the hut it is +10–12 °C by day and frost is possible at night — kgnomad), 1.5–2 L of water (the last stream is at the waterfall), a snack, category 3–4 sunglasses and SPF cream, a headlamp, cash for the entry fee. For an overnight stay — a sleeping bag (or rent one for $10).
kg-0030.warn: Altitude 3300+ m: risk of altitude sickness — on 29.06.2026 the Ministry of Emergencies evacuated a tourist from the route, and there were similar cases in 2024–2025 (24.kg). Don't gain altitude too fast, drink water, and if you have symptoms, descend and call 112. The scree above the waterfall is slippery and there is rockfall under the slopes; get back before dark. There is no signal. Outside summer it is avalanche-prone. Since 01.05.2025 combustion-engine cars are banned from entering the park — electric bus only.
kg-0030.food: At the hut you can order food from Ak-Sai Travel: breakfast $12, lunch $20, dinner $15, single dishes/sandwiches $10 (ak-sai.com, 2026); there is a kitchen for self-catering. Lower down there is a cafe and restaurant at the Ala-Archa alplager. The sources name no local specialties at the hut itself.
kg-0030.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 230 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: the “Ratsek Cabin” page (d10235109) with reviews; AllTrails: the route “Ala-Archa — Ak-Sai Racek Hut and Glacier” — 224 reviews (07.10.2026). Pros: views of the glacier and Korona peak, the atmosphere of a mountaineers' shelter, closeness to Bishkek. Cons: heavy, steep scree at the end, crowded on summer weekends, the altitude makes itself felt.
kg-0030.p.sum: There is no road to Ratsek Hut — only a 6–9 km trail with +1100–1350 m from the Ala-Archa alplager. The easiest way: bus No. 1 or a taxi to the park checkpoint (entry 250 som), a free electric bus to the alplager and 3–6 hours on foot past the Ak-Sai waterfall. Set off before 8:00 and preferably spend the night in the hut: a bunk with Ak-Sai Travel is $15, dinner $15. In summer (July–August) the trail has no snow and needs no technical gear. From mid-October to mid-April you need crampons on the approach, and above the hut, on the glacier and the peaks, you can't manage without experience or a guide.

kg-0030.p.transport.2.details: Every 10–15 min during the day; since 19.02.2026 a Doppelmayr gondola also operates in parallel (600/400 som, closed on Tuesdays)

kg-0030.p.transport.6.details: 2 days: day 1 — ascent and a night at Ratsek Hut, day 2 — climb of Uchitel peak (4530 m, +1030 m) and descent. Transport, guide, accommodation, sleeping bag, lunch and dinner and park entry are included; personal gear is not included
kg-0030.p.transport.7.details: Alpine school “7-Day Mountaineering Course” based at Ratsek Hut: rock, rope, ice, climbs of Ratsek peak (2A) and Uchitel. IFMGA guides. Transport, meals, accommodation and group gear are included; personal technical gear is not. Also the Uchitel + Yukhin program (11 days) — $1500/person.

kg-0030.p.onsite.camping: You can pitch tents around the hut: your own tent — $3/person per day, RedFox tent rental — $15 (Ak-Sai Travel, 2026). Water comes from the stream at the waterfall and meltwater at the hut. It is worth boiling or filtering it

kg-0030.p.food.1.details: The last place with hot food before the climb; it is better to buy a snack and water for the day in Bishkek
kg-0030.p.rent.0.what: Sleeping bag, gas, storage room at the hut

kg-0030.p.rent.3.price: rental prices for crampons and ice axes not found
kg-0030.p.svc.toilets: At the checkpoint and the alplager; there is a toilet at the hut. No toilets on the trail
kg-0030.p.svc.water: The stream at the Ak-Sai waterfall is the last reliable source on the climb; at the hut it is meltwater (boil it). A thermos of boiling water at the hut — $5
kg-0030.p.svc.shop: No shops in the park; buy food in Bishkek
kg-0030.p.svc.atm: Bishkek; none in the park. At the hut they accept dollars or som, check the payment method
kg-0030.p.svc.fuel: Fuel stations in the southern part of Bishkek / on the road to Ala-Archa
kg-0030.p.svc.mobile: There is a network at the checkpoint and the alplager; none on the trail or at the hut
kg-0030.p.svc.medical: The nearest hospitals are in Bishkek
kg-0030.p.svc.rescue: Ministry of Emergencies — 112; rescuers regularly evacuate tourists with altitude sickness from the route to the hut (24.kg, 2025–2026)
kg-0030.p.iti.0.title: One day from Bishkek
kg-0030.p.iti.0.plan: 6:30 taxi or the first bus No. 1 → 7:30 checkpoint (entry 250 som) → electric bus → 8:00 start from the alplager → 9:30 Tepshi plateau → 11:00 Ak-Sai waterfall → 12:00–12:30 the hut: lunch ($10–20) and the moraine → 13:30 descent → 16:30–17:00 alplager → electric bus → evening in Bishkek. Only for the well prepared
kg-0030.p.iti.1.title: 2 days with an overnight stay
kg-0030.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: start from the alplager after lunch, climb to the hut, dinner and the night (bunk $15, dinner $15). Day 2: sunrise on the moraine, a radial trip to the glacier and Lake Uchitel (2–3 h), descent, evening in Bishkek. Option for mountaineers: day 2 — climb of Uchitel peak (1B) with a guide
kg-0030.p.iti.2.title: What to combine
kg-0030.p.iti.2.plan: The Ak-Sai glacier is right at the hut, so it is one trip. Ala-Archa National Park: the Ak-Sai waterfall, the Adygene gorge, the gondola — for the next day. The Chunkurchak gorge — 40–60 min by car via Kashka-Suu, the following day
kg-0030.p.season: January–February: stable and sunny, −10…−20 °C at the hut, approach only for experienced people, with crampons. March–April: unstable, windy, avalanche danger. May: the first half is sunny, from the second half snowfalls. June: blizzards are possible at the hut until about the 20th. July–August: no snow, up to +25 °C by day, the hut is crowded, rockfall danger grows. September–early October: “golden autumn”, stable, little wind, getting colder down to −10 °C. Late October–November: snowfalls. From mid-October to mid-April you need crampons on the approach (summitx)
kg-0030.p.budget.economy: ≈1000–2500 som per day: bus No. 1 round trip 80–100 som, entry 250 som, electric bus 0, a snack from Bishkek 300–500 som, lunch at the hut $10–20 if you wish. With an overnight stay — plus a bunk $15, dinner and breakfast $27 (≈4000–5000 som in total); a weekend group tour — 1300 som (Ulush Travel, 2025) or 350 som (Travelbar)
kg-0030.p.budget.comfort: ≈$150–650 per person: taxi or transfer $40–90, entry, 2 days at the hut with meals ≈$70, a guide $80–100/day (Journal of Nomads); a ready-made 2-day tour with a climb of Uchitel ≈CA$611
kg-0030.p.permits: No border-zone permit is needed. Only an Ala-Archa park ticket is required at the checkpoint: 250 som, children 7–14 years — 180 som, under 7 — free (since 11.06.2026). For climbs, foreigners may need a climbing permit (Ak-Sai lists a “climbing permit” separately in the exclusions) — check with the operator
kg-0030.p.access: With small children, older people, or with a stroller — no: a steep climb of 1100+ m and scree. With teenagers — only if they are in good shape. With a stroller only the area around the alplager is accessible. Dogs: no special rules for the park were found, but a dog is inconvenient on scree and in the hut
