kg-0030.p.gaps.2: daily rate of a local mountaineering guide for Uchitel (only a rough guide of $80–100/day)

kg-0031.name: Juuku Hot Springs
kg-0031.near: Saruu (where the Juuku gorge meets the Balykchy — Karakol highway) and Darkhan; it is ~10–12 km up the valley from the highway to the springs. TripAdvisor lists the site as “Radon Springs Djuuku, Saruu”. The earlier reference to Jalgyz-Uryuk (14.7 km per OSM) is formally the nearest marker in the export, but the real approach goes through Saruu.
kg-0031.elev: 2236 m — per the Destination Jeti Oguz / Nomad's Land catalog (2024–2025). There is no independent measurement; an error of ±50 m is possible.
kg-0031.short: Radon-hydrogen sulfide warm springs (~34 °C) in the side valley of Juukuchak in the Juuku gorge on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul; simple concrete pools in the open air and in a “yurt”, entry 100–150 som.
kg-0031.desc: The springs are on the right side of the Juukuchak valley — a side tributary of the Juuku River, the longest gorge in the Terskey Ala-Too (40–50 km), along which in ancient times ran the route from the Issyk-Kul basin to the Inner Tian Shan and China. The water is thermal (about 34 °C regardless of the weather), mineralized, with radon and a noticeable smell of hydrogen sulfide; several small pools are set up, one of them covered by a concrete “yurt”. The infrastructure is simple, in places neglected — this is not a sanatorium but a village bathing spot. Nearby are a cold mountain river for contrast bathing, the “300 Sheep” cave, red cliffs at the gorge entrance and Tian Shan spruce higher up the valley. In 1932 the Swiss traveler Ella Maillart (“Turkestan Solo”) passed through the valley. Tourists often get confused: the hot springs are in Juukuchak, while the Juuku gorge itself is known for its lakes and the pass to the Arabel plateau.
kg-0031.guide: Come here not for a spa but for the atmosphere: warm water smelling of sulfur, red cliffs and spruces all around, and above — one of the wildest gorges of the Terskey. When ordering a car in Karakol or Saruu, say specifically “Juukuchak, hot springs” — otherwise you risk ending up in the neighbouring valley with no pools. Don't stay in the water for more than 30 minutes: locals themselves warn about the natural radioactivity. After bathing, dip into the icy river nearby and look into the “300 Sheep” cave. If you have a 4×4 / SUV and a spare day, continue up the Juuku to the lakes and the pass to the syrts (high plateaus) of Arabel, along the old caravan route.
kg-0031.see: Warm pools (34 °C) in the open air and in a concrete “yurt”; the cold Juukuchak River for contrast; the “300 Sheep” cave; red sandstone cliffs at the entrance to the Juuku gorge; higher up — spruce forests, a waterfall, the Kashka-Suu (3600 m) and Juukuchak lakes; petroglyphs and Turkic burial mounds in the valley.
kg-0031.skip: You expect a well-equipped spa complex — here there are simple concrete tubs and minimal service. You are without a 4×4 / SUV and not ready for a dirt road with fords. You have already been to Altyn-Arashan or Ak-Suu/Kerege-Tash — the water is similar, and the road there is easier.
kg-0031.diff: Easy on site (a bathing spot by the road); the difficulty is in the approach: 10–12 km of dirt road/off-road from the highway, TripAdvisor (2016–2025) recommends 4WD, mud and fords in spring.
kg-0031.when: May–October for driving the valley; the water is 34 °C year-round, in winter the approach depends on snow and is not guaranteed. In the shoulder season (April–May) the dirt road turns to mud (TripAdvisor reviews).
kg-0031.hours: Google Maps (viewed 03.10.2026): open 24 hours. In practice — a village bathing spot with a caretaker on site; per TripAdvisor reviews the owners opened up outside “hours” too. There is no schedule.
kg-0031.daytime: Daytime or early evening: warm water is nicer in cool weather, but it is better to drive back along the dirt road in daylight.
kg-0031.how: From Karakol (45–75 km) or Bishkek along the southern Balykchy — Karakol highway to the village of Saruu (or Darkhan), then south along the Juuku valley ~10 km to a fork and up the side valley of Juukuchak to the pools. Public transport: marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som (Visit Karakol), then ~2 hours on foot or hitchhiking; a taxi/4×4 / SUV is more convenient. When ordering a car, say specifically “Juukuchak, hot springs”.
kg-0031.needcar: Yes. It is 10–12 km from the highway with no public transport; a 4×4 / SUV is advisable (TripAdvisor reviews, too.kg: the road is good at the bottom, worse higher up).
kg-0031.self: Yes, by 4×4 / SUV or on foot from Darkhan/Saruu; no permit needed (not a border zone). Navigation: the Google marker “Juuku istochnik”, maps.me.
kg-0031.roadtype: Paved road along the highway to Saruu; then a dirt road along the valley, “quite good” at first, higher up — broken up, with fords (too.kg; TripAdvisor reviews 2016–2025: “4WD needed”, “a test for jeepers”). To the pools — a dirt road.
kg-0031.traveltime: From Karakol by car ~1.5–2 h (TripAdvisor review 2024: “a couple of hours from Karakol”); from Darkhan on foot ~2 h (Visit Karakol). From Bishkek ~5–6 h to the area.
kg-0031.stay: There is no lodging at the springs themselves (too.kg: no guesthouses, shops or cafes in the gorge; many places for tents). The nearest guesthouses are in Saruu, Darkhan, Kyzyl-Suu and Karakol; CBT Karakol and visitkarakol.com. Specific prices not found.
kg-0031.net: There is no mobile signal in the Juuku gorge (too.kg). By the highway (Saruu) all operators have a signal. Beeline and MegaCom strengthened their network around Issyk-Kul in 2024–2026, but Juuku is not mentioned in the lists.
kg-0031.entry: 100 som per person (Destination Jeti Oguz / Nomad's Land, catalog 2024–2025); issykkul.biz — 100–150 som. Pay on site in cash. Confirm the amount before your visit.
kg-0031.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som (visitkarakol.com). An excursion from Cholpon-Ata $417/group, 12 h (sputnik8, 2026). No published taxi tariff to the springs; a guide figure for a 4×4 / SUV from Karakol on comparable myway.kg routes — 9,500–13,200 som per car (2026, “the price is not final due to the fuel shortage”).
kg-0031.bring: Swimwear, a towel, flip-flops, water and food (no shops), cash in som, warm clothes (2200 m, cold in the evening), an offline map; for a 4×4 / SUV — a reserve of fuel.
kg-0031.warn: Water with natural radon: no more than 30 minutes in the pool (Destination Jeti Oguz recommendation); people with cardiovascular diseases and pregnant women should consult a doctor; advertised “healing” promises are not medical advice. The road through the gorge is dirt with fords, dangerous in spring; no mobile signal. Don't confuse it with the Juuku gorge without pools.
kg-0031.food: There is no cafe on site. Bring food with you; in the villages of Saruu/Darkhan and Kyzyl-Suu — ashkana (small eateries) with lagman, manty and kumis (seasonal). Specific places were not checked.
kg-0031.reviews: Google Maps “Juuku istochnik”: 4.7/5, 26 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Juuku Gorge”: 4.5/5, 15 reviews (2016–2025) — they praise the wild nature, the quiet, the marmots; cons — off-road, fords, 4WD needed. TripAdvisor “Radon Springs Djuuku, Saruu”: 10 reviews (2014–2018) — the water is “mineral, slightly sulfurous”, but the facilities are “simple and neglected”.
kg-0031.p.sum: The best option is a car with a driver from Karakol (1.5–2 h) or your own car with good ground clearance: along the southern highway to Saruu, then ~10–12 km of dirt road up the Juuku valley and into the side valley of Juukuchak to the pools (Google marker “Juuku istochnik”, 42.1818, 78.0073). Without a car — a marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan/Saruu and ~2 h on foot. There is no lodging, shops, cafes or mobile signal in the gorge: bring food, water and cash, and overnight in a tent by the river or in guesthouses in Kyzyl-Suu/Saruu. Entry to the bathing spot is 100 som, no more than 30 minutes in the water.

kg-0031.p.season: May — driving is questionable (mud, water at the fords); June–July — the fords are higher; August–September — the best time (dry, lower water in the rivers); October — cold, but bathing at 34 °C is pleasant; November–April — the approach in snow is not guaranteed. No crowds; ticks in the spruce forests May–June (for the region).
kg-0031.p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — southern shore 500–600 + Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som, 2 h on foot; entry 100; a tent free or a guesthouse in Kyzyl-Suu ~$19 (~1,650 som) with breakfast; your own food ~500. kg-0031.p.budget.comfort: A 4×4 / SUV with a driver from Karakol ~9,500–13,200 som/car (MYWAY guide figure) — split among 3–4 people ≈2,500–4,000; entry 100; a night in Karakol $40–60; food 1,000–1,500. In total ~6,000–9,000 som/person.
kg-0031.p.permits: Not needed: not a border zone. Only payment for the bathing spot (100 som) on site in cash.
kg-0031.p.access: With children — possible in the dry season (short bathing, radon); older people — a rough ride on the dirt road, people with cardiovascular diseases should consult a doctor; with a stroller — no (dirt, concrete steps); with a dog — possible, but there are shepherd dogs around.

kg-0032.name: Karakol Gorge
kg-0032.full: Karakol Gorge (Karakol canyon, Karakol Nature Park)
kg-0032.near: Karakol — the entrance to the gorge is 3–7 km south of the town (too.kg: “3 km south of Karakol”; the Ala-Kul trailhead at the “first bridge” is ~7 km from the last stop of marshrutka No. 101).
kg-0032.elev: Gorge entrance ~1,900–2,000 m (Nomad's Land: the park at 2,000 m), ski base 2,300 m, Lake Ala-Kul 3,532 m (ecostan.kg; kaktus.media gives 3,440 m), Ala-Kul Pass ~3,900 m. The earlier figure “3,532 m” referred to the lake, not the gorge.
kg-0032.short: The 40-km gorge of the Karakol River just south of the town of Karakol — the core of Karakol Nature Park (1997): spruce forests, an alpine camp, a ski base and the start of trails to Lake Ala-Kul and Altyn-Arashan.
kg-0032.desc: The gorge cuts through the eastern part of the Terskey Ala-Too from the outskirts of Karakol to the glaciers beneath the peaks of Karakol (5,281 m), Jigit (5,170 m) and Przhevalsky (4,283 m). This is the territory of Karakol State Nature Park (38,134 ha, established 15.04.1997): more than 300–700 plant species, snow leopard, golden eagle, and the saker falcon, listed in the Red Book. In the lower part there is the Karakol ski base (2,300 m, cable cars); higher up there are a summer alpine camp, yurt camps (Sirota) and trails: Kyrgyzstan's most popular trek, Karakol — Ala-Kul — Altyn-Arashan (3 days, 50–55 km, a 3,900 m pass). Since 2025 an eco post has operated at the entrance with a vehicle fee; the walk-in park entrance fee is 250–300 som per person according to 2025 guidebooks.
kg-0032.guide: Karakol Gorge is the very “front door” to Ala-Kul: from the last stop of marshrutka No. 101 to the first bridge it is another 7 km, so arrange a taxi to the bridge or to the alpine camp. If you aren't doing a multi-day trek, make a day loop: 10 km and 400 m of gain to the alpine camp through spruce forest with views of Przhevalsky Peak. In winter the same gorge is a ski area at 2,300 m with a view of Issyk-Kul; in summer the lift carries only groups. Pay the eco fee at the post (keep the receipt — it is checked on the trail) and don't count on mobile coverage above the base. In the evening go back to Karakol for ashlan-fu and Dungan cuisine.
kg-0032.see: Spruce forests and alpine meadows; the Karakol ski base (2,300 m) with a panorama of the town and the lake; the alpine camp and the Sirota yurt camp; waterfalls and moraine lakes in the upper reaches; the side valleys of Kashka-Suu and On-Tor; the route to Lake Ala-Kul (3,532 m) and over the pass to Altyn-Arashan; the peaks of Karakol, Jigit and Przhevalsky.
kg-0032.skip: You are not ready for a mountain trail — without strong legs the gorge is limited to the road up to the ski base. You have one day and want “postcard” views without effort — then Jeti-Oguz or Altyn-Arashan by SUV is easier. You've come in the shoulder season (April–May, October–November): the passes are under snow and the camps are closed.
kg-0032.diff: The lower part (up to the ski base/alpine camp) is easy: dirt road/trail, 10 km and +400 m to the alpine camp in 4–5 h (Destination Karakol). The Ala-Kul trek is hard: 3 days, 50–55 km, a 3,900 m pass (Snoezels on the road).
kg-0032.when: Trekking — mid-June to mid-September (Destination Karakol, Snoezels); July–August are the most stable. Ski base — December–March. In autumn (September) — golden larches and fewer people.
kg-0032.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): open 24 hours. The nature park's eco post at the entrance works daily (Sputnik, November 2025). The ski base and the alpine camp are seasonal.
kg-0032.daytime: Morning: set off on the trail before 9:00 to get through the forest before the midday heat and reach the camp before the thunderstorm (downpours are common in the afternoon in July–August).
kg-0032.how: From Karakol: marshrutka No. 101 from the city bus station to the terminus at the gorge entrance (10–20 som, 2025), then ~7 km on foot or by taxi to the “first bridge”/alpine camp; shared taxi ~200 som per person (backpackmoments, 2025). SUV transfer to the Ala-Kul trailhead — myway.kg. From Bishkek: marshrutka/taxi to Karakol (Bishkek bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., 6–8 h), then as above.
kg-0032.needcar: Not necessary: marshrutka No. 101 takes you to the park entrance; but to reach the start of the trail (7 km) a taxi or SUV is more convenient.
kg-0032.self: Yes: the Ala-Kul trail is marked and can be followed with maps.me; no permits are needed (not a border zone), only the park eco fee. Book yurt camps through CBT Karakol.
kg-0032.roadtype: Paved road through the town to the outskirts, then a gravel/dirt road through the gorge to the ski base and the alpine camp (passable by a passenger car up to the base, above that an SUV, too.kg); after that — mountain trails. You cannot drive to Ala-Kul.
kg-0032.traveltime: Karakol — park entrance: 15–20 min by marshrutka No. 101. To the alpine camp on foot from the first bridge: 10 km, +400 m, 4–5 h (Destination Karakol). To Ala-Kul: 2 days, to Altyn-Arashan — 3 days (50–55 km).
kg-0032.stay: In the gorge: the alpine camp (in summer), the Sirota yurt camp (day 1 of the trek), tent camps at Ala-Kul (booking through CBT Karakol), a hotel at the Karakol ski base (in winter). Camp prices are not published in the sources (“more expensive than the national average” — wanderlustdesigners, 2025). City base — Karakol: hostels and guesthouses from ~800–1,500 som (rough figure, not verified).
kg-0032.net: There is coverage at the entrance and at the ski base (outskirts of Karakol); higher up the gorge and along the whole Ala-Kul trek there is no signal (too.kg; wanderlustdesigners 2025: “there will be no signal for the whole trek”). Offline maps are a must.
kg-0032.entry: On foot: 250 som per person (visitkarakol.com; backpackmoments, 01.2025) — 300 som according to other reports (Snoezels on the road). Vehicles at the eco post since November 2025: passenger car — 200 som, truck/bus — 800 som (Sputnik Kyrgyzstan, 02.11.2025). Sputnik does not mention a separate rate for foreigners; gokyrgyzstan.info writes “$5 per person, $10 per car” (date not given).
kg-0032.transfer: Marshrutka No. 101 — 10–20 som (2025). Shared taxi to the bridge ~200 som/person (2025). SUV Karakol — Ala-Kul trailhead: 9,500–17,600 som per car (MYWAY.kg, 2026).
kg-0032.bring: Trekking boots, rain jacket, a warm layer (around 0 °C at night in the camps even in summer), sun protection, cash for the eco fee and camps, an offline map, a filter/water purification tablets (boil river water — too.kg), a food supply — there are no shops in the gorge.
kg-0032.warn: The eco fee is mandatory and the receipt is checked on the trail; there is a separate fee for entering by car. There is no mobile coverage above the base. Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) — altitude sickness and snow until the end of June; downpours and thunderstorms in the afternoon; solo hikers should register at the camp. In spring and after rain — rockfalls and fords.
kg-0032.food: In the gorge — only what the yurt camps cook (dinner/breakfast included). In Karakol: ashlan-fu (cold Dungan noodles, rows of stalls at the bazaar), Dungan dishes, lagman, manty, boorsoki — specific eateries have not been verified.
kg-0032.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 68 ratings (03.10.2026). Typical pros from 2024–2025 blogs: accessibility from the town, a marked trail, views from Ala-Kul; cons — paid entry, expensive yurt camps, no mobile coverage, 7 km from the marshrutka terminus to the trail.
kg-0032.p.sum: Your base is the town of Karakol: it is 3–7 km to the entrance of the nature park (marshrutka No. 101 or a taxi), and a per-person and per-vehicle fee is paid at the eco post. For a day trip a taxi to the “first bridge” (~2,000 som) and a walk to the alpine camp are enough; for the Ala-Kul trek, order an SUV to the alpine camp/second bridge (8,000–15,000 som per car) and rent gear from EcoTrek/4Rent. Overnight stays — the Sirota yurt camp (~$45 with dinner and breakfast) or a tent; in winter — the Karakol ski base, 7 km from the town.

kg-0032.p.iti.1.title: Ala-Kul in 2 days
kg-0032.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: SUV to the alpine camp (2 h) → Sirota (overnight in a yurt). Day 2: climb to Ala-Kul (3–4 h), rest, descend to the alpine camp and transfer to Karakol.

kg-0032.p.season: December–March — ski season (usually from late November, in 2025 — from 6 December). April–May — shoulder season, mud, the pass is closed. Mid-June–September — trekking; July–August is peak crowds and afternoon thunderstorms; September — golden larches, cold nights. October–May on the pass −25…−30 °C, only for the well prepared. Ticks in the spruce forest — May–June.
kg-0032.p.budget.economy: Marshrutka No. 101 20 + on foot; eco fee ~250–300; own tent/rental ~1,500/day for a set; camping 100–300; own food ~600/day. A 3-day trek ≈ 5,000–7,000 som/person (excluding the trip from Bishkek).
kg-0032.p.budget.comfort: SUV 9,500–15,000 som/car (÷4 ≈ 2,500–3,800); Sirota $45 (~3,900 som); guide $50–80/day; horse $100+/day. A 3-day trek ≈ 25,000–45,000 som/person.
kg-0032.p.permits: No border-zone permit needed. Karakol Nature Park: eco fee for walkers ~250–300 som (2024–2025 guides), for a car 200 som (eco post since 11.2025); keep the receipt — it is checked on the trail. Payment at the eco post is in cash.
kg-0032.p.access: With kids — the ski base and a walk to the first bridge; the Ala-Kul trek is for teenagers with experience. For older people — only the road section. Wheelchair — no (dirt). With a dog — allowed on the trail, but there are shepherd dogs at the camps; the park rules on dogs were not found.

kg-0033.name: Shatyly Panorama
kg-0033.near: Bokonbaevo is ~12 km west of the start of the trail (Lonely Planet: 12 km east of the roundabout in the center of the village; Asia Hikes: 11.5 km along the Boz-Salkyn valley). Kadji-Sai is closer in a straight line, but the approach is described only from Bokonbaevo.
kg-0033.elev: The viewpoint is ~2,600 m, the start ~2,490 m per the Wikiloc GPS track (max. 8,588 ft / min. 8,155 ft, recorded May 2017); gain 137–177 m (Wikiloc/Asia Hikes). Accuracy ±50 m; there is no official elevation mark.
kg-0033.short: An easy one-hour walk from the Boz-Salkyn valley to a grassy hill with a panorama of the whole southern shore of Issyk-Kul, the lake itself and the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges; the best place for sunrise near Bokonbaevo.
kg-0033.desc: Shatyly is a viewing ridge above the Boz-Salkyn valley in the foothills of the Terskey Ala-Too, east of Bokonbaevo. From a farm at a bend in the dirt road a jeep track climbs to a northern saddle, from which a short climb to the left leads to a lookout hill. The 3.5 km loop with a gain of under 200 m takes about an hour; the trail has no water or shade. From the top you can see the lake in its full width, the barren hills of the shore, the settlement of Kadji-Sai and snowy peaks. The name of the valley, “Boz-Salkyn” (“light coolness”), became established after the film of the same name and does not appear on topographic maps. The route is promoted by CBT/Destination South Shore as a “morning or half-day” outing from Bokonbaevo; there is no entry fee. Combined with the Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Manjyly-Ata and the eagle-hunter (berkutchi) show, it makes a standard day on the southern shore.
kg-0033.guide: Come for sunrise: the sun rises behind the ridge and paints the lake and hills orange — that is what people come here for. Leave Bokonbaevo before dawn, 12 km of dirt road to the farm at the bend, then along the jeep track to the saddle and left to the hill — all in 30–40 minutes. There is no water or shade on the trail, and the wind on the ridge is strong, so take a jacket and a thermos. If you have no car, arrange a taxi at CBT Bokonbaevo or walk the 18 km from the village (that is another +3 hours). Combine it with Skazka Canyon and the Manjyly-Ata springs — everything is within half an hour’s drive.
kg-0033.see: The panorama of the whole lake and the southern shore; the Boz-Salkyn valley with summer pastures; at sunrise — light on the barren hills; views of Kadji-Sai and the Terskey Ala-Too. Nearby — the Mars canyons (6 km), the Manjyly-Ata valley (7 km), Skazka Canyon (23 km).
kg-0033.skip: What matters to you is the route itself, not the view — it is only 1 hour of walking here. The weather is overcast or hazy: the point of this spot is the panorama. You have no car and are not ready to pay for a round-trip taxi for an hour’s walk.
kg-0033.diff: Very easy: a 3.5 km loop, gain 137–177 m, under an hour (Asia Hikes 2021, Wikiloc 2017). No water or shade; suitable for children in dry weather.
kg-0033.when: May–October; in summer — only the morning because of the heat on the open slope. In spring (May) the hills are green, in autumn the air is clear. In winter access along the dirt road depends on the snow.
kg-0033.hours: Open terrain, 24 hours; no ticket offices or barriers (Asia Hikes 2021: no fee).
kg-0033.daytime: Sunrise (Lonely Planet, Journal of Nomads 2025: “worth arriving before sunrise”); in the evening — sunset with the lake lit up, but you have to return along the dirt road in the dark.
kg-0033.how: From Bokonbaevo: from the central roundabout two blocks south, then the road east out of the village, 12 km along the Boz-Salkyn valley to a small farm at a bend in the road; then on foot along the jeep track to the saddle and left to the hill (~1.75 km one way). On foot from Bokonbaevo — +18 km/3 h. To Bokonbaevo: a marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek (Bishkek bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., 550–650 som, 5–6 h, every 1–2 h from 7:00 to 17:00 — Journal of Nomads, 2025) or from Karakol (1.5–2 h).
kg-0033.needcar: Yes, to the start of the trail (12 km of dirt road from the village); on site — on foot. A taxi from Bokonbaevo or a transfer through CBT.
kg-0033.self: Yes: the trail is obvious (a jeep track), GPS tracks on Wikiloc/AllTrails, no permits or fees.
kg-0033.roadtype: Paved only in Bokonbaevo; 12 km is a dirt village road along the valley (passable for a passenger car in dry weather, Asia Hikes: “old mountain roads”, a taxi or hitchhiking); then a jeep track on foot.
kg-0033.traveltime: Bokonbaevo – trailhead: 20–30 min by car (12 km of dirt road). The climb to the viewpoint is 30–40 min, the loop about an hour (Asia Hikes, Owl Over The World 2024).
kg-0033.stay: In Bokonbaevo: the guesthouses Baiel, Akbermet (budget), Amirhan, Ecoresort Kaiyrma (mid-range) — Journal of Nomads 2025; Guest House Teskei (Owl Over The World 2024); 4 CBT Bokonbaevo yurt camps from the shore to the foothills. Prices are not published (a regional guideline of 1,000–2,000 som/person with breakfast — not confirmed).
kg-0033.net: In Bokonbaevo and Kadji-Sai — coverage from all operators (a district center, the A363 highway). On the Shatyly ridge coverage is not documented; given the remoteness (12 km from the village, line of sight to the shore) a signal is likely but not confirmed.
kg-0033.entry: Free — there is no entry fee (Asia Hikes, 2021). No recent data on the introduction of a fee was found.
kg-0033.transfer: A taxi in Bokonbaevo to the start — the tariff is not published (a guideline of 500–1,000 som round trip, not confirmed). Marshrutka Bishkek – Bokonbaevo 550–650 som, shared taxi 800–1,000 som/seat, a whole car 3,500–4,000 som (2025).
kg-0033.bring: Water (there are no springs on the trail), a hat and sun protection, a windbreaker for the ridge, a flashlight if you set out before dawn, a camera; shoes with a tread — the slopes are loose.
kg-0033.warn: No water or shade — it is hot in the daytime in summer. The dirt road turns to mud after rain. Shepherd dogs at the farms in the valley — give them a wide berth. The name “Boz-Salkyn” is absent from maps — navigate by the GPS track, not by the place name.
kg-0033.food: There is nothing on site. In Bokonbaevo — the Argymak café (the CBT address, 16 Mambetov St.), home cooking at guesthouses; on the southern shore — smoked fish and kumis by the highway (seasonal). Specific establishments have not been checked.
kg-0033.reviews: Google Maps “Panorama Shatyly Issyk-Kul”: 4.9/5, 29 ratings (03.10.2026). AllTrails “Shatyly Overlook”: 9 reviews (content unavailable). Blogs 2021–2025 are unanimous: an easy climb, the best views at sunrise; cons — you need transport to the start, no water.
kg-0033.p.sum: Stay overnight in Bokonbaevo and set out by taxi or your own car before dawn: 12 km of village dirt road along the Boz-Salkyn valley to the farm at the bend, then 1.75 km on foot along the jeep track to the hill — in time for sunrise. Entry is free, and there is no water or shade. Without a car, arrange a taxi through CBT Bokonbaevo or a guesthouse; it combines conveniently into one day with Manjyly-Ata and the Mars and Skazka canyons.

kg-0034.name: Abshir-Ata Waterfall
kg-0034.dist: Nookat District, Osh Region, Kulatov rural municipality (aiyl okmotu)
kg-0034.near: Villages of the Kulatov aiyl okmotu in the Abshir-Say gorge (24.kg); per OSM the nearest pin is Kanaka (~0.5 km). It is 10 km to the main road and 70 km to Osh (24.kg); Nookat is ~40 km to the northeast (Nomad's Land).
kg-0034.elev: About 1800 m (Nomad's Land); the valley as a whole is 1500–2500 m (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The cascades are ~15 and ~12 m (I Love KG).
kg-0034.short: Abshir-Ata is a sacred karst waterfall in the Abshir-Say gorge: the stream bursts out of an opening in a sheer limestone wall, ~70 km from Osh.
kg-0034.desc: Abshir-Ata is a waterfall in the valley of the Abshir-Say river on the northern spurs of the Kichi-Alay Range (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The water emerges from a small karst cave — a dark opening 1.5–2 m in diameter at a height of 12–15 m — and falls down a sheer rock in two cascades of about 15 and 12 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, I Love KG). The water is considered mineral and holy; according to legend, a wanderer struck the rock with his staff and milk flowed from it (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The place is revered, and pilgrims come here. A good dirt road has been laid in the gorge up to the waterfall, there are guesthouses and cafes nearby, and souvenirs are sold (too.kg). In the area are the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves, the sacred spring Kotur-Bulak, a landslide-dammed lake (~10 km) and rock drawings (too.kg).
kg-0034.guide: Abshir-Ata is that rare waterfall that gushes straight out of the rock: the stream bursts from a dark opening at a height of 12–15 m. For locals it is a holy place — according to legend a wanderer struck a stone with his staff and milk flowed out of it — so behave as you would in a mosque: quietly and respectfully. In spring and early summer the flow is strongest; in summer the road is easier but there are more people (I Love KG). Do not stand under the wet overhanging walls — rockfalls happen. If you have time, drop by the sacred spring Kotur-Bulak and the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves (too.kg).
kg-0034.see: The stream from an opening in the rock (two cascades of ~15 and ~12 m); the revered holy spring; the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves; the Kotur-Bulak spring; the landslide-dammed lake ~10 km away; rock drawings at 5 and 20 km; old mine adits (too.kg, I Love KG).
kg-0034.skip: You have only one day in Osh — the road takes at least 2 h each way (I Love KG). You expect a big “wild” waterfall — this is a pilgrimage site with cafes and souvenirs (too.kg). You are going after heavy rain — the road and wet ledges are dangerous.
kg-0034.diff: Easy–moderate: access by dirt road, a short approach (~3 km up the gorge from the river mouth — Trip to Kyrgyzstan); the last sections are narrow and wet, and non-slip footwear is needed (I Love KG).
kg-0034.when: Late spring — early summer: the stream is most impressive, but the water is higher; dry summer — the road is easier, hotter and more crowded (I Love KG). A winter visit is not described.
kg-0034.hours: A natural/holy site with no opening hours; the cafes and guesthouses operate in season (too.kg); come back in daylight (I Love KG).
kg-0034.daytime: Morning — fewer pilgrims, less heat, light on the rock; plan your return before dark (I Love KG).
kg-0034.how: From Osh west to Nookat and then along local roads into the Abshir-Say gorge — about 70 km, at least 2 h each way (I Love KG). In the gorge there is a good dirt road all the way to the waterfall (too.kg); per Trip to Kyrgyzstan — about 3 km up the gorge from the river mouth. The direction “70 km east of Osh” (too.kg) is wrong: the valley and waterfall lie west–southwest of Osh (longitude ~72.36° versus ~72.80° for Osh); the road goes west through Nookat (I Love KG).
kg-0034.needcar: Yes: a car with a driver who waits, or your own car; there is no direct tourist transport (I Love KG).
kg-0034.self: Yes, in your own/rented car or with a driver: the road to the waterfall is dirt but good (too.kg); on site there are cafes and guesthouses.
kg-0034.roadtype: Paved Osh — Nookat, then local roads; in the gorge a good dirt road to the waterfall (too.kg); mud is possible after rain (I Love KG).
kg-0034.traveltime: Osh → waterfall: ~70 km, at least 2 h each way (I Love KG); on foot ~3 km along the gorge from the mouth (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The last 10 km are from the main road to the waterfall (24.kg).
kg-0034.stay: Guesthouses and cafes near the waterfall, camping spots (too.kg; Trip to Kyrgyzstan — Guest Houses); names and 2025–2026 prices not found. The main choice of accommodation is in Osh. Per 24.kg (05.2025): the gorge receives “more than 200 thousand” visitors per season, small recreation areas (tapchans, cafes) operate, but there are no proper toilets or hotels.
kg-0034.net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
kg-0034.entry: As of 2025 — free/there was no official fee: 24.kg (21.05.2025) writes that paid entry, parking and toilets are planned to be organized by 2026 under a World Bank project ($500 thousand). Whether a fee was introduced in 2026 and how much is not confirmed; have cash.
kg-0034.transfer: Not confirmed: 2025–2026 prices for a car with a driver Osh — Abshir-Ata were not found (there are no tours from Osh on Sputnik8/CBT). A guide: marshrutka Osh — Uzgen 70–100 som for ~55 km (eurasia.travel forum, 01.2025) — the fare to Nookat is comparable, then a taxi by arrangement.
kg-0034.bring: Water and food, non-slip shoes, a light rain jacket (spray), cash (I Love KG); for a pilgrimage site — covered clothing (editorial). Drink water from the river/lake only after boiling or filtering (too.kg, I Love KG).
kg-0034.warn: Do not stand under overhanging wet walls — rockfall; wet ledges are slippery; high water in spring (I Love KG). There is no signal (too.kg). Claims about the healing effect of the water are not confirmed by medical sources. The Google pin “Apshyr-Ata” ~75 km away is a different place; do not use it for navigation. The direction “70 km east of Osh” (too.kg) is wrong: the valley and waterfall lie west–southwest of Osh (longitude ~72.36° versus ~72.80° for Osh); the road goes west through Nookat (I Love KG). Mudflows on 28.06, 14.07 and 18.07.2024: 5 km of road and 4 of 5 bridges destroyed, 125 houses flooded; on 29.06.2024 more than 1,300 people were evacuated from the recreation area, and 6 people died in the district (Kaktus, 24.kg). As of May 2025 the old bridges were declared unsafe, and restoration was slow (24.kg 21.05.2025) — after downpours and in June–July do not enter the gorge, and watch for Emergencies Ministry warnings.
kg-0034.food: Cafes near the waterfall (too.kg) — national dishes (menu not confirmed); mineral water from springs (too.kg); in Osh and Nookat — Osh plov (editorial).
kg-0034.reviews: No cards with ratings were found on Google/2GIS/TripAdvisor (Google matched a different “Apshyr-Ata”; 07.10.2026). Per 24.kg (05.2025) — more than 200 thousand visitors per season; complaints about the lack of toilets and hotels, unsafe bridges. From videos/blogs: pluses — a unique “waterfall from a rock”, a holy place; minuses — summer crowds, the road.
kg-0034.p.sum: The waterfall is 70 km southwest of Osh (via Nookat, ≥2 h) — do it as a day trip by car with a driver from Osh or in your own car: the last ~10 km are a narrow dirt road (2 km of remaining asphalt + 8 km of single-lane dirt) after the 2024 mudflows. There is no public transport to the waterfall; on site there are seasonal tapchan cafes (raised platforms) and ~24 souvenir stalls, but no proper toilets, hotels or signal. Do not go after downpours and at the peak of floods (June–July).

kg-0036.name: Semyonovskoye Gorge
kg-0036.near: Semyonovka — a village on the north-shore highway at the mouth of the gorge (the Kichi-Ak-Suu gorge opens 4 km above the village — Nomad's Land); Grigorievka, 4 km to the west — the entrance to the neighbouring Chon-Ak-Suu. Kojoyar (OSM, 3.9 km) is the nearest marker to the catalogue point, but access is via Semyonovka.
kg-0036.elev: Gorge entrance ~1,900 m (Nomad's Land); Kyrchyn jailoo (summer pasture) ~2,100 m (eurasia.travel: the Kichi-Ak-Suu area ~2,100 m); Lake Sut-Bulak 2,450 m; Sut-Bulak Pass 3,924 m; peaks up to 4,260 m.
kg-0036.short: The most popular gorge on the north shore of Issyk-Kul: 30–35 km of spruce valley along the Kichi-Ak-Suu river above the village of Semyonovka, summer yurt camps on the Kyrchyn jailoo, horse rental, Lake Sut-Bulak; since 2026 a new paved road to Kyrchyn, the venue of the World Nomad Games.
kg-0036.desc: The gorge is named after P. P. Semyonov-Tian-Shansky and lies 40 km east of Cholpon-Ata on the southern slope of Kungey Ala-Too. From the village of Semyonovka the road climbs along the turbulent glacial Kichi-Ak-Suu river through spruce woods with barberry, sea buckthorn and currant to the broad Kyrchyn jailoo, where several rivers meet and where in summer yurt camps are set up with kumys and beshbarmak, horse rental and golden eagles for photos. Higher up is the “sacred” Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) and passes to the Grigorievskoye (Chon-Ak-Suu) gorge: at the head the two valleys join, so tours usually do a “Grigorievskoye — Semyonovskoye” loop. Kyrchyn is the ethnopark of the World Nomad Games (2016, 2018, 2026): for the Games of 1–6 September 2026, 35.5 km of road to the jailoo were paved, parking and fences were installed. At the entrance there is a barrier and a “modest eco fee” (eurasia.travel); 2GIS says “free entry”. Access year-round, in winter — ski slopes.
kg-0036.guide: If you have one day for the mountains on Issyk-Kul — take Semyonovskoye: since summer 2026 fresh asphalt leads to the Kyrchyn jailoo, and an ordinary car reaches the yurts. It is better to do the loop: go up via Grigorievskoye (steeper and narrower), cross the pass and come down via Semyonovskoye — this is what all the local guides show. At Kyrchyn take a horse for half an hour to an hour (a guide — 100 som for 10 minutes in 2024–2025), try kumys and shashlik in a yurt, but do not count on low prices — they are resort prices. If you have the energy, climb to Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m). On weekdays and in June there are many times fewer people than in August; on weekends in season there are traffic jams at the entrance.
kg-0036.see: Spruce slopes and the Kichi-Ak-Suu river; the Kyrchyn jailoo with yurt camps and the nomad games ethnopark; Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) — a side trip up; the pass into the Grigorievskoye gorge with views of the lake; eagle handlers and horse rental; in winter — ski slopes at the Kyrchyn tourist base.
kg-0036.skip: You are looking for untouched nature — in July–August this is the busiest gorge on the north shore. You are already planning Grigorievskoye: the landscape is similar and they are usually combined in one trip. You dislike “touristy” yurts with resort prices.
kg-0036.diff: Easy: to Kyrchyn — by car; walks on the jailoo — no elevation gain. The side trip to Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) — moderate, a few hours. Pass routes into Grigorievskoye — for the prepared (Sut-Bulak Pass 3,924 m).
kg-0036.when: The yurt camps run from late June/July to the end of September (too.kg: late July — late September; issykkul.biz: late June — late September). June — snowfields and greenery, August — peak; September — quiet and golden autumn. In winter there is access (eurasia.travel), skiing. On 1–6 September 2026 private-vehicle access was closed (World Nomad Games).
kg-0036.hours: Open terrain, around the clock; the barrier at the entrance works in daylight (eurasia.travel). Yurts — seasonal, daytime; the Kyrchyn tourist base — year-round.
kg-0036.daytime: First half of the day: tours from Cholpon-Ata start at 9:00–9:30, and by lunch Kyrchyn peaks; leave earlier or arrive after 15:00, when the groups leave. In the afternoon in summer thunderstorms are frequent.
kg-0036.how: From the Bishkek — Karakol highway (A363) in the village of Semyonovka (40 km east of Cholpon-Ata) turn south into the mountains; 35.5 km of road to the Kyrchyn jailoo were paved in 2026 (economist.kg, 20.07.2026). Marshrutkas (minibuses) Cholpon-Ata/Bosteri — Semyonovka/Grigorievka along the highway, then a taxi or on foot uphill (from the village to Kyrchyn ~15 km). From Bishkek ~4–5 h.
kg-0036.needcar: Yes: from the highway to Kyrchyn it is ~15 km; there are no regular marshrutkas in the gorge (free buses ran only for the World Nomad Games 2026). A passenger car manages the new road; for the upper reaches and the loop via Grigorievskoye — a 4×4.
kg-0036.self: Yes: the road has signs, no permits; at the entrance a barrier with an eco fee. Independently it is convenient in your own/rented car; on foot from Semyonovka it is long (15 km uphill).
kg-0036.roadtype: Paved from the highway to the Kyrchyn jailoo (35.5 km renovated and paved by July 2026 — economist.kg); previously issykkul.biz: ~15 km of paved road from the village, then dirt. Above Kyrchyn and over the pass into Grigorievskoye — dirt, 4×4 (2GIS: “a passenger car can pass, a 4×4 is recommended”).
kg-0036.traveltime: Cholpon-Ata — Semyonovka ~40 min; Semyonovka — Kyrchyn ~30–40 min on the new road; a tour with the loop via Grigorievskoye — 10 h (Tripster/Sputnik8). A walk in the gorge — 2 h (ru_travel).
kg-0036.stay: Yurt camps at Kyrchyn (an overnight in a yurt with meals is part of Tripster tours; prices are not published separately), the Kyrchyn tourist base (year-round — eurasia.travel), guesthouses in Semyonovka/Grigorievka, the Ananyevo and Bosteri guesthouse resorts. Specific 2025–2026 prices not found.
kg-0036.net: In May 2026 Beeline KG installed new base stations “in the Semyonovskoye gorge (Kyrchyn)” and in the villages of Ornok, Chok-Tal, Kojoyar, Frunze (economist.kg, 25.05.2026) — Beeline coverage exists in the Kyrchyn area; other operators — not confirmed; do not expect coverage above Lake Sut-Bulak.
kg-0036.entry: Contradictory: 2GIS — “free entry”; eurasia.travel — a barrier at the entrance and a “modest eco fee” (amount not stated). Separate paid services: horses, a golden eagle for photos, yurts. Check on site; a guide from similar places in the region — 50–200 som per car.
kg-0036.transfer: Tour from Cholpon-Ata: 700 som (group of 7–14) / 900 som (3–6) per person (issykkul.biz, date not stated); Tripster 4×4 €250 per car for up to 6 people (2025); Sputnik8 $230 per group (2024 archive). Horse — 100 som/10 min. Lunch in a yurt — from 600 som (Sputnik8).
kg-0036.bring: A windbreaker and a warm layer (Kyrchyn is 500 m higher than the lake, cold in the evening), sun protection, cash (yurts, horses, eco fee), water, swimwear for Ak-Bermet on the way, trekking shoes for Sut-Bulak.
kg-0036.warn: Do not confuse them: the Semyonovskoye gorge starts from the village of Semyonovka (Kichi-Ak-Suu), the Grigorievskoye from Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu); guidebooks mix them up. Prices in the yurts are resort prices (ru_travel). During mass events at Kyrchyn (nomad games) private-vehicle entry is closed. Thunderstorms after lunch, the river is glacial — do not swim. Photos with a golden eagle/eagle cost extra, and the animals are not always kept humanely.
kg-0036.food: In the Kyrchyn yurts: kumys, beshbarmak, kuurdak, shashlik, boorsok, apiary honey (too.kg, issykkul.biz, ru_travel); lunch in a yurt from 600 som (Sputnik8). Trout from the Ak-Suu — in cafes by the highway. Specific yurts were not checked.
kg-0036.reviews: 2GIS “Semyonovskoye Gorge (Kyrchyn)”: 4.9/5, 320 ratings, 73 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: 4.8/5, 73 ratings (03.10.2026). Tripster (tour): 4.89, 35 reviews. Pros: accessibility, spruce and river, yurts, horses; cons: crowds in season, inflated prices in the yurts, dirt road above Kyrchyn.
kg-0036.p.sum: The simplest mountain outing on the north shore: from the A363 highway in the village of Semyonovka (≈40 km east of Cholpon-Ata) turn south; since summer 2026, 35.5 km of road to the Kyrchyn jailoo are paved, so an ordinary sedan gets there. Without a car — a marshrutka along the highway to Semyonovka and a taxi up, or a tour from Cholpon-Ata (700–900 som per person in a group; 4×4 €250 per car). At Kyrchyn — yurts with lunch (from 600 som), horses (100 som/10 min), a short climb to Lake Sut-Bulak (≈3 km, +400 m). Stay overnight in a yurt at Kyrchyn, the Kyrchyn tourist base or the guesthouse resorts of Chok-Tal/Bosteri.

kg-0038.name: Karavshin Gorge
kg-0038.full: Karavshin Gorge (the Kara-Suu and Ak-Suu valleys, “Asian Patagonia”)
kg-0038.near: Ozgorush (Uzgurush/Ozguruush) — the starting village of the treks, ~23 km as the crow flies from the catalog point (OSM); there is a guesthouse in the village. From Osh to Uzgurush it is ~360 km, 8–9 h by car (goodway.club).
kg-0038.elev: The valleys are roughly 2500–3000 m (visitkyrgyzstan.org: 2500–5509 m for the district); peaks — Pyramidalny Peak 5509 m (the highest point of the Turkestan Range), Ak-Suu Peak 5355 m, Kotov Peak 4521 m, Usen Peak 4378 m, Asan Peak 4230 m, Slesov Peak 4240 m (central-asia.guide). The highest point of the trek is Ak-Tyubek Pass 4324 m (goodway.club).
kg-0038.short: A gorge in the Turkestan Range in the southwest of Batken Region, with the granite walls of Asan, Usen, Slesov and 4810 peaks — “Asian Patagonia”, one of the world's centers of big-wall climbing; a border zone with a mandatory permit.
kg-0038.desc: Karavshin is a system of valleys of the Kara-Suu and Ak-Suu rivers on the northern slope of the Turkestan Range near the border with Tajikistan (central-asia.guide; visitkyrgyzstan.org). The granite walls of Asan (4230 m), Usen (4378 m), Slesov (4240 m), Pyramidalny (5509 m) and 4810 peaks have made the area famous as “Asian Patagonia”; routes of the highest difficulty category (6B) are climbed here (central-asia.guide; YouTube). There are no roads into the gorge: you get there on foot (about 70 km, central-asia.guide) with pack animals over passes from the village of Uzgurush, or by helicopter. The classic “Asian Patagonia” trek is 106 km in 12 days over the passes Buljuma, Dalgychy (3774 m), Kosh-Moinok (3187 m), Kara-Suu (3702 m) and Ak-Tyubek (4324 m) (goodway.club). The area is in the border zone: a border permit is required for Karavshin and the whole Leilek district (tour.too.kg, 2026). After the armed conflicts of 2021 and 2022 on the border with Tajikistan, the area was hard to reach; on 13.03.2025 a state border treaty was signed and the Kairagach (Leilek district) and Kyzyl-Bel border crossings were opened (Times of Central Asia), and tourist seasons in 2025–2026 are running (Ak-Sai, goodway).
kg-0038.guide: Karavshin is a place for those ready for an expedition: no road, only a week or two on foot over passes up to 4300 m, but at the end — granite walls that climbers compare to Patagonia. The main “stars” are Asan and Usen peaks (by legend, two brothers) and 4810 with 6B routes; even without climbing you will see them from the trail at the confluence of the Kara-Suu and Ak-Suu. Arrange the border-zone permit at least two weeks ahead, or better still go with an operator who will handle the permit, horses and the drop-off from Osh (8–9 hours). The season is short — mid-July to early September, and the most stable window is August. Remember that this is an area by a recently delimited border: keep your documents with you and do not leave the agreed route.
kg-0038.see: The granite walls of Asan (4230 m), Usen (4378 m), Slesov (4240 m), 4810 and Pyramidalny (5509 m) peaks; the Kara-Suu and Ak-Suu valleys with alpine meadows and glaciers; the passes of the “Asian Patagonia” trek (Ak-Tyubek 4324 m, Kara-Suu 3702 m, Dalgychy 3774 m); herds of yaks (central-asia.guide; goodway.club).
kg-0038.skip: You have less than 8–12 days and no experience of multi-day hikes with passes of 3700–4300 m. You are not prepared to arrange a border permit in advance and accept the risks of a border zone. You need signal and infrastructure — there are none in the gorge (except Starlink at the Ak-Sai camps).
kg-0038.diff: Hard: a 106 km trek in 12 days, elevation range 1400–4324 m, 5 passes (goodway.club rates it 3/5 with pack support); the standard loop route is 8 days, 6+ passes, ~8 km of total ascent (epicexpeditions). Mountaineering — up to 6B.
kg-0038.when: Mid-July to early/mid-September; the most stable and driest weather is in August (goodway.club; visitkyrgyzstan.org; epicexpeditions). The Ak-Sai camps operate in July–August. Snow is possible on the high passes even in July.
kg-0038.hours: No schedule; entry into the border zone only with a valid border permit (3000 som, 7 working days to process, apply at least 14 days ahead — tour.too.kg, 2026). Ak-Sai camps — July–August.
kg-0038.daytime: Start early for the passes (before noon there is less risk of bad weather); the walls of Asan and Usen look most striking in morning and evening light (editorial).
kg-0038.how: Osh → Batken (marshrutka (minibus) 320–430 som, ~4.5 h; taxi ~3 h) → Uzgurush (private taxi/4×4). The whole of Osh — Uzgurush is ~360 km, 8–9 h, back ~340 km, 6–7 h (goodway.club). Alternative: a flight Bishkek — Batken (~1.5 h, visitkyrgyzstan.org). From Uzgurush — only on foot/with pack animals over passes (7–12 days by loop; ~70 km to the gorge) or by helicopter.
kg-0038.needcar: Yes: to Uzgurush — a drop-off by car (usually included in the tour); beyond that — on foot with horses/donkeys, or a helicopter.
kg-0038.self: Formally — with a personal border permit (tour.too.kg) and experience of self-sufficient hikes, but in practice a local guide/operator is recommended: almost nobody speaks English, there is no signal, there are no rescue services, and the area is on the border (epicexpeditions; visitkyrgyzstan.org).
kg-0038.roadtype: Paved to Batken; Batken — Uzgurush is a local road (part of the way from Osh passes Uzbek enclaves); from Uzgurush — only trails over passes (goodway.club; epicexpeditions).
kg-0038.traveltime: Osh — Uzgurush 8–9 h (back 6–7 h); Osh — Batken ~4.5 h by marshrutka; the trek to Karavshin takes 2–3 days from Uzgurush, the loop route 8–12 days (goodway.club; epicexpeditions; visitkyrgyzstan.org).
kg-0038.stay:
• Ak-Sai Travel camps (July–August): tent $55/night, with meals $85, single with meals $105; Starlink, generator, shower/toilet tents (ak-sai.com, 2026).
• Guesthouse in Uzgurush: 6 double rooms, contact Sulaiman +996 552 717 178 (WhatsApp) (epicexpeditions, 2026).
• Guesthouses in Batken — $15–25/night (visitkyrgyzstan.org).
• Otherwise — your own tents, and all equipment and food you bring yourself.
kg-0038.net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge (visitkyrgyzstan.org); there is signal at the guesthouse in Uzgurush (goodway.club); at the Ak-Sai camps — Starlink (ak-sai.com).
kg-0038.entry: There is no entrance fee, but a border permit is mandatory: 3000 som per person, 7 working days to process (tour.too.kg, 2026; one permit covers all border zones). Through operators/CBT — €20–30 (epicexpeditions) or included in the tour price.
kg-0038.transfer: Marshrutka Osh — Batken 320–430 som; taxi Osh — Batken $30–40; the Osh — Uzgurush drop-off is included in the goodway tour ($630 for 12 days); a porter at the Ak-Sai camps — $55; pack animals — $10–15/day (2025–2026 sources, some without a year).
kg-0038.bring: Border permit and passport; full equipment for a multi-day hike (tent, sleeping bag rated to −5 °C, stove, crampons/ice axe for Ak-Tyubek depending on conditions); a first-aid kit; food for the whole route; cash (there are no ATMs in Uzgurush — not confirmed); a satellite communicator.
kg-0038.warn: Border zone on the border with Tajikistan: a border permit is mandatory (3000 som, 7 working days, tour.too.kg 2026). The area suffered in the conflicts of 2021 and 2022; the border treaty was signed on 13.03.2025, but the US recommends “increased caution” in the 30 km zone and Australia says to “reconsider the need to travel”; a brief closure of the crossing near Leilek was reported in early 2026, as well as unexploded ordnance after 2022 (epicexpeditions, 2026). There is no signal and no rescue service; altitude up to 4300 m; snow on the passes is possible in summer.
kg-0038.food: Home cooking at the guesthouse in Uzgurush; Batken apricots (dried apricots, uryuk); at the Ak-Sai camps — three meals a day (ak-sai.com).
kg-0038.reviews: The Google Maps pin is not matched, no rating (07.10.2026). Reports from hikers and climbers (goodway, epicexpeditions, Mountain Project) unanimously note the outstanding granite walls and solitude; minuses — complicated logistics, the permit, no signal and no infrastructure.
kg-0038.p.sum: Karavshin is a multi-day trek / mountaineering expedition: first a border permit for Leilek District (tour.too.kg, 3000 som, 5–7 working days; with Ak-Sai it is $40 and ~1 month), then Osh/Batken → the village of Uzgurush (Ozgorush) by car (Osh — Uzgurush ~300–360 km, 7–9 h), then on foot with pack horses/donkeys: 18 km (1 day) to the base camp or 7–11 days around the “Asian Patagonia” loop. The easiest is a group tour (Visit Alay 11 days $500, goodway 12 days $630) or the Ak-Sai camps ($55–105/night).

kg-0039.name: Lake Issyk-Kul
kg-0039.dist: The shoreline runs through five districts
kg-0039.near: The catalog point is in the middle of the lake; the nearest shores are Cholpon-Ata / Bosteri (north shore, ~20 km) and Tamga / Tosor (south shore). The main towns on the lake: Cholpon-Ata, Karakol (12 km from the eastern shore), Balykchy (west).
kg-0039.elev: 1607–1608 m above sea level (Sputnik8: 1608 m; the commonly accepted value is 1607–1609 m, and the level fluctuates from year to year).
kg-0039.short: The world's second-largest high-mountain lake that never freezes (6,236 km², up to 668 m deep, 1607 m above sea level), lying between the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges. It is Kyrgyzstan's main resort region, with a beach season from late June to mid-September.
kg-0039.desc: Issyk-Kul (“warm lake”) is an endorheic, slightly brackish (5.9 ‰) lake 182 km long and up to 58 km wide, with a 688 km shoreline and a volume of 1,738 km³ (CAIAG). About 80 rivers flow in and none flows out; because of its salinity and depth the lake does not freeze in winter. In summer the water warms to 19–25 °C (22–25 °C near the shore in July–August). The north shore (Cholpon-Ata, Bosteri, Chok-Tal) has sandy beaches, pansionats (Soviet-style resort hotels) and lively holidays; the south shore (Tamga, Kadji-Sai, Bokonbaevo) is quieter, with canyons and yurt camps; the east has Karakol and the gateway to Terskey Ala-Too. The lake and its basin are part of the Issyk-Kul UNESCO biosphere reserve. Pleasure boats and yachts sail from Cholpon-Ata (500 som for 1–1.5 h, 2024), and the shores have petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, Kyrchyn and hot-spring baths.
kg-0039.guide: First choose a shore: the north if you want a beach, a pansionat and nightlife; the south if you want quiet, canyons and yurts; Karakol if you are here for the mountains. Don't only look at the lake from the beach: a two-hour boat trip from Cholpon-Ata with a swim in deep water costs ~500 som and runs from mid-June to mid-September. The water is 22–25 °C in July–August, but the sun at 1,600 m is harsh — you will burn in an hour. Beaches at pansionats are often paid (200–300 som); wild ones are free. June and September are quiet and cheaper, and the water is still/already good for swimming.
kg-0039.see: North shore: the beaches of Cholpon-Ata and Bosteri, the Cholpon-Ata petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, the Grigorievka and Semyonovka gorges. South shore: Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Manjyly-Ata, Barskoon, Jeti-Oguz, the beaches of Tamga and Kadji-Sai, and Bokonbaevo with its eagle hunters (berkutchi). East: Karakol, the Przhevalsky museum at the Pristan (port) area. Boat and yacht trips on the water; sunsets over the lake.
kg-0039.skip: You expect a warm sea: even in August the water is rarely above 25 °C. You are coming in October–May for the beach — the season is closed and only sanatoriums and the mountains are open. You want solitude on the north shore in July–August — there is none.
kg-0039.diff: Not applicable to the lake as a whole; beaches and boat trips have no restrictions; for mountain routes, see the gorge cards.
kg-0039.when: Beach season is late June to mid-September (freedom-travel.kz, 2026; Sputnik8: June–September, peak July–August); June and September have fewer people and lower prices. In winter: skiing in Karakol and the sanatoriums; the lake does not freeze.
kg-0039.hours: There is no single schedule: pansionat beaches are open in daytime and cost from 200–300 som (2026); boats from Cholpon-Ata run from 15 June to 15 September, with daytime trips and evening “parties”. For the hours of specific places, see their cards.
kg-0039.daytime: Swim after 12:00, when the water and air have warmed up; for photos, sunset on the north shore (the sun sets behind Kungey) and sunrise on the south; evening boat trips last 2 h.
kg-0039.how: From Bishkek: marshrutkas (minibuses) from the new bus station (Koltsevaya/Alma-Atinskaya; the Western bus station has been closed since late 2024): to Balykchy 300 som, to Karakol 450–500 som (Kaktus.media 04.2024; Destination Karakol), to Cholpon-Ata ~4 h; shared taxi to Karakol 1000–1500 som, private taxi to Cholpon-Ata ~7000 som, to Karakol ~11,000 som (Sputnik8, 11.2025). From Almaty: bus to Balykchy ~$4, transfer $100–150, flight Almaty — Tamchy (FlyArystan, seasonal). Issyk-Kul airport (Tamchy) gets charter flights in summer.
kg-0039.needcar: To move between shores — yes (the loop around the lake is ~440 km); marshrutkas run along the shore on the A363 highway Balykchy — Cholpon-Ata — Karakol and on the southern road Balykchy — Bokonbaevo — Karakol.
kg-0039.self: Yes, fully: the road around the lake is paved, marshrutkas run, and no permits are needed (the border zone is only in the upper reaches of the Sary-Jaz/Inylchek and near Kegen — not at the lake).
kg-0039.roadtype: Paved road all the way around the lake (A363 in the north, the southern road Balykchy — Karakol); the southern road is worse in places. Access roads to the gorges are dirt roads / 4×4.
kg-0039.traveltime: Bishkek — Balykchy ~3 h; — Cholpon-Ata ~4 h; — Karakol 5–7 h (marshrutka) / 5–6 h (taxi) (Destination Karakol 2024, Sputnik8 2025). Almaty — Issyk-Kul by car ~8 h.
kg-0039.stay: 2026 (freedom-travel.kz): north shore — 3–4* hotels $80–150/night at peak, guesthouses $50–80, budget $30–45; south shore — yurts/glamping $40–70, guesthouses $40–60; hostels $10–25 per bed. Sputnik8: budget $8–10, mid-range $15–20, premium $50–90 (outdated benchmarks). For specific places, see the town cards.
kg-0039.net: All three operators cover the coast (Beeline KG, MegaCom, O!); since 2019 MegaCom has 4G in Cholpon-Ata, Balykchy, Karakol, Bokonbaevo and Ananyevo; in 2024–2026 Beeline is putting up new base stations in resort villages (Ornok, Chok-Tal, Kojoyar, Kyrchyn). There is no signal in the gorges. Tourists recommend Beeline/MegaCom (freedom-travel.kz, 2026) or O! (eurasia.travel).
kg-0039.entry: There is no single entrance. Paid beaches at pansionats cost 200–300 som (freedom-travel.kz, 2026); wild beaches are free. A boat trip costs 500 som (2024).
kg-0039.transfer: Marshrutka Bishkek — Karakol 450–500 som (2024), — Balykchy 300 som (2024), — Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (2025); shared taxi to Karakol 1000–1500 som (2024); taxi Bishkek — Cholpon-Ata ~7000 som, — Karakol ~11,000 som (2025); Almaty — Issyk-Kul transfer $100–150 (2026).
kg-0039.bring: SPF 50 sunscreen and a hat (1,600 m, strong UV), swimsuit, a light jacket for the evening (nights are +10–15 °C even in summer), cash in som (cards are not accepted everywhere), water shoes for the pebble beaches of the south, warm clothes for trips into the mountains.
kg-0039.warn: The strong high-altitude sun burns you within an hour. The water is cool and gets cold quickly with depth; swimming in a storm is dangerous. Boats only with life jackets. Prices in season go up 1.5–2 times; on weekends the north shore has traffic jams and a shortage of rooms. Ticks in the gorges in May–June. The border zone is only far from the lake (upper Sary-Jaz); no permits are needed on the coast.
kg-0039.food: Smoked and fried fish from stalls along the highway and at bazaars (chebak/roach, farmed trout), ashlyan-fu in Karakol, beshbarmak and kumys in yurts, fresh apricots and apples on the south shore (July–August), honey. Specific eateries have not been checked.
kg-0039.reviews: Google Maps “Issyk-Kul”: 4.7/5, 2,690 ratings (03.10.2026). Typical pluses from 2025–2026 guides and reviews: clean water, views of snowy ranges, variety of shores; minuses — cool water, seasonal prices, crowds and litter on the north shore in August, service in old pansionats.
kg-0039.p.sum: First choose a shore. The north (Cholpon-Ata, Bosteri, Chok-Tal) has beaches, pansionats and boats, 4–5 h from Bishkek on the A363; the south (Bokonbaevo, Kadji-Sai, Tamga, Tosor) has quiet, yurts and canyons, 5–6 h. The easiest way to get there is a marshrutka/GoBus from the Bishkek bus station (400–600 som), in summer by train Bishkek-2 → Balykchy (daily from 26.06 to 13.09.2026, from 150 som); from Kazakhstan by FlyArystan flight to Tamchy or via the Kegen — Karkyra border crossing to Karakol. The loop around the lake (~440 km) is fully paved, and marshrutkas run along both shores.

kg-0039.p.permits: Not needed: there is no border zone on the coast (the border zone is in the upper reaches of the Ak-Suu district, Inylchek/Merzbacher). When entering from Kazakhstan — regular passport control at Kordai or Kegen — Karkyra.
kg-0039.p.access: Very accessible: flat beaches, pansionats with meals, medical sanatoriums; for wheelchairs — the promenades and grounds of large pansionats, but not the wild beaches. With children — July–August (warm water), but the sun is harsh. With dogs — many pansionats do not allow them, so check; wild beaches are fine.

kg-0040.name: Kyzart Pass
kg-0040.dist: On the highway between the Kochkor and Jumgal districts
kg-0040.near: The village of Kyzart (Jumgal district, population 1516 in 2021) — about 14 km southwest of the pass, at the descent into the Jumgal valley; Kochkor is the base for trips (~55–60 km along the highway, estimate); Chayek is the Jumgal district center.
kg-0040.elev: 2664 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Nomad's Land, Wikipedia, Knews).
kg-0040.short: A year-round road pass (2664 m) on the EM-18 highway (formerly A-367) Kochkor–Chayek between the Kochkor and Jumgal valleys; the starting point of horse routes to Song-Kol and the famous roadside trailers selling fried peled (whitefish).
kg-0040.desc: Kyzart is a modest pass between the Kum-Bel and Baba-Ata ranges on the international EM-18 highway (formerly A-367), which leads from Kochkor into the Jumgal valley, to Chayek and on toward Suusamyr. The eastern slope is gentle, the western is steep; the pass is open year-round, although in winter there is strong wind and snow here. The folk name is “Maiden Pass”: according to local legend, forty girls died of cold here. At a small parking area next to a mosque, blue trailer cafes serve only fried peled from Lake Song-Kol, bread and tea. In summer yurts stand around, and the pass itself and the village of the same name are the main starting points of horse and hiking trips by CBT Kochkor and local herders to Song-Kol via the Kyzyl-Kiya jailoo (summer pasture), Chaar-Archa Pass (3061 m), the Kilemche jailoo (summer pasture) and Jalgyz-Karagai Pass (3400 m).
kg-0040.guide: Stop at Kyzart for lunch — in the blue trailers by the mosque they fry peled from Song-Kol (100–150 som a fish in 2019), and tea is poured without limit. If you are riding to Song-Kol, clarify exactly where you meet: CBT Kochkor gathers groups at the pass itself, while private horse handlers and Horseback Holiday meet in the village of Kyzart, 14 km lower. Haggle: according to 2025 reviews, the price of a horse tour for two in the village was brought down from 15,000 to 10,000 som. In winter the pass is open, but the wind here is piercing — don't plan a long stop.
kg-0040.see: A view of the Kochkor and Jumgal valleys; trailer cafes with fried peled by the mosque; summer yurts; the start of horse trails to Song-Kol (Kyzyl-Kiya, Chaar-Archa 3061 m, Kilemche); Mount Baba-Ata on the way.
kg-0040.skip: You are not going to Jumgal or riding to Song-Kol — the pass itself is low, more a point on the highway than a destination in its own right. You don't eat fish. You want dramatic serpentines — there are more of them on Moldo-Ashuu.
kg-0040.diff: Easy for a car: a paved road with occasional gravel sections (Knews, 2019), open year-round. The horse/hiking route to Song-Kol is moderate: 2 passes above 3000–3400 m, 4–6 h a day (CBT Kochkor); on foot ~60 km in 3 days.
kg-0040.when: As transit — year-round (Nomad's Land, Wikipedia). For horse treks to Song-Kol — mid-June to the end of September (CBT Kochkor); yurts on the route — mid-June to early September.
kg-0040.hours: The highway is open year-round. Trailer cafes — hours not published (they work in season and by day, and per a 2019 review in autumn as well).
kg-0040.daytime: By day: in winter and the off-season ice and wind are possible in the morning; in season, lunch in the trailer cafes. For the start of a horse route — early in the morning (5–6 h of travel).
kg-0040.how: Along the EM-18 highway from Kochkor west toward Chayek: Kochkor → Kyzart Pass (~55–60 km, ~1 h; estimate) → descent to the village of Kyzart and into the Jumgal valley (Jumgal is 68 km from Kochkor per Nomad's Land). From Bishkek: Bishkek–Balykchy–Kochkor–Kyzart, ~260 km (estimate). From the south, from Song-Kol — on horseback via Jalgyz-Karagai and Kilemche.
kg-0040.needcar: For the pass — a car/taxi/marshrutka (minibus) toward Chayek. For the horse route — a transfer Kochkor → the pass/the village of Kyzart, then a horse.
kg-0040.self: Yes: the pass is on an open highway, no permits. The hiking trek to Song-Kol can be done independently with offline maps (no markings); a horse — only with a guide.
kg-0040.roadtype: International highway EM-18: paved with gravel sections (Knews, 2019); the eastern climb is gentle, the western descent to the village of Kyzart is steep. From the pass/village to Kilemche — horse and foot trails, not roads.
kg-0040.traveltime: Kochkor — the pass ~1 h (estimate); Bishkek — Kyzart ~4–4.5 h. Horse route: Kyzart Pass → Kilemche 4–5 h on horseback (5–6 h on foot), Kilemche → Song-Kol ~5 h on horseback (CBT Kochkor); on foot 18 + 18 + 24 km in 3 days (elprismadefer).
kg-0040.stay: Yurts at the pass in summer (Nomad's Land); Trip to Kyrgyzstan mentions guesthouses in the area. On the horse route: a CBT yurt camp at Kilemche — 1500 som without meals / 2000 som with dinner and breakfast; a yurt at Song-Kol — 1500–2000 som with breakfast/dinner (2024–2025). In the village of Kyzart — a homestay with horse handlers (Horseback Holiday), prices on request.
kg-0040.net: Not confirmed by sources for the saddle; on the Kochkor–Chayek highway and in the villages there is a signal (operators not named). On the horse route above Kyzyl-Kiya there is no signal — offline maps are essential.
kg-0040.entry: Free: the pass is on an open highway, no fees.
kg-0040.transfer: Kochkor — Kyzart: 350–400 som/seat shared (2025), a private car 3000 som; Kyzart — Kochkor back 3000 som per car (elprismadefer); Bishkek — Kochkor 350 som (May 2026).
kg-0040.bring: A windproof jacket (strong wind on the pass), cash for fish and tea; for a horse trek — a sleeping bag, rain jacket, sun protection, offline maps (Maps.me/Gaia GPS), water.
kg-0040.warn: The road pass and the village of Kyzart (the start of some horse treks) are different points 14 km apart: clarify the meeting place. In winter wind, snow and ice on the highway. Prices from private horse handlers in Kyzart are inflated — haggle and fix the terms in advance (TripAdvisor, May 2025; brokennavigation 2025).
kg-0040.food: Fried peled from Song-Kol in the blue trailers by the mosque on the pass — 100 som (small) / 150 som (large), tea without limit (Knews, autumn 2019; 2025–2026 prices not confirmed). On the route — kumys from herders, dinner in yurts.
kg-0040.reviews: Google Maps (“Pereval Kyzart”): 5/5, 2 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor on the Kyzart — Song-Kol routes: pros — beautiful pastures and passes, hospitality; cons — difficulties with transport from Kyzart and attempts to inflate the price (May 2025). No separate TripAdvisor page for the pass was found.
kg-0040.p.sum: Kyzart (2664 m) is a paved-and-gravel pass on the Kochkor–Chayek highway, passable year-round: ≈55 km (≈1 h) from Kochkor, and 14 km lower is the village of Kyzart, the main start of hiking and horse trips to Song-Kol via Kilemche. Getting there: marshrutka (minibus) No. 541 “Chayek” from Bishkek or a shared taxi from Kochkor (350–400 som/seat, 2025). A 3-day horse tour with local guides costs 15–20 thousand som/person (2025); there is a marked trail “Starry Song Kul Nights”.

kg-0041.name: Boom Gorge
kg-0041.near: Inside the gorge — roadside villages and stops (2GIS ties the object to the village of Kyz-Kuyoo); at the western entrance — Jil-Aryk/Kyzyl-Bulak, at the eastern — the town of Balykchy. The calculation “Jol-Bulak 7.2 km” referred to the wrong catalogue point.
kg-0041.elev: Not confirmed by an exact source. As a guideline: the floor of the gorge rises along the Chu from the western entrance to the Balykchy area at Issyk-Kul (~1600 m); exact elevations for individual sections were not found.
kg-0041.short: Boom is a narrow gorge of the Chu River about 30 km long, through which the Bishkek — Issyk-Kul highway and railway pass: cliffs, a turbulent river, rafting and roadside stops.
kg-0041.desc: Boom Gorge (Boom) was cut by the Chu River between the Kungey Ala-Too and Kyrgyz Ala-Too ranges and links the Chu Valley with the Issyk-Kul basin; it is about 30 km long (2GIS, Trip to Kyrgyzstan, TripAdvisor). Historically it was the only western route to Issyk-Kul: a carriage road was built in the 1870s, and the Bishkek — Balykchy railway (189 km) opened in 1948. Today the Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway and the summer tourist train to Issyk-Kul run through it. The slopes change from green to dry clay canyons; at the entrance are the “Cold Springs” (Kholodnye Klyuchi) spring and roadside cafes, and along the way Soviet and modern sculptures (a snow leopard, eagles, deer), the Red Bridge and the turnoff to the Konorchek canyons. Rafting operators work on the Chu (class II–IV rapids).
kg-0041.guide: Most people fly through Boom on the way to Issyk-Kul, but it deserves at least an hour. Stop at the “Cold Springs” (Kholodnye Klyuchi) spring at the gorge entrance — there is a cafe, yurts and ice-cold water — and then look for the sculptures of a snow leopard and deer along the highway. The most vivid way to see Boom is from the water: a one-day rafting trip on the Chu (May — mid-September) runs rapids up to class IV. In summer try riding through the gorge on the Bishkek — Balykchy tourist train: the windows look straight out onto the river. From the Red Bridge a trail leads into the Konorchek canyons — an excellent continuation of the day.
kg-0041.see: The Chu River in a rocky corridor; the “Cold Springs” spring at the entrance; sculptures of a snow leopard, eagles and deer and Soviet monuments along the highway; the Red Bridge over the Chu and the turnoff to the Konorchek canyons; the 1948 railway with tunnels and bridges; clay canyons on the dry slopes.
kg-0041.skip: You are already passing through it in transit to Issyk-Kul — the main things are visible from the window. You're looking for quiet: a busy highway runs through the gorge, and in summer there are traffic jams several kilometres long. You aren't planning rafting or Konorchek — a separate trip just for the gorge adds little.
kg-0041.diff: As a stop on the highway — no effort, roadside stops. Rafting on the Chu at Boom — class II–IV rapids (kyrgyzguidedtours; rafting.kg rates the Boom section as class IV), suitable for beginners with an instructor, not recommended if you can't swim.
kg-0041.when: Driving through — year-round. Rafting — May to mid-September, water 15–18 °C (kyrgyzguidedtours). The summer Bishkek — Balykchy train runs from 5 June to 13 September 2026 (24.kg). In spring — rock-clearing works and a risk of rockfalls.
kg-0041.hours: The highway is open round the clock. Planned closures are possible: for example, on 6–10 April 2026, from 10:00 to 16:00, dangerous rocks were brought down at km 131 of the Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway, with traffic running in alternating directions (Kaktus.media 03.04.2026). The Bishkek-2 → Balykchy train: departure 08:06, arrival 12:37; return 18:40 → 23:11 (summer 2026).
kg-0041.daytime: A weekday morning: fewer cars and soft light in the gorge. On summer weekend evenings (the return from Issyk-Kul) — traffic jams; try to drive through before lunch.
kg-0041.how: From Bishkek along the Bishkek — Balykchy highway (≈100–112 km to the gorge; eurasia.travel: 112 km). Marshrutkas (minibuses) and buses to Balykchy, Cholpon-Ata and Karakol go through Boom; in summer — the Bishkek-2 → Balykchy tourist train. For rafting, operators pick you up in Bishkek. The Konorchek canyons are a separate walking start at the Red Bridge.
kg-0041.needcar: Yes, the gorge is far from Bishkek, but any transport works: a marshrutka (minibus)/bus, the train, a taxi or your own car. For stops at the spring and sculptures, your own car or a taxi is more convenient.
kg-0041.self: Yes: a marshrutka (minibus) or the train passes through the gorge, and your own car lets you stop at the spring and sculptures. Rafting — only with an operator.
kg-0041.roadtype: A paved Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway with rockfall protection structures; the railway runs alongside. The turnoffs to Konorchek and the camps are dirt roads.
kg-0041.traveltime: Bishkek → the entrance to Boom ≈1.5–2 h by car; driving through the gorge (~30 km) takes about 30–40 min without traffic jams. A rafting tour is a full day 09:00–17:00, of which 40–60 min on the water (kyrgyzguidedtours); the Bishkek — Balykchy train — 4.5 h.
kg-0041.stay: Inside the gorge — roadside guesthouses and yurts at cafes (too.kg); pitching a tent by the highway is inconvenient because of the traffic. The main choice of accommodation is Balykchy and Chon-Kemin (guesthouses and yurt camps).
kg-0041.net: Too.kg reports full mobile coverage along the gorge; the specific operator and speed have not been measured.
kg-0041.entry: Entry is free: the gorge is a stretch of the state highway, with no toll or visiting fee (the sources mention no charges). Paid services — cafes, rafting, parking at cafes.
kg-0041.transfer: A marshrutka (minibus) to Issyk-Kul 500–600 som, GoBus ~650 som, a taxi ~1200 som/seat or 4500 som/car (24.kg, July 2026); the train 150–180 som standard (2026); rafting with transfer $70/person in a group (Kyrgyz Guided Tours). There is no separate fare specifically to Boom — you pay as for Balykchy.
kg-0041.bring: For a stop — a jacket (it's windy in the gorge), water and cash for cafes. For rafting — a change of clothes, shoes you don't mind getting wet, sun protection; the wetsuit and gear are provided by the operator.
kg-0041.warn: Rockfalls and mudflows: the gorge is on the list of sections where mudflows and rockfalls are possible (24.kg); in spring dangerous rocks are brought down with traffic closed. On summer weekends — traffic jams several kilometres long. Don't stop on narrow sections of the highway with no shoulder. Rafting — only with a licensed operator and in a life jacket.
kg-0041.food: Roadside cafes and yurts at the “Cold Springs” (Kholodnye Klyuchi)/“Cold Water” spring at the gorge entrance (eurasia.travel, 2GIS): Kyrgyz dishes, tea, spring water. Specific places and prices are not confirmed.
kg-0041.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 73 ratings (03.10.2026); 2GIS: 4.6/5, 281 ratings, 32 reviews (07.10.2026); TripAdvisor: 4.5/5, 25 reviews (07.10.2026). Pros: views of cliffs and the river, convenient stops, a good road. Cons: from the highway the gorge looks “unimpressive”, it's better seen from the river; traffic jams.
kg-0041.p.sum: Boom is not a separate trip but a ~30 km stretch of the Bishkek — Balykchy highway along the Chu River (1.5–2 h from Bishkek). All marshrutkas (minibuses) to Issyk-Kul pass through it (Bishkek bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St.; to Balykchy ~300 som, to the lakeshore 500–600 som) as does the summer Bishkek-2 — Balykchy train (08:06, 150–180 som standard). To stop at the spring, cafe and sculptures or to turn off to the Konorchek canyons and Chon-Kemin, you need your own car or a taxi. The main activity here is rafting on the Chu (classes II–IV, May — September, Kyrgyz Guided Tours $70 with transfer). In spring the gorge is periodically closed for rock clearing (in April 2026 — 13–17 and 20–30 April, 09:00–16:00), and on summer weekends there are traffic jams.
