kg-0042.name: Chunkurchak Gorge
kg-0042.near: The tract/village of Chunkurchak (the complex's address in 2GIS); approaches — from Kashka-Suu (the Ala-Archa side) and from Arashan (the Alamedin side). Tatyr is ~6.6 km as the crow flies from the former catalog point (OSM).
kg-0042.elev: The ski complex — 2060–2220 m (Nomad's Land, 2024–25 season); the “Sky Bridge” — about 2400 m, the meadows — from ~2000 m (asiamixtravel); Kyzyl-Beles Pass — about 2300 m (too.kg).
kg-0042.short: Chunkurchak is the nearest high-mountain gorge to Bishkek (~30–45 km): a ski complex, the suspension “Sky Bridge”, the Supara ethno-resort, the Dove Waterfall and the red slopes of Kyzyl-Beles.
kg-0042.desc: Chunkurchak stretches along the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too between the Ala-Archa and Alamedin gorges; it is about 30 km long (too.kg). The landscape is sharp snow-capped peaks, flowery meadows, sparse spruce forests and the red soils near Kyzyl-Beles Pass (~2300 m). The main centre is the Chunkurchak ski complex (2060–2220 m, 5 chairlifts, >10 km of runs per sxodim) and the Supara Chunkurchak ethno-resort; in summer a cable car operates to the suspension “Sky Bridge” (~125 m, ~2400 m, opened in 2021), along with horse rides and an archery range. From the complex it is a short walk to the 30 m Dove Waterfall. In 2025–2026 the Arashan — Chunkurchak road (20.7 km) was rebuilt: by 29.07.2026 the first layer of asphalt had been laid along its entire length and two bridges had been built.
kg-0042.guide: Chunkurchak is the simplest way to find yourself at 2000+ m within an hour of Bishkek. Take the cable car up to the “Sky Bridge” — the 125 m suspension bridge over the gorge gives the best panorama of the snowy peaks. Then walk down to the 30 m Dove Waterfall (20–30 minutes on foot) and have lunch in the Supara yurts. If you like wild views, drive (better in a 4×4) to the red slopes of Kyzyl-Beles Pass. With the new paved road from Arashan you can make a loop Alamedin — Chunkurchak — Ala-Archa in one day.
kg-0042.see: The “Sky Bridge” (suspension, ~125 m, ~2400 m) and the cable car; the Dove Waterfall (~30 m); the Supara Chunkurchak ethno-resort; the red slopes and Kyzyl-Beles Pass (~2300 m); spruce forests and flowering meadows; tulips from late April to mid-May (asiamixtravel).
kg-0042.skip: You are looking for deserted mountains — Chunkurchak is heavily developed (a resort, a cable car, restaurants) and crowded on weekends. You want serious trekking — Ala-Archa or Kegety are better. You dislike paid entertainment — most activities (the cable car, the bridge, horses) cost money.
kg-0042.diff: Easy: the main points are accessible by car and cable car; the walk to the Dove Waterfall is 20–30 min (asiamixtravel); meadow walks 2–3 h. The upper section via Kyzyl-Beles is off-road for a prepared 4×4 (too.kg).
kg-0042.when: June — early September — meadows and hikes; late April — mid-May — tulips (asiamixtravel). The ski season is December — April (Nomad's Land; asiamixtravel — mid-December — March). In winter you need studded tires.
kg-0042.hours: The ski complex: 10:00–16:00 daily (sxodim, Nomad's Land); summer activities — in daylight, the cable car's hours are not confirmed. The gorge is open 24 hours. Complex phone +996 558 586 898, info@chunkurchak.kg.
kg-0042.daytime: Weekday mornings: shorter queues for the cable car and clear views of the peaks; in summer there are often clouds after lunch. Sunset at the bridge — depends on the weather (editorial).
kg-0042.how: From Bishkek ~30–45 km, about 1 h by car. Two approaches: from the west via Kashka-Suu (the Ala-Archa side) and from the east via Arashan (the Alamedin Gorge) — the 20.7 km Arashan — Chunkurchak road was paved in 2026 (Kaktus.media 29.07.2026). There is no direct public transport: a taxi or marshrutka (minibus) to Arashan/Kashka-Suu + a local taxi.
kg-0042.needcar: Yes: a car, taxi or transfer — there is no direct public transport to the complex (too.kg, asiamixtravel).
kg-0042.self: Yes, by car or taxi; everything on site (cable car, cafe, rental) works without a guide. Without a car you will have to combine a marshrutka (minibus) and a taxi.
kg-0042.roadtype: Paved to the complex: from the Arashan side — the new 20.7 km road (the first layer of asphalt along its entire length by 29.07.2026, the second layer was being laid); from the Kashka-Suu side — paved. The upper section via Kyzyl-Beles is dirt, off-road for 4×4 (too.kg).
kg-0042.traveltime: Bishkek → complex ≈1 h by car (asiamixtravel); the Dove Waterfall — 20–30 min on foot; the climb to the bridge — by cable car or 20–30 min on foot.
kg-0042.stay: The Supara Chunkurchak ethno-resort (yurts and wooden cabins, 2GIS: 4.9/5, 2207 ratings, rooms from 7,500 som); hotel rooms at the Chunkurchak ski complex; a few more recreation bases (too.kg mentions four ski bases, and in summer — rest houses and kumis-therapy clinics).
kg-0042.net: Beeline and O! work at the complex, the signal weakens on the upper meadows (asiamixtravel, 2026).
kg-0042.entry: A separate fee for entering the gorge, per asiamixtravel, is under $1 per person (not officially confirmed). Paid services: the winter ski pass 1,500 som adult / 1,100 child (2024–25 season, Nomad's Land); the summer cable car and “Sky Bridge” are paid, the amount is not confirmed.
kg-0042.transfer: A taxi ~$12–18 one way (2026); a complex transfer 3,200–4,350 som (2024–25); an excursion $100–140 per group (Sputnik8), €100 (Tripster).
kg-0042.bring: A windbreaker and a warm layer (2000–2400 m, 8–10 °C cooler than Bishkek), sun protection, comfortable shoes for the descent to the waterfall, cash (cards are accepted only at the main venues — asiamixtravel). In winter — studded tires for the car.
kg-0042.warn: The upper road via Kyzyl-Beles is off-road, only a prepared 4×4 and an experienced driver (too.kg). In winter — black ice, studs are mandatory. The cable car and bridge are commercial attractions: check whether they are operating on the day of your trip. On the new paved Arashan — Chunkurchak road work was still going on in 2026 (barriers, markings).
kg-0042.food: Lunch at the Supara Chunkurchak ethno-resort — Kyrgyz cuisine in yurts (a full lunch $10–18 — asiamixtravel; the average check of the Supara restaurant in Bishkek is 1,700 som, 2GIS); a fast-food cafe at the ski complex (average check 1,200 som — sxodim); in summer — kumis at the bases.
kg-0042.reviews: 2GIS: the Chunkurchak ski complex — 4.9/5, 3515 ratings; Supara Chunkurchak — 4.9/5, 2207 ratings (07.10.2026). Google has no unambiguous listing for the gorge. Sputnik8 “Sky Bridge” — 5.0, 9 reviews. Pros: close to Bishkek, views from the bridge, good infrastructure. Cons: crowded and commercialized, everything is paid.
kg-0042.p.sum: Chunkurchak is the nearest “high-mountain” gorge to Bishkek (2000–2400 m) with a cable car, the “Sky Bridge”, horse rides and the Supara ethno-resort. The easiest way is by Yandex Go/inDrive taxi (≈1 h, ≈$12–18) or with an excursion. There is no direct marshrutka (minibus): you can take marshrutka No. 265 to Kashka-Suu and change to a local taxi. Since summer 2026 a new paved road from Arashan (20.7 km) also leads to the gorge. On site, per Datka Travel prices: the “Sky Bridge” ≈$6, the cable car or zipline $3–5, a horse ≈$12/hour. A night at Supara — from $73.

kg-0043.name: Taldyk Pass
kg-0043.near: Ak-Bosogo — about 6 km as the crow flies (OSM marker, catalogue calculation). The nearest base villages on the highway: Sopu-Korgon (north side, before the serpentine) and Sary-Tash (south side, ~20 km beyond the pass); Gulcha, the district centre, is ~80 km to the north. Road distances of the approaches are not confirmed.
kg-0043.elev: 3,615 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, the pass sign in travellers’ photos); other sources round it to 3,600 m (too.kg, economist.kg) or give 3,588 m (Nomad's Land). Nearby on the same highway is the “40 Years of Kyrgyzstan” pass, 3,541 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan).
kg-0043.short: Taldyk is a year-round drivable road pass (about 3,600 m) in the Alay range on the Osh — Sary-Tash highway, the gateway to the Alay valley and the Pamir Highway.
kg-0043.desc: The Taldyk Pass in the Alay range links the Gulcha river valley (the Fergana side) with the Alay valley. The Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam (China) and Osh — Sary-Tash — Kyzyl-Art (Tajikistan, Pamir Highway, M41) highways run over it; the pass lies at about km 163 of the Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam international corridor (economist.kg, 2026). The first wheeled road was built in the late 19th century, the modern highway in the 1930s–40s; at the pass stands a monument to the construction engineer Yu. Grushko (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The northern slope is a famous serpentine, the southern one a gentle descent to Sary-Tash. The road is paved and considered passable all year, but in winter the section at km 161–179 is avalanche-prone; construction of a ~3.2 km tunnel is planned to start in 2027 (economist.kg, 08.2026).
kg-0043.guide: Taldyk is the moment when the green of Fergana stays below and the Alay valley and the wall of the Trans-Alay range with Lenin Peak (7,134 m) open up ahead. Stop at the top by the monument to engineer Grushko, who built this road in the 1930s–40s — from here is the best view of the northern slope’s serpentine. On a single drive from Osh you can easily pass through “all four seasons” here: heat below, snow possibly lying at the top, so a warm jacket is needed even in July. The pass is a transit point: plan it as a photo stop on the way to Sary-Tash, Sary-Mogol or the Pamirs, and spend the night in the Alay valley. In winter watch for Emergency Ministry (MChS) warnings — the section at km 161–179 is avalanche-prone.
kg-0043.see: The northern-slope serpentine with a view of the Gulcha valley; the monument to engineer Yu. Grushko on the saddle; the pass sign with its elevation; views of the Alay valley and the Trans-Alay range (Lenin Peak 7,134 m — in clear weather); the neighbouring “40 Years of Kyrgyzstan” pass (3,541 m). Red cliffs and a change of landscape from forest-steppe to high-mountain tundra along the road.
kg-0043.skip: You are not continuing into the Alay valley, the Pamirs or China — driving 3+ hours one way from Osh specially for the pass makes little sense. You tolerate altitude and serpentines badly. In winter — if you have no winter tyres and no experience of driving on mountain roads.
kg-0043.diff: Easy to visit: it is a stop by a paved highway, no hiking climb. The load comes from the altitude of ~3,600 m (mild altitude sickness is possible with a fast climb from Osh, ~1,000 m) and the serpentine of the northern slope (editorial; too.kg).
kg-0043.when: June — September: the road is dry, views are open. The pass is officially passable all year (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan), but from November to March avalanches, drifts and black ice are possible — the Emergency Ministry (MChS) issues warnings for the km 161–179 section (Kaktus, 15.11.2024).
kg-0043.hours: Around the clock; it is a section of a state highway with no checkpoint. Temporary traffic restrictions are possible during snowfall and avalanche danger (Kaktus, 2024).
kg-0043.daytime: Morning — less cloud over the Alay valley and a better chance of seeing Lenin Peak; public transport from Osh leaves around 14:00, so by marshrutka (minibus) you pass the pass towards evening (nomadasaurus, 2026). Avoid the serpentine in the dark (editorial).
kg-0043.how: From Osh south along the Osh — Gulcha — Sary-Tash highway (M41 / EM-05): about 160 km to the pass (too.kg), about 3 hours by car; the Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka takes about 3 h (nomadasaurus, 2026). The tunnel fee on the Bishkek — Osh highway (50/200 som) does not apply to this route.
kg-0043.needcar: Yes. The pass is a point on the highway; you need your own/rented car, a taxi or a seat in a marshrutka/shared taxi Osh — Sary-Tash (Daroot-Korgon). On a marshrutka the driver does not always stop for photos — for a photo stop a taxi or your own car is more convenient (editorial).
kg-0043.self: Yes: the road is paved, there are signs, no guide is needed; a border-zone permit is not required for the Osh — Sary-Tash highway itself (permit requirements apply to the Lenin Peak area and other zones — tour.too.kg). In winter — only with a good forecast and winter tyres.
kg-0043.roadtype: Paved mountain highway M41 / Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam; the northern slope is a steep serpentine, the southern one gentle (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). Rockfalls, road subsidence and slope movements have been recorded on the section (Ministry of Transport, 2021, via economist.kg 2026). A ~3.2 km tunnel is planned (work to start in 2027).
kg-0043.traveltime: From Osh — about 3 h by car to the pass (~160 km, too.kg; editorial on the marshrutka time to Sary-Tash ~3 h, nomadasaurus 2026). From the pass to Sary-Tash — ~20–30 min (editorial).
kg-0043.stay: There is no accommodation at the pass. The nearest overnights are guesthouses in Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol; in Sary-Mogol: Tilek Guesthouse, Peak Lenin Guesthouse, Guesthouse Hamza — about $15 per person with breakfast, CBT Sary Mogol — $20 (nomadasaurus, 2026). Specific guesthouses in Sary-Tash were not checked.
kg-0043.net: Not confirmed for the pass saddle. Sary-Mogol has 4G (nomadasaurus 2026 writes “Megafon” — probably MegaCom). According to general reviews Beeline works best in the mountains (bestofosh). No reports on coverage specifically at Taldyk were found.
kg-0043.entry: Free: it is a section of a state highway, no source mentions a fee for crossing the pass (tunnel fees apply on the Bishkek — Osh highway, not here).
kg-0043.transfer: Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka ~350 som per person; Osh — Daroot-Korgon 300 som (marshrutka) / 400 som (shared taxi) (nomadasaurus, 2026); shared taxi $8–10 per person (eurasia.travel, 12.2024); private taxi Osh — Irkeshtam 4,500 som per car (2019, outdated).
kg-0043.bring: A warm jacket and hat even in summer (at the pass ~3,600 m it is sharply colder than in Osh); sunglasses and sunscreen; water and a snack (no shops at the pass — editorial). In winter — winter tyres, chains, a fuel reserve; keep 500 m between cars in avalanche periods (Emergency Ministry (MChS) recommendation, Kaktus 2024).
kg-0043.warn: Altitude about 3,600 m — headache and shortness of breath are possible with a fast climb. In winter and spring (November — March) — avalanches, snow drifts, black ice on the km 161–179 section; the Emergency Ministry (MChS) recommends winter tyres and a 500 m distance (Kaktus, 15.11.2024). Rockfalls and road subsidence are recorded on the section (economist.kg, 2026). In the coming years tunnel construction (start 2027) and related traffic restrictions are possible.
kg-0043.food: Not confirmed: no sources list any eateries at the pass itself. You can eat in the villages along the highway (Gulcha, Sary-Tash) and in the guesthouses of Sary-Mogol — it is recommended to have dinner at the guesthouse (nomadasaurus, 2026); specific cafes near the pass were not checked.
kg-0043.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 38 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, per catalogue check). Typical pros from travel notes: views of the serpentine and the Alay valley, a change of seasons in one trip, good asphalt. Cons: cold and wind at the top, winter avalanches. No separate listing for the pass was found on TripAdvisor or 2GIS.
kg-0043.p.sum: Taldyk is a photo stop on the paved Osh — Sary-Tash highway (M41), about 160 km and ~3 h from Osh. It is easiest to drive it in your own car or by taxi/transfer with a stop at the top; the Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka (350 som, until 14:00) does not always stop for photos. Spend the night in Sary-Tash (~20 km beyond the pass) or Sary-Mogol, not on the saddle. In winter (November — March) watch for Emergency Ministry (MChS) warnings for the km 161–179 section.

kg-0043.p.iti.0.plan: 08:00 leave Osh → 10:00 Gulcha (coffee/fuel) → 11:00 Taldyk, 20–30 min photo stop → 11:30 Sary-Tash → 12:30 Sary-Mogol, in the evening Tulpar-Kol.
kg-0043.p.iti.1.title: 2–3 days
kg-0043.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Osh — Taldyk — Sary-Mogol (overnight, acclimatisation). Day 2: Tulpar-Kol and Achyk-Tash. Day 3: back to Osh or on to the Pamirs via Kyzyl-Art (Tajikistan, a visa/GBAO permit is needed).
kg-0043.p.iti.2.title: Combinations
kg-0043.p.iti.2.plan: It makes sense to combine with Sary-Mogol, Tulpar-Kol and Achyk-Tash (along one highway). Kojokelen is through another valley (from Osh to the west) and cannot be combined into one car route.
kg-0043.p.season: June — September: dry road, best views. October — snow is possible on the saddle. November — March: avalanche danger and black ice at km 161–179, the Emergency Ministry (MChS) advises winter tyres and a 500 m distance. April — May: thaw, rockfalls. In summer — short mudflows after downpours (June 2026).
kg-0043.p.budget.economy: Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka 350 som + a guesthouse in Sary-Tash ~$20 (≈1,750 som) with dinner and breakfast ≈ 2,100 som per person.
kg-0043.p.budget.comfort: A 4×4 transfer Osh — Alay $300 per car (≈26,000 som, shared by 3–4) + a guesthouse/camp $15–85
kg-0043.p.permits: Not required: it is a section of a state highway, no fee. A border-zone permit is needed further on — for the Lenin Peak area (Achyk-Tash) and for the trip to Kyzyl-Art.
kg-0043.p.access: Suitable for everyone, including children and older people: a viewpoint by the road. Limitations — the altitude of ~3,600 m (fast climb from Osh, ~1,000 m) and cold/wind. Stroller — only by the car, the area is uneven.

kg-0044.name: Barskoon Gorge
kg-0044.near: Barskoon is a village on the southern highway at the entrance to the gorge (approx. 140 km from Balykchy, 80–90 km from Karakol); it is 17–20 km up the valley to the site with the Gagarin monuments and the waterfalls (faheyjamestravel 2024: 17 km; firsov.kz: 20 km).
kg-0044.elev: The gorge entrance ~2000 m (Destination Jeti Oguz); above 2800 m — spruce forests and juniper (2GIS); Sary-Moynok Pass 3442 m, Barskoon Pass 3816 m, the Arabel plateau ~3770 m (firsov.kz 2019; Destination Jeti Oguz). The elevation of the waterfall site was not found (approximately 2300–2500 m — not confirmed).
kg-0044.short: A gorge on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul with a cascade of waterfalls (“Snow Leopard's Tears” 24 m, “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray”, “Elder's Beard”), two Gagarin monuments and an excellent gravel Kumtor road leading over 3800 m passes to the syrts (high plateaus) of Arabel.
kg-0044.desc: The valley of the Barskoon River cuts into the Terskey Ala-Too for 30–40 km from the village of the same name. Below are steppe grasses and shrubs, above 2800 m — Tian Shan spruce and juniper, and above them the peaks of the Panfilov Heroes (4610 m) and the World Peace Council (4310 m). 17–20 km from the village is the main site: a bust and a “face in stone” of Yuri Gagarin (the cosmonaut vacationed here after his 1961 flight), a monument to a KamAZ truck — to the builders of the road to Kumtor, seasonal cafe yurts and parking. From here trails lead to the waterfalls: “Snow Leopard's Tears” (24 m, ~1.5 h climb, a legend about a snow leopardess mourning her cubs), “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray” and “Elder's Beard”. The road through the gorge is one of the best dirt roads in the country: it is maintained year-round by the Kumtor gold mine, so it is passable for a passenger car even in winter and leads over the Sary-Moynok (3442 m) and Barskoon (3816 m) passes to the Arabel plateau with its lakes; higher up is the Kumtor checkpoint (the drive to the plateau is open, the mine territory is closed). Entry to the gorge is free (2024).
kg-0044.guide: The main thing here is not to drive to the waterfalls but to walk to them: from the parking by Gagarin to “Snow Leopard's Tears” is an hour and a half of steep trail with a gain of about 350 m, but the water falls as a 24-metre wall. First pay your respects to Gagarin — the two monuments and the KamAZ on a pedestal look surreal among the spruces, and it is real history: the cosmonaut vacationed on Issyk-Kul in 1961. If you have half a day and a clear sky — drive on along the Kumtor gravel road: an hour of switchbacks and you are at 3800 m, on the syrts of Arabel, with lakes and yaks. Don't drink the river water — the mine is upstream; the springs on the slopes are clean. A taxi from the village — a guide figure of 1600 som, and horses at the yurts are offered “depending on the mood”, so haggle.
kg-0044.see: The waterfalls “Snow Leopard's Tears” (24 m), “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray”, “Elder's Beard”; the monuments to Gagarin (a bust and a bas-relief in the rock) and the KamAZ; spruce and juniper forests; the switchbacks up to Sary-Moynak Pass and Barskoon Pass (3816 m) with views of the lake; the Arabel plateau with its lakes (separate entry); the Petrov Glacier by Kumtor (not for visiting).
kg-0044.skip: You are not ready for a steep hour-and-a-half climb — the waterfalls can't be seen from the parking. You are already heading to Arabel with an overnight — you will see the gorge on the way. In rain: the trail to the waterfalls is slippery and dangerous.
kg-0044.diff: Driving through the gorge — easy (a passenger car). The trail to “Snow Leopard's Tears”: 3.1 km, +367 m, ~2.5 h round trip, “strenuous” (faheyjamestravel, 2024); to the third waterfall another +45 min (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). The climb to the passes — altitude 3400–3800 m.
kg-0044.when: May–October for the waterfalls (maximum water flow — June–July, snowmelt); September — quiet and golden. The road is maintained year-round (Destination Jeti Oguz); in winter — the waterfalls are frozen, the passes depend on the weather.
kg-0044.hours: Open terrain, open 24 hours, no ticket offices (faheyjamestravel 2024: “open all day and night”). The Kumtor checkpoint is higher up the road — a vehicle inspection, the drive to the plateau is open (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021).
kg-0044.daytime: Morning — set out from Barskoon by 8–9 a.m. to climb to the waterfalls before the heat and thunderstorms; in the second half of the day the light on the waterfalls is better for photos, but the trail is busier.
kg-0044.how: Along the southern highway Balykchy — Karakol to the village of Barskoon (marshrutka (minibus) from Karakol 100–150 som, from Bishkek 250–500 som — visitkarakol.com; fresher prices above), then south on the Kumtor gravel road for 17–20 km to the site with the Gagarin monuments (a taxi from the village ~1600 som, 2024). On foot from the village — 4–5 h. Beyond that — trails to the waterfalls or the road to the passes and Arabel.
kg-0044.needcar: Yes, from the village to the waterfalls it is 17–20 km with no public transport; a passenger car is fine (2GIS, firsov.kz). Hitchhiking is realistic because of the Kumtor traffic.
kg-0044.self: Yes: the road is obvious, no permits needed (the Kumtor checkpoint lets tourists through to the plateau after inspection), the trails to the waterfalls are well trodden; an offline map is advisable.
kg-0044.roadtype: Paved road along the highway to the village; then the Kumtor gravel road — “an excellent dirt road, packed down by trucks”, passable for a sedan and a motorcycle (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021, too.kg); to the waterfalls — walking trails, steep, slippery after rain.
kg-0044.traveltime: Karakol — Barskoon ~1.5–2 h; village — waterfall site 30–40 min; the trail to “Snow Leopard's Tears” ~1.5 h up, 2.5 h round trip; a whole day from Barskoon with a walk — ~6 h (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). Transfer Karakol — waterfalls — Karakol: 200 km, ~4 h of pure driving (MYWAY).
kg-0044.stay: In the village of Barskoon: guesthouses (Ryskeldi Guest House and others), CBT; in Tamga — a sanatorium and guesthouses; at the waterfall site — seasonal cafe yurts and camping (too.kg, firsov.kz). 2025–2026 prices not found.
kg-0044.net: Too.kg: coverage is “partial”; in the village of Barskoon all operators have a signal; at the waterfalls the signal is unstable, on the passes and plateau — absent (too.kg/arabel). The operator and the test date are not specified.
kg-0044.entry: Free (faheyjamestravel, 2024; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com 2023 — no fee mentioned). Only parking/yurts/horses, where available, are paid. Check on site.
kg-0044.transfer: Taxi Barskoon — waterfalls 1600 som (2024); Karakol — Barskoon 4500–5000 som (2024); MYWAY Karakol — waterfalls — Karakol 9,900 som per minivan (2026); marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Barskoon 100–150 som (date not given).
kg-0044.bring: Trekking shoes and poles (the trail is steep), a rain jacket, water (don't drink from the river — the mine is upstream; the springs are clean), a warm jacket for the passes (3800 m), cash for the yurts and taxis, an offline map, a reserve of fuel for the trip to the plateau.
kg-0044.warn: Water in the Barskoon River is not recommended for drinking because of the Kumtor mine upstream (too.kg). The trail to the waterfalls is steep and slippery after rain. Kumtor trucks on the road — keep to the side. The mine territory is closed, the checkpoint is above the passes; the 3400–3800 m passes — altitude sickness with a rapid ascent. Haggle at the yurts and with the horse owners.
kg-0044.food: Cafe yurts at the waterfalls (seasonal): shashlik, lagman, kumis, tea; in the villages of Barskoon and Tamga — ashkana (small eateries) and home cooking at guesthouses. Specific places and prices were not checked.
kg-0044.reviews: 2GIS “Barskoon Gorge”: 5.0/5, 55 ratings, 24 reviews (07.10.2026). Google — separate markers “Barskoon Waterfall” and “Gagarin Monument” (ratings not captured). Pros per 2019–2024 reports: road quality, the 24 m waterfall, the monuments, free; cons — the steep trail, pushy horse owners, dust from trucks.
kg-0044.p.sum: From the village of Barskoon on the southern highway it is 17–20 km along the excellent Kumtor mine gravel road to the site with the Gagarin monuments and cafe yurts — any passenger car can do it. Without your own car: a marshrutka (minibus) from Karakol to Barskoon (~100–150 som) + a taxi from the village (~1,600 som per car, 2024) or a taxi from Karakol (3,500–5,000 som one way). From the parking, a steep trail leads to the “Snow Leopard's Tears” waterfall (3.1 km, +367 m, ~2.5 h round trip). Overnight in Tamga or Barskoon; after 17:00 it is hard to find transport out of the gorge.

kg-0045.name: Przhevalsky Museum
kg-0045.dist: The urban-type settlement of Pristan-Przhevalsk is administratively part of the city of…
kg-0045.near: Pristan-Przhevalsk — the museum is at the entrance to the settlement, 9 km north of the center of Karakol (too.kg, issykkul.biz; TripAdvisor: ~12 km). Address: 1 Przhevalsky St.
kg-0045.elev: 1,643 m (Nomad's Land). A site above the Karakol Bay, slightly higher than the lake level (1,607 m).
kg-0045.short: A memorial complex above the Karakol Bay: a museum (since 1957) with the personal belongings, letters and stuffed animals from the expeditions of the Central Asia explorer, his grave and a 9-meter granite monument with a bronze eagle (1894) — the first monumental sculpture in Kyrgyzstan.
kg-0045.desc: Nikolai Przhevalsky (1839–1888), the author of four expeditions to Mongolia, China and Tibet, died of typhus in Karakol on 20 October 1888 at the start of his fifth journey and, by his will, was buried on the shore of Issyk-Kul. In 1893–1894 a monument was erected over the grave: a nine-meter granite rock crowned with a bronze eagle with an olive branch in its beak, with a bas-relief and a map of his routes. On 29 April 1957 a museum was opened next to it: 400 m² of exhibition in 10 sections — authentic letters and manuscripts, personal belongings, photographs, more than 8 editions published in his lifetime, from 1883–1947, stuffed animals collected on the expeditions, maps. Around it is a park with a view of the lake and the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges; in 1998 the linguist Husein Karasaev was buried here as well. In 1889–1921 and 1939–1992 Karakol bore the name Przhevalsk. Entry is 50–100 som (2024), the museum is open daily 9:00–17:00.
kg-0045.guide: The strongest thing here is not the display cases but the place: Przhevalsky himself chose this shore, and from the monument with the eagle opens the very view of the bay and the Terskey for which he asked to be buried “on the shore of Issyk-Kul”. Go into the museum first (an hour is enough; there are captions in English too), then walk 500 m through the park to the grave — many tourists do the opposite and skip the exhibition. The ticket is pennies (50–100 som), but the ticket office closes at 17:00 and may break for lunch at 12–13. From Karakol the easiest is a taxi for 10–15 minutes or the “Pristan” marshrutka (minibus) from the bus station — ask to be dropped at the museum before the settlement. Combine it with the Pristan beach or with the road north to Tyup.
kg-0045.see: The exhibition: authentic letters, manuscripts, personal belongings, stuffed animals from the expeditions, route maps, editions published in his lifetime; the grave and the monument with the bronze eagle (1894); a park with a view of the Karakol Bay and the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too; the grave of Husein Karasaev.
kg-0045.skip: The history of Russian expeditions to Asia leaves you cold — the exhibition is small-scale and old-fashioned. You have half a day in Karakol: the Dungan Mosque and the Holy Trinity Cathedral are closer. You expect interactive displays — there are none.
kg-0045.diff: Easy: the museum and park are on a level site, a 500 m walk to the monument; accessible to children and older people.
kg-0045.when: Year-round (the museum is open daily); May–September — the park is green and there is a view of the lake; in summer marshrutkas to Pristan run more often (too.kg).
kg-0045.hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (Google Maps, viewed 03.10.2026; Nomad's Land 9am–5pm; 2GIS “opens at 09:00”); a lunch break of 12:00–13:00 is possible (TripAdvisor, 2024). Check by phone before a visit on holidays.
kg-0045.daytime: Morning after opening — empty and soft light on the monument; closer to sunset the park is beautiful, but the museum closes at 17:00.
kg-0045.how: From Karakol 9 km north along the road to Pristan-Przhevalsk: the “Pristan Przhevalsk” marshrutka from the bus station (15–30 som — visitkarakol.com; too.kg: 30 som, regular in summer), ask to be dropped at the museum before the settlement; a taxi 10–15 min (Yandex Go, the Salam taxi 03922 52222). On foot from the center — 2 h.
kg-0045.needcar: Advisable: it is 9 km from the center; there is a marshrutka and a taxi, your own car is not required.
kg-0045.self: Yes, fully: public transport, a ticket office on site, captions in Russian and partly in English.
kg-0045.roadtype: Paved from Karakol to the settlement; parking at the museum. Inside — park paths.
kg-0045.traveltime: From the center of Karakol 10–15 min by taxi, 20–30 min by marshrutka. A visit to the museum and park — 1–2 h (Nomad's Land).
kg-0045.stay: In the settlement itself — dachas and private housing by the beach; the main base is Karakol (hostels, guesthouses, hotels; a guideline from 2025–2026 guides: guesthouses $40–60, hostels $10–25 per bed). Specific places have not been checked.
kg-0045.net: A suburb of Karakol — coverage by all operators (Beeline, MegaCom, O!), MegaCom 4G in Karakol since 2019 (Kaktus.media). No separate complaints found.
kg-0045.entry: 50 som (too.kg, date not given); 50–100 som (visitkarakol.com); a 2024 TripAdvisor review — “about 70 som”. A guideline for 2024–2025: 50–100 som, the guided tour is separate.
kg-0045.transfer: Marshrutka 15–30 som (visitkarakol.com, too.kg); a taxi from Karakol — the tariff is not published (a guideline of 200–300 som per Yandex Go, not confirmed).
kg-0045.bring: Cash in small som for the ticket and the marshrutka, a hat in summer (the park is open), a camera — the view of the bay; no documents are required.
kg-0045.warn: The museum closes at 17:00, a lunch break at 12–13 is possible; on Mondays/holidays check the hours. The view of the lake is partly blocked by dachas (TripAdvisor reviews). Do not confuse Pristan-Przhevalsk (the museum) with the center of Karakol, where there is a street monument to Przhevalsky.
kg-0045.food: There is no café at the museum. In Karakol — ashlyan-fu (cold Dungan noodle dish with starch noodles and a fried pastry, stalls by the central bazaar), Dungan cuisine, lagman; in Pristan in summer — beach cafés. Specific establishments have not been checked.
kg-0045.reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 137 ratings (03.10.2026). 2GIS: 5.0/5, 143 ratings, 52 reviews (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Monument N.M. Przhevalsky”: 4.3/5, 91 reviews, #7 of 40 in Karakol (the latest — August 2024). Pros: well kept, knowledgeable staff, a view of the lake, captions in English; cons: the museum is small, the dachas spoil the views.
kg-0045.p.sum: A simple half-day trip from Karakol: 9 km north on pavement to the settlement of Pristan-Przhevalsk — by the “Pristan-Przhevalsk” marshrutka (20–30 som, ask to be dropped at the museum) or by taxi/Yandex Go in 10–15 minutes. The museum is open daily 9:00–17:00 (lunch at 12–13 is possible), a ticket costs 100–120 som; after the exhibition — 500 m through the park to the monument with the eagle and the grave above the bay. Stay overnight and eat in Karakol.

kg-0047.name: Shah-Fazil
kg-0047.near: Safed-Bulan (Safedbulan; called Gulistan in some sources), the complex is in the village itself: 2GIS — 42a Muzeynaya St. (or 40/1 A. Shaitov St.). Kerben — ~10 km (Destination Jalal-Abad); Ala-Buka — 15 km per open.kg, ~50 km per Destination Jalal-Abad (discrepancy). It is ~5 km to the border with Uzbekistan (too.kg).
kg-0047.elev: Not confirmed: the elevation of Safed-Bulan village is not given in the sources found (roughly the foothills of the Chatkal Range; check on a map).
kg-0047.short: Shah-Fazil is a Karakhanid-era mausoleum (11th–12th centuries) with a unique truncated-pyramid dome and carved ganch plaster in the village of Safed-Bulan; the centre of a revered pilgrimage complex with the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain and the women-only Safed-Bulan mausoleum.
kg-0047.desc: The Shah-Fazil mausoleum is one of the rare monuments of the Karakhanid era: a building square in plan with a dome in the form of a truncated pyramid, its walls inside covered with carved ganch (gypsum plaster) ornament (too.kg, Destination Jalal-Abad). The dating in the sources is the 11th or 11th–12th centuries (too.kg, 24.kg); mir24 gives the 9th century. According to legend, about 2,700 warriors spreading Islam, led by Shah-Jarir, died here during Friday prayers; his widow turned grey with grief — hence the name Safed-Bulan (“white Bulan”); his son Shah-Fazil later peacefully completed the Islamization of the north of Fergana and is buried in the mausoleum (too.kg). The complex includes the sacred mountain Archa-Mazar, the mausoleums of Alambardar and Safed-Bulan (19th century, women only), a mosque of the 17th–19th centuries, a hermit's cave and a pre-Islamic upright stone — the “fertility stone” (too.kg, Destination Jalal-Abad, 24.kg). The monument has been state-protected since 2002 and is on UNESCO's Tentative List (Silk Roads Sites in Kyrgyzstan); in 2025 it was visited by more than 33,000 people; a new 400 m² museum building is being built by the end of 2026 (mir24).
kg-0047.guide: Shah-Fazil is surprising for its shape: there is no other pyramid-shaped dome like it in Central Asia, and inside the walls are covered with the finest ganch carving almost a thousand years old. It is an active pilgrimage site: people come here from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan, so dress modestly and keep quiet. Women should visit the Safed-Bulan mausoleum — entry there is for women only, and in the courtyard there is a “fertility stone” where people pray for children. Climb the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain — from it you can see the whole complex and the valley by the Uzbek border. The complex is open daily from 8:00 to 17:00, so come in the morning — the road from Jalal-Abad is not short.
kg-0047.see: The Shah-Fazil mausoleum (pyramid dome, carved ganch); the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain; the mausoleums of Alambardar (the standard-bearer) and Safed-Bulan (women only); a mosque of the 17th–19th centuries; the hermit's cave; the pre-Islamic “fertility stone”; a Bronze Age monument (24.kg); the reserve museum (new building — by the end of 2026, mir24).
kg-0047.skip: You aren't interested in Islamic architecture and pilgrimage sites. You don't have a whole day: the road from Jalal-Abad is long and accommodation is far. You're coming only for nature — this is first and foremost a shrine.
kg-0047.diff: Easy: a tour of the complex in the village; the climb up Archa-Mazar mountain is short, easy to medium (editorial).
kg-0047.when: April–October (warm season, convenient road — editorial); the complex operates year-round. On religious holidays there are many pilgrims (editorial).
kg-0047.daytime: Morning — fewer people and soft light for photographing the dome; arrive at the 8:00 opening so you can get back to Jalal-Abad before dark (editorial).
kg-0047.how: From Jalal-Abad: shared taxi to Kerben (~400 som), then a taxi to Safed-Bulan/Gulistan (~1,000 som) and on foot to the mausoleum; a private car from Jalal-Abad — ~5,000 som one way (Destination Jalal-Abad). Kerben is ~10 km from the complex. From Bishkek — about 600 km (mir24).
kg-0047.needcar: Yes: you need a car/taxi to reach the village; around the complex — on foot.
kg-0047.self: Yes: the complex is open to visitors, no permits needed. Observe the shrine's rules; the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only (too.kg, 24.kg).
kg-0047.roadtype: Paved road to Kerben/Ala-Buka, then village roads to Safed-Bulan (editorial, not confirmed by a source).
kg-0047.traveltime: Not confirmed: the exact time from Jalal-Abad is not given in the sources; roughly 3–4 h by car (editorial, estimated from the distance via Tash-Kumyr and Kerben).
kg-0047.stay: The nearest accommodation is in Ala-Buka (Destination Jalal-Abad, “about 50 km”); too.kg mentions cafés, shops and accommodation in Gulistan/Safed-Bulan. Names and prices not found; TripAdvisor shows nearby hotels without verified prices.
kg-0047.net: There is mobile coverage (too.kg). Operators not specified.
kg-0047.entry: Not confirmed: the amount of an entrance fee/donation was not found in the sources; the complex has the status of a museum-reserve (2GIS) — a museum fee is possible, check on site.
kg-0047.transfer: Jalal-Abad — Kerben shared taxi ~400 som; Kerben — Safed-Bulan taxi ~1,000 som; a private car from Jalal-Abad ~5,000 som one way (Destination Jalal-Abad, year not given).
kg-0047.bring: Modest clothing (long sleeves and a skirt/trousers; a headscarf for women; editorial for Muslim shrines); cash in som for taxis, donations and souvenirs (souvenirs are sold at the entrance — 24.kg); water and a hat for the climb up Archa-Mazar.
kg-0047.warn: An active pilgrimage site: keep quiet and follow the dress code; the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only. The complex is ~5 km from the border with Uzbekistan (too.kg) — do not approach the border. Shah-Fazil is only on UNESCO's Tentative List (Silk Roads Sites in Kyrgyzstan); the claims of some websites (open.kg, 24.kg) about inclusion in the World Heritage List in 1999 are not confirmed.
kg-0047.food: Not confirmed: cafés in Safed-Bulan are mentioned by too.kg without names; in Kerben and Ala-Buka — southern Kyrgyz cuisine (plov, samsa — editorial).
kg-0047.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 85 ratings (03.10.2026). 2GIS — rating not displayed. According to mir24: more than 33,000 visitors a year (+10%), including pilgrims from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan. Typical impressions: unique architecture, an atmosphere of calm; a downside is the remoteness and little infrastructure.
kg-0047.p.sum: The Shah-Fazil complex stands in the village of Safed-Bulan (Gulistan) ~10 km from Kerben, by the border with Uzbekistan. From Jalal-Abad — a shared taxi to Kerben (~400 som) and a taxi to the complex (~1,000 som per car) or a private car (~5,000 som one way); from Bishkek — a subsidized Asman Airlines flight to Kerben (3,600 som, twice a week, 01.2026). Open daily 08:00–17:00; dress modestly, the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only. It makes sense to combine with Sary-Chelek (Arkyt) and Chatkal (via Ala-Buka).

kg-0048.name: Barskoon Syrts (Arabel)
kg-0048.near: Barskoon is the village at the mouth of the gorge, ~50–55 km of road to the plateau (17–20 km to the waterfalls + the pass serpentine); there is no accommodation on the plateau itself. Soyok (OSM, 18.4 km) is the nearest marker, but it is a tract (valley) with no permanent population.
kg-0048.elev: The plateau is 3,700–3,800 m (too.kg: 3,800 m; Destination Jeti Oguz: 3,770 m; Trip to Kyrgyzstan: pass 3,754 m). Higher up the road — the Suyok/Seok Pass 4,016–4,040 m (firsov.kz: 4,016 m; Destination Karakol: 4,022 m; frantsouzov: 4,040 m), the Barskoon Pass 3,816 m (firsov.kz).
kg-0048.short: The Arabel syrts (high plateau) is a tundra plateau at 3,800 m with more than 50 lakes beyond the Barskoon Pass; the only place in the country where you can reach an altitude of 4,000 m in an ordinary car, thanks to the Kumtor mine road.
kg-0048.desc: Beyond the spruce forests and waterfalls of the Barskoon gorge, the Kumtor gravel road climbs in serpentines to the pass (3,754–3,816 m) and comes out onto flat syrts — an ancient glacial floor with glacial basins, bogs and more than fifty lakes (the largest is Arabel), where yaks graze and argali (mountain sheep) are found. The average annual temperature here is below zero (−7…−8 °C per the Trip to Kyrgyzstan catalog), snow lies by the road even in July, and only mosses, lichens and grasses grow. The road continues to the Suyok Pass (4,016–4,040 m) and to the Kumtor mine checkpoint, where tourists are turned back; passage to the plateau and lakes is free after a check of passports and vehicle documents (TripAdvisor, 2024; reports 2018–2021). From the plateau to the west, over the Arabel Pass, the Bolgart valley leads to Naryn, and to the north there are hiking and horse trails to Juuku (Kyrgyz Nomad Trail). There is no infrastructure: no shops, no yurts, no signal — only a tent and the wind.
kg-0048.guide: This is the fastest “four-thousander” in Kyrgyzstan: from warm Barskoon you are at 3,800 m in an hour, which makes it more dangerous than it seems — a headache and shortness of breath hit suddenly, so drink water and don’t run. Take your passport and vehicle documents: they are checked at the checkpoint, and you won’t be let past the lakes and the Suyok Pass (4,022 m) — that is the mine. The best shots are in the morning at Lake Arabel, when the water is like a mirror and the snowfields are reflected; by lunchtime the wind rises. If you spend the night in a tent, count on frost and on the nearest person being 30 km away. Boil river water — the mine is upstream. You will see yaks and, with luck, argali.
kg-0048.see: The serpentine up to the Barskoon Pass with a view of Issyk-Kul; Lake Arabel and dozens of small lakes; snowfields by the road and the glaciers of Terskey (Petrov Glacier ~4,300 m — not accessible); yaks, argali, marmots; the Suyok Pass (4,022 m) — the highest point of the road; the Gagarin monument and the waterfalls in the gorge on the way.
kg-0048.skip: You have heart/blood pressure problems or children under 5 — a sharp gain to 3,800 m. The weather is overcast: without sun the plateau is gray tundra. You are already planning Song-Kol or Kel-Suu — the impression of the syrts will be similar.
kg-0048.diff: By car — easy (gravel road, a passenger car gets through — TripAdvisor 2024, firsov.kz 2019); physiologically — an altitude of 3,800–4,000 m without acclimatization. Hiking/bike/horse routes via Juuku are hard, multi-day and self-sufficient.
kg-0048.when: June–September (lakes ice-free, the road dry); July–August — yaks on the jailoo (summer pasture); in May and October — snow on the plateau is possible on any day. The road is cleared year-round (Kumtor), in winter — ski touring (TripAdvisor), but −20 °C and below.
kg-0048.hours: Open terrain, 24 hours. The Kumtor checkpoint on the road checks documents in daylight; beyond the checkpoint (the mine) — closed to everyone. No fee (TripAdvisor, 2024).
kg-0048.daytime: Morning (8–11 am): calm, mirror-like lakes, clear sky; after 1–2 pm — wind, clouds, thunderstorms/snow. Overnight stays — only for the prepared.
kg-0048.how: From Barskoon along the Kumtor gravel road up the gorge: 17–20 km to the waterfall area, then the serpentine to the Barskoon Pass (3,754–3,816 m) and out onto the plateau — about 1–2 h from the village in all (TripAdvisor 2024; frantsouzov: to 3,800 m about an hour). From Karakol — 80–90 km to Barskoon + the plateau, a day round trip. An alternative is on foot/on horseback/by bike from the Juuku gorge (too.kg).
kg-0048.needcar: Yes, essential: there is no public transport, and it is 50+ km and 2,000 m of gain from the village. A passenger car is suitable (gravel road); for turning off to the lakes — an SUV.
kg-0048.self: Yes, by car: the road is unambiguous; carry your passport and vehicle documents for the checkpoint; no border-zone permit is needed (it is not a border zone). Self-sufficiency: food, water, fuel, warm clothing.
kg-0048.roadtype: The Kumtor gravel industrial road: “an excellent dirt road, packed down by trucks”, passable for a sedan and a motorcycle (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021, TripAdvisor 2024 — “very good in summer 2024”); a serpentine with steep climbs; turn-offs to the lakes — soft ground, ruts, easy to get stuck (frantsouzov 2018).
kg-0048.traveltime: Barskoon – plateau: 1–2 h (TripAdvisor 2024); Karakol – plateau – Karakol: 7–9 h of pure driving (Destination Karakol). On foot from Barskoon — more than 30 km (frantsouzov).
kg-0048.stay: On the plateau — only a tent (too.kg: no shops, cafés or guesthouses; many places for camping). The nearest accommodation is the guesthouses of Barskoon and Tamga, and yurt cafés at the waterfalls (seasonal, an overnight stay is not guaranteed). Prices are not published.
kg-0048.net: No signal (too.kg; Destination Karakol: “no cellular signal”). The last signal is in Barskoon village/the lower part of the gorge. A satellite messenger for self-sufficient routes.
kg-0048.entry: Free; at the checkpoint only a document check (TripAdvisor, 2024). There are no paid services on the plateau.
kg-0048.transfer: A jeep tour from Karakol €210–250 per car (Destination Karakol, 2025–2026); a transfer Karakol – Barskoon 9,900 som (MYWAY, 2026); a taxi from the village to the plateau — not published.
kg-0048.bring: Passport and vehicle documents; a warm jacket, hat, gloves (+5 °C and snow in summer); sun protection (UV at 3,800 m); water 2 L/person and a snack; altitude-sickness pills on a doctor’s advice (Destination Karakol recommends Diamox if you do not adapt); a full tank; an offline map; for a night out — a winter sleeping bag and a tent.
kg-0048.warn: A sharp gain to 3,800–4,000 m in an hour — a risk of altitude sickness; with a headache and nausea, descend. The Kumtor mine territory is closed, and the checkpoint checks documents; do not leave the road near the industrial zone. No signal, accommodation or fuel; the weather changes within minutes, snow in any month. River water — boil (the mine is upstream). Kumtor trucks on the serpentine — give way.
kg-0048.food: There is no food on the plateau — bring your own. On the way: yurt cafés at the Barskoon waterfalls (shashlik, lagman, kumis, seasonal), ashkans (eateries) in Barskoon and Tamga. A lunch box on the tour — 600 som (Destination Karakol).
kg-0048.reviews: Google Maps “Arabel Plateau”: 5.0/5, 24 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Barskoon Plateau”: 4.8/5, 8 reviews (the latest — July 2024). Pros: accessibility in an ordinary car, lakes, yaks, “Martian” views; cons: cold and wind, being turned back at the checkpoint, no infrastructure.
kg-0048.p.sum: The plateau at 3,800 m is reachable in 1–2 h from the village of Barskoon along the Kumtor mine gravel road — in summer even a sedan gets through, but turn-offs to the lakes are better in a 4×4. Be sure to have your passport and vehicle documents (a document-check checkpoint), a full tank, food, water and warm clothing: on the plateau there is no accommodation, signal or café. Without your own car — a Destination Karakol jeep tour (€210–250 per car, 7–9 h) or a taxi from Barskoon/Tamga by arrangement. Stay overnight in Tamga/Barskoon; a tent on the plateau is only for the prepared (frost and snow even in July).

kg-0049.name: Maiden's Tears Waterfall
kg-0049.full: Maiden's Tears Waterfall (Maiden's Braids, Kok-Jaiyk Waterfall) — Jeti-Oguz
kg-0049.near: The Jeti-Oguz resort (sanatorium) — 3.6 km to the north (silkadv.com); the Kok-Jaiyk tract/jailoo (summer pasture) with yurt camps — 1.5 km to the southeast, the start of the trail. Jeti-Oguz village — 12 km below the resort; Karakol — ~28–35 km.
kg-0049.elev: 2400–2500 m: 2GIS — 2400 m; silkadv — 2470 m; catalog — ~2500 m. This is the elevation of the waterfall, not the height of the drop.
kg-0049.short: A waterfall in a spruce side valley above the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo in the Jeti-Oguz gorge: water 20–50 m high (depending on the source) runs down a sloping rock wall in many streams, “like tears”; 30–50 minutes on foot or by horse from the yurt camps, free entry.
kg-0049.desc: The waterfall is known by two names — “Maiden's Tears” and “Maiden's Braids” (the Kyrgyz landmark being Kok-Jaiyk): 2GIS, Kaktus.media and the catalog use “Tears”, while silkadv, Google and English-language guides use “Braids/Maiden's Braids”; the coordinates in all sources converge on one point 1.5 km northwest of the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo and 3.6 km south of the Jeti-Oguz resort, so it is one and the same place. The water runs down a sloping rock 5–10 m wide among Tian Shan spruces and fallen trunks; the height of the drop is given in sources as from 20 m (Kaktus.media, 2016) to 40 m (silkadv, catalog) and 50 m (2GIS). The trail from Kok-Jaiyk is 2.5 km round trip with an ascent of ~160 m (Asia Hikes, 07.2024), narrow, on dark soil, muddy and slippery after rain; horses are offered at the camps (800 som for the first kilometer of the climb, 2024). A local belief: a girl who washes in the waterfall will soon marry (2GIS). There is no entrance fee (2024). The classic day from Karakol: the “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks, the resort, the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo, the waterfall.
kg-0049.guide: Don't look on the maps for “Maiden's Tears” and “Maiden's Braids” as two different places — it is one waterfall above Kok-Jaiyk, and drivers know it by either name. From the yurts the trail takes half an hour to an hour: narrow, in the spruce forest, and turning to mud after rain, so bring shoes with good tread, and a horse (about 800 som) makes sense only for the first kilometer. Come in June–July, when there is the most water — in August the streams are thinner. Washing in the waterfall, according to the local belief, means a quick wedding. Leave an hour for the jailoo itself: yurts, kumys and a view of the “Seven Bulls” from the upper trail.
kg-0049.see: The waterfall itself on a sloping rock among the spruces; the trail through the spruce forest with views of Kok-Jaiyk; the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo with yurt camps; lower down the gorge — the “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks, and the Jeti-Oguz resort with radon baths; higher up the valley — trails to Teleti and Lake Ala-Kul.
kg-0049.skip: You are going in late August–September — there is little water and the waterfall is “thin”. It is raining: the trail is dangerously slippery. You are short on time in Jeti-Oguz — the “Seven Bulls” rocks are more impressive.
kg-0049.diff: Easy–moderate: 2.5 km round trip, +161 m, 30–50 min one way (Asia Hikes 2024; 2GIS 40–50 min); a narrow trail, mud after rain; manageable for children from 6–7 years old.
kg-0049.when: June — early July — maximum water (snowmelt); July–August — the season of yurts and horses at Kok-Jaiyk; September — less water, but dry and empty. In winter access to Kok-Jaiyk over snow is not guaranteed.
kg-0049.hours: Open terrain, 24 hours, no ticket offices (Asia Hikes 2024: no fee). The yurt camps at Kok-Jaiyk — June–September.
kg-0049.daytime: Morning: the waterfall is in the shade of the spruces, the trail is drier and there are no tourists; in the afternoon in July–August — thunderstorms and crowds from the resort.
kg-0049.how: From Karakol: marshrutka (minibus) No. 355 to the Jeti-Oguz resort (100 som) or No. 371 to the village (80 som) + a shared taxi village — resort 50 som (Adventures of Nicole, 10.2026; Asia Hikes 2024); from the resort 3–4 km on foot up the jeep road to Kok-Jaiyk, or a taxi; from the yurts, a 1.2 km trail to the northwest to the waterfall. Taxi Karakol — Jeti-Oguz 1000–1200 som one way, shared ~250 som/person (2026).
kg-0049.needcar: To the resort — there is a marshrutka; to Kok-Jaiyk — on foot 1–1.5 h or by car (SUV/taxi); beyond that only on foot or on horseback.
kg-0049.self: Yes: the trail is obvious from the yurts (ask for the “waterfall”), no permits or payment; an offline map (maps.me/OsmAnd) shows the trail.
kg-0049.roadtype: Paved Karakol — village — resort; from the resort to Kok-Jaiyk, a dirt jeep road (3–4 km, mud after rain); to the waterfall, a narrow footpath/horse trail on dark soil (silkadv, Asia Hikes).
kg-0049.traveltime: Karakol — resort 40–60 min (marshrutka); resort — Kok-Jaiyk 1–1.5 h on foot / 15–20 min by car; Kok-Jaiyk — waterfall 30–50 min one way (2.5 km loop, Asia Hikes 2024; 2GIS 40–50 min).
kg-0049.stay: Yurt camps at Kok-Jaiyk: EcoTrek, Taberik, Golden Yurt (Asia Hikes, 2024) — a guide of ~700 som/person/night (Adventures of Nicole, 2026); the Jeti-Oguz sanatorium at the resort; guesthouses in Jeti-Oguz village and Karakol. Booking — CBT Karakol, Destination Jeti Oguz.
kg-0049.net: At the resort and in the village there is operator coverage; at Kok-Jaiyk and the waterfall coverage is unstable/absent (from reports on Jeti-Oguz; no direct tests found). An offline map is a must.
kg-0049.entry: Free: there is no fee for Kok-Jaiyk and the waterfall (Asia Hikes, 12.07.2024); kyrgyzstanplanner 2026 mentions no fees. The sanatorium and its grounds are separate.
kg-0049.transfer: Marshrutka 80–120 som (2026); taxi Karakol — Jeti-Oguz 1000–1200 som (2026); shared ride village — resort 50 som (2024); a horse to the waterfall 800 som (2024); a tour from Karakol from $85 (2026).
kg-0049.bring: Trekking shoes with good tread, a rain jacket, water, cash (horses, yurts, marshrutka), repellent (June–July), a warm layer for the jailoo (2400 m, cold in the evening).
kg-0049.warn: The trail is narrow and slippery after rain, in places “two people can't pass each other” (Trip to Kyrgyzstan); horses churn up the trail. Do not confuse it with the waterfalls of the same name, “Maiden's Braids” on Elbrus and “Maiden's Tears” in Abkhazia — in searches they overshadow the Kyrgyz one. A marshrutka “to the village” will leave you 12 km from the resort — check the final stop. The last marshrutkas back are ~16–17 h.
kg-0049.food: In the Kok-Jaiyk yurts: kumys, boorsoks, lagman, shashlik, home-baked bread (seasonal, prices negotiable); at the resort — the sanatorium canteen; in Karakol — ashlyan-fu. Specific eateries have not been checked.
kg-0049.reviews: 2GIS “Maiden's Tears Waterfall”: 4.7/5, 26 ratings, 10 reviews (07.10.2026). Google “Maiden's Braids Waterfall” — there is a pin, the rating was not captured. Pluses from 2024–2026 reports: a short scenic climb, spruce forest, free; minuses — mud after rain, horse handlers at the camps, little water at the end of summer.
kg-0049.p.sum: From Karakol — marshrutka No. 355 to the Jeti-Oguz resort (≈100 som) or a taxi (1,000–1,200 som), then 3–4 km along the jeep road on foot (1–1.5 h) or by SUV to the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo, and from the yurts 30–50 minutes along a narrow trail through the spruce forest (2.5 km loop, +160 m). Entry is free, a horse to the waterfall ~800 som. It is best in June — early July when the water is high, and in the morning; you can stay overnight in the Kok-Jaiyk yurt camps (EcoTrek, Taberik, Golden Yurt; a guide of ~700 som/person per place) or in Karakol.

kg-0050.name: Issyk-Ata Gorge
kg-0050.near: The resort settlement of Ysyk-Ata / Karagai-Bulak village (the sanatorium’s address on 2GIS); lower down the valley — the villages in the Ivanovka direction. The district center is the town of Kant.
kg-0050.elev: The resort is at about 1,775 m (sxodim); the peaks at the head of the gorge reach ~3,200 m (per TripAdvisor reviews), Mount Botvei/Batyi is ~3,800 m (sxodim; not confirmed by a second source).
kg-0050.short: Issyk-Ata is a gorge in the Kyrgyz Ala-Too ~60–75 km from Bishkek with one of the oldest resorts in the region: hot hydrogen sulfide springs (~54 °C), waterfalls and an ancient image of the Buddha on a rock.
kg-0050.desc: The Issyk-Ata (Ysyk-Ata) Gorge lies on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too in the Ysyk-Ata District. The main point is the Yssyk-Ata resort-sanatorium, operating since the late 19th century (sxodim: 1891, too.kg: 1895): hydrogen sulfide thermal water at 50–60 °C comes out of the ground and is cooled to ~36 °C for the pools and baths; it is used to treat the musculoskeletal system, skin and digestive tract. In the 2020s the resort was reconstructed: separate bathing areas, new buildings and A-frame cabins, an amphitheater, salt rooms, mud therapy. Above the resort there are trails to waterfalls: the nearest, “Marble” (~10 m), is ~1.5 km away, then Bala-Partak and Jary-Tash, and the lakes of the Ayak-Kol area (the largest is Orto-Kol). On a rock near the resort is an image of the Buddha with Tibetan inscriptions (dating differs between sources: the 10th century or the 12th–14th centuries) — a reminder that the gorge was one of the region’s Buddhist centers.
kg-0050.guide: Issyk-Ata is an ideal “mountains + thermal baths” day: in the morning climb to the waterfalls, after lunch soak in the sanatorium’s hot pool. The nearest Marble Waterfall is 1.5 km from the resort; for the far waterfalls allow 2–3 hours and take water. Be sure to find the stone with the image of the Buddha and Tibetan inscriptions — a reminder that in the Middle Ages there was a Buddhist center here. Locals tell a legend that Amir Timur himself was cured of an illness here. On weekends the resort is overcrowded — it is better to come on weekdays.
kg-0050.see: The hot hydrogen sulfide springs and the sanatorium’s pools; the stone with the Buddha image and Tibetan inscriptions; the Marble Waterfall (~10 m, 1.5 km from the resort), the Bala-Partak and Jary-Tash waterfalls; the Ayak-Kol lakes (Orto-Kol); coniferous forests and meadows in the upper reaches.
kg-0050.skip: You are looking for wilderness without people — the resort and the lower part of the gorge are crowded, with Soviet-era buildings and litter on the trails (TripAdvisor reviews). You are not interested in thermal baths — the waterfalls are more impressive at Kegety or Ala-Archa. You dislike disorganized service — 2GIS reviews complain about booking and cleaning.
kg-0050.diff: Easy–moderate: from the parking lot from 2.5 km and from 1 h on foot with a gain from 250 m to the nearest waterfall, 2–3 out of 5 on the hiking.kg scale; to the far waterfalls and lakes — 3+ h (TripAdvisor). Bathing in the thermal pools — no exertion, but with health restrictions (heart, blood pressure).
kg-0050.when: July–September is the peak trekking season (sxodim); the thermal baths work year-round and are especially popular in winter. Many cafés and hotels work only in summer (TripAdvisor).
kg-0050.hours: Sanatorium: 08:00–17:00 per sxodim; pools per 2GIS — Monday closed, Tuesday 12:00–21:00, Wednesday–Sunday 09:00–21:00 (07.10.2026). Tel. +996 709 833 833, WhatsApp +996 990 250 000, Instagram @sanatorii_ysyk_ata. The gorge and trails — no time restrictions.
kg-0050.daytime: Morning — for the climb to the waterfalls (fewer people, cooler); evening — for the thermal baths. On weekends come when the pools open.
kg-0050.how: From Bishkek ~58 km, 1 h 25 min by car (hiking.kg; sxodim — 77 km, too.kg — 40–50 km, depending on the starting point) via Koi-Tash/Gornaya Maevka (the upper road) or via Ivanovka (the lower road). Marshrutka (minibus) No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station to the resort (too.kg). Beyond that, to the waterfalls — on foot.
kg-0050.needcar: Yes, but marshrutka No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station is enough; a car or taxi is more convenient. Inside the gorge, to the waterfalls — on foot.
kg-0050.self: Yes: marshrutka No. 316 to the resort, pools without reservations, the trails to the nearest waterfalls are clear. For the far lakes you need an offline map.
kg-0050.roadtype: To the sanatorium — paved, in places of poor quality (sxodim: paved approach); to the waterfalls — trails.
kg-0050.traveltime: Bishkek → resort: 1 h 25 min by car (hiking.kg), about 1.5 h by marshrutka (TripAdvisor). Resort → nearest waterfall: from 2.5 km and from 1 h, gain from 250 m (hiking.kg); the Marble Waterfall — 1.5 km (too.kg).
kg-0050.stay: “Yssyk-Ata” sanatorium: rooms from 7,500 som a night, wellness packages with treatments and meals from 2,200 som (mir24, 2025–2026); new A-frames (2GIS reviews). Private guesthouses in the settlement — 700–2,500 som (2GIS reviews). Camping below the resort is limited, above it up the gorge it is possible (too.kg).
kg-0050.net: There is mobile coverage up to the resort grounds, further up the gorge — none (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
kg-0050.entry: According to hiking.kg, since 2025 entry to the sanatorium grounds has been paid — the amount is not published. A pool — from 100 som (too.kg), 200 som in 2GIS reviews; parking is paid (sxodim; 300 som in 2GIS reviews). The exact 2026 tariff is not confirmed.
kg-0050.transfer: Marshrutka No. 316 — 50 som (too.kg); taxi and excursion prices are not given in the sources (Kyrgyz Guided Tours/Silk Road Explore — on request).
kg-0050.bring: Swimwear, a towel and flip-flops for the thermal baths, trekking shoes and water for the waterfalls (do not drink from the river — only springs, too.kg), food with you (the cafés work mostly in summer), warm clothes for the evening (1,775 m), cash.
kg-0050.warn: Hot hydrogen sulfide baths are not recommended for heart disease and high blood pressure — ask the sanatorium’s doctor. Do not drink river water. The signal ends at the resort. On weekends and holidays it is overcrowded — book accommodation in advance. An entry/parking fee was introduced in 2025 — demand a receipt.
kg-0050.food: Cafés on the resort grounds and grocery shops (too.kg); mineral water from the springs; meals as part of the sanatorium packages (from 2,200 som). The sources name no specific well-known establishments; 2GIS reviews complain about cold food in the cafés.
kg-0050.reviews: 2GIS (“Yssyk-Ata” sanatorium): 4.8/5, 1,533 ratings, 234 reviews (07.10.2026); TripAdvisor “Issyk-Ata Gorge”: 4.5/5, 39 reviews. Pros: hot pools, nature, waterfalls, new A-frames. Cons: old Soviet buildings, litter on the trails, disorganized booking, rude staff, hot-water problems.
kg-0050.p.sum: Issyk-Ata is a convenient day trip from Bishkek: marshrutka No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station (40–50 som, roughly once an hour, about 1.5 h) goes straight to the “Ysyk-Ata” sanatorium. There are thermal pools with 54 °C spring water (per Travelbar — 200 som for adults, 100 som for children), the stone with the Buddha and trails to waterfalls: the Marble one is 1.5 km away, the nearest big one is 2.5 km with a 250 m gain. After a major renovation (opened 17.12.2024) the sanatorium belongs to the Presidential Administration. Since 2025 entry to the grounds and parking are paid, but we did not find an official tariff. On weekends there can be a real queue, and phone reservations are not always honored (Kaktus, 06.2026).

The thermal baths work year-round and are especially popular in winter; on weekends and holidays there are queues. Many cafés and guesthouses work only in summer. kg-0051.name: Achik-Tash Base Camp
kg-0051.near: Sary-Mogol (about 3000–3200 m; CBT gives 3200 m) — ~25 km to Tulpar-Kol and the camps (Visit Alay); also the village of Kashka-Suu, from which people ride horses to Tulpar-Kol (too.kg).
kg-0051.elev: About 3600 m (ak-sai.com, Central Asia Travel, Nomad's Land; ~12,000 feet per Univ. of Washington). The advanced camp / Camp 1 “Solnechny” (Sunny) — about 4200–4400 m (Central Asia Travel, Nomad's Land). Visit Alay mistakenly writes “Base Camp 4400 m”, nomadasaurus — “about 4000 m”.
kg-0051.short: Achik-Tash is the main base camp on the north side of Lenin Peak (7134 m) in the Trans-Alay Range, at an elevation of about 3600 m: yurt and tent camps of mountaineering companies, the starting point for ascents and treks.
kg-0051.desc: Achik-Tash is a valley and meadow at the foot of Lenin Peak (7134 m), where every summer (June — September) several mountaineering companies (Ak-Sai Travel, Central Asia Travel and others) and local yurt camps set up base camps. From here ascents of Lenin Peak start, via Camp 1 (~4400 m) and Travellers' Pass (~4150 m), as well as acclimatization outings to Yukhin Peak and Petrovsky Peak, and day walks to Lake Tulpar-Kol (~3500 m), ~4 km away. The camp lies about 25 km south of the village of Sary-Mogol in the Alay Valley; from Osh it is about 280 km and 5 hours by car along the Pamir Highway M41 via Taldyk Pass and Sary-Tash (Central Asia Travel). A border permit is needed to visit the area (tour.too.kg, Visit Alay, Central Asia Travel).
kg-0051.guide: Achik-Tash is a rare chance to see a seven-thousander almost from the door of your yurt: Lenin Peak rises above a green meadow at 3600 m, where edelweiss blooms in July. Even if you are not a mountaineer, come for 1–2 nights: a walk to the reddish shores of Tulpar-Kol (~4 km) and a hike toward Travellers' Pass give views of the glaciers without technical skills. The camps operate from late June to late August — at that time in the dining tent you can meet expeditions from all over the world. Arrange the border permit in advance (7–20 days), and after Osh give your body a night of acclimatization in Sary-Mogol. If you are lucky with the dates, in July Sary-Mogol hosts a festival of national games with yaks and horses (CBT).
kg-0051.see: The north face and glaciers of Lenin Peak (7134 m); the base camp meadow with edelweiss; Lake Tulpar-Kol with red slopes (~3500 m, ~4 km); the climb to Travellers' Pass (~4150 m); the acclimatization peaks Yukhin (5130 m) and Petrovsky; expedition infrastructure (dining tent, banya, gear shop).
kg-0051.skip: You are not ready to arrange a border permit in advance and pay for a transfer on a dirt road. You tolerate 3600 m and cold nights poorly (even in summer about zero). Views of Lenin Peak from Sary-Mogol or from Tulpar-Kol are enough for you.
kg-0051.diff: Access to the camp is not difficult: a car to the place, then short walks. A day walk to Tulpar-Kol is easy; the walk from Sary-Mogol is 8–9 h (Visit Alay); the hike to Camp 1 is moderate/hard, 4–6 h, and acclimatization is needed (Univ. of Washington; nomadasaurus 2026). Climbing Lenin Peak is a technical high-altitude expedition.
kg-0051.when: Late June — late August: Central Asia Travel camps operate ~28 June — 30 August, transfers 25 June — 1 September; the Ak-Sai camp — June — September. In July — the festival of games with yaks and horses in Sary-Mogol (the third weekend of July, Visit Alay). Out of season there is no infrastructure.
kg-0051.hours: Seasonal: the yurt/tent camps are open approximately from late June to late August — early September (ak-sai.com, centralasia-travel.com). Around the clock within the season; the limitation is the border regime.
kg-0051.daytime: Early morning — the clearest weather and a clean view of the summit; by midday clouds often gather over the peak (editorial). For the walk to Tulpar-Kol/Travellers' Pass, set out in the morning.
kg-0051.how: Osh → Gulcha → Taldyk Pass → Sary-Tash → west along the Alay Valley to Sary-Mogol (M41/the road to Daroot-Korgon) → south across the Kyzyl-Suu River on a dirt road ~25 km to Tulpar-Kol and Achik-Tash. From Osh about 280 km, ~5 h by car (Central Asia Travel). From Sary-Mogol: ~45 min by car, 4–5 h on horseback, 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
kg-0051.needcar: Yes. There is no public transport to the camp: a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Sary-Mogol, then a taxi/4×4 / SUV from CBT (or a transfer by a mountaineering company), a horse or a walk.
kg-0051.self: Partly: experienced travelers get there on their own (a marshrutka (minibus) + a taxi in Sary-Mogol) and overnight in the camps or a tent. Formally a border permit for the Lenin Peak zone is required — arranged in advance through a travel agency/CBT (tour.too.kg, Visit Alay). Nomadasaurus (2026) writes that in practice the permit was not checked for Tulpar-Kol and the base camp — do not rely on that.
kg-0051.roadtype: To Sary-Mogol — paved M41 via Taldyk and Sary-Tash; from Sary-Mogol ~25 km of dirt road with a ford/bridge over the Kyzyl-Suu to Tulpar-Kol and the camps (Visit Alay: “45 minutes by car”); there are signposts to the camps. The condition after rain is not confirmed.
kg-0051.traveltime: From Osh — about 5 h by car (~280 km, Central Asia Travel); by public transport to Sary-Mogol 4–5 h + 45 min by taxi (nomadasaurus 2026; Visit Alay).
kg-0051.stay:
• Ak-Sai Travel, the Achik-Tash camp (3600 m, June — September): a yurt for two $65 (breakfast) / $75 (breakfast+dinner) / $85 (three meals); a tent for two $40/50/65; single supplement $30–35; 15 yurts, 10 glamping capsules, 54 tents (ak-sai.com, 2026).
• Central Asia Travel — the “Edelweiss Meadow” base camp with heated yurts, a sauna, Wi-Fi (prices per the price list, 2027 season: 28.06–30.08).
• Yurt camps at Tulpar-Kol (CBT and private): from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay); ~$10 with meals per nomadasaurus 2026; a tent in designated places is free.
• Sary-Mogol guesthouses $15–20 (nomadasaurus, 2026).
kg-0051.net: Ak-Sai claims Wi-Fi (Starlink) and a mobile signal in the camp (ak-sai.com, 2026); Central Asia Travel — Wi-Fi in the base camp and Camp 1. Sary-Mogol has mobile 4G (nomadasaurus, 2026). Coverage of specific operators in the camp itself is not confirmed.
kg-0051.entry: There is no separate entry fee; a border permit is needed: 3000 som/person via tour.too.kg (covers all zones, 7 working days, apply 14 days ahead; 2026). Processing through CBT/Visit Alay takes 10–20 days (Visit Alay); nomadasaurus (2026) gives $65 and 5 days via CBT Sary-Mogol — the source probably mixes up the permit and the mountaineering permit. Climbing Lenin Peak requires separate permits through a mountaineering company.
kg-0051.transfer: Sary-Mogol → camp: from 1500 som per car (Visit Alay) / $10–15 (nomadasaurus 2026). Osh → Sary-Mogol: 300 som marshrutka (minibus) / 400 som shared taxi (nomadasaurus 2026). A direct Osh — Achik-Tash transfer from the mountaineering companies — per price list, exact 2026 prices not found.
kg-0051.bring: A passport and a printout of the border permit; warm clothes (about zero at night even in July), a down jacket, a hat and gloves; sunglasses and high-SPF cream; trekking boots; cash in som (no ATMs — editorial); a headlamp; a kit against altitude sickness (editorial).
kg-0051.warn: Border zone: without a permit you may have problems at checkpoints — arrange it 2–3 weeks ahead (tour.too.kg; Visit Alay). At 3600 m: risk of altitude sickness, don't go up from Osh in a single day without a night at an intermediate altitude (editorial). Above the camp — glaciers and crevasses, going to Camp 1 and higher only with experience/a guide. The weather changes quickly, and snow is possible in summer.
kg-0051.food: Meals at the camps — buffet/three meals a day (Ak-Sai) and home cooking at the Tulpar-Kol yurt camps (breakfast and dinner included in the price). From local herders you can try kymyz (fermented mare's milk) and ayran (editorial, general Alay practice; specific places not confirmed).
kg-0051.reviews: Google Maps: the camp's listing is not unambiguously matched (catalog check — “Ambiguous result”). Hotel aggregators (Hotels.com, Travelocity) have a listing “Achik Tash Base Camp Ak Sai Travel” — rating not checked. From travel notes: pros — views of Lenin Peak, the organization of the camps, Wi-Fi; cons — cold nights, altitude, prices higher than the local yurt camps (Visit Alay).
kg-0051.p.sum: The simplest way to get there: Osh → Sary-Mogol (marshrutka (minibus) 300 som at 14:00 or a transfer), a night of acclimatization in Sary-Mogol, then a taxi along the dirt road ~25 km (1500 som per car) to Tulpar-Kol and the camps. Arrange the border permit (3000 som via tour.too.kg) 2–3 weeks ahead. Overnight in yurt camps at Tulpar-Kol (from ~1000 som with meals) or in the mountaineering companies' camps on the Achik-Tash meadow (Ak-Sai $65–85 for a yurt for two). The best day outings are to Travellers' Pass (4130 m) and Yukhin Peak (5130 m) after acclimatization.
