kg-0051.p.iti.0.title: A day trip from Sary-Mogol
kg-0051.p.iti.0.plan: 08:00 taxi 45 min → 09:00 Tulpar-Kol → 10:00 BC → climb to Travellers' Pass and back (6–7 h) → 18:00 taxi to Sary-Mogol.
kg-0051.p.iti.1.title: 3 days from Osh
kg-0051.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Osh → Sary-Mogol (marshrutka (minibus) 14:00), a night in a guesthouse. Day 2: a taxi to Tulpar-Kol, a walk to BC, a night in a yurt. Day 3: sunrise at the lake, Travellers' Pass, return to Sary-Mogol/Osh.
kg-0051.p.iti.2.title: Combinations
kg-0051.p.iti.2.plan: Along one road: Taldyk → Sary-Tash → Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kol → Achik-Tash. By trek — from Kojokelen over Jiptyk (3 days).
kg-0051.p.season: June: the camps open ~25–28.06, snow on the passes. July — August: peak season, expeditions, the games festival in Sary-Mogol (the third weekend of July), about 0 °C at night. September: the companies wrap up ~30.08–1.09, some private yurts operate until late September. October — May: no infrastructure, snow.
kg-0051.p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Osh — Sary-Mogol 300 som + a taxi to the lake 1500 som/car (~400–750 per person) + a yurt at Tulpar-Kol ~1000–2000 som with meals + the border permit 3000 som ≈ 5000–6000 som/person for 2 days
kg-0051.p.budget.comfort: A transfer Osh — BC $300 per car + an Ak-Sai yurt $75–85 (for two with meals) + a horse $15/h + a sauna $25 ≈ $250–350/person for 2–3 days
kg-0051.p.permits: A border permit for the Lenin Peak zone is mandatory: via tour.too.kg — 3000 som, 5–7 working days (office at Isanov St. 105/3, Bishkek); via CBT/a tour operator — 10–20 days, $40–65 (travelers' logs). Apply 2–3 weeks ahead, and keep the printout and your passport with you. Climbing Lenin Peak requires a separate mountaineering permit through a company.
kg-0051.p.access: Children with mountain experience and adults without chronic illnesses — yes, but 3600 m requires acclimatization (a night in Sary-Mogol). Older people — only with caution and short walks. Stroller — no (dirt, tall grass). Dogs — at Ak-Sai a $20/day surcharge.
kg-0051.p.gaps.2: Prices of Pamir Extreme and Tien Shan Travel not found

kg-0052.name: Salkyn-Tor National Park
kg-0052.near: Alysh village (the park's address in 2GIS) and the town of Naryn: according to CBT Naryn the park is ~12 km east of Naryn (Nomad's Land — 18 km, Lonely Planet — 17 km); from the arch on the main road to the entrance is ~2 km.
kg-0052.elev: About 2200 m at the entrance (Nomad's Land); the CBT Naryn trail starts at 2167 m, and the highest point of the route, by the glacier, is 3221 m.
kg-0052.short: A 10,448-hectare nature park on the northern slope of the Naryn-Too range near Naryn: Schrenk spruce forests, a river with footbridges, a picnic area at the entrance and a 13 km trail to a glacier; it was created to protect the maral (Tian Shan red deer).
kg-0052.desc: Salkyn-Tor (“cool peak”) is a state nature park established in May 2001 on the northern slope of the Naryn-Too range, roughly 12–18 km east of Naryn, covering 10,448 hectares. Its main purpose is restoring the Tian Shan maral population; roe deer, lynx, brown bear, wolf, stone marten, ibex and marmots also live here, along with Red Data Book species. The lower belt is dense Schrenk spruce forest with Tian Shan rowan, wild rose and barberry. At the entrance are a picnic area, toilets, small cabins and yurts (partly abandoned according to reviews), and the famous bridge shaped like the letter “M” (the “lovers' bridge”). The main trail goes up the river valley: the first 2 km have three footbridges, then come fords, around km 10 there is a shepherds' camp in the spruce forest, and above it a rocky climb to the fork of the river and the glacier (13 km, 2167 → 3221 m). The territory also has the Kojo-Ungur cave, the historic Dubolu hill, the Kurga spring, and the Kok-Jayyk, Berkut-Uya and Kyzyl-Zoo canyons; the area has about 30 hot and cold springs.
kg-0052.guide: For an easy day the lower zone is enough: a picnic by the river, a walk across the three footbridges and a photo on the “M” bridge — it's a favorite weekend spot for Naryn residents. For a real hike, set out early and walk 13 km up to the glacier — the way to the shepherds' camp in the spruce forest (~10 km) is level, after which the rocky climb begins. Be ready to take your shoes off at the fords, and in June to cross the river on snow bridges, testing them with a stick. Entry is paid, so keep cash on hand. Take your trash with you — reviews complain about dirty picnic areas.
kg-0052.see: Schrenk spruce forests in the river valley; the footbridges and the “M” bridge at the entrance; the shepherds' camp in the spruce forest (~10 km); the glacier and the upper fork of the river (3221 m); the Kojo-Ungur cave, Dubolu hill, the Kurga spring, the Kok-Jayyk, Berkut-Uya and Kyzyl-Zoo canyons; nearby — the maral nursery (Pitomnik Bugu Maralov).
kg-0052.skip: You have already seen the spruce forests of Jeti-Oguz/Ala-Archa and aren't up for the full 26 km route — the lower zone is modest and littered in places. You're only passing through Naryn on the way to Tash-Rabat and have less than 3–4 hours. You're going in early summer with no experience of fords — the upper part of the trail with snow bridges is dangerous.
kg-0052.diff: The lower walking zone is easy (picnic, footbridges). The full CBT Naryn route is hard but not technical: 13 km one way, ~1690 m of ascent, several fords, rocky upper reaches; in early summer, snow bridges.
kg-0052.when: July–September for the full trail (at the end of June there is still snow and snow bridges over the river — CBT Naryn); the lower zone from late May to October. In summer it is popular with locals on weekends — quieter on weekdays.
kg-0052.hours: No official opening hours are published (2GIS, Google — hours not given). Entry is paid, with a check at the barrier/arch; ask CBT Naryn (+996 559 567 685).
kg-0052.daytime: An early start (7–8 am) for the glacier route — 26 km round trip; a picnic works any time of day. In the daytime the water at the fords is higher because of melting.
kg-0052.how: From Naryn east along the road beside the Naryn River toward the airport and At-Bashy for ~12–18 km to the arch by the main road (Alysh village area), then ~2 km to the entrance. From Bishkek to Naryn — 4.5–5 h (marshrutka (minibus) 600 som, GoBus 500 som).
kg-0052.needcar: Yes: from Naryn 12–18 km — taxi or car; on foot from the arch to the entrance is 2 km. The sources mention no public transport to the entrance (Naryn — At-Bashy marshrutkas may drop you at the arch — not confirmed).
kg-0052.self: Yes: the trail is obvious, along the river; there is a fee at the entrance. For the upper part beyond the shepherds' camp (the trail fades, snow) a guide or experience is better; central-asia.guide recommends a guide for the park's remote sites.
kg-0052.roadtype: Paved Naryn — At-Bashy highway to the arch; ~2 km of access road to the entrance (surface not given in the sources). Inside, a footpath: bridges in the first 2 km, then fords and a rocky trail.
kg-0052.traveltime: Naryn — park entrance ~20–30 min (12–18 km; estimate). The full route to the glacier is 13 km one way, a full daylight day round trip. To the shepherds' camp (~10 km) — 3–4 h (estimate).
kg-0052.stay: At the entrance there are small cabins and yurts (Lonely Planet; partly abandoned according to TripAdvisor reviews) and Soviet-era recreation bases with yurts and simple cabins (central-asia.guide) — prices are not published. Usonbak Yurt Camp in the Salkyn-Tor area is mentioned on TripAdvisor (prices not found). The main option is guesthouses and hotels in Naryn via CBT Naryn; camping in the park is with the administration's permission (not confirmed).
kg-0052.net: Not confirmed by sources. In Naryn and along the highway there is Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage; deeper in the gorge the signal probably drops out — an offline map is essential.
kg-0052.entry: Entry is paid (TripAdvisor reviews). Nomad's Land gives $1 per person (year not stated). The current 2025–2026 tariff in som is not confirmed; in June 2026 a member of the Jogorku Kenesh proposed charging foreigners $20–50 to enter national parks — no decision has been made (Vesti.kg, 22.06.2026).
kg-0052.transfer: No published taxi prices Naryn — Salkyn-Tor were found; a car via CBT Naryn is on request. Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (May 2026), GoBus 500 som (2024).
kg-0052.bring: Shoes you don't mind getting wet, or sandals, for the fords; trekking poles (snow bridges in June); warm clothes for the upper part (3221 m); water and food for the whole day; cash for the entrance; a bag for trash.
kg-0052.warn: Fords across the river; in June, snow bridges that can collapse (CBT Naryn). Above the shepherds' camp the trail fades. Brown bears and wolves live in the park — don't leave food in your tent. Trash and dirt at the picnic areas by the entrance (reviews).
kg-0052.food: No cafes in the park are confirmed — bring food for a picnic. In Naryn you'll find the national dishes of Naryn region: beshbarmak, naryn (thin noodles with meat), and kumys in summer; at the shepherds' camps on the route, kumys and ayran (by arrangement).
kg-0052.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 25 ratings (03.10.2026). 2GIS: 4.9/5, 27 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 12 reviews. Pros: beautiful mountains and spruce forests, family trails, convenient from Naryn, the “M” bridge. Cons: trash, abandoned picnic areas, fords where you have to take your shoes off, an entry fee with no stated tariff.
kg-0052.p.sum: Salkyn-Tor is the nearest nature to Naryn: 12–20 km east along the paved road toward At-Bashy, then ~2 km to the entrance; from town, a taxi or a CBT Naryn car (20–30 min). Entry is paid but token (20 som per Wikivoyage/Journal of Nomads; the current 2026 tariff is not confirmed). For an easy day: a picnic and the footbridges at the entrance; for a hike: 13 km to the glacier with 1690 m of ascent (a full daylight day, fords). It's more convenient to stay overnight in Naryn: guesthouses from $8–10 to $50 on Booking, CBT Naryn ≈600 som with breakfast.

kg-0053.name: Kojokelen Valley
kg-0053.near: The village of Kojokelen (Kojo-Kelen) in the valley itself — houses of red and black clay along the Diptyk River (open.kg). Further down the Ak-Buura is the area of the Papan Reservoir.
kg-0053.elev: The village is at about 2230–2250 m: the parking by the red cliffs ~2230 m (vpoxod), the lowest point of the Visit Alay track from Kojokelen is 2244 m; the campsite near Kojo-Keleng ~2760 m per a 2025 tracker (higher up the valley). The jailoo (summer pasture) ~2700 m, the grotto ~3100 m (Central Asia Travel); Jiptyk Pass 4162–4185 m.
kg-0053.short: Kojokelen is the valley of the Diptyk River at the foot of the Alay Range, 95–110 km southwest of Osh, known for its red Jurassic cliffs, a 50 m waterfall, a sacred grotto with an underground pool, and the trek over Jiptyk Pass to Lenin Peak.
kg-0053.desc: The Kojo-Kelen valley lies in a widening of the Diptyk River valley (a left tributary of the Ak-Buura) at the foot of the Alay Range and covers more than 300 km² (open.kg). At the upper edge of the village rise orange-red cliffs of Jurassic age — the “sculptures of Kojokelen”, called the “Three Dragons Gorge” in trekking descriptions (Visit Alay). 3 km from the village is a waterfall about 50 m high that makes rainbows in summer; higher up is a white-pink grotto with a crescent-shaped entrance and a blue underground pool, revered as a holy place (open.kg, Central Asia Travel). The slopes are covered with spruce forests and meadows; Alay Kyrgyz who keep a nomadic way of life live here. The valley is the start/intermediate point of treks over Sary-Bel Pass (~3137–3200 m) and Jiptyk Pass (~4175 m) into the Alay Valley to Sary-Mogol and the Lenin Peak base camp.
kg-0053.guide: Kojokelen impresses with its contrast: the spruce slopes of the Alay and bright red cliffs like a Martian landscape, right above the clay houses of the village. Walk to the 50 m waterfall 3 km from the village — in summer rainbows stand in its spray — and climb to the grotto with the blue underground pool, which locals consider holy: behave there as you would at a mazar (shrine). The valley is good as the start of a three-day trek over Jiptyk Pass (4185 m), from which Lenin Peak and other Pamir seven-thousanders are visible in clear weather — and the finish is already in Sary-Mogol. Overnight in a guesthouse: Visit Alay's has hot showers, electricity and internet. This is not a hyped place — there are few tourists and a lot of hospitality.
kg-0053.see: The red Jurassic cliffs (“Three Dragons Gorge”) at the upper edge of the village; the ~50 m waterfall 3 km from the village; the grotto with a holy spring and a blue underground lake (~3100 m); the Sharpyldak and Chal-Kuyruk canyons; spruce forests and jailoo (summer pasture) (~2700 m) with yurts where you can see felt and kymyz (fermented mare's milk) being made (Central Asia Travel, open.kg, Visit Alay).
kg-0053.skip: You are looking for a “half-hour by car” place — the valley requires at least an overnight and walking. You don't want a remote area: infrastructure is limited to guesthouses, and the road is dirt. You have already seen the red cliffs of Skazka/Jeti-Oguz and have no time for a long trip from Osh.
kg-0053.diff: Walks to the waterfall and red cliffs — easy/moderate (3 km from the village). The Kojokelen — Jiptyk — Sary-Mogol trek: 3 days, 36 km, 2211 m of ascent, “moderate to hard” (Visit Alay). A one-day crossing Sary-Bel — Kojokelen: 12 km, ~5 h, +400/−970 m (vpoxod). A TripAdvisor review calls the approach along the abandoned road one of the easiest treks in the country.
kg-0053.when: June — early September (the Visit Alay trekking season); weather on the trek is usually stable and sunny, +10…+30 °C in the daytime depending on altitude (vpoxod). Jiptyk Pass — summer only. In winter the village is cut off and cold (schoolchildren studied in yurts in winter — Azattyk).
kg-0053.hours: A natural area with a village; no visiting hours or fees found. Guesthouses mostly receive guests during the trekking season (June — September, Visit Alay).
kg-0053.daytime: Morning and early evening light — the red cliffs are especially bright in low sun (editorial). For the crossing to the pass, set out early in the morning.
kg-0053.how: From Osh west along the Osh — Batken — Isfana highway, then by dirt road toward the Papan Reservoir and up the Ak-Buura/Diptyk (Central Asia Travel): ~95–110 km, about 3 h by car (Visit Alay). Alternatives — on foot over the Kosh-Moynok/Sary-Bel passes from the Alay or over Jiptyk from Sary-Mogol.
kg-0053.needcar: Yes: a 4×4 / SUV or a transfer from Osh is needed; no public transport to the village was found in the sources. In the valley — on foot or on horseback.
kg-0053.self: Yes for experienced trekkers with a GPS track and a tent — the route along the old road/trail is easy to follow (TripAdvisor, qdraw 2025). The difficulties are the drop-off from Osh with no public transport and the crossing of 4185 m Jiptyk Pass. A border permit for the valley itself is not mentioned in the sources; for going on to the Lenin Peak base camp it is required.
kg-0053.roadtype: Paved Osh — Batken road to the turn-off, then a dirt road along the river (gorge) to the village (Central Asia Travel, Visit Alay); above the village — a sandy/abandoned road and trails (qdraw 2025, TripAdvisor).
kg-0053.traveltime: From Osh about 3 h by car (Visit Alay); 95–110 km (open.kg / Central Asia Travel). On foot: from the village to the yurt camp below Jiptyk ~3 h; from Sary-Bel Pass to the village ~3–5 h (Visit Alay, vpoxod).
kg-0053.stay: Guesthouses in the village of Kojokelen (hot shower, electricity, internet — Visit Alay); stays in locals' homes on Asia Mountains tours; a yurt camp at the foot of Jiptyk (B&B in a yurt on a Visit Alay tour); camping in the valley up to ~3500 m (TripAdvisor). Names and prices of individual guesthouses not found.
kg-0053.net: Visit Alay lists internet at the Kojokelen guesthouse (probably Wi-Fi). Operator coverage in the valley and on the passes is not confirmed.
kg-0053.entry: No entry fee found — according to the sources found the valley is not part of a protected area (Visit Alay, Central Asia Travel, open.kg).
kg-0053.transfer: There is no separate tariff. The Visit Alay Jiptick Pass Trek package with a transfer from Osh — $220–520/person (2 people — $360/person); the exact price of a one-off taxi Osh — Kojokelen was not found.
kg-0053.bring: Trekking shoes; warm clothing and a rain jacket (Jiptyk at 4185 m is cold even in summer); sun protection; cash in som; a water filter/tablets; offline maps (editorial, based on trek reports). For entering the sacred grotto — modest clothing (editorial).
kg-0053.warn: Remoteness: no regular transport, medical help is far away. Jiptyk Pass (4185 m) is high mountain terrain, cross it only in season and with preparation. The grotto is a pilgrimage site, respect local customs. Clay buildings and red cliffs are prone to rockfall — don't climb the cliffs (editorial).
kg-0053.food: Home cooking of the Alay Kyrgyz at guesthouses; kymyz (fermented mare's milk) on the summer jailoo — tourists are shown how it is made (Central Asia Travel). No cafe in the village found.
kg-0053.reviews: Google Maps: 5/5, 3 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, catalog check). TripAdvisor “Kozhokelen Valley”: 4.0/5, 3 reviews (2015–2016), No. 18 of 23 in Osh. Pros: red and white cliffs, an easy approach along the old road, a view of Lenin Peak from Jiptyk. Con: the last ~12 km to the Alay are “fast but boring”.
kg-0053.p.sum: Kojokelen is a remote valley with no public transport: it is best to arrange a drop-off from Osh (~95 km, ~3–4 h via Ak-Terek — Papan) through CBT Osh or Visit Alay, or arrive on a trek from Sary-Mogol over the Sary-Mogol/Sary-Bel passes. Overnights are in the village's homestays (no signs, arrange through CBT) and the yurt camp below Jiptyk. The best option is the 3-day Kojokelen — Jiptyk — Sary-Mogol trek with an extension to Lenin Peak.

kg-0054.name: Manjyly-Ata Valley
kg-0054.full: Manjyly-Ata Valley (the sacred springs of Manjyly-Ata)
kg-0054.near: Tong village — ~5 km to the northwest (Aigine); Bokonbaevo — ~10 min by car to the west (Backpack Adventures, 2026); Kaji-Say — ~15 min to the east. The complex is ~1 km from the lakeshore, south of the Bishkek — Karakol highway.
kg-0054.elev: ~1650 m (Nomad's Land) — hills 1 km from the shore, slightly above the lake level (1607 m).
kg-0054.short: A valley of sacred springs on the south shore of Issyk-Kul: 7–17 mineral springs among clay hills and old willows, a saint's mazar, a caretaker-shyrakchy and pilgrims from all over Kyrgyzstan; a place from the Manas epic, reachable from the highway in 10 minutes from Bokonbaevo.
kg-0054.desc: Manjyly-Ata is a maze of dry clay valleys (a “geological anomaly,” per Nomad's Land) between the highway and the Terskey foothills, 5 km southeast of Tong village. According to a study by the Aigine center, there are seven main springs here, each with a name and a “specialization”: Manjyly-Ata (the main one, ringed by black willows), Maytyk-Dubana, Ilim, Bala, Bugu-Ene, Aziz, Uy-Bulyolyuk — for ailments from infertility to liver and eye diseases; guidebooks count 12 main and 5 additional springs (17 in all). On the hill is the mazar of an Islamic preacher, where the round of the springs begins; the tradition blends Tengrism and Islam, and the place is mentioned in the Manas epic and became famous by the end of the 17th century. The caretaker (as of 2026, Zhakypov Kadyrbek, a healer from Jeti-Oguz) guides pilgrims and explains the properties of the water. A full round of the springs takes about 2 hours on foot along dry, shadeless paths. Religious leaders complain that the water in the springs is diminishing (drought, groundwater pumping) and that “entertainment” tourism robs the place of its power — kasiet (Religion News, 2024). There are no entrance tickets; a donation to the caretaker is customary (the amount is not set).
kg-0054.guide: This is not a park but a living shrine: come as a guest, not as a tourist — cover your shoulders and knees, keep your voice low, don't step into the water with shoes on, and ask the caretaker before drinking from a spring. Walking the seven to twelve springs takes a couple of hours over dry, shadeless hills, so morning or evening and a liter of water are essential. Each spring has its own “specialty” — the most famous is the one childless couples travel to. Climb up to the mazar on the hill: from there you can see the lake and the same “Martian” clay as in the neighboring canyons. No fee is charged, but leaving a donation for the caretaker is the right thing to do. Combine it with Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon (20 km) and the Shatyly panorama — all of it fits into one day based in Bokonbaevo.
kg-0054.see: The main Manjyly-Ata spring ringed by black willows; the springs Maytyk-Dubana, Ilim, Bala, Bugu-Ene, Aziz (you can hear water inside a willow trunk), Uy-Bulyolyuk; the mazar on the hill with a view of the lake; the “eight sacred willows”; healing mud nearby; a landscape of dry clay hills that merges into the Mars canyons (0.5 km).
kg-0054.skip: You're uncomfortable at active religious sites with rules of conduct. You expect waterfalls and “bathing pools” — the springs are small, the water is for drinking and ablution, not for swimming. Heat above 30 °C: there's no shade at all.
kg-0054.diff: Easy: a walk over gentle dry hills and hollows, ~2 h for the full round (Backpack Adventures, 2026); no elevation gain; no shade and no water (apart from the springs).
kg-0054.when: Year-round (Backpack Adventures): there is almost no snow in winter, but it's cold; summer is hot and shadeless — April–June and September–October are more comfortable. On Fridays and religious holidays there are more pilgrims.
kg-0054.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): open 24 hours. In practice, daylight hours; the caretaker lives at the complex, and it's best to arrange a tour through CBT Bokonbaevo.
kg-0054.daytime: Early morning or 2 hours before sunset — cool, soft light on the clay hills; midday in summer is hot.
kg-0054.how: On the southern Balykchy — Karakol highway (A363) between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say: a large sign by the road (Backpack Adventures), turn south to the springs. From Bokonbaevo — 10 min by taxi (via CBT Bokonbaevo) or a marshrutka (minibus) toward Kaji-Say to the sign; from Karakol — a marshrutka toward Bokonbaevo ~2 h, ~100 som (TripAdvisor 2018; more expensive now), get off at the sign. From Bishkek — a marshrutka to Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (2025).
kg-0054.needcar: Yes for convenience: it's 8–10 km from Bokonbaevo; you can take a marshrutka along the highway and walk ~1 km from the road. Within the valley — on foot only.
kg-0054.self: Yes: entry is free, the paths between the springs are readable, but without a guide it's easy to miss some of the springs (TripAdvisor); a dress code and respect for pilgrims are mandatory.
kg-0054.roadtype: Paved road along the A363 highway; the turn-off is a dirt/clay road to the springs (passable by an ordinary car in dry weather); then footpaths over clay (slippery after rain).
kg-0054.traveltime: Bokonbaevo — Manjyly-Ata 10 min; Kaji-Say — 15 min; Karakol — ~2 h; Bishkek — ~5 h. A round of the springs — ~2 h (Backpack Adventures, 2026), a short visit — 1 h.
kg-0054.stay: On site — the Manjyly-Ata yurt camp (6 yurts without beds; prices on request, 2020 data — jartour.ru; operation in 2025–2026 not confirmed). Base: Bokonbaevo — guesthouses Nurgul, Guljan, Gulmira, Ayim (Backpack Adventures 2026), Baiel, Akbermet, Amirhan, Ecoresort Kaiyrma (Journal of Nomads 2025); CBT and Bel-Tam yurt camps on the shore. Prices not published.
kg-0054.net: Along the highway between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say there is operator coverage (MegaCom 4G in Bokonbaevo since 2019 — Kaktus.media); in the hollows of the valley the signal may drop out — no direct tests were found.
kg-0054.entry: There is no entrance fee (no source from 2017–2026 mentions one); a donation to the caretaker/the mazar is customary — the amount is up to you. The caretaker's tour is by arrangement.
kg-0054.transfer: Taxi from Bokonbaevo — not published; marshrutka Karakol — Bokonbaevo ~100 som (TripAdvisor, 2018); Bishkek — Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (Journal of Nomads, 2025).
kg-0054.bring: Modest clothing (shoulders, knees covered; a headscarf is desirable for women), 1–1.5 L of water, a hat and sun protection, shoes with firm soles (clay, thorns), small cash for a donation, an empty bottle — pilgrims collect water from the springs.
kg-0054.warn: An active pilgrimage site: don't make noise, don't photograph people at prayer without permission, don't wash your feet/shoes in the springs, don't leave trash; the “healing” quality of the water is a local belief, not a medical fact, and drinking safety is not guaranteed (boil it). In summer the heat is shadeless; after rain the clay is slippery. The springs are drying up (2024) — in a dry year some may be empty.
kg-0054.food: There is no food on site. In Bokonbaevo — the Argymak cafe (Mambetov St. 16), home-cooked lunches at guesthouses, smoked fish along the highway; in the yurt camps — beshbarmak and kumys. Specific establishments have not been checked.
kg-0054.reviews: Google Maps “Manjyly-Ata”: 4.7/5, 55 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Manjyly-Ata Valley”: 4.0/5, 2 reviews (2015–2018). Pros: authenticity, quiet, scenery, free; cons: it's hard to find all the springs without a guide, infrequent transport, no shade.
kg-0054.p.sum: A shrine right by the southern highway between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say: a large sign on the road, then a turn south ~1 km along a dirt road to the mazar and the springs (Google marker 42.1478, 77.0858). Base: Bokonbaevo (10 minutes by taxi); without a car — any marshrutka along the south shore, asking to be dropped at the sign. Entry is free, a donation to the caretaker is customary; the full round of the springs takes ~2 h over dry, shadeless hills, so morning/evening, water and modest clothing are essential.

kg-0056.name: Lake Kol-Ukok
kg-0056.near: The village of Isakeev (start of the transfer/trail, CBT Kochkor, TUK); Kochkor is the organisation’s base, about 20 km of dirt road to the start of the trail (Beyond Wild Places).
kg-0056.elev: About 3,050 m at the lake (TUK, Kyrgyzstan-tourism); trail start ~2,600 m (TUK); the highest point of the hiking approach is 3,166 m (Beyond Wild Places).
kg-0056.short: A mountain lake at about 3,000 m in the Terskey Ala-Too range south of Kochkor: 4.5 hours on foot (14.5 km) or on horseback, summer yurt camps and a side trip to Lake Kol-Tor.
kg-0056.desc: Kol-Ukok (“chest lake”) is a high-mountain lake at about 3,050 m in the north-eastern part of the Terskey Ala-Too range south of Kochkor, up to 17 m deep (Kyrgyzstan-tourism). Sevan trout, brought from Armenia, live in the lake (Eurasia Travel). All around is the herders’ summer jailoo (summer pasture); in summer three small yurt camps operate on the shore (including Cholponai). Approach: a transfer from Kochkor to the village of Isakeev/the start of the trail (~2,600 m), then 14.5 km on foot with a climb of about 1,100 m (4.5 h) or on horseback through the Ters-Tor valley. A popular side trip from the lake goes to the higher Lake Kol-Tor (10–12 km round trip, up to ~3,400–3,489 m) — not to be confused with the Kol-Tor in the Kegety gorge. Multi-day horse routes over the Ukok Pass (3,871 m) into the Tuura-Suu valley also start from here.
kg-0056.guide: Leave Kochkor early: a taxi to the start of the trail costs about 600 som, then it is 4.5 hours up the valley — the 1,100 m gain is noticeable, but the trail is clear. Spend the night at the lake: at Cholponai camp a yurt with dinner and breakfast costs about 2,100 som. In the morning go light to Kol-Tor (5–6 h round trip) — it is the best view of the hike. There is no phone coverage at the lake, but you can get a signal on the road above the camps — warn your family in advance. If you do not want to walk, CBT Kochkor can arrange a horse from Isakeev.
kg-0056.see: The lake itself in its mountain bowl; yurts and herds on the jailoo; the Ters-Tor valley on the approach; as a side trip — Lake Kol-Tor (up to 3,489 m) with views of the range; panoramas of the Kochkor valley on the way down. For anglers — Sevan trout in the lake (Eurasia Travel); for a multi-day trip — the Ukok Pass (3,871 m) and the Tuura-Suu valley.
kg-0056.skip: You are not ready for a 4.5 h climb (+1,100 m) and do not want to ride — you cannot drive to the lake. You are already going to Song-Kol or Kol-Suu and are short of time. You tolerate altitude above 3,000 m badly.
kg-0056.diff: Moderate: 14.5 km one way, ~1,100 m gain, ~4.5 h (Beyond Wild Places); TUK rates its two-day route (24 km, ~450 m gain per day) as moderate. The side trip to Kol-Tor: 12 km, +520 m, 5.5 h.
kg-0056.when: June to August (TUK departures); Kyrgyzstan-tourism runs tours from May to August (hiking) and from June to September (horse). Plan the trip for dry weather: rain washes out the dirt road from Kochkor (Eurasia Travel). In winter and spring there is snow on the trail.
kg-0056.hours: An open natural area with no ticket office. The yurt camps operate only in summer (June to August/early September; check the exact dates of Cholponai camp on Google Maps/Instagram).
kg-0056.daytime: Start on the trail in the morning (7–9 h) to arrive by noon and avoid afternoon thunderstorms; evening and dawn at the lake have the best light; go to Kol-Tor in the morning.
kg-0056.how: Bishkek → Kochkor (200 km, ~3 h; marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek bus station). Kochkor → start of the trail at Isakeev: ~20 km of dirt road, about 1 h (4×4 or taxi). Then 14.5 km on foot (4.5 h) up through the Ters-Tor valley, or on horseback.
kg-0056.needcar: Yes, to the start of the trail: a taxi/car from Kochkor (~600 som per car, can be shared), a CBT Kochkor or TUK transfer. The approach to the lake itself is on foot or by horse; there is no road to the lake.
kg-0056.self: Yes: the trail is obvious, no permits or fees; you need an offline map/track, a tent or a yurt booking. A taxi to the trail can be found in Kochkor.
kg-0056.roadtype: Paved road Bishkek — Kochkor; from Kochkor ~20 km of dirt road to Isakeev/the start (4×4 preferable); then only a foot/horse mountain trail through Ters-Tor — not a road for cars. After rain the dirt road washes out and becomes hard to pass (Eurasia Travel).
kg-0056.traveltime: Bishkek — Kochkor ~3 h; Kochkor — trail start ~1 h; the climb to the lake 4.5 h (14.5 km); to Kol-Tor and back 5.5 h. The TUK programme: 2 days, 24 km in total.
kg-0056.stay: Three small yurt camps by the lake; Yurt Camp Cholponai — 2,100 som per person per night with dinner and breakfast (Beyond Wild Places; contact via Google Maps/Instagram). Tents — free camping by the lake (in the TUK programme tents, the yurt and dinner cost extra). In Kochkor — CBT Kochkor guesthouses. Kyrgyzstan-tourism uses a family yurt camp (up to 4 people per yurt, B&B).
kg-0056.net: No phone coverage at the lake; a signal can be caught on the road above the yurt camps (Beyond Wild Places). The operator is not stated; in Kochkor — Beeline/O!/MegaCom.
kg-0056.entry: Free: no source (TUK, CBT Kochkor, Beyond Wild Places) reports any entry fee or eco fee.
kg-0056.transfer: Taxi Kochkor — trail start ~600 som per car (Beyond Wild Places); Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka 350 som (May 2026); a 2-day TUK tour 5,000 som per person with transport. A ready-made 2-day tour from Bishkek by 4×4 with a yurt and guide — $150–390 per person depending on group size (Kyrgyzstan-tourism).
kg-0056.bring: Trekking footwear, a tent and a warm sleeping bag (nights at 3,000 m are cold), a rain jacket, sun protection, water and a snack for the 4.5 h climb, cash for the yurt, an offline map, a power bank, a water purifier.
kg-0056.warn: Altitude ~3,000–3,500 m (with Kol-Tor) — altitude sickness is possible; weather changes quickly, thunderstorms after noon. No phone coverage at the lake. Do not confuse the Kol-Tor above Kol-Ukok with Lake Kol-Tor in the Kegety gorge (Chuy region). Herders’ dogs near the camps.
kg-0056.food: Dinner and breakfast in the yurt camp (included in the 2,100 som at Cholponai): national dishes, tea, bread; in summer the herders have kumys. A local feature is the Sevan trout from the lake (Eurasia Travel); whether the camps serve it is not confirmed.
kg-0056.reviews: Google Maps (“Kelukek”): 4.9/5, 48 ratings (03.10.2026). Blogs (Beyond Wild Places): pros — an accessible overnight hike from Kochkor, a beautiful lake, a side trip to Kol-Tor; cons — a noticeable altitude gain, no phone coverage at the lake, simple yurts.
kg-0056.photos.0.cap: A yurt camp on the approach to Kol-Ukok; not a view of the lake itself
kg-0056.p.sum: Kol-Ukok (~3,050 m) is the easiest high-mountain hike from Kochkor: marshrutka No. 513 Bishkek — Kochkor (300–350 som), a taxi to the bridge at the edge of the village/start of the dirt road (≈600 som per car, saves ~7 km), then 14.5 km along a dirt road with a climb of ≈1,100 m (≈4.5 h) through the Ters-Tor valley. At the lake there are three small yurt camps (Cholponai — 2,100 som per person with dinner and breakfast, 2025) and free camping; on the second day — a side trip to Lake Kol-Tor (12 km, 5.5 h). No phone coverage at the lake; after rain the dirt road from Kochkor turns to mud.

kg-0057.name: Kegety Gorge
kg-0057.near: The village of Kegeti at the mouth of the gorge (approach via Rot-Front); higher up are the Kegeti dachas (~3.6 km as the crow flies from the catalog point, OSM). ~20 km to Tokmok (too.kg).
kg-0057.elev: From ~1250 m at the mouth to ~3200 m at the river's source (too.kg); Nomad's Land — 1500 m for the lower part. The Kegeti Pass — 3704 m per Pereval.Space (ungraded), 3805 m in other sources (mykg.club) and “about 4000 m” (too.kg).
kg-0057.short: Kegeti is one of the longest (~27 km) gorges of the Kyrgyz Range, ~70 km east of Bishkek: dense Tian Shan spruce forests, a 30 m waterfall, the way to Lake Kol-Tor and a jeep pass into the Kochkor valley.
kg-0057.desc: The Kegeti (Kegety) gorge lies on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too in Chuy district, between the Issyk-Ata and Shamsi gorges, 70 km east of Bishkek and 20 km from Tokmok. It is about 27 km long, with elevations from 1250 m to 3200 m at the source (too.kg). The densest Schrenk spruce forests in the Chuy Valley are here. In the lower part is the Kegeti waterfall, about 30 m high; in the right tributary is the turquoise Lake Kol-Tor (in summer 2026 the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) drained water from it with siphons because of the threat of overflow). In the upper reaches the road goes to the Kegeti Pass (3704 m per Pereval.Space) — a crossing to the East Karakol valley and Kochkor, popular with jeepers and cycle tourists. Tourist infrastructure is minimal: yurts and guesthouses by the first waterfall and in the Kol-Tor tract.
kg-0057.guide: Kegeti is a gorge for those who want spruce forests and open space without the crowds of Ala-Archa. For an easy day the Kegeti waterfall (30 m, 5 minutes from the road) is enough, and if you have the energy, turn onto the trail to Lake Kol-Tor: 14 km round trip and turquoise water surrounded by spruces. Keep away from the edge of the road above the river: in summer 2026 a car with children fell into the river here. For experienced jeepers there is the road over the Kegeti Pass (about 3700 m) into the Kochkor valley, but only in a prepared 4×4. Bring your own water — do not drink from the river because of livestock.
kg-0057.see: The Kegeti waterfall (~30 m) in the lower part of the gorge; Lake Kol-Tor in the right tributary; dense Schrenk spruce forests; the mountain Kegeti River; the road to the Kegeti Pass (3704 m) with views of the main range.
kg-0057.skip: You have an ordinary car and aren't ready for a bumpy dirt road — after ~10 km of asphalt the road gets worse. You have already been to the Kegeti waterfall and Kol-Tor (separate entries) — the gorge itself without a trek adds little. You are looking for services: there is almost no infrastructure.
kg-0057.diff: The waterfall — easy (≈200 m and 5 minutes from the road, hiking.kg). Lake Kol-Tor — moderate: ~14 km round trip, several hours (TripAdvisor). The Kegeti Pass — ungraded on foot (Pereval.Space), but by vehicle only a prepared 4×4 and an experienced driver (too.kg).
kg-0057.when: June — September for hikes to Kol-Tor and driving the upper road; the waterfall is accessible from spring to autumn. The trails are slippery in rain (TripAdvisor). The Kegeti Pass — only at the height of summer; in winter the upper part is covered with snow (based on the general mountain regime, not confirmed).
kg-0057.hours: The gorge is open 24 hours. At the entrance there is a checkpoint/barrier with an eco fee (2024). There is no fixed operating schedule; guesthouses and yurts operate mostly in summer.
kg-0057.daytime: Morning: the drive and the trail to Kol-Tor take the whole day, and the light on the lake is better before noon; leave Bishkek by 7–8 a.m. At the waterfall — midday, when the sun is in the gorge (editorial).
kg-0057.how: From Bishkek east via Krasnaya Rechka, Yuryevka, Syn-Tash and Rot-Front to the village of Kegeti, then up the gorge (85 km / 2 h 15 min to the waterfall — hiking.kg). Paved for ~10 km in the gorge, then dirt (too.kg). The turn to Kol-Tor and the parking area are a separate route.
kg-0057.needcar: Yes: a car, taxi or tour. Public transport does not go into the gorge itself (too.kg); the marshrutka (minibus) goes only to the village of Kegeti.
kg-0057.self: Yes, by car (preferably with high ground clearance): the waterfall is next to the road, and the trail to Kol-Tor is popular. Over the pass — only with experience and a prepared vehicle.
kg-0057.roadtype: Paved for ~10 km from the village into the gorge, then a rocky dirt road (“very bumpy at the end” — TripAdvisor); the upper section and the Kegeti Pass — only a prepared 4×4 (too.kg).
kg-0057.traveltime: Bishkek → Kegeti waterfall: 85 km, 2 h 15 min (hiking.kg); TripAdvisor — ~2 h. The hike to Kol-Tor — ~14 km round trip, 5–7 h.
kg-0057.stay: Yurts with meals opposite the first waterfall; a small hotel beyond the first barrier; a guesthouse in the Kol-Tor tract (too.kg); Kegety Tour guesthouse — 1500 som/person with three meals a day (asia-hikes, per group 6 data). A few tent spots between the first and second waterfalls.
kg-0057.net: There is a signal only in the lower part of the gorge up to the first waterfall, higher up it is unstable (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
kg-0057.entry: Eco fee of about 200 som per passenger car at the Kegeti checkpoint (hiking.kg, 2024). The current 2026 tariff is not confirmed.
kg-0057.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) to the village of Kegeti — 50 som (2024, not confirmed); tours $70–370 (TripAdvisor). The price of a taxi Bishkek — Kegeti was not found.
kg-0057.bring: A supply of drinking water (springs are few, and river water must not be drunk because of livestock — too.kg), trekking shoes (slippery after rain), a rain jacket, a snack, cash for the eco fee and yurts, an offline map (the signal disappears after the waterfall).
kg-0057.warn: A narrow road above the river: on 23.06.2026 a car's brakes failed and it fell into the river — two children died (Kaktus.media, Vesti.kg). Drive slowly, in a roadworthy car. Lake Kol-Tor was under threat of overflow in August 2026 — the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) installed 204 m siphons (Gazeta.kg 12.08.2026); watch for mudflow warnings. The upper road — 4×4 only. Do not drink river water.
kg-0057.food: Lunch in the yurts by the first waterfall (Kyrgyz cuisine, kumis in summer — per too.kg the yurts feed guests); at the Kol-Tor guesthouse — full board. Specific menus and prices are not confirmed.
kg-0057.reviews: TripAdvisor “Kegety Gorge”: 4.6/5, 10 reviews (07.10.2026); Google Maps — no unambiguous listing for the gorge (the Kegeti waterfall — 4.7/5, 682 ratings as of 03.10.2026, group 6). Pros: a picturesque gorge with spruce forests, fewer people, the waterfall and Kol-Tor. Cons: a bumpy road at the end, high clearance needed, few services.
kg-0057.p.sum: Kegety is 85 km and about 2 h 15 min east of Bishkek; drive via Rot-Front to the village of Kegeti. The first ~10 km in the gorge are paved, then a bumpy dirt road, so a car with high ground clearance, a taxi or a weekend group tour (from 690–900 som, 2025) is best. Marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the East Bus Station only goes to the village. The main goals are the waterfall, 5 minutes from the road, and the turquoise Lake Kol-Tor (2725 m): 7.5 km and +900 m one way, 4–7 h round trip. You can overnight at the Kegety Tour guesthouses (≈1500 som with meals) or Sun City (Ak-Sai). Drive carefully: in June 2026 a car fell into the river from the narrow road above it.

kg-0058.name: Mars Canyons
kg-0058.near: Kaji-Sai (urban-type settlement, Ton district) — the turn-off from the highway is about 2.5–3 km west of the village; the red hills themselves are 3 km from Kaji-Sai.
kg-0058.elev: About 1,700–1,800 m: the Issyk-Kul shore is 1,607 m, Kaji-Sai village 1,740 m; the “Mars” hills rise a few dozen metres above the road. There are no exact measurements of the canyon's elevation in the sources (calculated from the heights of nearby points).
kg-0058.short: Red clay-and-sandstone hills and gullies near Kaji-Sai on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul, nicknamed “Mars” for the colour of the rock.
kg-0058.desc: The Mars Canyons are a ridge of red eroded hills between the south-shore highway and the Terskey Ala-Too, 3 km from the village of Kaji-Sai. It is not a true rock canyon but dozens of rain-carved channels and ridges of red clay and sandstone; from the upper points there is a panorama of Issyk-Kul and snowy peaks. The place is almost undeveloped: no ticket offices, signs or trails, and noticeably fewer people than at Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon 20 km to the west. The rock crumbles, and after rain the clay becomes slippery.
kg-0058.guide: Turn off the highway about 2.8 km west of the Kaji-Sai river — the landmark is an “unfinished multi-storey building” on the right — and drive along the dirt road/dry riverbed to the spot where the channel narrows; continue on foot. Climb any ridge: from here you see the red “Martian” folds, the turquoise Issyk-Kul and the snowy Terskey all at once — this is the main shot of the place. Come for sunset (17–19 h): the red colour of the rock intensifies noticeably, while by day it fades and it is hot. In spring, spiny anabasis bushes with red-yellow flowers bloom among the clay. Don't look for trails — there aren't any: walk along the ridges rather than the narrow gullies, and remember that the clay turns into a skating rink after rain.
kg-0058.see: Red eroded ridges and gullies; a panorama of Issyk-Kul and the Terskey Ala-Too from the upper points; sunset light; desert flora (anabasis). A good spot for drone photography (locationscout.net lists the place as a drone spot — you need a flying licence).
kg-0058.skip: You've already been to Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon and want something fundamentally different — the same red clays are here, just without infrastructure and crowds. You're going in the rain — the clay is slippery, and the dry channels may fill with water. You have a low-clearance car and don't want to walk 2–3 km from the highway.
kg-0058.diff: Easy: a 1–2 h walk over hills without trails, with little elevation gain; you only need sturdy shoes. Be careful on the crumbling clay ridges.
kg-0058.when: June–September (sunny, little rain, around +25 °C). Spring and autumn are also fine, but after rain the clay is impassable. In winter access is limited by the condition of the dirt road.
kg-0058.hours: Open area, open 24 hours (Google Maps, viewed 03.10.2026: “Daily: 24 hours a day”). There are no ticket offices, barriers or guards.
kg-0058.daytime: The “golden hour” before sunset (17:00–19:00) — the red colour of the rock intensifies; also sunrise. Avoid midday: harsh light and heat.
kg-0058.how: The Balykchy — Karakol highway along the southern shore. From Bishkek ~270–290 km, 4–4.5 h via the Boom Gorge and Balykchy; from Karakol ~120 km (about 2 h). The turn-off from the highway is 2.5–3 km west of Kaji-Sai (there is a sign; according to a 2022 description, the landmark is an unfinished building on the right), then 1–3 km along a dirt road and a dry riverbed to the red hills; people leave their car where the channel narrows and continue on foot. On foot from the highway it is about 3 km.
kg-0058.needcar: Yes: from the highway to the hills it is 1–3 km of dirt road. You can get there by taxi/with a tour or walk from the marshrutka (minibus) stop in Kaji-Sai (~3 km).
kg-0058.self: Yes, completely: there is no ticket office, guide or permits; you need offline maps (Maps.me/2GIS/Organic), water and shoes. The only difficulty is finding the turn-off, which has no sign, and not getting lost among identical gullies.
kg-0058.roadtype: Paved road along the Balykchy — Karakol highway; from the turn-off a dirt road and dry riverbed (gravel, sand, clay). In dry weather a passenger car can make it with care (locationscout.net: “4x4 not needed”; nomadcar.kg recommends high ground clearance); after rain the clay is slippery and impassable.
kg-0058.traveltime: From Bishkek 4–4.5 h (270–290 km); from Karakol ~2 h; from Barskoon ~1 h; from Tosor ~45 min; from Bokonbaevo/Ton ~20 min. Sightseeing — 1–2 h.
kg-0058.stay: In Kaji-Sai: Salima Resort, Legenda Health Resort, Solema guest house, private guesthouses (prices are not given in the sources). Yurt camps on the shore: Bel-Tam Yurt Camp (Bokonbaevo, ~20 min), Yurt Camp Sonun, Yurt Camp Kyzyl Bulak (at the turn-off to the canyon, a Google Maps point). 2025–2026 prices are not confirmed — check when booking.
kg-0058.net: Mobile coverage and internet disappear in the canyons themselves (nomadcar.kg; a 2024 blog: “limited reception”). In Kaji-Sai and on the highway there is Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage. Download offline maps in advance.
kg-0058.entry: Free: there is no official entrance or ticket office (2024 blog: “no official entrance point… free to visit”). In 2022 iXBT mentioned rumours of a summer fee for driving in — not confirmed by any 2024–2026 source. For comparison: at neighbouring Skazka the eco fee is 50–100 som/person.
kg-0058.transfer: Taxi from Ton/Bokonbaevo round trip with waiting — 1,200 som (July 2024). Jeep tour from Cholpon-Ata through the south-shore canyons — €470 per group of up to 6 people (Tripster, 2025–2026). Bishkek — Kaji-Sai marshrutka: the 2025 price is not confirmed.
kg-0058.bring: Water (1.5 L/person — no shade), a hat and sun protection, shoes with a tread (clay and scree), offline maps, cash (there are few ATMs in Kaji-Sai), a camera/drone (licensed), a windbreaker for the evening.
kg-0058.warn: No trails or signs — it is easy to get lost among identical gullies, so return before dark. The clay is slippery after rain; dry channels can quickly fill with water in a downpour — don't drive or walk along the channel in the rain. The ridges crumble — don't go near the edges. Don't leave belongings visible in the car.
kg-0058.food: In Kaji-Sai and on the highway — cafés with lagman, manty and shashlik; on the southern shore the classic option is smoked and dried Issyk-Kul fish by the road and in Bokonbaevo. There are no eateries at the canyon itself — bring food with you.
kg-0058.reviews: Google Maps (“Canyon ‘Mars’”): 4.8/5, 29 ratings as of 03.10.2026. Blogs (2022–2024): pros — deserted, free, a spectacular sunset, a panorama of the lake; cons — no signs, hard to find the turn-off, dusty dirt road, impassable after rain. No separate TripAdvisor listing was found.
kg-0058.p.sum: The Mars Canyons are a free “wild” stop on the southern shore between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Sai: turn off the Balykchy — Karakol highway 2.5–3 km west of Kaji-Sai (a sign; the landmark is an unfinished building), then 1–3 km of dirt road to the spot where you leave the car. It is most convenient by your own car or by taxi from a yurt camp in Ton/Bokonbaevo (about 1,200 som round trip with waiting, 2024); without a car — any south-shore marshrutka to Kaji-Sai and 3 km on foot. Combine with Manjyly-Ata (0.5 km) and Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon (20 km), come for sunset, and spend the night in a yurt camp on the shore.

kg-0059.name: Dolon Pass
kg-0059.dist: On the border of Kochkor and Naryn districts of Naryn…
kg-0059.near: On the north side — Sary-Bulak (a highway junction with cafes and shops; 48 km from the A367/A365 junction to the pass per quaeldich.de), on the south side — the villages of the Ottuk valley. The town of Naryn is about 70 km to the southeast (open.kg). The earlier value “Ken-Suu ~6.5 km” was based on a catalog point offset by ~4.8 km from the pass.
kg-0059.elev: 3030–3038 m: 3038.4 m (silkadv.com, open.kg, Nomad's Land, 3038 m), 3028 m (quaeldich.de), 3030 m (previous catalog/Wikipedia). The recommended label is “about 3030–3038 m”.
kg-0059.short: Dolon is a paved pass (≈3030–3038 m) on the Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway between Kochkor and Naryn, the main road entrance into the Naryn basin.
kg-0059.desc: Dolon is the highest section of the Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway (roughly km 285–294 from Bishkek), linking the Kochkor valley with the Naryn basin. The saddle is a broad plateau trampled by livestock, with gentle slopes; to the north the water drains into the Sary-Bulak River (Chu basin), to the southeast into the Kichine-Kara-Kuzhur (Naryn basin); on the southern descent is the picturesque gorge of the Ottuk River with spruce forest on the north-facing slopes. The asphalt was renewed in 2024, and trucks run along the road to China and back. Since 1946 the Dolon snow and avalanche station has operated on the pass (modernized and reopened in 2023 with the support of UNDP and Japan), monitoring 17 avalanche-prone sections of the highway. The film “I Am Tian Shan” (1972), based on the work of Chingiz Aitmatov, was shot here.
kg-0059.guide: Dolon is not a destination but a gateway to Naryn: stop at the top for 10–15 minutes, where the road comes out onto the broad plateau, and look at the snowy ridges of the Tian Shan in every direction. Notice the buildings of the snow and avalanche station — it has stood here since 1946, and in 1972 “I Am Tian Shan” after Aitmatov was filmed here. The most beautiful part is the southern descent through the Ottuk gorge with its spruce forests, so don't doze in the marshrutka (minibus) on this stretch. It's better to have a snack in Sary-Bulak before the climb: there are no services on the pass itself. In winter and spring, check the Ministry of Transport reports before setting out — the pass is closed during controlled avalanche releases.
kg-0059.see: The panorama from the saddle (≈3030–3038 m) over the snow-covered ranges of the Tian Shan; the Dolon snow and avalanche station (since 1946); the Ottuk River gorge with spruce forests on the southern descent; the Kara-Unkur gorge next to the highway (open.kg); on the northern ascent, the last 3 km with a gradient of up to 8% (quaeldich.de).
kg-0059.skip: You aren't going to Naryn/At-Bashy/Torugart — there's no point traveling to the pass specially for the view. You want walks and trails: Dolon has no infrastructure or marked routes, it's just a point on the highway. In winter, with avalanche danger, it's better to wait for the road to open than to stand in a queue at the barrier.
kg-0059.diff: Easy for a drive: a paved highway renewed in 2024; the climb from the north is 48.2 km with 1196 m of ascent, the last 3 km up to 8% (quaeldich.de). For cyclists, a long but steady climb. Difficulty rises in winter and spring (black ice, avalanches, restrictions for trucks).
kg-0059.when: June to September — no snow and the best visibility. The highway is open year-round, but snow can fall as early as September (snow at km 285–294 — 24.kg, 10.09.2024) and even in early June (up to 35 cm on the Balykchy — Naryn — Torugart highway — economist.kg, 05.06.2026). The claim by trvlland.com that “the pass is passable only from June to October” is wrong — it is a year-round highway.
kg-0059.hours: An open highway, round the clock and year-round. Temporary closures during snowfall and controlled avalanche releases (for example 20.02.2023 — the road closed until 16:00, 24.kg) and restrictions for heavy trucks in winter (akchabar.kg). The current situation is published by the Ministry of Transport of the Kyrgyz Republic.
kg-0059.daytime: In the daytime, in the first half of the day — cleaner air and less cloud over the ranges; in winter drive through only in daylight and no later than midday, when avalanche activity and black ice increase (editorial).
kg-0059.how: Along the Bishkek — Balykchy — Kochkor — Naryn — Torugart highway (A365): about km 285–294 from Bishkek (24.kg), about 70 km from Naryn (open.kg). You can stop on the saddle in your own/rented car or a taxi; Bishkek — Naryn marshrutkas (minibuses) go over the pass without stopping.
kg-0059.needcar: Yes: the pass lies on the highway far from villages, and nobody walks here (except on horse treks — Nomad's Land: the Kol-Ukok — Song-Kol horse route crosses the pass).
kg-0059.self: Yes. No permits are needed and no fee is charged; your own car or a seat on a Bishkek — Naryn marshrutka is enough.
kg-0059.roadtype: Paved road (A365 highway, renewed in 2024 — quaeldich.de); a serpentine climb, gradient up to 8% on the northern slope; open.kg gives a maximum gradient of 14% on some sections.
kg-0059.traveltime: From Bishkek ~290 km — about 4.5–5 h by car; from Kochkor ~70 km (per quaeldich: 48 km from the A367/A365 junction) — about 1 h; from Naryn ~70 km — about 1–1.2 h (calculated from the distances of 24.kg/open.kg/quaeldich at an average speed of 60–70 km/h).
kg-0059.stay: There is no accommodation on the pass. The nearest bases are the guesthouses of Kochkor (CBT Kochkor, Shepherd's Life) and the town of Naryn (CBT Naryn); in Sary-Bulak there are roadside cafes. For specific prices see the Kochkor/Naryn entries; not applicable to the pass.
kg-0059.net: Not confirmed by operator coverage maps (unavailable). The highway is served by the snow and avalanche station with real-time data transmission (UNDP), but mobile coverage on the saddle may drop out — don't count on stable internet between Sary-Bulak and Ottuk.
kg-0059.entry: Free: an open public road, no fee for crossing the pass was found.
kg-0059.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn (passing over the pass) — 600 som, Bishkek — Kochkor — 350 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026). An individual transfer to the pass itself is not sold separately; agree the taxi price from Naryn/Kochkor on the spot (not confirmed).
kg-0059.bring: A warm jacket even in summer (≈3030 m, wind, snow possible in June and September), sunglasses and sunscreen; water and a snack from Sary-Bulak or Naryn. In winter — winter tires/chains, a full tank, a supply of warm clothes in case the pass is closed.
kg-0059.warn: In winter and spring the pass is temporarily closed for controlled avalanche releases (24.kg, 20.02.2023) and restrictions for heavy trucks are introduced; snow is possible from September to June (24.kg 10.09.2024; economist.kg 05.06.2026). At an elevation of ≈3030 m, mild altitude sickness is possible after a fast ascent from Bishkek. The highway is busy with trucks to/from China — don't stop on bends or in narrow spots.
kg-0059.food: There are no establishments on the pass itself. In Sary-Bulak at the foot there are roadside cafes and shops (quaeldich.de): the typical highway menu is lagman, shorpo, manty, beshbarmak (editorial). Specific places with ratings are not confirmed.
kg-0059.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 21 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, from the catalog check). On TripAdvisor there is a “Dolon Pass” listing (Kochkor, Naryn Province) — the number of reviews has not been checked. Typical pros: open space and mountain panoramas, good asphalt; cons: cold and wind, snow outside summer, trucks.
kg-0059.p.sum: Dolon (≈3030 m) is a paved pass on the Bishkek — Naryn — Torugart highway between Sary-Bulak and Naryn: people don't come here specially but stop on the way. It's most convenient in your own/rented car or with a driver (Bishkek — Naryn transfer from $51/person); Bishkek — Naryn marshrutkas (minibuses) (600 som) go over the pass without stopping. Eat and stock up in Sary-Bulak or Naryn; in winter check the Ministry of Transport reports: closures for avalanche releases are possible. An alternative for long trips is the Asman Airlines flight Bishkek — Naryn (2100 som, ≈40 min).

kg-0060.name: Arslanbob Walnut-Fruit Forests
kg-0060.near: Arslanbob (Arstanbap) is ~2–3 km in a straight line from the catalog point; the neighboring village is Gumkhana. The transport hub is Bazar-Korgon on the Bishkek–Osh highway; Jalal-Abad is ~50 km to the south (Trip to Kyrgyzstan).
kg-0060.elev: The village is at about 1,600 m (CBT Arstanbap); other sources give 1,400 m (Journal of Nomads) and 1,700 m (eurasia.travel). The forest covers slopes from roughly 1,500 to 2,000+ m; the waterfall area is at about 2,200 m (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com).
kg-0060.short: One of the largest wild walnut forests in the world, on the slopes of the Fergana and Babash-Ata ranges around the village of Arslanbob, with waterfalls and holy sites.
kg-0060.desc: The Arslanbob walnut-fruit forests are a relict walnut forest mixed with wild apple, pear, cherry plum, cherry, almond and pistachio; the forests hold more than 130 species of trees and shrubs (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The forest around Arslanbob itself is estimated at about 11,000 ha (Journal of Nomads, 2026); the figures of 608,000–700,000 ha found at Trip to Kyrgyzstan and eurasia.travel refer to all the walnut-fruit forests of southern Kyrgyzstan, not to a single valley. Some trees reach 30 m in height and, according to legend, an age of about 1,000 years; the annual nut harvest in the valley is over 1,500 tonnes (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). Legend links the forest with the campaign of Alexander the Great (329 BC), who supposedly took nuts from here to Greece. The valley has the Big (~80 m) and Small (25–35 m) waterfalls, the holy lake Kel-Mazar and Mount Babash-Ata.
kg-0060.guide: Arslanbob is not a single “forest attraction” but a whole valley: you stay in a guesthouse in the village and walk out into the walnut groves on foot. Start with the Small Waterfall (about 40 minutes on foot) and the panoramic hill above it, and on the second day walk to the Big Waterfall, 80 m high — about 7 km one way. Legend says this is where Alexander the Great took the nuts to Greece — hence the name “Greek” walnut. Come in late September or early October: it is harvest time in the forests, the whole village lives in the woods, and the leaves turn yellow. Bring cash — the ATM in the village is unreliable.
kg-0060.see: Ancient walnut trees around the village; the Small Waterfall (25–35 m, ~1.5 km from the center) with a souvenir market; the Big Waterfall (~80 m, ~7 km); the panoramic hill above the Small Waterfall; the holy lake Kel-Mazar and Mount Babash-Ata (multi-day hikes); natural caves; a walnut oil workshop (CBT tour, 100 som). Sources: Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Journal of Nomads (2026).
kg-0060.skip: You expect “wow” landscapes like Song-Kol — the forest itself is quiet and shady, and the hikes and waterfalls make the bigger impression. You have only one day: the road from Osh/Jalal-Abad takes half a day each way. You would feel uncomfortable in a conservative rural environment (covered clothing is needed).
kg-0060.diff: Easy — walks in the forest and to the Small Waterfall (40 min, 1.5 km); moderate — the Big Waterfall (7 km one way, ~2 h, 4–5 h round trip, the trail is rocky and slippery after rain); hard — a 3-day hike/horse tour to Lake Kel-Mazar with nights in a tent (Journal of Nomads 2026; TripAdvisor; Beyond Wild Places 2026).
kg-0060.when: May to October. For hiking — early May and early October; nut harvest — late September to October, autumn foliage — from late September (Journal of Nomads, Beyond Wild Places 2026). July–August: cooler than Osh, but the guesthouses fill up. In winter (December–January) — backcountry skiing, rental 600 som/day (Journal of Nomads).
kg-0060.hours: The forest is open year-round, 24 hours a day; it is a natural area next to the village with no checkpoint. A fee is charged in summer at the waterfalls (see “Entry cost”); in September, according to 2026 observations, the checkpoint at the Big Waterfall was not operating (Beyond Wild Places).
kg-0060.daytime: Morning is best for the Small Waterfall, before the crowds arrive (Beyond Wild Places, 2026), and for setting off to the Big Waterfall so you can be back by evening. In the daytime the forest is shady and cool.
kg-0060.how: From Osh: a direct marshrutka (minibus) to Arslanbob runs once a day at about 13:30–14:00 from the Osh bus station, 370 som, ~4 h (Beyond Wild Places, 2026). Via Jalal-Abad: Osh – Jalal-Abad (220 som, 2 h) → Bazar-Korgon (60 som, 1 h) → Arslanbob (100 som, ~1.5–2 h). Marshrutkas Bazar-Korgon – Arslanbob run every 30–60 min (eurasia.travel). From Bishkek: shared taxi to Bazar-Korgon (~800–1,200 som), then a marshrutka; 10–12 h in total, ~600 km.
kg-0060.needcar: To get there — yes (marshrutka/taxi to the village). In the village itself and in the forest you go on foot; to the Big Waterfall and the holy sites you can go on horseback through CBT.
kg-0060.self: Yes: the village and the short trails (Small Waterfall, panoramic hill, Big Waterfall along a well-trodden path) can be done without a guide. Deep in the forest the trails are confusing — for longer routes and Kel-Mazar you need a CBT guide (TripAdvisor; Journal of Nomads).
kg-0060.roadtype: To Bazar-Korgon — the paved Bishkek–Osh highway; from Bazar-Korgon to Arslanbob — a paved mountain road through a gorge (eurasia.travel; Beyond Wild Places writes that the transfer is slow). In the forest — dirt trails, rocky and slippery after rain.
kg-0060.traveltime: Osh – Arslanbob: ~4 h on the direct marshrutka, 4–5 h with transfers; Jalal-Abad – Arslanbob: ~2.5 h with a change at Bazar-Korgon; Bishkek – Arslanbob: 10–12 h (Beyond Wild Places 2026; Journal of Nomads; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com).
kg-0060.stay: Guesthouses and CBT homestays in Arslanbob and Gumkhana: about 600 som/person with breakfast, dinner +250 som (Journal of Nomads, updated 2026); private rooms $15–30, more organized ones $20–35 (kgnomad, 2026). Recommended: Guesthouse Ibrahim / CBT Guesthouse 6 (WhatsApp +996 777 733 056, available on Booking.com), Homestay Kelechek; the old Arslanbob tourist base. Through CBT Arstanbap. In July–August and on weekends the best rooms get taken — book in advance.
kg-0060.net: Contradictory: in 2026 Beeline 4G worked well (Beyond Wild Places, 08.2026); in an earlier version of the Journal of Nomads guide, mobile internet was available only on O!. Wi-Fi in guesthouses is unreliable. In the forest and at the Big Waterfall the signal may drop out (unconfirmed).
kg-0060.entry: The forest itself is free. In summer a fee is charged at the waterfalls: Small Waterfall — 10 som, Big Waterfall — about 50 som (Journal of Nomads, updated 04.2026; Beyond Wild Places, 2026 — 50 som, the checkpoint was not operating in September). A tour of the walnut oil workshop — 100 som.
kg-0060.transfer: Marshrutka Osh – Arslanbob 370 som (2026); Osh – Jalal-Abad 220 som, Jalal-Abad – Bazar-Korgon 60 som, Bazar-Korgon – Arslanbob 100 som (Beyond Wild Places, 2026); shared taxi Bishkek – Bazar-Korgon ~800–1,200 som/seat (various years). Private taxi from Jalal-Abad — price not confirmed.
kg-0060.bring: Cash (the ATM is unreliable), covered clothing (conservative village), comfortable trekking shoes (rocky and slippery trails), a rain jacket, water and a snack for the hike to the Big Waterfall; for Kel-Mazar — a tent and sleeping bag (or rent them through CBT).
kg-0060.warn: It is a conservative Muslim community — dress modestly. The ATM in the village is unreliable — bring cash. The trails to the Big Waterfall are rocky and slippery after rain; it is easy to get lost deep in the forest — take a guide for longer routes. The waterfall fees should be small (10–50 som) — check the amount in advance. No border permit is required.
kg-0060.food: Walnuts and walnut oil (tasting at the CBT oil workshop, 100 som with bread), local honey, flatbreads, seasonal fruit and home-cooked dinners at the guesthouse (plov, lagman — typical southern cuisine) (Journal of Nomads; kgnomad).
kg-0060.reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.3/5 from 26 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026), No. 1 of 3 attractions in Arslanbob. Pros: shade, quiet, beautiful hikes, waterfalls. Cons: some tourists expected more from the forest itself, complaints about pushy pricing by guides, the trails are easy to lose. Google Maps — rating not collected (the pin is not matched).
kg-0060.p.sum: Arslanbob is a base for 2–3 nights: you get there by marshrutka from Osh (direct one ~13:30–14:00) or via Jalal-Abad and Bazar-Korgon, stay in a CBT-network guesthouse and walk into the forest on foot. Day 1 — the Small Waterfall and Panoramic Hill, day 2 — the Big Waterfall (7 km one way); for the Holy Rock (16 km, 7 h) and the Holy Lake Kel-Mazar (3–4 days) take a guide/horses through CBT Arstanbap. Bring cash in advance: the only reliable ATM is in Bazar-Korgon.

kg-0060.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: arrive from Osh on the direct marshrutka (~18:00), dinner at a CBT house. Day 2: Big Waterfall (7 km, 4–5 h round trip), oil workshop. kg-0060.p.season: April–May: fresh greenery, hiking, mud is possible. June–August: warm (cooler than Osh), guesthouses are full, the trek to the Holy Lake is open June–September. kg-0060.p.budget.economy: ~3,000–4,000 som/person for 2 nights: marshrutka Osh – Arslanbob 370×2 som, guesthouse 600 som×2 + dinners 250×2, waterfall fees 60 som, oil workshop 100 som, snacks ~500 som.
kg-0060.p.budget.comfort: ~$150–300/person: taxi/driver from Osh (~$40–60 one way, estimate), the best guesthouse $25–35, guide $15–25/day, horse $20–40/day; eurasia.travel 3-day tour from $300.
kg-0060.p.permits: Not needed: there is no border zone. In summer there are token fees at the waterfalls (Small 10 som, Big 50 som); in September 2026 the checkpoint at the Big Waterfall was not operating.
kg-0060.p.access: With children — the Small Waterfall (40 min) and walks in the forest; the Big Waterfall — for teenagers with some experience. For older people — the village and short walks. With a stroller — only on the village streets. With a dog — allowed on the trails, but the village is conservative and has many guard dogs.

kg-0061.name: Lake Ala-Kul
kg-0061.near: Karakol — ~20 km as the crow flies to the north; the trek starts from the Karakol gorge (the entrance to the Karakol nature park, ~10 km from the town) or from Altyn-Arashan (the village of Ak-Suu/Teplokluchenka — the marshrutka (minibus) terminus). The OSM marker “Lesnoye” at 17 km is technical; the approach does not go through it.
kg-0061.elev: The lake 3532 m (advantour, eurasia.travel; 3500–3560 m in blogs); Ala-Kul Pass 3860 m (up to 3900–3990 m in some guides); Sirota camp ~2800 m; the mountaineering camp/entrance to the Karakol gorge ~2600 m.
kg-0061.short: Ala-Kul (“motley lake”) is a glacial lake at 3532 m in the Terskey Ala-Too, the goal of Kyrgyzstan's most popular trek from Karakol.
kg-0061.desc: Ala-Kul is a high-mountain glacial lake 2.3 km long, up to 700 m wide and more than 70 m deep, dammed by a moraine between the Karakol gorge and the Altyn-Arashan valley. The water is turquoise in clear weather and grey in rain, hence the name “motley lake”. It freezes in late autumn and opens in May. There is no road to the lake — only a 2–4 day walking route ~55 km long from the Karakol gorge via Sirota camp, Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) and the Altyn-Arashan hot springs; a day out-and-back from the mountaineering camp is possible with a 4×4 / SUV drop-off.
kg-0061.guide: The classic is a 3–4 day trek: from the Karakol gorge across a bridge to Sirota camp (2800 m), then a steep climb onto the moraine — and the lake opens suddenly, all at once, with a glacier at the far end. Overnight in yurts by the lake and get up before dawn: in the early morning the water is at its most turquoise, and by lunchtime clouds often roll in. Take Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) in the morning over the scree, trekking poles are a must; from the saddle you can see both the lake and the Altyn-Arashan valley, where you will descend to the hot baths. If you are short of days — order a UAZ to the mountaineering camp and visit the lake as a day out-and-back (about 7 km one way, 4 h up), as local groups do. Sirota has Wi-Fi, beyond that there is no signal — download the track in advance.
kg-0061.see: The turquoise lake with the Takyr-Tor glacier at its head; the panorama from Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) of the lake and Altyn-Arashan; Sirota camp in the spruce forest; a waterfall on the climb from Sirota; the Altyn-Arashan hot springs (2500 m) and a view of Palatka Peak; the Karakol gorge with Tian Shan spruces.
kg-0061.skip: You have less than 2 full days or no acclimatization — the pass at nearly 3900 m with a daily gain of 1000 m. You are not ready to overnight in a yurt/tent without a shower or mobile signal. You are going before mid-June or after the end of September — the yurt camps are packed up and there is snow on the pass.
kg-0061.diff: Moderate–high: 55 km over 3–4 days, a total ascent of ~2570 m, the hardest day is the climb to the pass (+1000 m, 6–10 h) over scree; altitude up to 3860–3900 m, risk of altitude sickness. A day out-and-back from the mountaineering camp is ~7 km and ~900 m of ascent one way (4 h). Good physical fitness and experience of overnights are required.
kg-0061.when: Late June — mid/late September; best July — early September. The yurt camps operate roughly from 1 July to 15–20 September. The lake is under ice from late autumn to May. The weather is “four seasons in a day”, snow on the pass is possible in any month.
kg-0061.hours: The Karakol nature park — entry through the eco-post in the Karakol gorge in the daytime (hours are not published); the lake is an open area, around the clock. Yurt camps: seasonal, ~1 July — 20 September.
kg-0061.daytime: Dawn and morning at the lake — the purest turquoise and calm, cross the pass in the morning before daytime cloud and thunderstorms; in the evening it is cold and windy at the lake.
kg-0061.how: From Karakol: marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 or a taxi to the entrance of the Karakol nature park (the eco-post in the Karakol gorge), then on foot ~16 km to the Sirota bridge and another ~8–12 km to the lake; or a drop-off by UAZ/GAZ-66 to the mountaineering camp (Ayu-Tor) and an out-and-back. The return is over the pass to Altyn-Arashan and 16 km down to Ak-Suu (marshrutka (minibus) No. 350/501 to Karakol) or by 4×4 / SUV from Altyn-Arashan. From Bishkek to Karakol is ~400 km, marshrutkas (minibuses) from the new bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1).
kg-0061.needcar: Only to the start: a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to the eco-post or a 4×4 / SUV to the mountaineering camp. To the lake and over the pass — only on foot or partly on horseback.
kg-0061.self: Yes — the trail is well trodden and marked, no permits needed (only the park entry fee); many go on their own with a tent or from yurt to yurt. You need a map/GPS track, food for 3–4 days (the camps have food, but it is expensive), and insurance for altitude up to 4000 m.
kg-0061.roadtype: Paved to Karakol; a dirt road in the Karakol gorge to the eco-post and mountaineering camp (passable for a UAZ/4×4 / SUV, in places for passenger cars in dry weather); beyond that only a mountain trail: forest, moraine, scree on the pass. There is no road access to the lake.
kg-0061.traveltime: The classic 4-day trek: day 1 — 12–16 km, 4–5 h to Sirota; day 2 — 8–12 km, 6 h to the lake (+1000 m); day 3 — 10–16 km, 6 h over the pass to Altyn-Arashan; day 4 — 16–18 km, 4–5 h to Ak-Suu. The 3-day option: 18/18/18 km, the second day 9–10 h. The out-and-back from the mountaineering camp: ~7 km, 4 h up, the same down (a group, June 2025). A UAZ drop-off from Karakol to the mountaineering camp ~2 h one way.
kg-0061.stay: Sirota camp (yurts, ~2800 m): 2000 som/person without meals (negotiable), 4200 som with meals (2025); Keldike camp: 2000 som/person without meals (2025); the yurt camp at Lake Ala-Kul: ~$50/person with dinner and breakfast (2025 season); Altyn-Arashan guesthouses: 500–2000 som/person per bed, dinner+breakfast ~450 som, on average ~$45/night with meals (2025); “Elza” in Altyn-Arashan — 4000 som/night with lunch and dinner (2022). Tent: a spot by the lake/Sirota, tent fee ~100 som. In Karakol — dozens of guesthouses and hostels.
kg-0061.net: There is no mobile signal in the Karakol gorge and at the lake (2025 reports); Wi-Fi only at the Sirota hut (paid/by arrangement). In Altyn-Arashan the signal is patchy. Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage ends at the edge of Karakol.
kg-0061.entry: The Karakol nature park entry fee — the data differ: 100 som/person for CIS citizens (mustvisit.ru, September 2025) and 250–300 som/person at the bridge to Sirota (guides for foreigners, 2024–2025); 500 som per car at the eco-post (June 2025 report); a tent permit ~100 som. Since November 2025 the eco-post tariff is 200 som per passenger car and 800 som per bus/truck (Sputnik, 02.11.2025). Check the 2026 pedestrian tariff on site.
kg-0061.transfer: UAZ Karakol → mountaineering camp and back: 10,000 som for 6 people (June 2025). Taxi Karakol → eco-post 345 som (2025). Marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 — 10–50 som; No. 350 Ak-Suu → Karakol — 40–50 som (2024–2025). An organized trek with a guide, meals and a transfer: €330–530/person for 3–4 days (2026).
kg-0061.bring: A sleeping bag rated to −5 °C (the yurts provide blankets, but it is cold), wind and waterproof gear, a warm layer, trekking poles (a must on the pass), ankle-support boots, a water filter (streams are near grazing), sun protection and sunglasses, cash (only cash in the camps, 8–10 thousand som recommended), a first-aid kit with altitude sickness remedies, a power bank, an offline GPS track.
kg-0061.warn: Altitude up to 3860–3990 m — acclimatize in Karakol/Sirota, descend if a headache is getting worse. The pass is steep scree, with rockfall from people climbing above; poles and a helmet for caution are a must. The weather changes within an hour: snow and thunderstorms in summer. Shepherd dogs at the yurts. Entry fees are collected in cash — the amounts vary, ask for a receipt. The camps close after 15–20 September — out of season only a tent.
kg-0061.food: In the yurts at Sirota and by the lake — dinner of soup/plov/lagman, flatbreads, tea with jam (tea in a yurt ~100 som/person, 2025); in Altyn-Arashan — home cooking at guesthouses, kumis in summer. In Karakol — ashlyan-fu (Dungan cold noodles) at the market, Dungan cuisine, lagman.
kg-0061.reviews: Google Maps (“Ala-Kul”): 4.9/5, 84 ratings as of 03.10.2026. Blogs and forums 2024–2026: pros — one of the most beautiful lakes in the Tian Shan, a good trail, yurts and hot springs at the end; cons — a hard pass and scree, cold and wind at the lake, unpredictable weather, inconsistent entry fees, expensive food in the camps.
kg-0061.p.sum: Only a trail leads to the lake. The classic is a loop of ≈55 km over 3–4 days: the Karakol gorge (marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 or a taxi/UAZ to the bridge) → Sirota camp → the lake → Ala-Kul Pass (3860–3900 m) → the Altyn-Arashan hot springs → Ak-Suu (marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 to Karakol). It is better to go in this direction: the climb to the lake is gentler, and from the pass there is a steep descent over scree. The season is from 1 July to ~20 September, when the yurts operate (Sirota 2500–4500 som with dinner and breakfast, 2025–2026). Without a tent you can go from yurt to yurt; gear can be rented in Karakol.

kg-0061.p.iti.1.title: The classic 3–4 days
kg-0061.p.iti.1.plan: D1: marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 → Karakol valley → Sirota. D2: climb to the lake, a night in a yurt by the lake. D3: the pass in the morning → Altyn-Arashan, bathhouses. D4: on foot/by UAZ to Ak-Suu → marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 to Karakol.
kg-0061.p.iti.2.title: Combinations
kg-0061.p.iti.2.plan: Karakol gorge + Ala-Kul + Altyn-Arashan — one loop; extensions: Altyn-Arashan → Anaarkhar → Jyrgalan or Kok-Zhaiyk → Teleti Pass → the Karakol valley (Jeti-Oguz).
kg-0061.p.season: May–June: the yurts are closed, snow on the trail and the pass, the lake may be under ice until the end of May. 1 July — 20 September: the main season, July–August — the peak (queues at the yurts, book ahead). Late September — October: the camps are packed up, only self-sufficient with a tent, below zero at night. November–April: the lake is under ice, avalanche danger — don't go without winter hiking experience.
kg-0061.p.budget.economy: ≈12,000–16,000 som/person for 3–4 days: marshrutkas (minibuses) No. 101 and No. 350 (≈70 som), park entry 100–300, gear rental ≈2,500 for 4 days (a tent for two — split), your own food ≈2,000, a night at Sirota without food 2,000 or a tent, Elza with breakfast 1,600 + dinner 500, a bathhouse 200.
kg-0061.p.budget.comfort: ≈30,000–45,000 som/person: an organized trek €330–530 (Journal of Nomads) or $310–510 (Nomad's Land) with a guide, meals, transfers and pack horses; or independently with yurts (Sirota 4,500, the lake ≈$50, Altyn-Arashan) + a UAZ to the mountaineering camp and a jeep from Altyn-Arashan (8,000 per vehicle).
kg-0061.p.permits: No border permit needed. Entry to the Karakol nature park is paid: at the eco-post/bridge — 250–300 som/person for foreigners, ≈100 som for CIS (2024–2025), a car — 200 som (since 11.2025); a tent ≈100 som. A descent via Altyn-Arashan — the Karakol forestry fee 20/100/220 som per person (Kyrgyz/CIS/foreigners). Pay in cash, ask for a receipt.
kg-0061.p.access: Children under 12–14 and older people — only with serious preparation (altitude 3900 m, scree). With a stroller — no. With a dog — physically possible, but there are shepherd dogs at the yurts and dogs are unwelcome in the park. An easy alternative for families — a walk in the lower part of the Karakol valley or a UAZ ride to Altyn-Arashan.
