kg-0062.name: Jeti-Oguz Gorge
kg-0062.near: Jeti-Oguz village (at the mouth of the gorge, ~16 km from Karakol); the Jeti-Oguz resort settlement is another 12 km up the gorge.
kg-0062.elev: The “Seven Bulls” rock massif ~2140 m; sanatorium 2000–2200 m; upper Kok-Jaiyk valley ~2300–2500 m (central-asia.guide: 2050 m — contradicts other data); “Maiden's Braids/Tears” waterfall ~2500 m; mouth of the gorge at the lake 1603 m.
kg-0062.short: Jeti-Oguz is a gorge with the red “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks, an old radon spa and the alpine Kok-Jaiyk valley, 25–30 km from Karakol.
kg-0062.desc: Jeti-Oguz (“seven bulls”) is a gorge about 30 km long in Terskey Ala-Too, southwest of Karakol. The main sight is a row of bright red sandstone cliffs, the “Seven Bulls”, and a separate rock, the “Broken Heart”, at the entrance to the narrows; according to legend, they are petrified bulls sacrificed by a khan at a feast where a kidnapped beauty died. Above the rocks is the Soviet-era Jeti-Oguz sanatorium (founded 1932, radon baths), and beyond it the Kok-Jaiyk valley with yurts and a trail to the 20 m “Maiden's Braids” waterfall. Tian Shan spruce grows on the slopes. The gorge is a popular day trip from Karakol and the starting point of treks to Ala-Kul over Teleti Pass.
kg-0062.guide: The first thing you meet is the “Broken Heart” — a red rock with a crack at the entrance to the narrows; stop, but the main view is further on: climb the hill opposite the sanatorium, from where the whole row of the “Seven Bulls” is visible against the spruces — in the morning the sun hits the rocks and the red is at its deepest. Further on the road leads to Kok-Jaiyk, an alpine meadow with yurts where shepherds offer horses; poppies bloom here in May. From the meadow it is 1–1.5 km on foot (20–25 min) to the “Maiden's Braids” waterfall along a forest path with handrails. Since summer 2026 locals have restricted car access to Kok-Jaiyk — count on an extra 3 km on foot from the sanatorium or a paid local shuttle. In the sanatorium you can take a radon bath for 100–200 som — a rare chance in the mountains.
kg-0062.see: The “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks; the viewpoint hill opposite the sanatorium (20–30 min climb); the Jeti-Oguz sanatorium with radon baths; the Kok-Jaiyk valley (Valley of Flowers) with yurts; the “Maiden's Braids” waterfall (~20 m); Tian Shan spruces; a view of Boris Yeltsin Peak (5168 m) from the upper reaches.
kg-0062.skip: You only want the “photo rocks” and are short on time — then a 30-minute stop at the Seven Bulls on the way is enough, without the climb to Kok-Jaiyk. You are going in the rainy season (spring/autumn) — the trail to the waterfall gets washed out. You have already seen Skazka Canyon and don't like the yurt “tourist circus” in season.
kg-0062.diff: Easy for a roadside stop at the rocks and the walk to the waterfall (1.5 km, 20–30 min on a trail with a little climbing); moderate for the climb to the viewpoint hill and for treks from Kok-Jaiyk (Teleti Pass ~3800 m is hard).
kg-0062.when: June–September: yurts are open and the trail to the waterfall is dry; May — poppies bloom at Kok-Jaiyk, but the waterfall may be frozen; September — fewer people and golden autumn. The sanatorium is open year-round; in winter there is the Ecotrek winter yurt camp and ski outings, and the waterfall is not accessible.
kg-0062.hours: The gorge and the rocks are open territory, 24 hours. The sanatorium is open year-round. The yurts, cafes and souvenir stalls at Kok-Jaiyk are summer only. The last marshrutka (minibus) to Karakol leaves around 17:00.
kg-0062.daytime: Morning: the sun lights the red rocks from the east, and by lunchtime the contrast fades; at Kok-Jaiyk there are many groups during the day — leave Karakol by 8–9 am. Sunset is beautiful on the way back, with a view of the lake.
kg-0062.how: From Karakol, 16 km west along the highway to Jeti-Oguz village, then turn south and go 12 km up the gorge to the resort (25–30 km in total, 40–60 min). The “Broken Heart” and “Seven Bulls” rocks are by the road before the sanatorium; further on, a dirt road leads to Kok-Jaiyk (3–5 km), then on foot to the waterfall. Public transport: marshrutkas No. 371/366 from Karakol (the Aldasheva/Torgoeva crossroads by the Ak-Tilek bazaar) to the resort. From Bishkek ~400 km.
kg-0062.needcar: Yes as far as the resort (marshrutka/taxi/car); in the gorge, on foot or by horse. Since summer 2026 private cars are restricted from driving to Kok-Jaiyk — the last 3 km are on foot or by the local paid shuttle.
kg-0062.self: Yes: a marshrutka or taxi to the resort, then everything on foot along obvious trails; no permits are needed, and sources from 2022–2026 mention no entrance fee for the gorge. For a night in a yurt it is better to book ahead in season.
kg-0062.roadtype: Paved from Karakol to the sanatorium (including 12 km in the gorge); above the sanatorium a dirt road leads to Kok-Jaiyk — passable by a regular car in dry weather (2025), but from 2026 cars are restricted from entering the jailoo (summer pasture); to the waterfall there is a forest path with handrails, which gets washed out in the rains. TripAdvisor: “the road to the Seven Bulls is not very good”.
kg-0062.traveltime: Karakol → resort 40–60 min (25–30 km); resort → Kok-Jaiyk 10–15 min by car or ~1 h on foot; meadow → waterfall 20–25 min on foot; viewpoint hill — up to 30 min; the “Broken Heart” — a 20 min walk. Allow half a day to a day for the whole gorge.
kg-0062.stay: Jeti-Oguz sanatorium (radon spa, year-round; ~740 som/person in a double in 2017, ~1500 ₽/night in 2022); yurt camps at Kok-Jaiyk — booking via nomads-yurt.com (price did not load), Ecotrek Yurt Camp (Destination Karakol, also in winter); guesthouses in Jeti-Oguz village — Emir's Guesthouse ~1230 som/room, Kok Jaiyk Guesthouse 650–800 som, yurt 400 som/person (2017). Current 2025–2026 prices are not published — check.
kg-0062.net: Almost everywhere in the gorge up to the sanatorium and at Kok-Jaiyk there is good mobile signal and 4G (dorogi-ne-dorogi.ru, updated 06.2025); higher up, at the waterfall and on the passes, the signal disappears.
kg-0062.entry: No source from 2022–2026 mentions an entrance fee for the gorge (2022 travel stories: “we paid nothing to enter”). A radon bath in the sanatorium is 100 som/15 min (2017) / 200 som (2023). A fee for driving to Kok-Jaiyk (barrier) is possible from 2026 — the amount has not been published.
kg-0062.transfer: Marshrutka ~100 som (2017, current price not confirmed); shared taxi 150–350 som/person (2017); guided excursion from Karakol/Cholpon-Ata ~€240–243 per group of up to 4 (2025–2026).
kg-0062.bring: Footwear for the waterfall trail (wet, roots), a rain jacket, a windproof layer (2200–2500 m), cash for yurts, cafes and baths, a swimsuit and towel for the radon baths, water and a snack (food at Kok-Jaiyk is only available in summer).
kg-0062.warn:
Since 21.07.2025 there has been an eco-checkpoint at the entrance to Kok-Jaiyk: private cars are not allowed onto the pasture (24.kg). Go up on foot, on horseback or by permitted transport.

Since summer 2026 locals have restricted car access to Kok-Jaiyk — the last 3 km from the sanatorium are on foot or by paid shuttle; check on the spot. The trail to the waterfall is slippery after rain and gets washed out in spring/autumn. In season there are many groups and horses; dogs near the yurts. The information on guesthouses is inconsistent: Too.kg wrote that there is no accommodation in the gorge, while local organizations publish options — book ahead.
kg-0062.food: At Kok-Jaiyk in summer, in the yurts: kumys, boorsoks, lagman, shashlik; in the sanatorium — a canteen; in Jeti-Oguz village — shops and simple cafes (lunch ~130 som in 2017). Bring ashlyan-fu, the Dungan cold noodle dish, from Karakol.
kg-0062.reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 317 ratings, 75 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Jeti-Oguz Canyon (Seven Bulls Rocks)”: 4.5/5, 146 reviews, No. 3 of 96 attractions in the region (07.10.2026). Pluses: red rocks against spruces and the river, a beautiful valley, yurts; minuses: a bad road near the rocks, part of the infrastructure is abandoned, and it takes time to reach the waterfall.
kg-0062.p.sum: The easiest day trip from Karakol (25–30 km, 40–60 min): paved road to the sanatorium, with the “Broken Heart” and “Seven Bulls” rocks right by the road. Without a car — marshrutka No. 371/355 from the southwest corner of the Karakol bazaar (the Torgoeva/Aldasheva crossing, departing ≈10:00 and around noon) or a taxi via a guesthouse (≈700 som, waiting 100 som/h). Above the sanatorium it is 6–8 km of dirt road and five small bridges to the Kok-Jaiyk yurts (since 07.2025 there is an eco-checkpoint at the entrance and private cars are not allowed onto the jailoo — you leave the car in the parking area and walk to the yurts), and from there 2.5 km to the waterfall. It is worth spending the night in a yurt at Kok-Jaiyk (from $13) or in the sanatorium itself (≈$10/night, radon baths).

kg-0063.name: Kyrgyz-Ata National Park
kg-0063.near: Kalday — a village/gorge at the park entrance, about 2.5 km from the catalog point (OSM); recommended as the entry point and a place to find a local guide (central-asia.guide). The base town is Nookat (bus station, ~25–30 km to the north); the road heads toward Eski-Nookat (Nomad's Land).
kg-0063.elev: About 2000–2400 m in the main (tourist) part (Central Asia Travel; Nomad's Land — 2400 m). The heights of the peaks on the northern slope of the Alay Range within the park boundaries are not confirmed.
kg-0063.short: Kyrgyz-Ata is a nature park (since 1992, 11,172 ha) on the northern slope of the Alay Range in Nookat district: juniper forests, the marble canyons of Karagoy, Kalday and Mazar, mineral springs and petroglyphs.
kg-0063.desc: The Kyrgyz-Ata State Nature Park was established on 18 March 1992 to preserve and restore juniper forests, mountain tulips and saffron; its area is 11,172 ha (Nomad's Land, Central Asia Travel). The park occupies a river basin on the northern slope of the Alay Range (Pamir-Alay) at an elevation of about 2000–2400 m: limestone and marble cliffs with coloured veins, the deep gorges of Karagoy (the most popular), Kalday and Mazar, the mineral springs of Tuya-Muyun and Eski-Nookat, ancient settlements, burial grounds and petroglyphs (too.kg, Central Asia Travel). Dirt roads lead to most of the gorges; there is almost no mobile signal or formal infrastructure, and there are many places to camp (too.kg). In July 2026 an automated checkpoint with cashless payment was installed at the entrance, and from August 2026 a new entrance arch, checkpoint and wastewater treatment facilities are being built (time.kg, economist.kg, Kaktus).
kg-0063.guide: Kyrgyz-Ata is the nearest real mountain forest to Osh: ancient juniper, marble cliffs with coloured veins and clear streams. Start with the Karagoy gorge — it is the most popular, with picnic and camping spots — and then look into Kalday and Mazar. The park is quiet and sparsely visited, the trails are almost unmarked, so a local guide from Kalday will make the walk much easier. There is almost no mobile signal anywhere, except, according to reviews, Beeline — warn your family in advance. The park is also good as an acclimatization stop before the Pamirs: 2000–2400 m is exactly what you need for a first night in the mountains.
kg-0063.see: The gorges of Karagoy (the main walking area), Kalday and Mazar; juniper forests; marble cliffs with coloured veins; the mineral springs of Tuya-Muyun and Eski-Nookat; petroglyphs (rock drawings of animals in the Aravan canyon), ancient settlements and burial grounds; in spring — mountain tulips and saffron (too.kg, Central Asia Travel, dwc.kg).
kg-0063.skip: You expect a developed park with marked trails, cafes and mobile signal — there is almost none of that here. You have no car and no time for a day trip from Osh. You are already heading to Sary-Chelek or Arslanbob and want forests specifically — the infrastructure there is better.
kg-0063.diff: Easy-moderate: day walks and horse rides through the gorges, the trails are unmarked and sometimes confusing (TripAdvisor). The altitude of 2000–2400 m is suitable for acclimatization (dwc.kg, Central Asia Travel).
kg-0063.when: May — September: tulips and saffron bloom in spring, in summer it is cool in the juniper forest at 2000+ m; TripAdvisor reviews — May — August. In winter the dirt roads may be impassable (editorial).
kg-0063.hours: The checkpoint's official opening hours are not published. Since July 2026 an automated checkpoint with cashless payment has operated at the entrance (time.kg, 28.07.2026); since 14.08.2026 a new entrance complex is under construction — check the access route and whether the checkpoint is working before you go (ilovekg).
kg-0063.daytime: Leave Osh in the morning: the drive is ~2 h, a walk through the gorges takes more than 3 hours (TripAdvisor), and towards evening it gets dark quickly in the gorges (editorial).
kg-0063.how: Osh → Nookat (highway west, ~45 km) → south on the road toward Eski-Nookat and Kalday → dirt roads to the Karagoy/Kalday/Mazar gorges. About 2 h by car from Osh (Central Asia Travel). The often-quoted “40 km from Osh” is an understatement: it is ~54 km to the park as the crow flies, and roughly 70–80 km by road (calculation, not confirmed by a navigator). There are few signs to the park (TripAdvisor).
kg-0063.needcar: Yes: there is no public transport all the way to the park; take a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Nookat, then a taxi to Kalday/the gorges. Your own car or a tour is more convenient.
kg-0063.self: Yes, by your own car or by taxi from Nookat; no border permit needed (the park is not on the border-zone list — tour.too.kg). The trails are unmarked and locals know little about the park — bring an offline map and ask for directions in Kalday (central-asia.guide, TripAdvisor).
kg-0063.roadtype: Paved road Osh — Nookat, then rural roads and “good quality” dirt roads to most of the gorges (too.kg); the condition of the different approaches varies.
kg-0063.traveltime: About 2 h by car from Osh (Central Asia Travel). By public transport — Osh → Nookat + taxi, roughly 2.5–3 h (editorial).
kg-0063.stay: Camping — many spots in the gorges (too.kg); Kyrgyz-Ata Yurt Camp — a yurt camp (TripAdvisor 5/5, 1 review from 2019; prices not published); guesthouses/yurts in the gorges — by arrangement (Central Asia Travel mentions this indirectly). No current 2025–2026 prices found.
kg-0063.net: There is no mobile signal over most of the territory (too.kg); according to reviews, Beeline is the only operator that gets a signal in Kyrgyz-Ata (bestofosh).
kg-0063.entry: An entry fee is charged (Nomad's Land); since July 2026 it is paid through the automated checkpoint by card, QR code or e-wallet (time.kg, 28.07.2026). The tariff amount was not found in open sources for 2024–2026 — check at the checkpoint/with the park administration.
kg-0063.transfer: Not confirmed: prices for a taxi Nookat — Kalday and for CBT tours are not published in the sources found.
kg-0063.bring: Cash and a bank card/QR app to pay the entry fee; food and water (there are few shops near the stops — TripAdvisor); a bag for rubbish (there are no bins on the trails); offline maps; a warm sweater for the evening; tick repellent (editorial).
kg-0063.warn: There are almost no signs or trail markings — it is easy to get lost (TripAdvisor). No mobile signal (except Beeline in places). The entrance is being rebuilt (2026) — the access route may change. The “Kyrgyz-Ata” point in Google Maps leads to the administration office near Nookat, not into the park. Protected area: campfires, cutting juniper and picking plants (tulips, saffron) are restricted by the park regime (editorial, based on protected-area status).
kg-0063.food: Not confirmed: no cafe in the park was found. In Nookat and along the road — southern Kyrgyz cuisine (plov, samsa — editorial, specific places not checked); bring a picnic.
kg-0063.reviews: TripAdvisor “Kyrgyz Ata National Park”: 4.5/5, 8 reviews (2017–2019). Pros: mountain views, forests, clean streams, few tourists, good with a local guide. Cons: no signs or trail markings, no rubbish bins, few shops, language barrier. Google Maps: the administration listing found has no rating (03.10.2026).
kg-0063.p.sum: Kyrgyz-Ata is a day trip from Osh (~2 h by car via Nookat) to the juniper gorges of Karagoy, Kalday and Mazar. It is most convenient by your own/rental car or with a guide (for example, the Kochmon Spirit tour with a climb to the holy mountain); public transport goes only as far as Nookat, then a taxi. Entry is 250 som per person, and since July 2026 payment is at the automated checkpoint by card/QR. There is almost no mobile signal; bring food and water from Osh; overnight in a tent in the gorges or return to Osh.

kg-0064.name: Juuku Gorge
kg-0064.near: Saruu (a village on the Balykchy — Karakol highway, 42–45 km west of Karakol) — the turnoff into the gorge; the gorge entrance is about 10–12 km south of the highway.
kg-0064.elev: The gorge entrance at the red cliffs is ~1900–2100 m (estimate: Saruu on the shore is ~1650 m, plus a climb of 10–12 km up the valley); the middle part of the valley by the hot springs is ~2600 m (jetioguz.travel); the upper reaches — the Arabel plateau above 3700 m, the Juuku Pass 3700 m (Nomad's Land). The sources give no exact elevation for the catalogue point.
kg-0064.short: Juuku is the longest gorge of the Terskey Ala-Too (the river is 55 km) on the south shore of Issyk-Kul: red cliff “gates” at the bottom, spruce forests and lakes higher up, with access to the Arabel plateau and the historic route to Kashgar.
kg-0064.desc: Juuku Gorge begins at the village of Saruu and stretches more than 50 km into the Terskey Ala-Too, up to the Juuku Pass (3700 m) and the Arabel plateau. The lower part is known for red sandstone cliffs forming “gates”, the middle for dense spruce forests and the side gorge of Juukuchak with hot springs (the Jiluu-Suu resort), the upper for high-mountain lakes (Kashka-Suu, Chokaly-Kol and others) and glaciers. The valley has petroglyphs, Saka burial mounds of the 7th–1st centuries BC and stone statues; a caravan route to China ran over the Juuku Pass, used by Xuanzang and Semenov-Tian-Shansky. There is almost no infrastructure: no shops, cafes or guesthouses, no mobile signal, but plenty of spots for tents. The road is tolerable in the lower part and deteriorates quickly higher up — you need an SUV.
kg-0064.guide: Turn off the highway at Saruu and after 7 km keep right at the fork — toward Juukuchak, where, 15 km from the village, the concrete tubs of the Jiluu-Suu hot-spring resort stand; this is one of the least crowded thermal springs in the country. But the main thing is the red cliff “gates” in the lower part of Juuku: drive through them slowly, preferably in the morning when the sun colours the sandstone. Higher up come spruce trees, fords and potholes — don't go without 4WD, and after rain and during snowmelt the road turns to mud. Look for petroglyphs on the rocks and stone statues by the burial mounds — this is the ancient caravan route to Kashgar. Bring everything with you: there are no cafes or shops in the gorge, and no signal either; boil river water — livestock graze higher up.
kg-0064.see: The red cliff “gates” in the lower part; spruce forests; the Juukuchak hot springs (Jiluu-Suu resort); the lakes Kashka-Suu, Chokaly-Kol and Small Kashka-Suu in the upper reaches; the Juuku waterfall; petroglyphs, Saka burial mounds and stone babas; access to the Arabel plateau and the Juuku Pass (3700 m) with views of glaciers; wildlife — ibex, argali, marmots, golden eagles.
kg-0064.skip: You have an ordinary passenger car and aren't ready to drive through fords — beyond the first few kilometres the gorge is impassable. You need developed springs and cafes — here there are only concrete tubs and wild camping spots. You are limited to one day on the south shore — Jeti-Oguz and Barskoon are easier to reach.
kg-0064.diff: By car — moderate/high: ~50 km of unmaintained dirt road with fords and sharp rocks; you need an SUV with good clearance and an experienced driver. Hikes and horse trips to the lakes and the Juuku Pass (3700 m) are multi-day and high-altitude (TUK treks “Jukuchak and Juku”). A walk near the red cliffs is easy.
kg-0064.when: July — September (TripAdvisor: optimal; the road is passable from about April, but during snowmelt there is mud and dangerous fords). After rain the road and trails wash out. In winter the upper reaches are closed by snow.
kg-0064.hours: An open area, round the clock. There is a barrier at the entrance; the eco tax collection has reportedly been suspended (status unclear). The Jiluu-Suu resort operates in summer.
kg-0064.daytime: Morning: the red cliffs are lit up, the fords are shallower (the river rises toward the evening from glacier melt); leave Karakol early to get back before dark.
kg-0064.how: The Balykchy — Karakol highway to the village of Saruu (42–45 km from Karakol, ~205 km from Cholpon-Ata), turn south; after 7 km the gorge forks: the right branch — Juukuchak to the hot springs (~15 km from the village), the left — the main Juuku to the red cliffs, forest and lakes. There is no public transport in the gorge — marshrutkas (minibuses) Karakol — Balykchy along the south shore drop you in Saruu, then take a taxi/hitch a ride.
kg-0064.needcar: Yes, an SUV: from Saruu it is 10–12 km to the cliffs, 15 km to the springs, and fords beyond. It is far on foot from the highway; horses are available from local shepherds/CBT by arrangement.
kg-0064.self: Yes, in a prepared SUV with a reserve of fuel and food; no permits are needed (the border zone begins further south, in the Arabel/Kumtor area — check if you plan to go up to the plateau). There is no signal — tell someone your route.
kg-0064.roadtype: Paved up to Saruu; then a packed gravel road of acceptable quality in the lower part (Kolesa.kz, Too.kg), higher up — a dirt road with fords, sharp rocks and potholes, “4x4 only” (TripAdvisor 2024–2026); in snowmelt and after rain — mud.
kg-0064.traveltime: Karakol — Saruu ~45 km, about 1 h; Saruu — red cliffs/entrance 10–12 km, 20–30 min; Saruu — Juukuchak springs 15 km, 30–40 min; further up the gorge the speed is 10–20 km/h. Allow a full day for the gorge with the springs; 2–4 days for the lakes and the pass.
kg-0064.stay: There are no guesthouses, shops or cafes in the gorge (Too.kg); at the Juukuchak springs there are simple cabins of the Jiluu-Suu resort at ~300 som/day (Kolesa.kz, year not specified); lots of tent spots; guesthouses in Saruu and Kyzyl-Suu; shepherds' yurts in summer by arrangement (CBT).
kg-0064.net: There is no signal in the gorge (Too.kg; TripAdvisor). Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage ends at Saruu/the highway.
kg-0064.entry: There is a barrier at the entrance; according to TripAdvisor reviews (2024–2026) the eco tax collection is suspended/not charged — the exact amount is not published. Bathing in the Jiluu-Suu hot spring — 50 som/hour (Kolesa.kz, date not specified). The current 2026 rate is not confirmed.
kg-0064.transfer: No carrier offers with 2025–2026 prices were found; as a guideline, rent a 4x4 with a driver from Karakol for the day (ask Destination Karakol/Visit Karakol). TUK/Nomad's Land tours — on request.
kg-0064.bring: A full tank and spare fuel, a shovel/tow rope for fords, food and water for the whole day (boil river water), warm clothes (2000–3700 m), a rain jacket, a swimsuit for the springs, offline maps and GPS, a first-aid kit; in the upper reaches — a tent and sleeping bag.
kg-0064.warn: River fords are dangerous during snowmelt and after rain; the road has sharp rocks — a risk of a flat tyre, a spare is a must. There is no signal — help is far away. Livestock and shepherd dogs graze higher up the gorge. The upper reaches (Arabel, Kumtor) adjoin restricted zones — check with the Border Service whether permits are needed before going up to the plateau. Don't drink river water without boiling it.
kg-0064.food: Kumis and homemade ayran from shepherds at the jailoo (summer pasture) in summer; in Saruu and Kyzyl-Suu — simple cafes with lagman and shashlik, Issyk-Kul fish on the highway. There is no food in the gorge — bring your own.
kg-0064.reviews: Google Maps (“Juuku Gorge”): 4.9/5, 9 ratings as of 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor “Juuku Gorge” (Karakol): 4.5/5, 15 reviews, no. 14 of 40 (07.10.2026). Pros: the red cliff “gates”, few people, wild nature, the springs; cons: a hard road, fords, a 4x4 is needed, no infrastructure.
kg-0064.p.sum: Juuku is a wild gorge with no infrastructure: turn off the southern highway at Saruu (≈45 km from Karakol), then 10–12 km of dirt road to the red cliff “gates”, and after ≈7 km the right branch goes to Juukuchak and its hot tubs (100 som). Higher up are fords and rocks, so you need a 4×4 with a local driver (from Karakol ≈5000 som a day, 2024, or 9500–13,200 som per SUV via MYWAY). Bring food, water, fuel and cash with you: the gorge has no shops, guesthouses or signal. Stay in a tent by the river or in guesthouses in Kyzyl-Suu (Homestay Ak-Jol, $19 with breakfast). The multi-day trek upward (Juuku lake, the 3640–3700 m pass, Arabel) takes 3–4 days.

kg-0065.name: San-Tash Burial Mound Complex
kg-0065.near: The settlement of San-Tash — about 0.9 km; the mound is 500 m from the Tup — Kegen road (A-363/A-364). Larger places: the village of Tup (~30 km to the west), Karakol (~56–79 km).
kg-0065.elev: 1,992–1,996 m above sea level (silkadv.com — 1,992 m; Nomad's Land — 1,996 m). The nearby San-Tash Pass is 2,166–2,195 m.
kg-0065.short: San-Tash (“counted stones”) is a huge stone heap over a Saka kurgan of the 6th–1st centuries BC near the San-Tash Pass on the way to Kazakhstan, tied to a legend about Tamerlane’s army.
kg-0065.desc: The San-Tash burial mound complex lies in the Tup river valley between the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges, 500 m from the Tup — Kegen road. The central mound is a stone heap 4 m high and 50–56 m in diameter (more than 3,500 m³ of stone) with a crater left by an ancient robbers’ shaft; around it are more than 250 large and small kurgans of the Saka period (6th–1st centuries BC), burials of nomad chiefs, as well as the ruins of a caravanserai of the 10th–12th centuries (a 48 m square with a tower). According to legend, Timur (Tamerlane) ordered each warrior to lay a stone before the campaign to China and take one back on the return; the stones that were left showed the number of the dead — hence the name. No modern excavations have been carried out. The famous east wind “santash” blows from the pass, raising storms on Issyk-Kul.
kg-0065.guide: Stop at the Tup — Kegen road: it is 500 m on foot across a meadow to the mound. Climb the four-metre pile of stones — you can see the crater in the centre, a trace of ancient robbers; from there make out dozens of smaller mounds around — that is the Saka necropolis, two and a half thousand years old. Locals will tell you the legend of Tamerlane, but remember: the kurgans are a thousand years older than his campaign. If you are continuing to Karkyra or to Kazakhstan via Kegen, it is an ideal “warm-up” stop; there is no ticket office or cafe nearby, but there is always wind — not for nothing is the wind that whips up storms on Issyk-Kul called “santash”. In spring and September the Tup valley is golden, and in summer it is cooler here than on the lakeshore.
kg-0065.see: The central stone mound (4 m, Ø 50–56 m) with its crater; a field of 250+ small kurgans; the ruins of the 10th–12th century caravanserai; a panorama of the Tup valley and Kungey Ala-Too; on the way — the San-Tash Pass (2,166–2,195 m) with spruce slopes and the Jergalan valley.
kg-0065.skip: You want “impressive” ruins — outwardly it is a heap of stones in a field, and the value lies in history and context. You are not heading towards Tup/Karkyra/Kegen — driving 60–80 km from Karakol specially for a 20-minute stop is not for everyone. Strong wind and rain — it is uncomfortable on the open mound.
kg-0065.diff: Very easy: 500 m across a flat meadow from the road and a climb onto a 4 m mound.
kg-0065.when: May — October; in summer (July–August) combine it with the nomad games at Karkyra. In winter the San-Tash Pass can be hard to cross because of snow (silkadv).
kg-0065.hours: An open area with no fence or ticket office, around the clock.
kg-0065.daytime: Morning or the hour before sunset — low sun emphasises the relief of the mounds and the crater; during the day the open field is windy.
kg-0065.how: From Karakol east through Tup along the Kegen road (A-363/A-364), ~79 km via Tup or ~56 km via Novoznesenovka and the Kok-Kiya farm, then over the San-Tash Pass; the mound is 500 m to the right of the road, 0.9 km from the settlement of San-Tash. From the Kazakhstan side — 10–15 km from the Karkyra — Kegen border crossing.
kg-0065.needcar: Yes: public transport to the settlement of San-Tash is limited (marshrutkas (minibuses) Karakol — Tup, then a taxi/hitchhike); it is easier by car or with a tour to Karkyra/Kazakhstan.
kg-0065.self: Yes: no permits or fees; the mound is visible from the road. The border zone starts closer to the border crossing; documents are not checked at the mound, but keep your passport with you (it is a border area).
kg-0065.roadtype: From Karakol to Tup — paved; the section over the San-Tash Pass (A-364) is a broken gravel-and-rock road with potholes (silkadv), passable for a passenger car in the dry season; the last 500 m on foot across the meadow.
kg-0065.traveltime: Karakol — San-Tash ~1–1.5 h (56–79 km depending on the route); from the Karkyra border crossing ~15–20 min; the visit takes 20–40 min.
kg-0065.stay: There is no accommodation at the mound. Nearest: guesthouses and yurts in the Karkyra valley (in summer, via CBT/Destination Karakol), guesthouses in Tup; the main choice is Karakol (60–80 km). 2025–2026 prices not confirmed.
kg-0065.net: Along the Tup — Kegen road there is mobile coverage near the settlements (the settlement of San-Tash is 0.9 km away); on the pass and in the Karkyra valley the signal is unstable. No reports on specific operators were found.
kg-0065.entry: Free: no ticket offices, fences or fees (silkadv, Nomad's Land, Atlas Obscura — no fee is mentioned).
kg-0065.transfer: No offers with a price specifically to San-Tash were found; a guide — a taxi from Karakol to the Tup district by agreement, tours to Karkyra via Destination Karakol/CBT (on request).
kg-0065.bring: A windbreaker (constant “santash” wind), a hat, water and a snack (no cafe nearby), a passport (border area), a wide-angle camera for the valley panorama.
kg-0065.warn: Border zone with Kazakhstan: do not walk from the mounds towards the border without documents; a passport is needed at the border crossing. Do not dismantle or move stones — it is an archaeological monument. On the San-Tash Pass the road is broken, with snowdrifts in winter; wind tears tents and raises storms on the lake. The Tamerlane legend is folklore: the monument is Saka, a thousand years older.
kg-0065.food: In Tup and at Karkyra in summer — kumys, boorsok, kuurdak from herders; the nearest cafes are in Tup and Karakol. There is no food at the mound.
kg-0065.reviews: 2GIS: 5/5, 6 ratings, 2 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: no separate listing matched (meta: ambiguous result). TripAdvisor: listing not found. From descriptions: pros — atmosphere, the legend, the view of the valley; cons — “just a pile of stones”, far from Karakol.
kg-0065.p.sum: San-Tash is a 20–40-minute stop by the Tup — Kegen road (A-363/A-364): the central stone mound 500 m to the right of the highway, 0.9 km from the settlement of San-Tash. It is worth coming here specially only on the way to Karkyra or to Kazakhstan via the Karkyra — Kegen border crossing (open 24 hours since 11.2024). From Karakol — 1–1.5 h by car or taxi; the Karakol — Almaty bus (since 7.09.2025, 1,200 som) passes by, but you need to arrange a drop-off. The nearest comfortable overnight is the Ak-Sai yurt camp at Karkyra (from $45 for a tent for two with breakfast, horse $15/h) or Karakol.

kg-0066.name: Belogorka Gorge
kg-0066.near: The village of Belogorka/Konush at the mouth of the gorge (~1.8 km from the catalog's previous point, OSM); the district center is Sokuluk (too.kg: the gorge is “above the village of Sokuluk”). From the waterfall to the last villages it is ~20 km along the valley.
kg-0066.elev: The Belogorka waterfall is at about 2200 m above sea level (open.kg); the drop is about 60 m (too.kg, open.kg, travelbar.kg).
kg-0066.short: Belogorka is a picturesque rocky gorge of the Sokuluk River ~50–80 km west/southwest of Bishkek with the 60 m Belogorka waterfall — one of the highest in northern Kyrgyzstan.
kg-0066.desc: The Belogorka Gorge is a section of the Sokuluk River valley on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too, above the village of Sokuluk. The gorge is notable for its abundance of tall cliffs (a recognizable peak, the “Black Spire”), springs and streams; the slopes have Turkestan birch, hawthorn and wild currant, and there are wild boar, ibex and wolves (open.kg). The main attraction is the Belogorka waterfall, about 60 m high at ~2200 m: the water, as it falls, almost never reaches the ground, turning into a cloud of spray that you can feel from 200 m away (too.kg, open.kg). The origin of the powerful stream is a mystery — there is neither a glacier nor a snowfield above the waterfall. 1.5–2 h of walking higher up is a second waterfall of 7–8 m; experienced hikers go further to the Sokuluk Pass into the West Karakol valley. There is no infrastructure: no signal, no cafes, no accommodation.
kg-0066.guide: Belogorka is the best “one-day” waterfall west of Bishkek: 3 km of an almost flat trail along the river and 60 meters of water breaking into a cloud of spray. Come in May–June, when the waterfall is full — by the end of summer the flow weakens noticeably. Bring a rain jacket: the spray reaches 200 m, and on a sunny day there is a rainbow in it. If you want more, a steep trail for another 2 hours uphill leads to a viewpoint and a small waterfall. There is no signal or shops in the gorge — bring food and water.
kg-0066.see: The Belogorka waterfall (~60 m) and the cloud of spray with a rainbow; the small waterfall of 7–8 m higher up the gorge; the cliffs and the “Black Spire” peak; the Sokuluk River valley, birch groves and meadows; for the experienced — Sokuluk Pass to West Karakol.
kg-0066.skip: You have a low sedan and aren't ready to walk extra kilometers — the road up the gorge is bad. You are going at the end of summer — the waterfall is low on water. You need cafes, a signal and accommodation — the gorge has none of these.
kg-0066.diff: Easy: from the parking area 3 km one way, ~1 h 10 min, ascent ~200–250 m, 2 out of 5 on the hiking.kg scale (the overall trip rating is 4 out of 5 because of the road); the last climb to the waterfall is steeper. The continuation to the viewpoint is a steep trail for another ~2 h (ionlytakepics).
kg-0066.when: May–June — the waterfall is fullest (hiking.kg); in summer you can swim in the river (open.kg). At the end of summer there is little water (ionlytakepics, 2021). In winter the road and trail are not maintained.
kg-0066.hours: A natural area, no time restrictions; the sources do not mention any fee-collection points.
kg-0066.daytime: On a sunny day before lunch a rainbow is visible in the spray; after sunset the waterfall looks like “gray smoke” (open.kg). Leave Bishkek early: the drive takes ~2–2.5 h.
kg-0066.how: From Bishkek west along the Kara-Balta highway to Sokuluk, then turn south along the Sokuluk River (70 km, 2 h 30 min — hiking.kg). The road in the gorge gets worse; sedans are left before the last bridge, and a car with high clearance can drive closer. From the parking area it is 3 km on foot.
kg-0066.needcar: Yes: no public transport runs into the gorge (too.kg). You need a car with high clearance, a taxi or a group tour.
kg-0066.self: Yes, if you have a car with high clearance and an offline map: the trail along the river is clear. Without a car it is easier with a group tour (Travelbar, TUK).
kg-0066.roadtype: Paved road to Sokuluk; up the gorge a dirt road whose quality deteriorates (high clearance needed, too.kg); the last section is a foot trail along the river.
kg-0066.traveltime: Bishkek → parking: 70 km, 2 h 30 min (hiking.kg); travelbar — ~2 h by bus. Parking → waterfall: 3 km, 1 h 10 min (hiking.kg).
kg-0066.stay: There is no accommodation in the gorge (too.kg); there are convenient spots for tents by the waterfall. The nearest hotels are in Sokuluk and Bishkek (specific places not checked).
kg-0066.net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge (too.kg).
kg-0066.entry: An entry fee or eco fee is not mentioned in the sources (too.kg, hiking.kg, travelbar, ionlytakepics); there is no official confirmation that it is free.
kg-0066.transfer: Travelbar.kg group tour — 380 som per person (transport + guide; the date of the listing is not given). Taxi prices Bishkek — Belogorka were not found.
kg-0066.bring: Shoes with a grippy sole, a rain jacket/windbreaker against the spray, a warm layer, water (there are few springs, drinking from the river is not recommended — too.kg), a snack, a first-aid kit, SPF cream (travelbar). For an overnight stay — a tent.
kg-0066.warn: There is no signal — tell acquaintances your route. The rocks at the waterfall are wet and slippery. Wild boar and wolves live in the gorge (open.kg). The road is limited for sedans. Don't drink the river water.
kg-0066.food: There are no cafes or shops in the gorge (too.kg) — the classic format is a picnic by the river (Travelbar and YouTravel tours include a picnic). The nearest cafes are in Sokuluk.
kg-0066.reviews: There is no separate reliable Google Maps listing for the gorge (meta: “ambiguous result”). Tourist reviews (ionlytakepics, otzovik about the “Pigeon Waterfall in Sokuluk”, YouTube): pros — a powerful waterfall, an easy trail, cliffs; cons — a bad road, little water at the end of summer. The hiking.kg rating is 7/10.
kg-0066.p.sum: Belogorka is the highest waterfall in northern Kyrgyzstan (~60 m), ~70–80 km and 2–2.5 h from Bishkek: through Sokuluk and the villages of Belogorka/Konush, then along a worsening dirt road. Sedans are left at the last bridge, and a car with high clearance can drive closer; from the parking spot it is 3 km and ~1 h 10 min along an easy trail by the river. Public transport does not run into the gorge: bus No. 32 only takes you as far as Sokuluk (35 som), so the realistic options are your own car or a taxi with a wait, or a group hike (Travelbar 380 som, TUK, Master Tour). The gorge has no signal, cafe or accommodation — bring water and food, and you can sleep in a tent.

kg-0067.name: Sacred Mountain Sulaiman-Too
kg-0067.near: Osh: the mountain stands in the center of the city; the main entrance is on Gapar Aitiev St. at the intersection with Shota Rustaveli St. (eurasia.travel); the museum is at 71/2 Gapar Aitiev St. (2GIS).
kg-0067.elev: About 1,175 m — the highest peak, Rushaan-Too; the mountain rises about 200 m above the city and is about 1.5 km long (eurasia.travel; some sources give 1,172 m for the mountain as a whole).
kg-0067.short: Sulaiman-Too is a five-peaked sacred mountain in the center of Osh, Kyrgyzstan’s first UNESCO World Heritage site (2009): pilgrim paths, caves, petroglyphs, “Babur’s house” and a cave museum.
kg-0067.desc: The sacred mountain Sulaiman-Too has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2009. A rocky massif about 1.5 km long rises about 200 m above Osh and has five peaks: Takhti-Sulaiman (Buura-Too), Shor-Too, Kattama-Too, Rushaan-Too (the highest, ~1,175 m) and Eer-Too (eurasia.travel). On the mountain there are places of worship, caves, petroglyphs and polished rock “slides” used in healing and fertility rituals; on the main peak is the reconstructed “khujra” (house) of Babur, built in the late 15th century by the future founder of the Mughal Empire, destroyed in the 1950s and restored from photographs (eurasia.travel, travel-tramp). A cave museum was opened in the mountainside in 1978; the National Historical and Archaeological Museum Complex “Sulaiman-Too” (founded in 1949) holds about 33–35 thousand exhibits (24.kg, 2025). About 300,000 people visit the mountain a year; from October 2026 to the end of 2028 a reconstruction costing ~$12 million (the World Bank) is under way: the cave, ethnographic and archaeological museums, three entrance zones (Suu-Darbaza, Ot-Darbaza, Too-Darbaza), a visitor center, staircases and lighting will be renovated; there are no plans to close the site completely (Kaktus, 01.07.2026).
kg-0067.guide: Climb from the east side — up the steps straight to “Babur’s house” on the summit: the climb takes 15–25 minutes, and from the top all of Osh lies in the palm of your hand. Notice the stones polished to a shine: these are the “slides” down which women asking for children and pilgrims who believe in healing have slid for centuries. Descend by the gentle road to the west, to the cave museum — the exhibition is built right into a natural cave — and to the large mosque at the foot. It is best to come at dawn or sunset: it is cooler and the light over the city is beautiful. Since autumn 2026 a reconstruction has been under way — some areas may be temporarily fenced off.
kg-0067.see: The five peaks and the pilgrim paths; “Babur’s house” (khujra) on the Takhti-Sulaiman peak; the ritual “slides” and caves; petroglyphs; the mausoleum of Asaf ibn Burkhiya at the southeast entrance (vitalik.kz); the cave museum and the historical and archaeological museum complex; viewing platforms with a panorama of Osh; the large mosque at the western foot; a medieval bathhouse (24.kg).
kg-0067.skip: You dislike stairs in the heat — in summer at midday the climb is hard (travel-tramp). You are looking for wild nature — this is an urban shrine with paved paths. You come in 2026–2028 for the museums — some exhibitions may be closed for reconstruction.
kg-0067.diff: Easy: paved paths, steps and handrails; to the upper platform ~15–25 min (TripAdvisor; vitalik.kz). In places the stones are polished and slippery, and some steps are damaged (TripAdvisor).
kg-0067.when: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–October): blossoms and a comfortable temperature (vitalik.kz — March). In summer at midday it is hot on the open slopes (travel-tramp). Accessible year-round.
kg-0067.hours: Museum: 09:00–17:30 per 2GIS (2026); other sources say 09:00–18:00, Tuesday–Sunday, Monday closed (kupi.com, year not given); the museum is sometimes closed after lunch (TripAdvisor reviews). The mountain: daytime visits; since 2024 night entry has been restricted (TripAdvisor review, 04.2024). From 10.2026 — a phased reconstruction with temporary closure of individual zones (Kaktus, 2026).
kg-0067.daytime: Sunrise or sunset — coolness and the best views of the city (TripAdvisor); the museum — before lunch, while it is surely open.
kg-0067.how: The mountain is in the center of Osh: on foot from the center/Jayma bazaar; by taxi (Yandex Go, inDrive) to the entrance on Gapar Aitiev St. at the intersection with Shota Rustaveli St. For cars — paid parking; the barrier is opened for tour buses/taxis for an extra fee (eurasia.travel). There are no entrances on the north side (vitalik.kz).
kg-0067.needcar: No: on the mountain — on foot only; you can walk to the entrance from the center or get there by taxi/city transport.
kg-0067.self: Yes: the route is well equipped, with map boards at the entrances (vitalik.kz). A guide is needed only for a detailed story about the shrines and petroglyphs.
kg-0067.roadtype: City streets to the entrance; on the mountain — paved paths and steps with handrails; the western slope — a gentle road (travel-tramp, TripAdvisor).
kg-0067.traveltime: From the center of Osh — 5–15 minutes by taxi or 15–30 minutes on foot (editorial). The climb to the summit — 15–25 minutes; a full visit with the museum — 2–3 hours (editorial, per reviews).
kg-0067.stay: Hotels and guesthouses of Osh within walking distance (the city center). Specific hotels have not been checked within this card — look on Booking/2GIS.
kg-0067.net: Osh’s city 4G coverage by all operators (Beeline, O!, MegaCom) — no specific complaints about a lack of signal on the mountain were found (editorial; specific coverage maps were not checked).
kg-0067.entry: A ticket to the complex grounds — 70 som (Kaktus, 01.07.2026). The museum — a separate fee: 150 som for foreigners (travel-tramp, year not given); kupi.com says “about 30 som” (probably an outdated price for citizens). Old reviews (2018) — 20 som for the mountain. The current 2026 museum tariffs are not confirmed.
kg-0067.transfer: Not required for a visit on foot; taxis in Osh — at Yandex Go/inDrive rates (prices not checked). Parking is paid, the amount was not found.
kg-0067.bring: Comfortable non-slip shoes (the stones are polished); water and a hat in summer; modest clothing — this is a sacred place (shoulders and knees covered; editorial); cash som for tickets.
kg-0067.warn: An active shrine: respect those praying, and do not photograph people during rituals without permission. Stories about healing belong to belief; medical effectiveness is not confirmed. Slippery polished stones and damaged steps — be careful with children (TripAdvisor). From October 2026 to the end of 2028 — reconstruction: temporary restrictions in individual areas are possible (Kaktus, 2026). Night entry is restricted (2024).
kg-0067.food: Osh plov and southern samsa — in the teahouses of central Osh and by the Jayma bazaar (editorial; specific establishments not checked).
kg-0067.reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 335 ratings (the mountain, 03.10.2026). 2GIS (the “Sulaiman-Too” museum): 4.9/5, 739 ratings, 127 reviews (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Mountain Sulaiman-Too”: 4.2/5, 192 reviews, No. 1 of 23 in Osh. Pros: an easy climb, a panorama of the city, history, the museum. Cons: slippery stones, damaged steps, the museum closed after lunch, restricted night entry.
kg-0067.p.sum: The mountain is in the center of Osh: get there by Yandex Go to “Gapar Aitiev 67” (the Aitiev–Rustaveli intersection) or walk from the Jayma bazaar. The best route is to climb from the western (gentle, by the mosque) entrance and descend the steep eastern staircase to the museum; ~1.5 h for everything. A ticket for the mountain is 70 som, the cave museum and the state museum another 70 som each. From October 2026 to the end of 2028 a reconstruction is under way — some areas are fenced off, the mountain is not closed.

kg-0069.name: Too-Ashuu Pass
kg-0069.near: From the north — Sosnovka (toll checkpoint, ~2 h from Bishkek) in the Kara-Balta valley; from the south — the villages of the Suusamyr Valley (Kaysar — ~16 km as the crow flies, OSM). At the southern portal of the tunnel is the Too-Ashuu ski base.
kg-0069.elev: The pass — 3586 m (2GIS, asiamixtravel); the old gravel road over the saddle climbed to ~3594 m (dangerousroads). The K. Kolbaev Tunnel is at ~3120–3180 m (asiamixtravel, dangerousroads); the ski base is at about 3000 m.
kg-0069.short: Too-Ashuu (Töö-Ashuu, “Camel Pass”) is a 3586 m pass through the Kyrgyz Range on the Bishkek — Osh highway; vehicles go through it by a tunnel ~2.7 km long at an altitude of ~3150 m and descend by switchbacks into Suusamyr.
kg-0069.desc: Too-Ashuu is one of the two road crossings of the Kyrgyz Range connecting the Chuy Valley with the Suusamyr Valley (2GIS). The saddle of the pass is at 3586 m; in the 1960s a tunnel about 2.7 km long was bored under it at an altitude of ~3120–3180 m (now the K. Kolbaev Tunnel), replacing the dangerous gravel road over the top (dangerousroads, asiamixtravel). From the north, switchbacks lead to the tunnel from the Kara-Balta gorge, and from the south there is a descent to Suusamyr. The name translates as “camel pass”. The tunnel is narrow and poorly ventilated; in 2001 a carbon monoxide poisoning tragedy occurred in it. A fee is charged for passing through the tunnels of the Bishkek — Osh highway at the Sosnovka and Kara-Kol checkpoints. At the southern portal, the highest ski base in Central Asia, Too-Ashuu (~3000 m), has operated since 2009–2010. The construction of a new long tunnel under the pass is being discussed at government level.
kg-0069.guide: Too-Ashuu is the first real “3000+” on the way from Bishkek to Osh. Before the tunnel, on the northern switchbacks, there are viewing platforms overlooking the Kara-Balta valley — stop only at the road's wider spots. In the tunnel itself (about 2.7 km) turn on your headlights, close the windows and set the ventilation to recirculation — it is narrow and smoky. Right after you exit, the Suusamyr Valley opens up — one of the most spectacular views on the highway. In winter check the Ministry of Transport bulletins: restrictions are introduced here during snowfalls.
kg-0069.see: The switchbacks of the northern slope and the view of the Kara-Balta valley; the K. Kolbaev Tunnel (~2.7 km, ~3150 m); the panorama of the Suusamyr Valley after the tunnel; the Too-Ashuu ski base at the southern portal; the old road to the 3586 m saddle (dangerous out of season).
kg-0069.skip: You aren't going to Suusamyr, Talas or Osh — in summer there is little point in driving 2–2.5 h from Bishkek just for the pass. You tolerate switchbacks and altitude above 3000 m poorly. You're driving in winter without winter tires — dangerous.
kg-0069.diff: For a passenger — no effort. For the driver — serious mountain switchbacks and a narrow, poorly ventilated tunnel at ~3150 m; in winter — snow, black ice, avalanche danger. On foot to the 3586 m saddle along the old road — only for the acclimatized; the sources do not describe a route.
kg-0069.when: June — September: dry road and a green Suusamyr. The highway is open year-round, but from November to April there is snow and temporary restrictions (for example, on 11–13.02.2026 truck traffic was restricted because of snowfall — 24.kg). The ski season at the Too-Ashuu base is from late November to March/April.
kg-0069.hours: The Bishkek — Osh highway and the tunnel operate around the clock, except for temporary closures: repairs (for example, 26.07–06.08.2023 — daily 06:00–16:00 for passenger cars, Kyrtag), snowfalls and avalanches (Ministry of Transport). Check the Ministry of Transport/24.kg bulletins before you travel.
kg-0069.daytime: In the daytime, in daylight: the best views are on the switchbacks and in Suusamyr, and there is less risk of black ice. Avoid driving at night in winter.
kg-0069.how: From Bishkek along the Bishkek — Osh highway west to Kara-Balta, then south along the gorge via Sosnovka (toll checkpoint) and the switchbacks to the tunnel (~130 km to the pass, 2–2.5 h — asiamixtravel). The modern road goes through the tunnel, not over the upper saddle.
kg-0069.needcar: Yes: your own car, a taxi or intercity transport Bishkek — Osh/Suusamyr/Talas. A public transport stop at the viewpoints is not guaranteed.
kg-0069.self: Yes, by your own car or taxi. In winter — only on winter tires and after checking the bulletins. A walk to the saddle — there are no sources, so it cannot be recommended.
kg-0069.roadtype: The paved Bishkek — Osh trunk road (M41) with mountain switchbacks; the ~2.7 km tunnel is narrow, and its asphalt was renewed in summer 2023 (Kyrtag). The old road over the upper 3586 m saddle is gravel, its condition is not confirmed.
kg-0069.traveltime: Bishkek → Too-Ashuu tunnel/base: ~130 km, 2–2.5 h (asiamixtravel); to the Sosnovka checkpoint ~2 h (TollGuru). Passing through the tunnel takes a few minutes.
kg-0069.stay: The Too-Ashuu ski base at the southern portal: a guesthouse with 66 beds plus cottages and cabins, ~100 beds in total; a cafe-bar, sauna, rental (asiamixtravel, 2026; prices not stated). In summer — yurt camps and guesthouses in the Suusamyr Valley.
kg-0069.net: Too.kg notes incomplete coverage on the pass section; in the tunnel the signal may drop out. The operator is not specified.
kg-0069.entry: No entry fee. Toll for passing through the tunnels of the Bishkek — Osh highway: 50 som for a car (Kyrgyz plates), 200 som — foreign plates; buses 100/1000 som (since 01.01.2024; Kaktus.media). Payment at the Sosnovka/Kara-Kol checkpoints.
kg-0069.transfer: Shared taxi Bishkek — Osh 2500 som/seat (2025–2026, asocialnomad); tunnel toll 50 som/car. Transfers to the ski base — by arrangement, prices not confirmed.
kg-0069.bring: A warm jacket even in summer (at ~3150 m it is cool and windy), sunglasses, water and a snack (there are few services on the switchbacks), cash or an app to pay the toll. In winter — chains/studs, a reserve of fuel, a shovel.
kg-0069.warn: The tunnel is narrow and poorly ventilated: thick exhaust, visibility drops — turn on your headlights, keep your distance, do not stop inside (dangerousroads; in 2001 people died from carbon monoxide during a traffic jam). In winter — snow, black ice, avalanches, temporary bans for trucks (24.kg 13.02.2026). At ~3150–3586 m altitude — altitude sickness is possible when stopping. Periodic closures of the tunnel for repairs.
kg-0069.food: The cafe-bar of the Too-Ashuu ski base (asiamixtravel); in summer on the road in Suusamyr — kumis and Kyrgyz cuisine at yurts along the highway (per too.kg for Suusamyr). Specific places at the pass itself are not confirmed.
kg-0069.reviews: Google Maps (Pereval Teo-Ashuu): 4.8/5, 94 ratings (03.10.2026); 2GIS: 4.7/5, 30 ratings, 14 reviews (07.10.2026); TripAdvisor: the “Too-Ashu Pass” page (d10112269). Pros: spectacular switchbacks, views of Suusamyr, “high and beautiful”. Cons: a smoky narrow tunnel, dangerous in winter.
kg-0069.p.sum: Too-Ashuu (3586 m; the Kolbaev Tunnel at ~3150 m) is the gateway of the Bishkek — Osh highway between the Kara-Balta valley and Suusamyr, ≈130 km and 2–2.5 h from Bishkek. The pass is driven through on the way: by your own car (tunnel toll 50 som for Kyrgyz plates and 200 som for foreign ones, at the Sosnovka/Kara-Kol checkpoints), by shared taxi Bishkek — Osh (2500 som per seat) or by marshrutka (minibus) to Osh/Talas/Suusamyr. You can stop at the ski base at the southern portal: ski pass 1000/800 som, cottages for 66 guests. In 2026 the asphalt and parapets were replaced at km 130–146, and by October the approaches to the portals were repaired — restrictions are possible in summer. In winter, check the Ministry of Transport bulletins before the trip, and in the tunnel keep your distance, turn on your headlights and do not stop.

kg-0071.name: Ak-Sai Glacier
kg-0071.near: Kashka-Suu — about 20 km as the crow flies (OSM marker). The real starting point is the Ala-Archa alpine camp (~12 km above the park checkpoint), from where it is ~6–7 km on foot via the Racek Hut to the edge of the glacier.
kg-0071.elev: The lower part of the glacier is about 3,300–3,500 m (at the Racek Hut ~3,300–3,400 m; Trip to Kyrgyzstan/Baibol give 3,500 m), the upper reaches are under the crest of the Ak-Sai spur at 4,700–4,875 m (Semenov-Tian-Shansky Peak 4,875 m, Korona 4,860 m, Svobodnaya Koreya 4,740 m).
kg-0071.short: Ak-Sai is the largest glacier of the Ala-Archa gorge, about 5 km long, with a huge icefall; it descends to the Racek Hut from the crest of the highest peaks of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too.
kg-0071.desc: The Ak-Sai Glacier lies at the head of the side gorge of the same name in the Ala-Archa nature park, ~40 km from Bishkek. It is about 5 km long (Baibol Travel), with a huge icefall in the middle section. The glacier flows down from the Ak-Sai spur, where the highest points of the Kyrgyz range rise: Semenov-Tian-Shansky Peak (4,875 m), Korona (4,860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (4,740 m), Baylyan-Bashi (4,700 m), Simagin (4,400 m) and Boks (4,240 m). At the foot are several climbers’ bases, the best known of which is the Racek Hut; about 80 climbing routes have been laid out on the slopes around. Tourists usually look at the glacier from the moraine by the hut; going onto the ice itself is already a mountaineering task.
kg-0071.guide: The Ak-Sai Glacier is the “stage” for Korona Peak: the best view opens from the moraine right above the Racek Hut, which is reached by a hard but non-technical day hike from the alpine camp. Look closely at the icefall in the middle section — it is the approach to the walls of Korona and Svobodnaya Koreya, where generations of climbers have trained in Ala-Archa. Do not go onto the ice without a rope and skills: crevasses are covered by snow even in summer. If you want to touch the glacier safely, stay overnight at the hut and go with an Ak-Sai Travel guide.
kg-0071.see: The icefall in the middle section of the glacier, a view of Korona, Svobodnaya Koreya and Semenov-Tian-Shansky peaks from the moraine by the Racek Hut; on the way — the Ak-Sai waterfall and the Tepshe plateau; nearby — the Uchitel glacier and lake.
kg-0071.skip: You expect to reach the ice light in half a day — it is 6–7 km and +1,300 m from the alpine camp to the edge of the glacier. You do not tolerate altitude of 3,300+ m. You want to “walk on the glacier” without mountaineering gear and a guide — that is dangerous because of hidden crevasses.
kg-0071.diff: To the edge of the glacier (the moraine by the Racek Hut): a hard non-technical trek of 6–7 km and +1,100–1,350 m one way. Going onto the glacier and climbs are at mountaineering level (crampons, ice axe, rope team, belaying skills); Uchitel Peak is grade 1B, Korona and Svobodnaya Koreya are difficult routes.
kg-0071.when: Late June — September for the trek to the hut and moraine; for climbs — July–August. In winter the glacier and approaches are under avalanche threat; the hut is open year-round, but in winter experience is needed.
kg-0071.hours: No time limits: a natural area within the Ala-Archa park (the checkpoint is open daily). The Racek Hut at the glacier operates year-round (Ak-Sai Travel).
kg-0071.daytime: Morning: the view of the icefall and Korona is best before noon; after lunch there is often cloud and thunderstorms. Set off from the alpine camp before 8:00.
kg-0071.how: Bishkek → Ala-Archa park checkpoint (bus No. 1 from Usubaliev Sq., 50/40 som, or a taxi) → free electric bus ~12 km to the alpine camp → on foot along the Ak-Sai gorge past the waterfall to the Racek Hut (5.7–6 km) → the moraine and the edge of the glacier next to the hut.
kg-0071.needcar: To the park checkpoint — bus No. 1 or a taxi; inside — a free electric bus to the alpine camp (combustion-engine cars have not been allowed in since 01.05.2025); beyond that only on foot.
kg-0071.self: To the moraine by the Racek Hut — yes, if you are fit. Onto the glacier itself — only with mountaineering experience or a guide (Ak-Sai Travel and others).
kg-0071.roadtype: Paved up to the checkpoint and then a road for electric buses to the alpine camp; above — a mountain trail, above the Ak-Sai waterfall steep scree and moraine; on the glacier — ice, snow and crevasses.
kg-0071.traveltime: Bishkek → checkpoint 45–60 min; electric bus to the alpine camp; alpine camp → Racek Hut 4–6 h up, 3–4 h down (ilovekg). As a day hike — 8–11 h; better with an overnight at the hut.
kg-0071.stay: Racek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel): bunk $15 per person, VIP $25, your own tent $3 per person per day; the Light House hut is nearby (ak-sai.com, 2026). Lower down — cottages and yurts at the Ala-Archa alpine camp.
kg-0071.net: There is no mobile network on the route to the hut and at the glacier (asiamixtravel) — offline maps are essential. A signal is available around the checkpoint/alpine camp.
kg-0071.entry: Entry to the Ala-Archa park from 11.06.2026: 250 som for adults, 180 som for children aged 7–14 (24.kg; group 6 data). There is no separate fee for the glacier; an overnight at the hut is at Ak-Sai Travel rates.
kg-0071.transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50/40 som; electric bus — free; taxi Bishkek — checkpoint ~$12–18, private transfer $40–90 (kgnomad 2026).
kg-0071.bring: Trekking boots, poles, a waterproof shell and a warm layer, hat and gloves, 1.5–2 l of water, category 3–4 sunglasses and SPF, a headlamp. For going onto the ice — crampons, ice axe, helmet, harness and rope (only with skills).
kg-0071.warn: The glacier is a mountaineering zone: hidden crevasses, an icefall, rockfall from the moraine. Altitude 3,300+ m — risk of altitude sickness (Emergency Ministry (MChS) evacuations at the Racek Hut in 2026). No phone coverage; in an emergency — 112. Outside summer — avalanches. The glaciers of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too are retreating, moraine edges are unstable.
kg-0071.food: Food at the Racek Hut per the Ak-Sai Travel menu: breakfast $12, lunch $20, dinner $15 (2026); lower down — the cafe at the Ala-Archa alpine camp. There are no local dishes at the glacier — bring a snack and a thermos.
kg-0071.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 11 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: a separate “Ak-Sai Glacier” page (d10112272) with reviews; AllTrails: the route to the hut and glacier — 224 reviews. Pros: a real glacier close to the capital, views of Korona. Cons: a hard climb, acclimatisation needed.
kg-0071.photos.0.cap: Svobodnaya Koreya Peak in the Ak-Sai glacier area; not an overview of the whole glacier
kg-0071.p.sum: The edge of the Ak-Sai Glacier is the moraine right by the Racek Hut: the route is the same — bus No. 1 or a taxi to the Ala-Archa checkpoint (entry 250 som), the free electric bus to the alpine camp and 6–9 km on foot with +1,100–1,350 m of climbing. You can look at the glacier from the moraine without equipment. Onto the ice itself — only roped, with crampons, ice axe, helmet and a guide: crevasses and bergschrunds, and routes to the surrounding peaks start at 1B–3A. It is most convenient to spend the night at the Racek Hut ($15 bunk) and head out to the glacier snout and Lake Uchitel early in the morning.

kg-0071.p.apps.0.last: Phone coverage, cafe and toilets — at the checkpoint and alpine camp. Food, sleeping bag and gas — at the Racek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel). ATMs and fuel stations — in Bishkek

kg-0072.name: Lake Kol-Kogur
kg-0072.near: Kok-Oirok — ~12.5 km as the crow flies (OSM); inhabited villages with guesthouses — Kalmak-Ashuu, Karool-Debe, Shabdan, Tar-Suu lower down the Chon-Kemin valley; on the south side of the range — Tamchy on Issyk-Kul (2–3 days' travel over a pass).
kg-0072.elev: About 2470–2500 m: 2468 m (Nomad's Land), 2500 m (Sputnik8, 2026 tour). The value “about 2000 m” (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Silk Road Explore) contradicts other sources and is probably too low.
kg-0072.short: Kol-Kogur is a secluded forest lake on the northern slope of Kungey Ala-Too in Chon-Kemin National Park (~2470 m), formed by an ancient landslide; it can be reached only on foot or on horseback.
kg-0072.desc: Kol-Kogur (Kel-Kogur) lies in the Kemin district in Chon-Kemin State Nature Park on the northern slope of Kungey Ala-Too, at about 2470–2500 m, ~5 km below Kol-Tor Pass. The lake is held by a natural dam from an ancient landslide at its northern end; its waters feed tributaries of the Chon-Kemin (Silk Road Explore). Spruce forests come down to the shore from the west and meadows from the east; the surroundings are home to Turkestan lynx, maral deer and golden eagles. There is no road to the lake: from the Chon-Kemin valley it is a river crossing on horseback and a climb on foot (day tours), or a long approach along the left bank of the Chon-Kemin of 20–25 km; from the Issyk-Kul side — 2–3-day horse routes from Tamchy over passes of ~3320–3342 m.
kg-0072.guide: Kol-Kogur is the “lost lake” of Chon-Kemin: you can't get here by car, and that is its main charm. The fastest way is a day tour: crossing the Chon-Kemin on horses and climbing through spruce forest to the lake at ~2500 m. If you have 3 days, ride from Tamchy over Kol-Tor Pass, starting on the shore of Issyk-Kul and finishing in the Chon-Kemin valley. Pay attention to the northern shore — the lake is dammed by an ancient landslide. Don't try to cross the river on your own: hire horses from locals or CBT.
kg-0072.see: The lake itself with spruce forests on the western shore and meadows on the eastern; the landslide dam at the northern end; the crossing of the Chon-Kemin; views of the Kungey Ala-Too range and Kol-Tor Pass; nearby in the valley — Lake Jashyl-Kol.
kg-0072.skip: You aren't ready for a long day (10–12 h) or a multi-day horse trek — you can't drive up. You're afraid of crossing a turbulent river. You're limited by budget: a one-day jeep tour from Bishkek costs about $420 per group (Sputnik8).
kg-0072.diff: Moderate to hard. One-day option: crossing on horseback + climbing on foot, ~10 h of trail (Sputnik8; “moderate physical effort” in reviews). The walking approach along the left bank is 20–25 km one way, better done over 2 days (hiking.kg). From Tamchy — 3 days on horseback over passes of 3320–3342 m, designed for beginner riders (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, CBT).
kg-0072.when: June to September (CBT Tamchi); for the horse trek from Tamchy — July–August (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). In spring and early summer the Chon-Kemin is in high flow — the crossing is more dangerous.
kg-0072.hours: A natural area of Chon-Kemin National Park, no opening hours. Tours: a one-day trip from Bishkek takes ~12 h; CBT Tamchi — start at 9:00, return on day 3 around 16:30.
kg-0072.daytime: Set off as early in the morning as possible: the one-day route takes ~10 h, and it is safer to cross the river before the daytime rise in water from snowmelt (editorial).
kg-0072.how: From Bishkek along the Balykchy highway through the Boom Gorge, turn into the Chon-Kemin valley in the Kemin district (140 km, 2.5–3 h — ilovekg; to Jashyl-Kol 170 km, 3.5 h — hiking.kg). Then: cross the Chon-Kemin on horses and climb on foot; or approach along the left bank from the bridge downstream (20–25 km, hiking.kg); or from Issyk-Kul from Tamchy over the pass (2–3 days).
kg-0072.needcar: Yes: a car (an SUV on the upper sections of the valley) to the start in Chon-Kemin, plus horses for the crossing/approach. The sources name no regular transport to upper Chon-Kemin.
kg-0072.self: Partly: the walking approach along the left bank of the Chon-Kemin is possible for experienced hikers with a tent and navigation. The river crossing and the horse option — only with locals (CBT, guesthouses). There is no reliable crossing opposite Jashyl-Kol.
kg-0072.roadtype: Paved road to the valley (Bishkek–Balykchy highway); in Chon-Kemin a road that turns to dirt in the upper part (hiking.kg rates the drive to Jashyl-Kol 4 out of 5 for difficulty). To the lake — only a horse/foot trail with a river crossing.
kg-0072.traveltime: Bishkek → Chon-Kemin: 2.5–3 h (140 km, ilovekg); to the upper part of the valley (Jashyl-Kol) — 3.5 h (170 km, hiking.kg). A one-day tour takes 12 h, of which ~10 h is trail. From Tamchy — 2–3 days on horseback.
kg-0072.stay: At the lake — tents only. In the Chon-Kemin valley: CBT Chon-Kemin guesthouse (Karool-Debe, 7 rooms, yurt, 700–1200 som/person — travelbar.kg; +996 771 327 781); Ashuu guesthouse (Kalmak-Ashuu, 2GIS 4.9/5, 168 ratings, ashu.kg, +996 552 700 552); Kordon guest house (Kalmak-Ashuu); Kemin Guest House (Tar-Suu).
kg-0072.net: In the upper part of the Chon-Kemin valley the signal is poor — save offline maps (ilovekg); coverage at the lake is not confirmed (probably none). There is Wi-Fi in the guesthouses lower down (travelbar.kg).
kg-0072.entry: The lake is in Chon-Kemin National Park; tour operators mention the park entrance fee (Trip to Kyrgyzstan: the “park entrance fee” is not included in the tour), but the 2025–2026 amount was not found in open sources. Horses for the crossing are paid separately (Sputnik8).
kg-0072.transfer: One-day jeep tour from Bishkek $420 per group (Sputnik8, 2026); marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek–Balykchy to the turnoff 500–600 som (24.kg, 07.2026). Prices for renting horses and for a taxi to upper Chon-Kemin were not found.
kg-0072.bring: Trekking boots and sandals/spare shoes for the crossing, a rain jacket and warm clothes (2500 m, and storm protection on passes above 3300 m — Trip to Kyrgyzstan), water and food for the whole day, an offline map, a first-aid kit, cash for the horses. For a multi-day trip — a tent and sleeping bag.
kg-0072.warn: Crossing the Chon-Kemin is dangerous, especially during high water (May–July): there is no reliable crossing opposite Jashyl-Kol, and homemade suspension crossings are an unproven method (hiking.kg). There is no signal. It is a national park — follow the rules and don't light fires outside designated camps. Multi-day routes over passes above 3300 m carry a risk of bad weather and altitude sickness.
kg-0072.food: On tours — a picnic by the lake and a Kyrgyz dinner in a mountain cafe (Sputnik8); in Chon-Kemin guesthouses — home-cooked Kyrgyz food (CBT: partial board; CBT Tamchi and Trip to Kyrgyzstan — full board on horse tours). There are no eateries at the lake itself.
kg-0072.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 26 ratings (03.10.2026). Sputnik8 (one-day tour, guide Denis): 5.0 — “magical landscapes”, but “moderate physical effort” and cleanliness not perfect in places. No TripAdvisor/2GIS reviews of the lake itself were found.
kg-0072.p.sum: Kol-Kogur (≈2460–2500 m) is the “lost” lake of Chon-Kemin National Park. There is no road to it, and the main obstacle is crossing the Chon-Kemin River. So there are two realistic options. The first is to base yourself at a Chon-Kemin guesthouse (Ashuu in Kalmak-Ashuu, CBT in Karool-Debe, 700–1200 som/person), from where locals will take you across on horses and guide you to the lake in a day (≈10 h). The second is a horse trek from Issyk-Kul from Tamchy over Kol-Tor Pass (3320 m): 32 km and about 5 h in the saddle on the first day, 2–3 days in all. A direct marshrutka (minibus) runs from Bishkek to the Chon-Kemin villages (250 som, Kaktus 02.2026); you can also take a bus toward Balykchy to the turnoff, and then a taxi or a guesthouse transfer. Ready-made jeep tours from Bishkek start at $420 per car; horses for the crossing are paid separately.

kg-0073.name: Lake Chatyr-Kul
kg-0073.near: There are no permanent villages on the shore. The nearest places with accommodation are the Tash-Rabat caravanserai with its yurt camps (on the north side, over the Panda Pass, a 2-day horse/hiking trek of 44 km round trip) and the Torugart border/customs complex on the highway south of the lake. The town of Naryn is the base for the trip (about 2 h by car to Tash-Rabat). The earlier “Torugart ~10.6 km” is an OSM marker for the settlement at the checkpoint, not a tourist locality.
kg-0073.elev: 3,530 m (Nomad's Land, TripAdvisor); too.kg and Advantour round it to 3,500 m.
kg-0073.short: Chatyr-Kul is the third-largest lake in Kyrgyzstan (≈153–160 km²) at an elevation of 3,530 m between the At-Bashy and Torugart-Too ranges near the Chinese border; it is endorheic, fishless, and a Ramsar site within the Karatal-Japyryk Nature Reserve.
kg-0073.desc: A high-mountain endorheic lake of glacial origin lies in an intermontane basin between the At-Bashy Range and Torugart-Too, with the Bishkek–Kashgar highway running alongside it via the Torugart Pass. The area is 153.5 km² with a shoreline of 58 km (TripAdvisor) or 160 km² (Advantour), and the depth is up to 16.5–20 m. About 17 rivers flow into the lake, of which only one is permanent; there are no fish. For most of the year the lake is covered with ice: the average annual temperature is about −5 °C, down to −50 °C in winter, in summer the air warms up to +24 °C and the water to no more than +10 °C. The shores are marshy, and the vegetation is low, coarse grass. The lake is part of the Karatal-Japyryk State Nature Reserve and a Ramsar wetland: thousands of migratory birds stop here in summer, so you must not approach the water itself. The name is translated as “Heavenly Lake” / “roof lake”. A visit is possible only with a border-zone permit.
kg-0073.guide: The best way to see Chatyr-Kul is a two-day horse trek from Tash-Rabat over the Panda Pass (about 4,000 m): from the saddle the basin with the huge lake and the Torugart-Too range opens up in full. You spend the night in a yurt by the lake, and at dawn, if you are lucky, you will see flocks of migratory birds — this is a Ramsar site, so do not approach the water and keep your distance from the nesting areas. There are no fish in the lake and the ice stays for most of the year, so it can snow even in July. You will not be let in without a permit: arrange it in advance through CBT Naryn together with the trip to Tash-Rabat.
kg-0073.see: The panorama of the basin from the Panda Pass (≈4,000 m) on the trek from Tash-Rabat; migratory and waterbirds (Ramsar site); the snowy Torugart-Too range on the Chinese border; marshy shores and mineral springs (Nomad's Land); along the highway — a view of the lake on the way to Torugart.
kg-0073.skip: You have no time to arrange a border-zone permit (up to 1–2 weeks). You want to swim or go up to the water — the shore is a reserve and marshy. You tolerate altitudes of 3,500–4,000 m and unpredictable weather with snow in any month poorly.
kg-0073.diff: Moderate: the horse/hiking trek Tash-Rabat – Chatyr-Kul is 44 km over 2 days, gain ~1,350 m, the Panda Pass is about 4,000 m (snoezelsontheroad; CBT Naryn — “moderate”); on foot one way is 5–7 h (TripAdvisor). By car on the highway — easy, but only with a permit and within what is allowed.
kg-0073.when: July–August (the lake is under ice most of the year; snow is possible at any time of year — TripAdvisor). The yurt camps at Tash-Rabat operate in summer.
kg-0073.hours: Border zone and nature reserve: visits only with a border-zone permit; access to the shoreline is restricted to protect birds (TripAdvisor). There is no schedule.
kg-0073.daytime: Dawn and morning — birdwatching, calm weather, a clear view of Torugart-Too; on the trek set out early to cross the Panda Pass before the weather worsens in the afternoon (editorial).
kg-0073.how: 1) On foot/on horseback: from Naryn by car to Tash-Rabat (~2 h), then the trek over the Panda Pass to the lake and back the next day (CBT Naryn). 2) By car: along the Naryn–Torugart highway, which runs along the lake (Nomad's Land; central-asia.guide mentions a border checkpoint on the highway) — only with a permit, and stops and turn-offs to the shore are restricted.
kg-0073.needcar: Yes: there is no public transport to Tash-Rabat (snoezelsontheroad) — a taxi/transfer from Naryn; then a horse or on foot; or a car on the highway with a permit.
kg-0073.self: Partly: the permit is mandatory (CBT Naryn, tour.too.kg); the trek over Panda is not recommended without a guide — snoezelsontheroad calls the guide “indispensable”. Independent driving on the highway is possible only with a permit.
kg-0073.roadtype: To Tash-Rabat — the paved Naryn–Torugart highway and a dirt road to the caravanserai; then a horse/hiking trail over the Panda Pass. The Torugart highway along the lake is a main road (Bishkek–Kashgar direction).
kg-0073.traveltime: Naryn – Tash-Rabat ~2 h by car (snoezelsontheroad); Tash-Rabat – Chatyr-Kul 5–7 h on foot/on horseback one way (TripAdvisor); the whole trek is 2 days.
kg-0073.stay: A yurt camp on the lake shore as part of a CBT Naryn tour; yurt camps at Tash-Rabat — 1,500–2,000 som/person with breakfast and dinner, cash payment (snoezelsontheroad, 2025–2026). Also guesthouses in Naryn (CBT Naryn).
kg-0073.net: Not confirmed on operators’ coverage maps. On the trek and by the lake expect no signal; at the Torugart checkpoint a signal is possible (unconfirmed).
kg-0073.entry: No separate reserve fee for tourists was found. A border-zone permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn Region, one week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent; tour.too.kg — 3,000 som (all zones, 2026); about 2,000 som according to the snoezelsontheroad report.
kg-0073.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek – Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026). Horse — 1,500 som/day, guide — 2,500 som per group (snoezelsontheroad). The cost of the CBT Naryn tour and of a taxi Naryn – Tash-Rabat is not given in the sources — check with CBT Naryn.
kg-0073.bring: Your border-zone permit and passport; warm and waterproof clothing (snow at any time of year), a hat, gloves; sunscreen and sunglasses; binoculars for birds; cash som; trekking shoes; an altitude-sickness first-aid kit.
kg-0073.warn: It is a border zone near the Chinese border — you will not be let through without a permit. Nature reserve and Ramsar site: approaching the water, disturbing birds and camping on the shore outside permitted places are not allowed. The altitude is 3,530 m, the Panda Pass ~4,000 m; the weather changes abruptly. The existence of a road along the lake does not give you the right to drive freely down to the shore.
kg-0073.food: In the yurt camps at Tash-Rabat and at the lake — home-cooked dinner and breakfast (included in the 1,500–2,000 som); typical dishes are shorpo, beshbarmak, boorsok, kumis (editorial).
kg-0073.reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.6/5, 7 reviews, No. 2 of 3 in At-Bashy (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps: 4.8/5, 22 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, catalog check). Pros — powerful mountains, few tourists, inexpensive yurts with good food. Cons — unpredictable weather, a hard day on the trek, you cannot go up to the water, little information from operators in Naryn.
kg-0073.p.sum: There are two ways to Chatyr-Kul, both only with a border-zone permit. The best is from Tash-Rabat on foot or on horseback over the pass (≈3,996 m): 21.6 km one way, a night in a yurt camp by the lake, and back the next day (2 days; a horse at Tash-Rabat ≈1,500 som/day + a guide 2,500 som per group). The second is along the Naryn–Torugart highway, which runs along the southern shore: views from the car, but swamps and reserve rules prevent you from driving up to the water, and the permit is checked at the posts. The base is the yurt camps of Tash-Rabat (1,500–2,000 som with breakfast and dinner; Ak-Sai — from $65) or Naryn; fill up your tank in Naryn.
