kg-0087.name: Kok-Kyya Valley
kg-0087.near: There are no permanent villages: at the head of the valley is a seasonal camp of ~20 yurts (the end of the road) and summer camps of yak herders. The last sizable settlement is At-Bashy; the town of Naryn is about 100 km as the crow flies (Nomad's Land) and 150–200 km by road. The earlier “Karaul-Tobe ~45 km” is a straight line across the ridges and is no guide for a trip.
kg-0087.elev: About 3300 m (canyon, Nomad's Land); the yurt camps at the head of the valley are on the order of 3300–3400 m (not precisely confirmed). TripAdvisor gives 3514 m — this is probably the elevation of Lake Kel-Suu.
kg-0087.short: Kok-Kyya is a remote border valley in the Ak-Sai basin with a winding canyon of the river of the same name (walls 300–400 m) and yurt camps — the base for the hike to Lake Kel-Suu.
kg-0087.desc: The Kok-Kyya River flows out of Lake Kel-Suu (Kol-Too and Sary-Beles mountains), meanders for about 40 km across the Kapshygay plateau, cutting a series of rock canyons, and joins the Kakshaal, which flows into China (Nomad's Land). The canyon walls rise 300–400 m, the granite gradually gives way to limestone, and dark cave entrances are visible in the rocks (eurasia.travel). The main occupation of the locals is yak breeding. The road ends at the head of the valley: here stand seasonal yurt camps (~20 yurts), from which it is 8–12 km to Kel-Suu on foot or on horseback, with a river ford. The valley lies in the border zone — a permit is needed, which is checked at the post after Kyndy Pass. In 2026 locals complained of trash and overloading by tourist traffic (time.kg, 14.08.2026).
kg-0087.guide: People often drive straight through Kok-Kyya on the way to Kel-Suu, and they shouldn't: stop at the canyon, where the river cuts through the plateau with walls of 300–400 meters, and look for the black cave entrances. Yak herders live here — you'll see herds of yaks on the meadows, and at the camp they'll pour you tea with kaymak. Stay overnight in a yurt at the head of the valley so you can set out for the lake at dawn, while the water at the ford is low. If you have time left, walk down the river — the change from granite to limestone is clearly visible in the walls. There is no signal here, so warn your family in advance.
kg-0087.see: The Kok-Kyya River canyon with walls of 300–400 m and caves; the change from granite to limestone; herds of yaks and summer camps; fords across the river; yurt camps at the head of the valley; the 8–12 km foot/horse route to Lake Kel-Suu.
kg-0087.skip: You aren't going to Kel-Suu — it's not worth spending 3 days and arranging a permit just for the valley. You count on comfort: the camps have mattresses on the floor, a stove and outdoor toilets. Late June is still cold and snowy, and from September the camps close.
kg-0087.diff: The road — high (4×4, gravel “washboard,” bogs, fords); staying at the camp — easy; the walk to the lake — moderate (~12 km round trip with almost no ascent, a ford — OunTravela). Elevation ~3300 m.
kg-0087.when: Mid-July to late August (NomadCar); the camps operate from late June to early September (kgnomad, 2026). TripAdvisor: season July to early September. In June snow is possible, in September there are night frosts, and in winter (down to −40 °C in neighboring Ak-Sai) the road is impassable.
kg-0087.hours: An open natural area in the border zone — permit only; the yurt camps are seasonal (late June to early September), and 2GIS gives “around the clock” for Kel-Suu Yurt Camp in season.
kg-0087.daytime: Morning — for the fords and the walk to the lake (the water rises by 30–50 cm after noon — NomadCar); evening — for the light in the canyon and on the slopes (editorial).
kg-0087.how: Bishkek → Naryn (≈350 km) → At-Bashy → Kyndy Pass (3400 m) and the border post → Ak-Sai valley → down the Kok-Kyya valley to the camps (the end of the road). From Naryn 150–200 km, 4–8 h (Kabar, OunTravela, kgnomad); 4×4 / SUV only.
kg-0087.needcar: Yes, a prepared 4×4 with an experienced local driver (clearance of 200–220 mm or more, low-range gear — NomadCar); there is no public transport.
kg-0087.self: With restrictions: the permit is arranged in advance (CBT Naryn — €30–50, tour.too.kg — 3000 som), and you can go only with a prepared 4×4 and a local driver; navigation and fords are dangerous without experience.
kg-0087.roadtype: Gravel/dirt with “washboard” from Naryn via Kyndy and Ak-Sai, then boggy sections and river fords (NomadCar); in the valley, a rutted dirt road to the camps; the At-Bashy — Kyndy — Torugart road was graded in 08.2026 (time.kg).
kg-0087.traveltime: Bishkek — Naryn ~5–6 h; Naryn — Kok-Kyya camps 4–8 h depending on the road and ford conditions (OunTravela 4–5 h; Kabar 5–6 h; kgnomad 5–8 h).
kg-0087.stay: Yurt camps at the head of the valley: Kel-Suu Yurt Camp (2GIS: from 1800 som, up to 40 beds, breakfast, cafe, horses; +996 552 979 696), Golden Moon (kgnomad), Jyrgal's Yurt Camp. 2024 prices (too.kg): a yurt for 2 — 1700 som/person with breakfast, for 4–7 — 1500 som/person, meals 800 som; 2026 (kgnomad): 1500–2500+ som/person with meals. Conditions are simple: mattresses on the floor, a stove, an outdoor toilet (NomadCar).
kg-0087.net: There is no mobile signal (NomadCar, kgnomad 2026; too.kg); some camps have Wi-Fi (2GIS — Kel-Suu Yurt Camp), the type and quality are not confirmed.
kg-0087.entry: No fee for entering the valley was found. A border permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region, one week) / €50 urgent; tour.too.kg — 3000 som (2026).
kg-0087.transfer: Jeep Naryn — Kok-Kyya — Naryn: 13,000–20,000+ som per car, ≈3500–5000 som/person for four (kgnomad, 07.2026). Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026).
kg-0087.bring: Border permit and passport; warm clothes and a sleeping bag/thermal underwear (0…−5 °C at night), a rain jacket, sunscreen and sunglasses; shoes for fords; cash in som; a flashlight, power bank, offline maps; a trash bag.
kg-0087.warn: A border zone on the border with China — they won't let you through without a permit. The fords across the Kok-Kyya are dangerous in flood and in the second half of the day. Elevation ~3300 m, abrupt weather. No signal or medical aid — report your route in advance. Don't set off on your own routes in the valley without clearing it: exact directions are confirmed with the border guards (eurasia.travel).
kg-0087.food: In the yurt camps — home-style Kyrgyz cooking: beshbarmak, shorpo, boorsok, kaymak, dairy products from yaks and mares (editorial; meals ~800 som each — too.kg 2024).
kg-0087.reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 9 reviews, No. 3 of 16 in Naryn (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps “Kok-Kyya Canyon” — no rating (check 03.10.2026). Pros: wild nature, yaks, canyons, few people; cons: a very hard and expensive road, fords without bridges, a short season, the need for a permit; in 2026 — complaints about trash (time.kg).
kg-0087.p.sum: Kok-Kyya is the end of the road and the base for Lake Kel-Suu: yurt camps stand here (Kel-Suu Yurt Camp, Meder's camp, Jyrgal and others). You can get here only with a border permit and in a 4×4 with a driver: Naryn → At-Bashy → Kyndy → Ak-Sai, ≈145–160 km, 4.5–6 h (a round-trip jeep 13,000–20,000+ som per car). A night in a yurt 1500–2500 som with meals, in the morning to the lake on foot 7.5–9 km, on horseback ≈2000–2500 som or by UAZ 10,000 som/car. Fill up, withdraw cash and stock up in Naryn.

kg-0087.p.iti.3.title: From the west via Chatyr-Kol
kg-0087.p.iti.3.plan: Tash-Rabat → the Bishkek—Kashgar highway → along Chatyr-Kol → Ak-Sai valley → Kok-Kyya: 205 km in a day (Nomad's Land) — with one permit it combines Tash-Rabat, Chatyr-Kol and Kel-Suu without returning to Naryn.
kg-0087.p.season: Late June — 25 September: the camps operate (best mid-July to August). June — snow and high fords; September — night frosts and few tourists. October to May: the road through Ak-Sai is under snow, the camps are closed (Meder's family has a herder's house/trailer in winter by arrangement, Nomad's Land).
kg-0087.p.budget.economy: ≈12,000–17,000 som/person for 3 days (group of 4): marshrutka 600×2, jeep 3500–5000, permit 3000, yurt 2 nights ≈3000–5000, horse 2000 or on foot.
kg-0087.p.permits: A border permit is mandatory (the border zone of At-Bashy district on the border with China). Ways to arrange it: 1) tour.too.kg — 3000 som (all border zones) / $35 for the Kel-Suu—Kok-Kyya—Chatyr-Kol zone; 5–7 working days; office at Isanov St. 105/3, Bishkek (2026). 2) CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region only, ~1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent in 2 working days (stage 1); Nomad's Land: from Naryn it's fastest — a few days, via Bishkek — up to 2 weeks. Step by step: (1) send a scan of your passport and the trip dates (WhatsApp/form); (2) pay a 50% prepayment; (3) the Border Service reviews it for ~1 week; (4) pick up the paper original in Bishkek or Naryn (or via a guide/tour — then send a copy of your passport a few days ahead). The permit is valid for up to 1 month. It is checked at military posts at Kyndy Pass/the entrance to the Ak-Sai valley (2 posts per Eurasia Travel) — you need the original permit with the stamp and your passport. Photographing the posts is forbidden. No fee for entering the lake/valley was found. JoN (04.2026) advises applying for the permit through CBT Naryn at least 2 weeks ahead; if traveling independently the driver needs a permit too.
kg-0087.p.access: With children — from school age (elevation ~3300 m, long jolting, fords); life at the camp is simple — mattresses on the floor, a stove, an outdoor toilet, no hot shower (JoN). Older people — only in good health. With a stroller — not accessible. With a dog — not advisable (herding dogs, border zone).

kg-0088.name: Orto-Tokoy Reservoir
kg-0088.near: Orto-Tokoy village — ~2 km from the dam (Asiamixtravel); Kochkor — ~20 km to the south; Balykchy — ~20 km to the northeast; the Kok-Moinok canyons — 20 km.
kg-0088.elev: About 1700 m above sea level (Wikijournal, Asiamixtravel); the water level changes by tens of meters with the season.
kg-0088.short: Orto-Tokoy is Kyrgyzstan's first artificial lake (1956–1960) on the Chu river between Balykchy and Kochkor: 18 km of turquoise water among bare hills, a convenient stop on the way to Song-Kol and Naryn.
kg-0088.desc: The Orto-Tokoy Reservoir was built on the Chu river where it leaves the Kochkor valley (construction 1941–1960, filling from 1956) to irrigate the Chu valley and southern Kazakhstan. Design parameters: volume ~470 million m³, area ~25–26 km², length ~18 km, depth up to 47 m, and a dam 52 m high and 365 m long. In spring the reservoir is almost full, and by the end of summer the level drops noticeably — in the low-water year 2023 the bottom was exposed (inflow 250 million m³ against 360 million in 2021). The color of the water ranges from soft blue to emerald and almost black depending on the stretch; around are treeless hills, and Bactrian camels graze along the shores. The A-363 road Balykchy — Kochkor runs along the north shore, so people mostly view the reservoir from the roadside and stop for a picnic; fishing (marinka, osman, trout, whitefish), camping and SUP are possible. There is no beach infrastructure, rental or lifeguards; walking on the ice is forbidden in winter.
kg-0088.guide: Don't plan a separate trip here — but don't just drive past either: on the road from Balykchy to Kochkor and Song-Kol, find a wide pull-off by the A-363 above the water, where the color shifts from turquoise to inky. It is best in spring and early summer, when the basin is full; by September the water recedes, and the exposed bottom with sticky silt looks bleak (in 2023 it showed completely). Look for Bactrian camels on the shore — they are grazed here. If you are going with a fishing rod, ask in Kochkor about spawning bans; nets are prohibited. For a night, choose shallow bays far from the road, and bring warm clothes — even in summer the water is rarely warmer than +15 °C.
kg-0088.see: The shore landscape of the reservoir on the Chu; the outlines of the shores and the color of the water change with the level — from turquoise to emerald; the dam (52 m) near Orto-Tokoy village; camels on the shore; spring high water and the autumn “terraces” of the exposed bottom; in winter — ice (walking on it is forbidden).
kg-0088.skip: You are not driving along the Balykchy — Kochkor road: as a standalone destination the reservoir is “not particularly memorable” (TripAdvisor reviews). Late summer/autumn of a low-water year — instead of a lake there will be silt and bare bottom. You need an equipped beach — there isn't one.
kg-0088.diff: Very easy: a stop by the road, a 50–100 m descent to the water down a slope; for camping — dirt turn-offs.
kg-0088.when: Spring — early summer (April — June): a full basin and green slopes; July — August for swimming (cold water) and camping; in autumn the level is low; in winter — photos of the ice, without walking on it.
kg-0088.hours: Open territory, around the clock; the dam is a hydraulic facility, and access to the structures is restricted (guarded by the Water Resources Service).
kg-0088.daytime: Morning and evening — calm water and color without glare; in the daytime the treeless shores are hot and windy.
kg-0088.how: From Bishkek through Boom Gorge and Balykchy, then along the A-363 towards Kochkor — the road runs along the north shore; ~190 km, 3–3.5 h. From Kochkor ~20 km north. Stop at the wide pull-offs by the road; the turn-offs to the water are dirt.
kg-0088.needcar: Yes: the reservoir is along the road, and without your own car — only in passing on a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi with a stop on request.
kg-0088.self: Yes: free access to the shores from the road; follow the roadside parking rules, don't approach the dam and spillway, don't walk on the ice, take your litter away; fishing — observing spawning bans, nets are prohibited.
kg-0088.roadtype: Paved A-363 along the north shore; turn-offs to the water are dirt, in places across the exposed bottom (sticky silt — don't drive onto it).
kg-0088.traveltime: Bishkek — reservoir ~190 km, 3–3.5 h; Balykchy — 20–30 min; Kochkor — 20–30 min; a stop of 15–30 min, picnic/camping — as you wish.
kg-0088.stay: On the shore — only wild camping (no infrastructure). The nearest accommodation: CBT Kochkor guesthouses and hotels in Kochkor (20 km), hotels in Balykchy (20 km). 2025–2026 prices are not confirmed.
kg-0088.net: Along the A-363 there is operator coverage (the settlements of Orto-Tokoy, Kok-Moinok, Kochkor); in bays behind the hills the signal weakens. There are no reports by operator.
kg-0088.entry: Free: sources mention no fees for access to the shore.
kg-0088.transfer: Train Bishkek — Balykchy 40–60 som (summer 2024); marshrutka Bishkek — Kochkor: the 2025 price is not confirmed (a guide — Bishkek — Karakol 500 som in 2024); taxi Balykchy — Orto-Tokoy by arrangement.
kg-0088.bring: A windbreaker (open shores), sun protection, water and food (there are no cafes by the water), a picnic mat, trash bags; for camping — a tent with good pegs (wind), for fishing — tackle and knowledge of the bans; warm clothes for swimming (+15 °C).
kg-0088.warn: The water level fluctuates greatly: by the end of summer and in low-water years (2023) the water recedes, and the bottom is sticky silt — don't drive or walk onto it. In winter walking on the ice is forbidden. The dam and spillway are a restricted facility. Park only at wide pull-offs, fully off the carriageway of the A-363. Cold water, sharp wind. Administratively this is Naryn Region — keep this in mind when planning routes and insurance.
kg-0088.food: There are no cafes at the reservoir. In Kochkor — CBT families with home cooking, beshbarmak, kumys in summer; in Balykchy and on the road — Issyk-Kul fish and roadside cafes (“Ak-Jol” at the turn to Kochkor).
kg-0088.reviews: Google Maps (“Orto-Tokoy reservoir”): 4.8/5, 76 ratings as of 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor “Orto-Tokoy Water Reservoir” (Kochkor, Naryn Region): 3.9/5, 10 reviews, No. 2 of 5 in Kochkor (07.10.2026). Pluses: bright blue water in summer, a good stop on a long drive, camels; minuses: “nothing special” unless you are passing through; no infrastructure.
kg-0088.photos.1.cap: Naryn Region, Orto-Tokoy above the water
kg-0088.p.sum: Orto-Tokoy is a photo stop by the A-363 Balykchy — Kochkor road (20 km to each, 20–30 minutes, ≈190 km from Bishkek). The road runs along the north shore; stop at the wide pull-offs. Without a car, any marshrutka Bishkek — Kochkor or Naryn will do (350–600 som, 2026): ask to be dropped off by the water. It is best in spring and early summer while the basin is full; by the end of summer the bottom may be exposed, as in 2023. For a night — wild camping in the bays or CBT guesthouses in Kochkor. Fishing is possible: in 03.2026, 1.2 million whitefish fry were released into the reservoir, and nets are prohibited.

kg-0089.name: Besh-Tash National Park
kg-0089.near: Kojuchak — the village at the gorge entrance (Lonely Planet); Beshtash — ~12.9 km in a straight line from the catalogue point (OSM). The town of Talas is ~13 km north of the start of the park (central-asia.guide).
kg-0089.elev: From 1,100 to 3,500–3,600 m (too.kg — up to 3,500 m; central-asia.guide — up to 3,600 m); the main lake is at about 3,000 m.
kg-0089.short: A nature park in the Talas Ala-Too (established 1996) along the 30-km Besh-Tash Gorge: juniper and spruce forests, eight mountain lakes, rare animals and the turquoise Lake Besh-Tash at ~3,000 m.
kg-0089.desc: Besh-Tash State Nature Park was established in 1996 in the Talas Range mountains south of the town of Talas and covers the gorges of Besh-Tash, Kolba, Kumush-Tag and Urmaral (too.kg; nomad.kg). Elevations range from 1,100 to 3,500–3,600 m; the park has eight mountain lakes, the largest being Besh-Tash (~3,000 m, depth 28 m) (too.kg; central-asia.guide). Flora — more than 800 plant species, including Tian Shan spruce and the endemic Semenov's fir, juniper, sea buckthorn; fauna — snow leopard, Turkestan lynx, brown bear, golden eagle, bearded vulture, maral (Altai red deer) (about 100 marals were brought in 2022) (nomad.kg; map.kg; central-asia.guide). Hunting is prohibited, and poaching is monitored with camera traps (map.kg, 2024). The area differs between sources: 13,701 ha (central-asia.guide) and more than 30,000 ha (nomad.kg). The name means “five stones” — from a legend about robbers and five stones in the gorge (too.kg).
kg-0089.guide: Besh-Tash is the most accessible “real” mountain park in Talas: the gorge entrance is only 13 km from the town, and the road along the river valley runs almost 30 km to a turquoise lake at three thousand metres. Pay the fee at the checkpoint (250 som per person and 400 per car), then choose: in a passenger car — a picnic and a night by the river; in an SUV or on foot — to the lake. Look for Semenov's fir in the forest — an endemic found almost nowhere else — and keep an eye on the slopes: maral live in the park, and camera traps catch the tracks of snow leopards. In May–June the slopes are full of tulips; in September there is golden autumn and sea buckthorn.
kg-0089.see: The gorges of Besh-Tash, Kolba, Kumush-Tag and Urmaral; Lake Besh-Tash (~3,000 m) and the other of the eight mountain lakes; forests of Tian Shan spruce, Semenov's fir and juniper; the “five stones” in the gorge; tulips in bloom (May–June); sea buckthorn and golden autumn (September) (too.kg; nomad.kg).
kg-0089.skip: You've already been to Ala-Archa or the Karakol park and aren't planning an overnight stay — a day trip will give similar views. You have no SUV and no strength for 20–25 km on foot to the lake. You're looking for developed infrastructure — there is almost none here.
kg-0089.diff: Easy — walks and picnics in the lower part of the gorge by the checkpoint; medium — the hike to the lake (20–25 km one way) or the TUK loop trek; hard — multi-day treks (for example, the 9-day Explore-Share trek) (nomad.kg; tuk.kg).
kg-0089.when: May–June — tulips and blossoms; July–August — passes are open, it is warm, yurt camps operate; September — golden autumn, sea buckthorn; in winter access is limited and trails are under snow (nomad.kg).
kg-0089.hours: Entry is through the park checkpoint with payment of the fee; the checkpoint's opening hours are not published. In winter access is limited (nomad.kg).
kg-0089.daytime: Morning — for the drive to the lake and clear air; in the evening it gets cold quickly in the gorge (editorial).
kg-0089.how: From Talas south ~13 km to the gorge entrance at Kojuchak (central-asia.guide; Lonely Planet), then along a dirt road beside the Besh-Tash River to the checkpoint; from the checkpoint to the lake 20–25 km (nomad.kg). To Talas from Bishkek: GoBus via Kazakhstan (500 som, Kaktus 06.2025) or a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi via Suusamyr and Otmok (~350 / from ~650 som). Your own car from Bishkek — about 4 h to the park (map.kg); fee for the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels at the Sosnovka post: 50 som (Kyrgyz) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024.
kg-0089.needcar: Yes: a taxi or your own car from Talas to the checkpoint; inside the park — an SUV, on foot or on horseback (through CBT Talas).
kg-0089.self: Yes: no permit needed, only the fee at the checkpoint. For long routes and horse treks a CBT Talas guide is better; there is no mobile coverage in the upper part of the gorge.
kg-0089.roadtype: Paved road Talas — Kojuchak; then a dirt road along the gorge: to the checkpoint — passenger cars, further on — an SUV (nomad.kg).
kg-0089.traveltime: Bishkek — park ~4 h by car (map.kg, 2024; by public transport to Talas 5.5–8 h); Talas — gorge entrance ~20–30 min (estimate, 13 km).
kg-0089.stay: Equipped camping zones at different elevations, campfires allowed (map.kg, 2024); in summer — yurt camps in the gorge (nomad.kg; names and prices not found); at the lake — tents. Guesthouses — in Talas ($10–30, kyrgyzstan-tourism.com) and through CBT Talas.
kg-0089.net: There is no mobile coverage at the lake or in the upper part of the gorge (too.kg); in the lower part at Kojuchak — not confirmed.
kg-0089.entry: 250 som per person and 400 som per car (nomad.kg; publication year not given). At the entrance there is a gate where the fee is paid (central-asia.guide).
kg-0089.transfer: Not confirmed: a taxi/SUV from Talas — by arrangement. To Talas: GoBus 500 som (2025), marshrutka ~350 som, shared taxi from ~650 som.
kg-0089.bring: Cash for the fee (250 som/person + 400 som/car), a tent and warm clothes if staying overnight, water purification, repellent, trekking shoes; food — there are no shops inside the park.
kg-0089.warn: A protected area: hunting is prohibited, camera traps are in operation (map.kg). Brown bears live in the park — store your food properly. No mobile coverage in the upper part. Without an SUV, the lake is reachable only on foot, 20–25 km. In winter access is limited (snow).
kg-0089.food: Kumys and home cooking at the yurt camps in summer (not confirmed for specific places); sea buckthorn in September (nomad.kg); in Talas — dishes with Talas beans.
kg-0089.reviews: Google Maps: 5.0 from 7 ratings (listed as “Besh-Tash State Nature National Park”, catalogue check 10.2026). No large sample of reviews was found on TripAdvisor/2GIS.
kg-0089.p.sum: Besh-Tash National Park begins ~13 km south of Talas at the village of Kojuchak: at the entrance there is an automated checkpoint (since 28.07.2026; 250 som/person and 400 som/car according to the latest data), then a dirt road along the river with camping zones and summer yurts. A passenger car is enough for a picnic and a walk in the lower gorge, but for the upper meadows and the lake you need a 4×4. Stay overnight in Talas or in a tent; look for guides and horses through CBT Talas.

kg-0090.name: Saimaluu-Tash
kg-0090.near: Kazarman — the centre of Toguz-Toro District and the start of all routes: ~38 km by dirt road to the foot of the mountain (Nomad's Land), then a climb on foot or horseback. To Kazarman: 157 km from Jalal-Abad, 220 km from Naryn (CBT Kazarman).
kg-0090.elev: About 3000–3200 m: a plateau “above 3000 m” (too.kg, CBT Kyrgyzstan); travellers in 2025 — about 3100 m with the trail starting at ~2000 m (takali.org). The climb from Kazarman is about 1970 m (Nomad's Land).
kg-0090.short: One of the largest “galleries” of rock art in Central Asia — more than 90,000 images from the Bronze and early Iron Ages on basalt boulders in a high-mountain tract of the Fergana Range; accessible only in summer.
kg-0090.desc: Saimaluu-Tash (“patterned stones”) is a high-mountain tract on the eastern slope of the Fergana Range, where more than 90,000 petroglyphs have been carved into black basalt boulders (too.kg, CBT Kyrgyzstan). The drawings are dated from the 3rd–1st millennia BC to the 1st–8th centuries AD: animals, hunting scenes, people, solar signs and “sun-headed” deities, geometric symbols. Since 2001 the territory has been a state nature park (decree no. 249 of 25.05.2001; boundaries clarified in 2018, 24.kg). There are proposals to digitize the site and nominate it for the UNESCO World Heritage List (Kaktus) — it is not on the list yet, despite CBT's wording. Because of snow, the tract is accessible only from about mid-July to mid-August (CBT Kazarman); modern vandalism is visible on the stones (takali.org, 2025).
kg-0090.guide: Saimaluu-Tash is an expedition, not an excursion: after 38 km of dirt road from Kazarman you face 5 hours in the saddle or a steep 4–6 hour climb on foot, and on the plateau a night in a tent at 3000+ m. But you will find yourself among tens of thousands of drawings up to 4–5 thousand years old: look for bulls with huge horns, ploughing scenes and “sun-headed” people. Plan the trip for the second half of July — early August: in 2023 and 2024 snow lay longer than usual. Take a guide from Kazarman — the trail and the river ford have to be found anew in different years. Don't touch or trace the drawings — they are already being spoiled by modern inscriptions.
kg-0090.see: Fields of basalt boulders with petroglyphs (more than 90,000 images): ibexes, bulls, horses, hunting and ploughing scenes, chariots, solar signs and anthropomorphic “sun-headed” figures; alpine meadows and views of the Fergana Range; the night sky from the plateau (too.kg; CBT Kyrgyzstan).
kg-0090.skip: You don't have 2–3 days and the physical fitness for a climb to 3000+ m with a night in a tent. You aren't travelling in July — August: the rest of the time the petroglyphs are under snow. Simpler petroglyphs will do for you — for example the open-air museum in Cholpon-Ata.
kg-0090.diff: Hard: 7.5 km one way with a gain of ~1100 m (from ~2000 to ~3100 m), 4–6 h up and ~2 h down, steep slippery sections, fords, and at the start of the season thickets of thistles and nettles (takali.org, 07.2025). The horse option is 2 × 2.5 h in the saddle via Besh-Beren (Nomad's Land). A night at altitude is required.
kg-0090.when: The window is roughly mid-July to mid-August (CBT Kazarman); too.kg and CBT Kyrgyzstan say July — August; Nomad's Land offers a tour from 15 June to 30 September. In 2023 and 2024 the snow melted late — travellers advise going from mid-July (takali.org, 2025).
kg-0090.hours: No schedule: a nature park, round-the-clock access in season. A park ranger collects a fee at the fenced parking lot at the start of the trail (takali.org, 2025). Out of season (September — June) the approach is effectively closed by snow.
kg-0090.daytime: Leave Kazarman early in the morning (Nomad's Land) to reach the petroglyphs by noon. The drawings read better in the slanting light of morning and evening; in the evening there can be a strong wind on the plateau (takali.org).
kg-0090.how: 1) To Kazarman: from Jalal-Abad — 157 km; since 01.06.2026 the alternative North — South road Balykchy — Jalal-Abad (433 km) with the Kok-Art tunnel (~3.9 km) has been temporarily open, traffic 06:00–20:00, a toll of 100–5000 som depending on the vehicle, in operation until November 2026 (Kaktus, lada.kz 01.06.2026). From Naryn — 220 km (CBT Kazarman). 2) Kazarman — the foot of the mountain: ~38 km on a gravel road (Nomad's Land; too.kg — first ~10 km west). 3) The climb: on foot 7.5 km / 4–6 h or on horseback ~5 h via Besh-Beren.
kg-0090.needcar: Yes: to Kazarman — marshrutka (minibus)/taxi, from Kazarman to the start of the trail — an SUV or an arrangement with a local driver (travellers in 2025 hitchhiked). Then on foot or by horse.
kg-0090.self: Technically yes (travellers did it on their own in 2025, hitchhiking to the trail), but the trail is poorly marked and the fords and snow bridges change from year to year — a CBT Kazarman guide is recommended. No border permit is required (outside the border zone). The park fee is collected at the parking lot.
kg-0090.roadtype: To Kazarman — the paved new alternative North — South road (some sections are still under construction, 2026 restrictions); Kazarman — foot of the mountain — ~38 km of gravel/dirt road (Nomad's Land); then a mountain trail with steep slippery sections and fords.
kg-0090.traveltime: Jalal-Abad — Kazarman: 157 km, roughly 3–4 h (estimate); Balykchy — Jalal-Abad on the new road ~6 h (lada.kz, 2026). Kazarman — foot of the mountain: ~1–1.5 h on dirt road (estimate). The climb: 4–6 h on foot / ~5 h on horseback; the descent ~2 h (takali.org 2025; Nomad's Land). Plan at least 2 days with a night out.
kg-0090.stay: At the petroglyphs — tents only (camping 300 som, takali.org 2025); boil water from streams and springs (too.kg). In Kazarman — guesthouses at $15–45/night depending on the season and meals (visitkyrgyzstan.org); Guesthouse Islam (in the Nomad's Land catalogue); book via CBT Kazarman. In July — August cycling groups take up the rooms — book in advance.
kg-0090.net: There is no mobile signal at the petroglyphs (too.kg). Kazarman has coverage (operator not confirmed).
kg-0090.entry: 300–400 som for entry and 300 som for camping — collected by the nature park ranger at the parking lot at the start of the trail (takali.org, 07.2025). The park's official price list was not found.
kg-0090.transfer: A guide with a day trip — 4000–9000 som (2025 quotes, takali.org); the Kok-Art tunnel — from 100 som for cars (2026). Prices of marshrutkas (minibuses) to Kazarman and of a jeep Kazarman — foot of the mountain are not published.
kg-0090.bring: A tent, a warm sleeping bag and a down jacket (nights are cold at 3100 m), long trousers and sleeves (thistles, nettles), trekking poles, shoes for fords, a stove and a water filter/tablets, cash (300–700 som for park fees), sun protection. Food for all days — there is nothing on the plateau.
kg-0090.warn: The access window is about a month (mid-July — mid-August); outside it there is snow. Altitude 3100 m — risk of altitude sickness, a night out is mandatory. Fords and snow bridges are unreliable. The alternative North — South road with the Kok-Art tunnel is open only temporarily in 2026 (06:00–20:00, until November) and closes in winter because of avalanches. The petroglyphs are a protected monument: do not touch, trace or write on the stones. There is no signal on the plateau.
kg-0090.food: In Kazarman — home cooking at guesthouses; at the summer pastures on the way — kumis and ayran from shepherds (typical for a jailoo, not confirmed by a specific source).
kg-0090.reviews: Google Maps: a “Saimaluu Tash” marker was found, the rating was not recorded in the cross-check (07.10.2026). Travellers (takali.org 2025, CNN) call the place an impressive “museum under the sky”; cons — a hard climb, late snow, modern vandalism on the stones.
kg-0090.p.sum: Saimaluu-Tash is a 2–3 day expedition in the window of mid-July to mid-August. The trail starts at the Kok-Art River, off the Jalal-Abad — Kazarman road (the new North — South road through the Kok-Art tunnel): from the south you can drive straight from Jalal-Abad, from the north via Kazarman (≈38 km, of which ~28 km is dirt road). Then 7.5 km and +1100 m on foot (4–6 h) or ~5 h on horseback via Besh-Beren, a night in a tent below the petroglyphs (fee 300–400 som + camping 300 som). CBT Kazarman (+996 777 688 803) arranges the jeep, horses and guide.

kg-0091.name: Alamedin Gorge
kg-0091.near: Koi-Tash is the last village on the approach to the gorge (on the Hiking.kg route: Kok-Jar → Besh-Kungei → Tash-Moinok → Koi-Tash); Bishkek is 30–35 km to the north (too.kg, Hiking.kg). “Tatyr 7.7 km” is a straight-line calculation, not an access route.
kg-0091.elev: The Teplye Klyuchi (Warm Springs) resort is at about 2,000 m (sxodim, 2022); the gain from the parking lot to the Teke-Tor waterfall is about 370 m (Hiking.kg), i.e. the waterfall is roughly ~2,300 m (calculation). Usechenko Peak above the gorge is 4,650 m (2GIS).
kg-0091.short: Alamedin is the mountain gorge closest to Bishkek (30–35 km), with the Teplye Klyuchi radon hot springs and the Teke-Tor waterfall.
kg-0091.desc: Alamedin is the mountain gorge of the Alamedin River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range, about 30 km south of Bishkek; it is called the gorge closest to the capital (too.kg). The paved road goes up to the Teplye Klyuchi resort — the only radon spring on the Kyrgyz Range: a 25 m pool, a mud-therapy clinic, water at 50–55 °C (too.kg, sxodim). From the end of the road it is about 5 km to the waterfall (Teke-Tor); farther up are the “Quiet Backwater” grove at the confluence of the Salyk stream and the Alamedin, Lake Altyn-Tor ~20 km away, and the Alamedin Pass into the Issyk-Ata gorge for the experienced (too.kg). The gorge has birch and juniper forests, berry meadows, and views of glaciers and Usechenko Peak (4,650 m); there are horseback rides, kymyz and a café (2GIS).
kg-0091.guide: Come in the morning: Hiking.kg warns that by evening the western slope shades the valley early. The classic is the 5.7 km trail to the Teke-Tor waterfall (about 2 h 10 min one way, gain ~370 m), and afterwards a hot radon pool at Teplye Klyuchi to loosen your legs. Drink water from springs, not from the river — livestock graze higher up the gorge (too.kg). The signal drops after about the 10th kilometer, at the resort, so an offline map does not hurt. If you want more, go to the “Quiet Backwater” grove by the Salyk stream, while the prepared continue to Lake Altyn-Tor (~20 km).
kg-0091.see: The Alamedin River, birch and juniper forests and meadows; the Teke-Tor waterfall (5.7 km from the parking lot); the radon springs and pool of Teplye Klyuchi; the “Quiet Backwater” grove by the Salyk stream; Lake Altyn-Tor (~20 km up the valley); views of the glaciers and Usechenko Peak, 4,650 m (too.kg, Hiking.kg, 2GIS).
kg-0091.skip: You are going on a weekend and dislike crowds — this is one of the most visited gorges near Bishkek (per video and 2GIS, 2,500+ ratings). You want wilderness without cafés and cottages — Kegety or Ala-Archa higher up the trails are better. You have already been to Ala-Archa and do not want hot springs — the scenery is similar.
kg-0091.diff: The approach is paved, easy. The trail to Teke-Tor: 2/5 on the Hiking.kg scale, 5.7 km one way, gain ~370 m; there is a steep section at the waterfall. The hike to Altyn-Tor and the Alamedin Pass are for the experienced (too.kg).
kg-0091.when: May–October for hiking (editorial: greenery, dry trails); the Teplye Klyuchi springs work year-round, and the road to the resort is paved. In winter the trail to the waterfall ices over — crampons/ice grips are needed (Hiking.kg).
kg-0091.hours: The gorge is open 24 hours; entry and parking are free (too.kg). The working hours of the Teplye Klyuchi resort and pool are not given on the pages — check by tel. +996 312 36-66-18, +996 773 48-58-80 (sxodim).
kg-0091.daytime: Early morning: in the evening the western slope shades the valley (Hiking.kg); also, before noon there are fewer people on the trail to the waterfall.
kg-0091.how: From Bishkek south along Shabdan Baatyr Avenue / via Kok-Jar, Besh-Kungei, Tash-Moinok and Koi-Tash to the start of the trail in the gorge — 35 km, about 1 h 10 min (Hiking.kg); paved to the Teplye Klyuchi resort (too.kg). Public transport does not run to the gorge — a taxi or a tour (sxodim).
kg-0091.needcar: Yes: a car, taxi or transfer to the parking lot at the resort; beyond that on foot. There is no public transport in the gorge (sxodim, 2022).
kg-0091.self: Yes: the road is paved, entry is free, the trail to Teke-Tor is simple (2/5) and popular (too.kg, Hiking.kg). For Altyn-Tor and the pass you need experience and equipment.
kg-0091.roadtype: Paved to the start of the walk / the Teplye Klyuchi resort (Hiking.kg, too.kg); beyond that — a footpath.
kg-0091.traveltime: Bishkek → parking lot: 35 km, ~1 h 10 min by car (Hiking.kg); on foot to Teke-Tor 5.7 km, ~2 h 10 min one way (Hiking.kg); the Sputnik8 tour — 1–1.5 h of driving one way.
kg-0091.stay: Teplye Klyuchi resort/recreation base: 9 three-block cottages, each block with 2 rooms with a shower and toilet (sxodim, 2022; prices by phone +996 312 36-66-18). Also the Jannat hotel, the “Koi-Tash” rest house, cottages at the resort, and summer bases with tapchans (raised platforms) (too.kg). Camping is deeper in the gorge, with few places by the road (too.kg). 2025–2026 prices were not found.
kg-0091.net: There is mobile coverage for the first ~10 km of the gorge — up to the Teplye Klyuchi resort; above it there is none (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
kg-0091.entry: Entry to the gorge and parking are free (too.kg). The pool/treatments at Teplye Klyuchi are paid, and the tariffs are not given on the pages (sxodim).
kg-0091.transfer: The Sputnik8 tour to the hot springs — $120 per group/excursion (5 h, transfer + guide; reviews 2023–2025). Taxi Bishkek – Alamedin: 2025–2026 prices were not found (Yandex Go/inDrive at the tariff).
kg-0091.bring: Trekking poles and non-slip shoes for the descents and the section by the waterfall; in winter — ice grips (Hiking.kg); swimwear for the springs; water or a filter (do not drink from the river — livestock), an offline map — the signal disappears above the resort (too.kg).
kg-0091.warn: Do not drink river water — livestock graze higher up (too.kg). The signal exists only up to the resort. The trail at the waterfall is steep and ices over in winter (Hiking.kg). Radon baths have contraindications — consult a doctor. The Alamedin Pass into Issyk-Ata is only for experienced groups (too.kg).
kg-0091.food: Kymyz and national cuisine at the local café (2GIS); the “12 Kaminov” (12 Fireplaces) café in the gorge (too.kg); berries and mushrooms in summer (2GIS) — pick only those you know.
kg-0091.reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 2,566 ratings (168 reviews) — as of 07.10.2026; Google Maps (the “Alamudun Gorge” listing): 4.9/5, 14 ratings — as of 03.10.2026; the Sputnik8 tour to the springs 4.7 (3 reviews). Pros: proximity to Bishkek, the waterfall, hot springs, nature; cons (per video/descriptions): crowded on weekends, cottage development by the road, the river water is not drinkable.
kg-0091.p.sum: The gorge closest to Bishkek (30–35 km, ~1 h): paved to the Teplye Klyuchi resort, free parking, then 5.5–5.7 km on foot to the Teke-Tor waterfall. Public transport does not run to the gorge — people go by taxi (Yandex Go one way; arrange waiting for the return), their own car, or with a tour ($90–190). An ideal day trip: the waterfall in the morning, then the radon pools and lunch at a café by the resort.

kg-0092.name: Tosor Pass
kg-0092.near: Tosor village on the south shore of Issyk-Kul (turn-off from the Balykchy — Karakol highway at about km 120 from Balykchy). From the village to the summit of the pass is about 34.7 km of mountain road.
kg-0092.elev: 3893 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, 2GIS, central-asia.guide); dangerousroads.org gives 3901 m, Too.kg — rounded 3900 m. Elevation gain from Tosor village — about 2295 m.
kg-0092.short: A high-altitude off-road pass (3893 m) over the Terskey Ala-Too range — the only road pass on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, leading into Naryn region.
kg-0092.desc: Tosor is a dirt pass over the Terskey Ala-Too range, linking the south shore of Issyk-Kul with the Kichi-Naryn valley and Naryn region. From Tosor village the road climbs 34.7 km up the gorge at an average gradient of 6.6%: at the bottom are sea buckthorn and sandy-stony sections, in the middle deep ruts and narrow spots right by the river, a “stone gate” beyond which the gorge widens, and at the top a stony moraine climb. This is an unmaintained road: it can be driven only in a prepared 4×4, usually in July–September; on the Naryn side there are fords across the Uchemchek River. The gorge and pass are part of the route by which the Kyrgyz fled to China in 1916 during the Urkun; in July 2026 a memorial trek marking the 110th anniversary of the events went along it.
kg-0092.guide: Tosor is not a spot but a whole day on the road: allow all the daylight hours for the Tosor — Naryn crossing (about 11 h according to reviews). If you aren't ready for the pass, drive the lower 5–10 km of the gorge as far as the “stone gate” — sea buckthorn thickets, springs and picnic spots are reachable without assaulting the summit. At the top look at the Terskey glaciers and, on a clear day, at Issyk-Kul behind you; beyond that the road heads toward Jyluu-Suu and the Kichi-Naryn valley. Remember the history: refugees of the Urkun came this way in 1916 — in 2026 a memorial expedition passed here. Don't go with a single car: there is no signal, and the fords on the south side behave differently in the morning and in the afternoon.
kg-0092.see: The Tosor gorge with sea buckthorn thickets and springs in its lower part; the “stone gate” where the gorge turns into a mountain valley; the moraine climb and a panorama of the Terskey Ala-Too glaciers from the 3893 m summit; at the fork at about 3000 m, a turn-off to the neighboring Tamga gorge; on the south side the Uchemchek/Kichi-Naryn valley with its fords, then the Jyluu-Suu hot springs and Lake Teshik-Kol (an alternative approach).
kg-0092.skip: You don't have a prepared 4×4 with an experienced driver and a second vehicle accompanying you. You're going in June or after heavy rain — snow at the top and high water at the fords. What you want is specifically a panorama of Issyk-Kul, not mountain off-roading — for that Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon nearby is easier.
kg-0092.diff: High (for the vehicle and driver): 34.7 km of dirt road, a drop of 2295 m, an average gradient of 6.6%, a stony moraine climb below the summit, fords across the Uchemchek on the south side. For cyclists, long stretches on foot in the upper part. The lower gorge for a walk/picnic is easy.
kg-0092.when: July–September; best August–September, when the snow has gone and the water in the fords is lower (OunTravela). Dangerousroads: usually passable June–August, but snow on the pass can lie until June–July. A late snowfall can close the summit for several days even in season. Closed in winter and spring.
kg-0092.hours: An open area with no barriers or ticket offices; there is no official opening schedule — passability is determined by snow, mudflows and water at the fords. Check conditions with locals in Tosor or with jeep operators before setting out.
kg-0092.daytime: Start the climb early in the morning (6–8 am): the water at the fords is lower in the morning and rises toward evening because of melting; it's best to cross the summit before noon, before afternoon thunderstorms and fog.
kg-0092.how: Balykchy — Karakol highway (south shore) to Tosor village: from Bishkek about 295 km (Bishkek — Balykchy ~175 km + ~120 km along the south shore), 4.5–5 h; from Karakol about 100 km, ~1.5–2 h. In the village turn south into the gorge: the right fork is a mountain road to Bokonbaevo, the short left one goes to the forestry station, straight on leads up to the pass (34.7 km). On the south side, a descent into the Uchemchek/Kichi-Naryn valley and on to Naryn (Tosor — Naryn about 200 km, ~11 h according to a TripAdvisor review).
kg-0092.needcar: Yes — only a prepared 4×4 with high ground clearance, all-terrain tires and a spare, with an experienced driver; best in a convoy of 2+ vehicles (dangerousroads, OunTravela, Too.kg). On foot/by bicycle — a multi-day trek with a tent.
kg-0092.self: Yes, in your own prepared 4×4 and with off-road experience — no permits or fees, and no border zone is mentioned. But going alone (a single car) is not recommended: there is no signal, no fuel stations and no people for tens of km; if you break down it is hard to get out. Beginners — only with a local driver or a jeep tour.
kg-0092.roadtype: Entirely dirt, unmaintained: at the bottom a sandy-stony track, in the middle part deep washouts and ruts, sections right up against the river; below the pass from the north, a stony moraine climb of large rocks. On the south side, several fords across the Uchemchek River with boulders; the water level depends on the time of day and snowmelt (higher in June–July). Conditions change greatly from year to year (OunTravela).
kg-0092.traveltime: Bishkek — Tosor: 4.5–5 h. Karakol — Tosor: ~1.5–2 h. Tosor — summit (34.7 km): 2.5–4 h by 4×4 depending on the condition of the track (estimate from the length and nature of the road). The full Tosor — Naryn crossing: about 11 h (TripAdvisor, ~200 km); central-asia.guide advises allowing the whole daylight day.
kg-0092.stay: There are no guesthouses, cafes or shops in the gorge or on the pass — only a tent (plenty of camping spots and springs, Too.kg). Overnight stays before/after are in the yurt camps and guesthouses of the south shore (Tosor, Tamga, Barskoon, Bokonbaevo): budget options from 500–600 som/person (economist.kg, July 2026). On the Naryn side — guesthouses and CBT Naryn in Naryn.
kg-0092.net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge or on the pass (Too.kg, dangerousroads, central-asia.guide). Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage exists in Tosor village and on the south-shore highway. The participants of the 2026 memorial trek used satellite Starlink. Download offline maps and tracks in advance.
kg-0092.entry: Free: no source from 2016–2026 mentions a transit fee, eco fees or permits (no protected area is noted on the route).
kg-0092.transfer: No published prices for a jeep crossing over Tosor were found — on request only from operators (Ak-Sai, Eurasia Travel, DWC). Reference points for getting there: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — south shore 500–600 som; taxi 1200 som/person or 4500 som/car (24.kg, July 2026).
kg-0092.bring: A full tank and spare fuel (there are no fuel stations), a spare tire, a compressor, a shovel, a tow rope; warm clothing (at 3900 m there is snow and frost even in summer), a rain jacket, water and purification (livestock in the river — boil the water, Too.kg), a day's food beyond the plan, a first-aid kit, offline maps and a track, and if possible a satellite communicator.
kg-0092.warn: Serious off-roading: a moraine climb, fords with boulders, washouts; don't go without 4×4 experience and a second vehicle. Snow on the pass is possible until July and from late August; after downpours there are mudflows and rockfalls on sections of the road. No signal and no fuel stations. At 3900 m altitude sickness is possible after a fast ascent from lake level (1600 m). River water — only after boiling (livestock graze).
kg-0092.food: There are no establishments on the route — bring food. Before/after, cafes and yurt camps of the south shore: lagman, beshbarmak, kumys in summer; smoked and dried Issyk-Kul fish by the highway. On the 2026 trek, participants cooked traditional kulazyk (Time.kg) — an excellent snack for the road.
kg-0092.reviews: Google Maps (“Tossor Pass”): 5/5, 8 ratings on 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor (Tosor Pass): 4 reviews, 3 “excellent” and 1 “average” (2016–2017; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: one of the best mountain roads, glaciers and valleys, wild nature, almost no cars. Cons: a very hard stony road, unpredictable weather (snow, fog, hail), a high risk of breakdown far from help.
kg-0092.p.sum: Tosor (≈3893 m) is a serious off-road pass between the south shore of Issyk-Kul and Naryn: from Tosor village it's 34.7 km of rough track to the summit (2.5–4 h), and from the south fords across the Uchemchek and the Kichi-Naryn valley; the whole Tamga — Tosor — Naryn crossing is ≈365 km (90% dirt), a full daylight day. Go only in a prepared 4×4, preferably two vehicles, in August–September (less water at the fords, snow gone). Without your own vehicle — jeep tours (Eurasia Travel, Ak-Sai, DWC). Stay overnight before/after in Tosor, Tamga or Barskoon (guesthouses $12–40, yurt camps $80–90 on Booking); on the pass — a tent only.

kg-0093.name: Ala-Bel Pass
kg-0093.near: There are no permanent villages by the pass. Taldy-Bulak is ~18 km as the crow flies (OSM marker, catalog calculation); to the north are the villages of the Suusamyr Valley, to the south through the Chychkan gorge (~30 km) are the Toktogul Reservoir and Toktogul.
kg-0093.elev: 3175 m (Nomad's Land, Trip to Kyrgyzstan, central-asia.live, trvlland). Some guidebooks give 3184 m — not confirmed by the sources found.
kg-0093.short: Ala-Bel (3175 m) is the highest point of the main Bishkek — Osh highway in the Talas Ala-Too: a pass between the Suusamyr Valley and the Chychkan gorge, with alpine meadows in summer and a snowy “white desert” in winter.
kg-0093.desc: Ala-Bel Pass lies in the Talas Ala-Too at an elevation of 3175 m and is considered the highest point of the main Bishkek — Osh road (travel2unlimited; Nomad's Land). It connects the Suusamyr Valley with the valley of the Chychkan River, which flows parallel to the road south toward the Toktogul Reservoir. The ascent and descent are relatively gentle; in summer the slopes are covered with alpine meadows with flowering grasses, and in winter the pass is buried in snow (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The stretch of highway from km 198 to km 255 (Ala-Bel and the Chychkan gorge) is one of the most avalanche-prone in the country: on 28.01.2026 an avalanche at km 247 blocked traffic in both directions (economist.kg).
kg-0093.guide: Ala-Bel is the main “ceiling” of the north-south road: here you climb above 3100 m without leaving your car. Stop at the top — in summer the meadows are bright with flowers and smell of herbs, and beyond the pass the green Chychkan gorge begins, with a rushing river alongside the road. Even in July it can be cold and windy here, so keep a jacket handy. In winter, don't plan the crossing without checking the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) and Ministry of Transport bulletins — the 198–255 km stretch is regularly closed because of avalanches. If altitude makes you feel unwell, don't linger at the top for long.
kg-0093.see: The 3175 m saddle with views of the snowy peaks of the Talas Ala-Too; alpine meadows in bloom (June — July); the descent into the Chychkan gorge with the river alongside the highway; the Suusamyr Valley on the northern side (Trip to Kyrgyzstan; Nomad's Land).
kg-0093.skip: If you aren't driving the Bishkek — Osh highway, it isn't worth making a trip just for the pass — it is a photo stop. In winter, when there is avalanche danger, it is better to postpone the crossing or fly Bishkek — Osh.
kg-0093.diff: Easy: a stop on a paved highway, no walking section. The 3175 m altitude can cause mild altitude sickness if you stay for long (editorial).
kg-0093.when: June — September: flowering meadows, dry road. The highway is formally open year-round, but from December to March avalanches, black ice and closures are possible (the avalanche of 28.01.2026 at km 247; MChS warning 31.01–02.02.2026 for the 198–255 km stretch — economist.kg).
kg-0093.hours: Open 24 hours, a section of the state highway. Temporary closures during avalanches and snowfalls; restrictions for trucks have been introduced at Ala-Bel (Kaktus). Check the Ministry of Transport and MChS bulletins before a winter trip.
kg-0093.daytime: Morning and the first half of the day — less cloud over the pass and better visibility; in winter, drive only in daylight (editorial).
kg-0093.how: Along the Bishkek — Osh highway: from Bishkek via Kara-Balta, the Too-Ashuu tunnel and the Suusamyr Valley (about 4 h by car, estimate; the pass is at roughly km 200–210 — based on MChS data about the avalanche-prone 198–255 km stretch, to be verified). From Osh/Jalal-Abad — north via Tash-Kumyr, Kara-Kol, Toktogul and the Chychkan gorge. Highway tunnel toll: 50 som for cars with Kyrgyz plates / 200 som for foreign ones (since 01.01.2024), at the Sosnovka and Kara-Kol checkpoints.
kg-0093.needcar: Yes: your own/rental car, a taxi, or a seat in a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi along the highway (a stop at the pass is by arrangement with the driver).
kg-0093.self: Yes: a paved highway, no permits. In winter — only with winter tires and when the road is open.
kg-0093.roadtype: Paved mountain highway Bishkek — Osh (EM-02/M41); the ascent and descent are gentle (Nomad's Land), in winter snowdrifts, black ice and avalanches on the 198–255 km stretch (economist.kg, 2026).
kg-0093.traveltime: From Bishkek — about 4 h to the pass (estimate; 5–6 h to the Chychkan gorge per avtoprokat.kg); from the pass to Toktogul — ~1.5 h (estimate).
kg-0093.stay: There is no lodging at the pass. The nearest options: the Chychkan tourist base/hotel (~km 240, $51–58 for a standard room, per 2026 checks of the Chychkan gorge), the Oson motel in the Chychkan gorge, guesthouses and yurt camps in Suusamyr, hotels in Toktogul (via toktogulvisit/CBT Toktogul).
kg-0093.net: Not confirmed for the saddle. In the neighbouring Chychkan gorge there is no signal or it is limited (too.kg). No reports about operators at the pass were found.
kg-0093.entry: Free: a section of the state highway. Only the toll for the tunnels of the Bishkek — Osh highway is paid (50/200 som since 01.01.2024).
kg-0093.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Toktogul 400 som, shared taxi 600–800 som, private taxi 3200–5600 som (toktogulvisit); shared taxi Bishkek — Osh ~2500 som/seat (2026).
kg-0093.bring: A warm jacket and hat even in summer (3175 m), sunglasses, water; in winter — chains/winter tires, and a reserve of fuel and food in case the highway is closed.
kg-0093.warn: Avalanche-prone stretch 198–255 km (Ala-Bel and the Chychkan gorge): in winter the highway can be closed (avalanche of 28.01.2026); when driving through, keep a distance of at least 500 m (MChS recommendation, 2026). The 3175 m altitude — altitude sickness is possible. The weather changes quickly, and snow is possible in summer. Stop only at safe pull-offs — there are many trucks on the highway.
kg-0093.food: On the highway in the Suusamyr Valley in summer, kumis and dairy products are sold at yurts (typical for the highway; specific places at the pass are not confirmed). Cafes are in the Chychkan gorge and Toktogul.
kg-0093.reviews: Google Maps: 4.6 from 59 ratings (catalog check, 10.2026). Travelers note the views, meadows and snow; cons — cold, wind, winter closures (travel2unlimited, trvlland).
kg-0093.p.sum: Ala-Bel (3175 m) is a photo stop on the Bishkek — Osh highway, about 4 h drive from Bishkek; you get here by your own/rental car or by marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Toktogul with a stop by arrangement. In summer, overnight in the Chychkan gorge or Toktogul; in winter, check the MChS bulletins before setting out: the 198–255 km stretch is avalanche-prone, and trucks are not let through during blizzards.

kg-0094.name: Toktogul Reservoir
kg-0094.near: Kara-Suu — ~8 km in a straight line from the catalogue point (OSM). The town of Toktogul (the district centre) — on the northern shore by the highway; the town of Kara-Kul (~21,000 residents) — by the dam in the southwest (central-asia.guide).
kg-0094.elev: Not confirmed by the sources found: the normal pool level is about 900 m (a widely cited value, needs checking); the actual level fluctuates strongly — in 2026 the volume fell almost to the “dead” level (24.kg).
kg-0094.short: The largest reservoir in Kyrgyzstan and Central Asia, on the Naryn River — a 65 km turquoise bowl among the Ketmen-Tyube mountains along the Bishkek — Osh highway.
kg-0094.desc: The Toktogul Reservoir was created by the dam of the Toktogul hydropower plant on the Naryn (filled 1973–1975, the plant has operated since 1975; the dam is 215 m high) and flooded the Ketmen-Tyube basin (fb.ru; water.gov.kg). Its area is about 284 km², total volume 19.5 billion m³ (Water Resources Service), length about 65 km; the depth in places is up to 120 m per fb.ru (central-asia.guide says “more than 200 m” — probably a mix-up with the dam height of 215 m). The reservoir regulates flow for the Naryn cascade of hydropower plants and for irrigation of the Fergana Valley, so the level changes noticeably: on 24.02.2026 a volume of 6.8 billion m³ was forecast for 1 April against a “dead” level of ~6.5 billion m³ (24.kg). The shores are rocky, with no sandy beaches; in summer the water warms to ~28 °C (central-asia.guide).
kg-0094.guide: You can see the Toktogul reservoir from the Bishkek — Osh highway for dozens of kilometres: turquoise water, red-ochre cliffs and bare shores — you'll immediately understand that the water level here swings by metres. Stop at one of the viewpoints above the water and be sure to try fresh fried trout or carp at the roadside cafes — it is the local classic. In summer you can swim: the water reaches +28 °C by August, but the shore is rocky, so bring water shoes. The dam and hydropower plant at Kara-Kul can be visited only with a permit arranged in advance and a passport.
kg-0094.see: Panoramas of turquoise water and coloured cliffs from the viewpoints on the M41 highway; the dam of the Toktogul hydropower plant at Kara-Kul (entry by permit); the town of Toktogul (the museum of the akyn (bard) Toktogul Satylganov — not checked); the Kok-Bel pass with a view of the reservoir on the road to Kara-Kul; rocky coves for swimming (TripAdvisor; central-asia.guide).
kg-0094.skip: You're looking for a sandy beach and resort infrastructure — the shores are rocky, service is minimal. You're not ready to drive the Bishkek — Osh highway — nothing else leads here. In spring, at low water, the shores look like an exposed lake bed.
kg-0094.diff: Easy: viewing from the highway and swimming from the shore. Rocky descents to the water (editorial).
kg-0094.when: July — September for swimming (water up to ~28 °C in August — central-asia.guide); spring and autumn — for views (TripAdvisor). In spring the water level is usually at its lowest (24.kg, 2026).
kg-0094.hours: Free access to the shores along the highway, round the clock. The dam and hydropower plant area is a restricted facility, visits only with a permit arranged in advance and a passport (TripAdvisor).
kg-0094.daytime: Morning and evening — soft light on the cliffs and the turquoise water; by day in summer it's hot (editorial).
kg-0094.how: On the Bishkek — Osh highway: the reservoir is roughly halfway (~250 km from Bishkek and from Osh — central-asia.guide; the Kok-Bel guesthouse — ~350 km from Bishkek). From Bishkek via the Too-Ashuu tunnel, Suusamyr, Ala-Bel and the Chychkan gorge to Toktogul; the highway runs along the northern and western shores to Kara-Kul. Tunnel toll: 50 som (Kyrgyz plates) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024, at the Sosnovka and Kara-Kul posts.
kg-0094.needcar: Yes: your own/rented car or a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to Toktogul or Kara-Kul; along the shore — by car, a local taxi around Toktogul District — from 100 som (toktogulvisit).
kg-0094.self: Yes: the shores by the highway are accessible without permits. Fishing — check the permit requirements (central-asia.guide). The hydropower plant — by permit only.
kg-0094.roadtype: The paved Bishkek — Osh highway along the shore; to the water — dirt turnoffs and rocky descents (editorial). The Kok-Bel pass between Toktogul and Kara-Kul.
kg-0094.traveltime: Bishkek — Toktogul ~5–6 h by car (estimate; to the Chychkan gorge 5–6 h per avtoprokat.kg); Osh — Toktogul ~6 h (estimate); marshrutkas take longer.
kg-0094.stay:
• Kok-Bel guest complex on the shore (Kara-Kul zone, ~350 km from Bishkek): 30 rooms, a pool, courts, jet-ski rental; prices on request (centralasia-travel.com).
• Arbat Toktogul Hotel (Toktogul, 63/3 Sadakan Apa St.): 26 rooms, ~3660 PHP (~$60–65) a night, 8.4/10 from 7 reviews (trip.com, 2026).
• Hotel Akbermet (Toktogul) — in the Nomad's Land catalogue.
• Former hydropower plant builders' camps are used as holiday bases; camping on the shore is possible (central-asia.guide).
• Guesthouses via CBT Toktogul / toktogulvisit.
kg-0094.net: In Toktogul and Kara-Kul — mobile signal and Wi-Fi in hotels (Arbat — free Wi-Fi, trip.com). On remote shores coverage is not confirmed.
kg-0094.entry: Free: the shores along the highway are open. Paid — the services of holiday bases and rentals; a visit to the hydropower plant is by permit (cost not found).
kg-0094.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Toktogul 400 som; Osh — Toktogul 600 som; Jalal-Abad — Toktogul 400 som; shared taxi from Bishkek 600–800 som/person; private taxi from Bishkek 3200–5600 som (toktogulvisit, year not specified).
kg-0094.bring: Water shoes (a rocky shore), a swimsuit, sun protection and a hat (hot in summer), water; for fishing — check the permit. Take your litter with you — reviews complain about plastic.
kg-0094.warn: The water level fluctuates strongly (in 2026 close to the “dead” level, 24.kg) — the shores and descents change. The shore is rocky, and beaches with lifeguards are not confirmed. The hydropower dam is a restricted facility, photography and visits are by permit only. Don't confuse the dam height (215 m) with the depth of the reservoir.
kg-0094.food: Fresh fried trout and carp at roadside cafes along the reservoir (TripAdvisor; central-asia.guide). The reservoir holds carp, crucian carp, silver carp, grass carp and trout; there are fish farms.
kg-0094.reviews: Google Maps: 4.7 from 181 ratings (catalogue cross-check, 10.2026); TripAdvisor: 4.5/5 from 25 reviews, no. 1 of 2 in Toktogul (07.10.2026). Pros: views, turquoise water, swimming, fish cafes. Cons: plastic litter, rocky shores without sand, little entertainment — better as a stop on the way.
kg-0094.p.sum: The Toktogul reservoir is visible from the Bishkek — Osh highway for dozens of kilometres; the best base is the town of Toktogul (CBT Toktogul, guesthouses from $13–24, the Arbat hotel ~$60) or the Kok-Bel complex on the shore near Kara-Kul with a pool and jet skis. Get there by marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Toktogul (265–400 som) or in your own car; to the water — via dirt turnoffs, the shore is rocky, bring water shoes.

kg-0095.name: Ak-Say Valley
kg-0095.near: There are practically no permanent villages in the valley — in summer there are yak herders’ camps, border posts and hunting bases. Entry is via the Kyndy pass (3,400 m) and the border post south of the At-Bashy range; the nearest large settlement with services is At-Bashy, the town of Naryn is about 120 km of gravel from the valley (NomadCar). The earlier “1 Maya ~34 km” is an OSM point in a straight line across the range, not a guide for travel.
kg-0095.elev: About 3,000–3,100 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Baibol — 3,000 m; Nomad's Land — 3,100 m; map.kg — “above 3,000 m”).
kg-0095.short: Ak-Say is a huge high-altitude (≈3,000–3,100 m) treeless valley between the At-Bashy range and Kakshaal-Too on the border with China, Kyrgyzstan’s “cold pole” (−56.3 °C) and the way to Lake Kel-Suu.
kg-0095.desc: The valley stretches for about 100 km, up to 40 km wide (Nomad's Land), south of the At-Bashy range as far as the Kakshaal-Too range, along which runs the border with China. The absolute minimum temperature in Kyrgyzstan was recorded here — −56.3 °C; because of the harsh climate only low grasses and rare shrubs grow, there are no trees, and there are small lakes and marshes. Ak-Say is a key biodiversity area (KGZ24, ~90,000 ha): Marco Polo argali, snow leopard, ibex, wolf, marmot, demoiselle crane; 93 glaciers in the Aksai river basin with an area of 120.9 km². In summer yak herders come up here, and some stay with their yaks in winter too. There is a Neolithic site in the valley, hunting bases operate, and mountains up to 6,000 m attract climbers. The road to the Kok-Kyya valley and Lake Kel-Suu passes through Ak-Say; the whole valley is a border zone with a mandatory permit.
kg-0095.guide: Ak-Say is a vastness you will not see anywhere else in Kyrgyzstan: after the Kyndy pass the road comes out onto a flat steppe up to 40 km wide, and to the south the Kakshaal-Too stands like a wall with the Chinese border. Look around — argali, marmots and demoiselle cranes live here, and yaks graze by the road. Remember that this is the country’s “cold pole”: even in July there can be sub-zero temperatures at night, so keep warm things at hand. Most people drive through the valley in transit to Kel-Suu — ask the driver to stop for a couple of photo breaks at the small lakes and on the climb to Kyndy. You cannot get here without a permit, so arrange it in advance.
kg-0095.see: A steppe valley up to 40 km wide and a panorama of the Kakshaal-Too range (the Chinese border); the Kyndy pass (3,400 m) at the entrance; wildlife — argali, marmots, demoiselle cranes; herds of yaks and summer camps; small lakes and marshes; the descent into the Kok-Kyya canyon.
kg-0095.skip: You are not going to Kel-Suu or on an expedition — it makes little sense to arrange a permit and drive 120+ km on gravel for the valley itself. You want forests and warm nights: here is a treeless steppe and a “cold pole”. You do not have a prepared 4×4.
kg-0095.diff: Moderate-high — because of the road: washboard gravel, dust, vibration, risk of punctures (NomadCar); altitude 3,000–3,400 m; the valley itself has no trails or infrastructure.
kg-0095.when: July — August (warm, the road is dry, the Kok-Kyya camps operate). In June snow is possible, from September frosts; in winter down to −40…−56 °C, snow up to 80 cm — trips are not recommended.
kg-0095.hours: An open border area — only with a border permit, checked at the post after the Kyndy pass. Hunting bases operate seasonally, hunting is by licence (Baibol). Since 10.04.2026 permanent residents working on the Ak-Say and Arpa pastures pass without a permit or fee according to lists from the ayil kenesh (village councils) (time.kg); this does not apply to tourists.
kg-0095.daytime: Daytime: plan to cross the valley in daylight to reach the Kok-Kyya camp by evening; morning and evening have the best light and animal activity (editorial).
kg-0095.how: Bishkek → Naryn (≈350 km, paved) → At-Bashy → the Kyndy pass (3,400 m) and the border post → Ak-Say valley. From Naryn to the valley it is about 120 km of gravel (NomadCar), then 60–80 km to Kok-Kyya.
kg-0095.needcar: Yes, a 4×4 with a local driver; there is no public transport.
kg-0095.self: Only with a border permit (CBT Naryn, tour.too.kg) and in a prepared 4×4; not recommended without a local driver.
kg-0095.roadtype: Gravel/dirt with washboard and dust (NomadCar); the Kyndy pass 3,400 m; the At-Bashy — Kyndy — Torugart road was graded in August 2026 (time.kg); in the valley — rutted dirt tracks and swampy sections.
kg-0095.traveltime: Bishkek — Naryn ~5–6 h; Naryn — Ak-Say valley ~3–4 h on gravel (calculated: ~120 km at 30–40 km/h, NomadCar); from Almaty to Ak-Say — 15–16 h (Freedom Travel, 07.2025).
kg-0095.stay: There are no tourist hotels in the valley itself; there are hunting bases (by arrangement) and tents. People usually stay overnight in yurt camps in the Kok-Kyya valley (Kel-Suu Yurt Camp — from 1,800 som per 2GIS; 1,500–2,500+ som per person with meals — kgnomad 2026) or in Naryn/At-Bashy.
kg-0095.net: There is no mobile coverage after leaving Naryn/the last villages; a weak signal is occasionally found on the passes (NomadCar, kgnomad 2026).
kg-0095.entry: There is no fee to visit the valley; a border permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region, one week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent; tour.too.kg — 3,000 som (2026). Hunting — by separate licences.
kg-0095.transfer: 4×4 Naryn — Kok-Kyya (via Ak-Say) — Naryn: 13,000–20,000+ som per car for up to 4 people (kgnomad, 07.2026). Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026).
kg-0095.bring: Permit and passport; very warm clothing even in summer, hat and gloves; sunscreen and sunglasses; a supply of water and food (no shops); cash; a spare tyre and tools for the car; binoculars for watching animals.
kg-0095.warn: Border zone: a mandatory permit, do not drive towards the border and do not photograph the border posts. A “cold pole” — sharp temperature swings, snow is possible in summer. Altitude 3,000–3,400 m. No phone coverage, medical help or fuel — a full tank from Naryn/At-Bashy. Gravel washboard — frequent punctures.
kg-0095.food: There are no eateries in the valley. At the yak herders’ and in the Kok-Kyya camps — dairy products, kaymak, boorsok, beshbarmak (editorial). Stock up on food in Naryn.
kg-0095.reviews: No separate listings with ratings found on Google Maps (search is ambiguous, 03.10.2026) or TripAdvisor. In travellers’ reports (Freedom Travel 2025, TripAdvisor on Kel-Suu) the road through Ak-Say is called one of the most beautiful parts of the trip; cons — a bumpy gravel road and cold.
kg-0095.p.sum: Ak-Say is a huge high-altitude valley beyond the Kyndy pass (≈3,400 m), the “cold pole” of Kyrgyzstan; tourists drive through it on the way to Kok-Kyya and Kel-Suu. A border permit (checked at the posts at the entrance) and a 4×4 are needed: from Naryn ≈120 km of gravel, 3–4 h. There is no infrastructure — people overnight in the Kok-Kyya yurt camps or in At-Bashy/Naryn; bring a full tank, cash and food from Naryn.

kg-0095.p.permits: A border permit is mandatory (the border zone of the At-Bashy district by the Chinese border). Ways to arrange it: 1) tour.too.kg — 3,000 som (all border zones) / $35 for the Kel-Suu—Kok-Kyya—Chatyr-Kol zone; 5–7 working days; office at 105/3 Isanov St., Bishkek (2026). 2) CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region only, ~1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent in 2 working days (stage 1); Nomad's Land: from Naryn fastest — within a few days, via Bishkek — up to 2 weeks. Step by step: (1) send a passport scan and travel dates (WhatsApp/form); (2) pay a 50% prepayment; (3) the Border Service reviews it for ~1 week; (4) pick up the paper original in Bishkek or Naryn (or via the guide/tour — then the passport copy is sent a few days ahead). The permit is valid for up to 1 month. It is checked at the military posts at the Kyndy pass/at the entrance to the Ak-Say valley (2 posts per Eurasia Travel) — you need the original permit with the stamp and your passport. Photographing the posts is prohibited. No fee for entry to the lake/valley was found. Hunting — by separate licences.
kg-0095.p.access: By car only: with children and older people — possible as part of a Kel-Suu trip if they tolerate the altitude of 3,000–3,400 m and the bumps well; in a wheelchair — only from the car window; with a dog — not advisable.

kg-0096.name: Konorchek Canyons
kg-0096.near: There are no settlements near the canyons; the start is at the Red Bridge in the Boom Gorge on the Bishkek — Balykchy highway (~141 km from Bishkek, ilovekg). The nearest villages are the roadside villages of Boom (Kyz-Kuyoo) and Jil-Aryk at the western entrance; the town of Balykchy is at the eastern exit of the gorge.
kg-0096.elev: Not confirmed: no exact elevations were found. The elevation gain from the parking lot to the far parts of the canyon is about 430 m (ilovekg).
kg-0096.short: Konorchek (Suluu-Terek) is a maze of red sandstone canyons north of the Boom Gorge, ~120–140 km from Bishkek.
kg-0096.desc: Konorchek, also Suluu-Terek, is a system of red sandstone and clay canyons carved by water in the eastern part of the Kyrgyz Range; the area covers about 200 km² (too.kg). The entrance is at the Red Bridge in the Boom Gorge, roughly 120 (too.kg) – 141 km (ilovekg) from Bishkek. The approach follows a dry, stony riverbed: about 1.5 h to the main walls, and a full round-trip walk takes 4–5 h; the route has steep sections and places with ropes, and no technical climbing (ilovekg). The area has the remains of an ancient volcano and fossilized shells (too.kg). In summer it is noticeably hotter here than in the Chu Valley, with almost no shade; there is no water, cafe or signal.
kg-0096.guide: Konorchek is called the Kyrgyz “Grand Canyon”: red walls rise straight out of the dry riverbed, and the farther you go, the narrower and higher the corridors become. Start at the railway crossing before the Red Bridge and stay in the riverbed — there are almost no other trails, and no markings either (drunkyhorse). It's about an hour and a half to the first big walls; allow 4–5 hours for the whole walk and set out early — it gets dark early in the canyons, and in summer the heat goes over +40 (too.kg). The main rule is dry weather: if the Chu is red with silt or there is fresh mud in the riverbed, don't go in (ilovekg).
kg-0096.see: Red sandstone walls and narrow corridors in a dry riverbed; “aeolian castles” (orexca); a plateau with a view of the cliffs; the remains of a volcano and fossilized shells (too.kg).
kg-0096.skip: You're going in July–August at midday — the heat is over +40 and there is almost no shade (too.kg, ilovekg). You have knee problems or small children — rockfall piles and steep sections (ilovekg). The forecast promises rain — the canyons are dangerous.
kg-0096.diff: Moderate: 4–5 h round trip, up to 6 km from the parking lot with ~430 m of gain, boulders, steep sections, places with ropes; no technical climbing (ilovekg). Hard for people with bad knees, small children and dogs.
kg-0096.when: Spring and autumn (too.kg); tours run from May to October (orexca). Summer heat up to +40 °C (too.kg); in winter there is little snow, but daylight is short.
kg-0096.hours: A natural area with no opening hours; go by daylight — set out early and return before dark (ilovekg, drunkyhorse).
kg-0096.daytime: Early morning: less heat and a reserve of daylight — it gets dark early in the narrow canyons (drunkyhorse, ilovekg). Evening light beautifully lights the red walls, but returning in the dark is dangerous.
kg-0096.how: Along the Bishkek — Balykchy highway to the Boom Gorge, to the Red Bridge (~141 km from Bishkek, 2–2.5 h by car — ilovekg). Cars are left at a dirt area by the barrier/crossing; you can't drive to the canyon itself (drunkyhorse). Then on foot along the dry riverbed ~1.5 h to the main walls. Marshrutkas (minibuses) to Balykchy go through Boom, but catching a ride back is unreliable (ilovekg).
kg-0096.needcar: Preferably: a car with a driver or an organized transfer (ilovekg). You can take a marshrutka (minibus) to Balykchy and ask to be dropped at the Red Bridge, but getting back is hard.
kg-0096.self: Yes, in dry weather and with an offline map: entry is free, and the way follows the riverbed (too.kg, ilovekg). There are no markings and it is easy to stay out until dark — bring a flashlight (drunkyhorse).
kg-0096.roadtype: To the start — the excellent-quality asphalt of the A365 Bishkek — Balykchy highway; parking at a dirt area by the barrier; beyond that only on foot along the stony dry riverbed (drunkyhorse, ilovekg).
kg-0096.traveltime: Bishkek → Red Bridge: 2–2.5 h by car, ~141 km (ilovekg); on foot to the main red walls ~1.5 h, the full route 4–5 h (ilovekg); tours — 8–10 h (orexca, Tripster).
kg-0096.stay: There are no cafes, shops or hotels at the canyons; you can pitch a tent (too.kg). The nearest lodging is guesthouses and yurts in the Boom Gorge and Balykchy, and also Chon-Kemin (see the Boom Gorge card).
kg-0096.net: There is no mobile signal in the canyons (too.kg). Along the highway at Boom there is coverage (too.kg for Boom). The operator is not specified.
kg-0096.entry: Free (too.kg). Orexca includes “entrance tickets” in the tour price — no official rate was found.
kg-0096.transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) to Balykchy 500–600 som (24.kg, July 2026); an Orexca tour $140–340/person depending on the group; Tripster €338 per group of up to 4 (2026); Sputnik8 from $150/person.
kg-0096.bring: 1.5–2 L of water per person (there is no water on the route), a hat and sun protection, closed shoes with grippy soles, a flashlight, a snack, an offline map (ilovekg, too.kg).
kg-0096.warn: Dangerous during and after heavy rain: a risk of flash floods and mudflows in the narrow channels; if the Chu is red or there is fresh mud in the riverbed — don't go in (ilovekg). No water, shade or signal; in summer the heat reaches +40 (too.kg). There are no markings and it gets dark early — don't linger (drunkyhorse).
kg-0096.food: There is no food on site. On the way — the roadside cafes of the Boom Gorge (fried fish, samsa, lagman) and smoked/fried fish near Balykchy (editorial; specific places not checked).
kg-0096.reviews: No separate Google Maps card with a rating was found (cross-check 03.10.2026: several objects). Tours: Tripster 5.0 (16 reviews), Sputnik8 “From the Konorchek canyons to the shores of Issyk-Kul” 4.9 (13 reviews) — as of 07.10.2026. Pros: “Martian” landscapes, proximity to the highway; cons: heat, a hard approach over boulders, no water or markings.
kg-0096.p.sum: The red Konorchek canyons are a day trip from Bishkek (~140 km, 2–2.5 h): turn off at the Red Bridge in the Boom Gorge, cross the railway tracks and take 2 km of dirt road to the parking area, then on foot along the dry riverbed ~3.5 km to the “Central Square” and another 1.8 km to the panorama. The most convenient way is your own car or Yandex Go (~4000 som one way, arrange waiting) or a group hike (TUK and others); a marshrutka (minibus) to Balykchy will drop you at the Red Bridge, but you'd have to flag down transport back. Don't go during or after rain.
