kg-0097.name: Snow Leopard's Tears Waterfall
kg-0097.full: Snow Leopard's Tears Waterfall (Bars Tears; Barskoon Gorge)
kg-0097.near: Barskoon village (Barskaun) at the gorge entrance — about 15–17 km along the gorge road to the parking area by the waterfalls (Nomad's Land, Silk Road Adventures). Karakol — about 90 km.
kg-0097.elev: About 2,470 m above sea level (Silk Road Adventures; the waterfall cascade — 2,470–2,700 m). Nomad's Land gives 2,300 m for the waterfall area.
kg-0097.short: The best-known waterfall of the cascade in Barskoon Gorge — a natural monument, 30–40 minutes on foot from the Kumtor road.
kg-0097.desc: Snow Leopard's Tears is the main and most accessible waterfall of the Barskoon Gorge cascade on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul (together with “Champagne Spray”, “Manas's Bowl” and “Aksakal's Beard”). The water falls in several steps in a narrow canyon among Tian Shan spruces; at the foot the noise is so loud that no other sounds can be heard, and the spray flies dozens of metres. The height differs between sources: about 100 m according to Trip to Kyrgyzstan and 2GIS (probably the whole cascade), about 20 m for the main step according to Silk Road Adventures. The waterfall has the status of a state natural monument; in winter it freezes into an ice “palace” under which water continues to flow. According to legend, the waterfall is the tears of a female snow leopard mourning her cubs who died on the rocks.
kg-0097.guide: Leave your car by the Kumtor road near the yurt cafés and follow the trail up for 1.6 km — in 30–35 minutes you're at Snow Leopard's Tears. If you have energy left, 20 minutes higher up is “Champagne Spray”, and another hour on, with 300–350 m of gain, is “Manas's Bowl”: allow 3–4 hours for all three. The trail is not marked and is slippery from the spray — don't go up to the stream itself; good shots come from a distance. On the way into the gorge, stop at the monument to Yuri Gagarin (the cosmonaut only drove through here, but the legend lives on). In winter come for the ice sculptures — the waterfall freezes completely.
kg-0097.see: The Snow Leopard's Tears waterfall itself with its stepped cascades in a spruce canyon; higher up — “Champagne Spray” (~2,500 m, 20 min) and “Manas's Bowl” (~2,700 m, another 1 h); from the road you can see the “Rocky” waterfall; monuments to Yuri Gagarin and a Vostok capsule in the gorge; yurts with kumys by the parking area; in winter — ice cascades.
kg-0097.skip: You find it hard to walk 30–40 minutes uphill on a slippery, rocky, unmarked trail. You've already seen large waterfalls (Abshir-Ata, Arslanbob) and aren't ready to spend a day on the road from Cholpon-Ata/Bishkek. You're going right after heavy rain — the trail is especially dangerous.
kg-0097.diff: Easy to medium: 1.6 km one way, 30–35 min of climbing to Snow Leopard's Tears; the trail is unmarked, slippery and rocky. The lower cascade is accessible to children (DWC); to Manas's Bowl it is already medium (+300–350 m).
kg-0097.when: June–September: full water and the yurt cafés are open; late May — early June — peak snowmelt. In winter (December–February) the waterfall freezes — beautiful ice formations, but the trail becomes icy; the Kumtor road is cleared year-round.
kg-0097.hours: Open natural area, open 24 hours; no ticket offices or time restrictions. The yurt cafés by the parking area — summer only. Daylight lasts until 17:00: after that it is hard to catch a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi back (Nomad's Land).
kg-0097.daytime: Until noon — early afternoon: fewer people, the sun lights the gorge; return to the highway before 17:00. In the heat it is cool at the waterfall from the spray.
kg-0097.how: Along the southern-shore highway to the village of Barskoon (Bishkek — Barskoon about 315 km, 5–5.5 h; Karakol — Barskoon ~90 km, ~1.5 h). In the village turn south into the gorge along a good dirt road to Kumtor/Arabel; after ~15–17 km there is a parking area by the yurts and the start of the trail, then 1.6 km on foot.
kg-0097.needcar: Yes, to the parking area it is 15–17 km along the gorge from the village: your own car (almost any car can make it — Too.kg), a taxi or a tour. On foot from the village — a whole day.
kg-0097.self: Yes: no fee or permits needed, the trail is short. You need transport to the parking area and an offline map; the trail has no signs — keep to the main stream bed.
kg-0097.roadtype: Paved road along the southern-shore highway; in the gorge — a well-worn dirt road to Kumtor (“a good dirt road to Arabel”, almost any car and motorcycle can pass — Too.kg). The last 1.6 km is a rocky footpath.
kg-0097.traveltime: From Karakol ~1.5–2 h one way (MYWAY: 4 h round trip, 200 km); from Bishkek 5–5.5 h; from Cholpon-Ata ~3.5 h. On foot from the parking area to Snow Leopard's Tears 30–35 min; all three waterfalls — 3–4 h.
kg-0097.stay: Tent — there are many places to pitch one in the gorge (Too.kg). In Barskoon village and neighbouring Tamga — guesthouses and yurt camps of the southern shore: budget from 500–600 som/person (economist.kg, July 2026). Trip to Kyrgyzstan mentions yurt camps nearby (specific names and 2025–2026 prices not confirmed).
kg-0097.net: Coverage in the gorge is partial (Too.kg). In Barskoon village and on the highway — Beeline/O!/MegaCom. Don't count on a signal at the waterfall itself.
kg-0097.entry: Free: no source (too.kg, Nomad's Land, mir24, DWC, 2023–2026) reports an entrance fee/eco fee in Barskoon Gorge.
kg-0097.transfer: Taxi Karakol — waterfalls 3,500 som per car one way (Nomad's Land); MYWAY Karakol — Barskoon — Karakol 9,900 som per car for up to 5 people (2025–2026); Tripster from Karakol €250 per group of 1–7 people; marshrutka Karakol — Barskoon ~100 som (another 15–17 km to the parking area).
kg-0097.bring: Trekking shoes with a tread (slippery), a windbreaker/rain jacket against the spray, water and a snack, cash for the yurt café (kumys), in winter — crampons/ice cleats. Don't drink water from the Barskoon River: Kumtor is upstream (Too.kg); drink from springs.
kg-0097.warn: The trail is unmarked, wet and slippery; don't go close to the stream — a safe distance is about 100 m (mir24). In winter — ice on the trail. Don't drink water from the main river below Kumtor. Heavy Kumtor trucks run on the road — be careful on the dirt road. The names of the cascade's waterfalls are confused in different sources — check against the map (2GIS).
kg-0097.food: Kumys and tea in the summer yurt cafés by the parking area (Too.kg, Nomad's Land); in Barskoon and on the highway — lagman, beshbarmak, smoked Issyk-Kul fish.
kg-0097.reviews: 2GIS: 5/5, 106 ratings (viewed 07.10.2026). Google Maps: a separate listing could not be matched (meta). Tripster excursion “Skazka and Barskaun”: 4.84, 108 ratings. Pros: a spectacular cascade in a spruce gorge, a short trail, yurts with kumys, ice formations in winter. Cons: a slippery unmarked trail, confusion over waterfall names, the long road from Bishkek.
kg-0097.p.sum: The easiest way is from Karakol (≈90 km) or from the southern shore: along the highway to Barskoon, then 15–20 km along the good Kumtor dirt road (almost any car can make it) to the parking area with yurt cafés and 30–35 min on foot (1.6 km) along a slippery trail. Without a car — a marshrutka to Barskoon (~100 som from Karakol) and a taxi into the gorge, or a taxi from Karakol (3,500 som one way) / a MYWAY transfer (9,900 som per car round trip). Entry is free, overnight stays are in guesthouses in Barskoon and Tamga ($22–36) or in a tent in the gorge.

kg-0099.name: Tash-Rabat Caravanserai
kg-0099.near: There are no permanent villages in the valley — only seasonal yurt camps by the monument. The nearest large village is At-Bashy (~60 km by road, kyrgyzstanguides 2026), the town of Naryn is ~110–113 km (about 2 h). The earlier “Tash-Rabat marker in OSM at 1.3 km” is a tract (valley)/camps, not a village.
kg-0099.elev: About 3,100–3,200 m: too.kg — 3,100 m; thisis-kyrgyzstan and snoezelsontheroad — 3,200 m; journalofnomads — 3,000 m. The recommended label is “about 3,100 m”.
kg-0099.short: Tash-Rabat is a 15th-century stone caravanserai (on the site of an earlier, presumably monastic, structure of the 10th–11th centuries) at about 3,100 m in a side valley of the At-Bashy range, on the old route to the Torugart pass.
kg-0099.desc: Tash-Rabat is an almost square (about 33×35 m) stone building of slabstone with a central dome and 31–34 domed and vaulted rooms (24.kg says 34, thisis-kyrgyzstan — 31). Too.kg dates the caravanserai to the 15th century and notes that it was built on the remains of a monastery of the 10th–11th centuries (Buddhist or Nestorian — not firmly established). The building stands in the Kara-Koyun valley about 15 km from the Naryn — Torugart highway; in Soviet times (1970s–80s) it was cleared of rubble and restored. Since 2025–2026 a comprehensive restoration has been under way under the state programme “Koono Tarykh Syrlary” (2023–2027): a temporary metal canopy covers the monument and some areas are fenced off. Around it are seasonal yurt camps, from which hiking and horse routes depart, including to Lake Chatyr-Kol (border zone).
kg-0099.guide: Tash-Rabat is a rare case where a medieval caravanserai stands almost intact in the middle of an empty high-mountain valley: step under the central dome and count the side cells — there are three dozen. Look at the mysterious well-pit inside: it is thought to be a dungeon, a burial shaft or a secret passage. Spend the night in one of the yurt camps by the monument — in the evening and at dawn the valley empties, and at night at 3,100 m it is very cold even in July. In 2026 restoration is under way and the Ministry of Culture asks people to refrain from visiting — before the trip be sure to check whether they let people inside. Horse treks to Chatyr-Kol also start from here, but they require a border permit.
kg-0099.see: The central domed hall and 31–34 side cells; the mysterious well/shaft inside; the slabstone masonry and traces of the Soviet restoration; the Kara-Koyun valley with yurt camps and yaks; hikes onto the surrounding slopes (the “Panda Pass” viewpoint without a permit — snoezelsontheroad) and the horse route to Lake Chatyr-Kol (with a permit). In 2026 access to the interior is restricted because of the restoration.
kg-0099.skip: You are not ready for a long drive: from Naryn about 2 h one way, from Bishkek a whole day. In 2026 restoration is under way: if getting inside matters to you and access is not confirmed — postpone the trip. You tolerate altitude and cold nights badly — the overnight is at ~3,100 m.
kg-0099.diff: Easy to visit: from the parking at the camps to the building it is a few minutes on foot. The load comes from the altitude of ~3,100 m (shortness of breath, cold nights). A horse/hiking trip to Chatyr-Kol is moderate, 2 days, 22 km one way, 1,338 m of gain (journalofnomads).
kg-0099.when: From mid-June to mid-September the yurt camps operate (kyrgyzstanguides 2026; snoezelsontheroad: June–September); July–August are the warmest (15–20 °C in the day, frosts at night). From November to April access is difficult or impassable because of snow (journalofnomads 2026). Restoration work runs in June–August (24.kg, 2026).
kg-0099.hours: Restricted because of the restoration: the Ministry of Culture of Kyrgyzstan asked tourists to temporarily refrain from visiting (Kaktus/Kabar, August 2026; earlier 24.kg on 18.05.2026 reported that visitors were let in while some areas were closed). Work is in stages until 2027; they promised to announce the resumption of full access separately. In normal times there are no official hours — the key is held by the caretaker from a neighbouring yurt camp (journalofnomads, thisis-kyrgyzstan). Google Maps marked the site as temporarily closed on 03.10.2026.
kg-0099.daytime: Morning and evening: soft light on the stone walls and an empty valley without tour vehicles; during the day groups arrive from the Torugart highway (editorial, based on descriptions of overnight camps).
kg-0099.how: Along the Naryn — Torugart highway (A365) to the south; the turn to Tash-Rabat is at about the 100th km from Naryn (too.kg), then ~15 km along a side valley (kyrgyzstanguides; the last ~15 km is bumpy gravel, snoezelsontheroad). Without a car: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek → Naryn (new bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., ~600 som), then a taxi from Naryn (~3,000 som one way) or a marshrutka/shared car to At-Bashy and a taxi from there.
kg-0099.needcar: Yes. Public transport does not run to the valley: you need your own/rented car, a taxi from Naryn or At-Bashy, or a tour (thisis-kyrgyzstan, kyrgyzstanguides 2026).
kg-0099.self: Yes, if you have a car: a border permit is not needed for Tash-Rabat itself (journalofnomads, thisis-kyrgyzstan, kyrgyzstanguides 2026) — it is required only for Chatyr-Kol/Kel-Suu and beyond. The 2026 limitation is the restoration: check access to the interior in advance. Cash is essential (no ATMs).
kg-0099.roadtype: Paved along the Naryn — Torugart highway up to the turn-off; then ~15 km along the valley — dirt/gravel, “bumpy but passable for a careful passenger car” (kyrgyzstanguides 2026; snoezelsontheroad). In winter (November–April) snowdrifts are possible.
kg-0099.traveltime: From Naryn about 2 h (~110–113 km) by car (thisis-kyrgyzstan, journalofnomads); from Bishkek to Naryn by marshrutka 6–7 h (kyrgyzstanguides), so from Bishkek 8–9 h with a change. From the camps to the building it is a few minutes on foot.
kg-0099.stay: Several yurt camps right by the monument (season ~June–September): Sabyrbek’s camp (the oldest, recommended by snoezelsontheroad and kyrgyzstanguides), Tash Rabat Yurt Camp from Nomad's Land (double $28 with breakfast, with a winter shelter), Tash-Rabat yurt camp from ak-sai.com, the “Tash-Rabat ethno-complex”. A guide to 2026 prices: 1,200–2,000 som per person with dinner and breakfast (kyrgyzstanguides, thisis-kyrgyzstan, snoezelsontheroad).
kg-0099.net: There is no mobile coverage or Wi-Fi in the valley (too.kg, journalofnomads 2026, thisis-kyrgyzstan, snoezelsontheroad); the operator is not specified. The nearest coverage is on the highway closer to At-Bashy/Naryn.
kg-0099.entry: In the normal season — 100–150 som in cash to the caretaker (journalofnomads 2026: 100 som; snoezelsontheroad and thisis-kyrgyzstan: 150 som; kyrgyzstanguides 2026: 100–150 som). No official Ministry of Culture tariff found; during the 2026 restoration entry is restricted.
kg-0099.transfer: Taxi Naryn → Tash-Rabat ~3,000 som (≈$35) per car one way (thisis-kyrgyzstan, journalofnomads, 2026); round trip with waiting: from Naryn 4,000–6,000 som, from At-Bashy 3,000–4,500 som (kyrgyzstanguides, 21.09.2026).
kg-0099.bring: Warm clothes and a hat (frosts at night even in summer at ~3,100 m), sun protection, cash in som (no ATMs or shops), a torch for the dark cells, water purification tablets or boil river water (too.kg), passport; for Chatyr-Kol — a border permit arranged in advance.
kg-0099.warn:
The Ministry of Culture has closed the complex to visitors until the main stages of the restoration are completed (Kaktus, 08.2026); work proceeds in stages until 2027. The yurt camps in the valley operate.

Restoration 2025–2027: the Ministry of Culture (August 2026) asks people to temporarily refrain from visiting, some areas are fenced off, machinery is working — check access before setting out. Altitude ~3,100 m — altitude sickness is possible, night frosts in summer. No phone coverage. Lake Chatyr-Kol and the area beyond Tash-Rabat are a border zone, a permit is needed (2–3 weeks to arrange); for the caravanserai itself no permit is required. An overnight in the yurts does not give the right to enter the fenced-off monument.
kg-0099.food: Food is served only in the yurt camps (no shops or cafes in the valley — journalofnomads): usually home-style Kyrgyz dishes included in the price of the overnight — breakfast and dinner; reviews and videos mention a Kyrgyz lunch in a yurt, as well as kumys and dairy products from local herders (editorial; check the menu at the camp).
kg-0099.reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 344 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: there is a Tash Rabat (Naryn Province) page with reviews, the rating was not read from this environment. Typical pros — the Silk Road atmosphere, the building’s preservation, the yurt camps and the quiet of the valley; cons — a long road, a gravel approach, cold, no phone coverage and (in 2026) restrictions because of the restoration.
kg-0099.p.sum: Tash-Rabat is an overnight, not an hour’s stop: from Bishkek it is 8–9 h, so the base is Naryn (marshrutka 600 som or an Asman flight 2,100 som), then a taxi/car with a driver for 2 h (≈3,000 som one way, 3,000–6,000 som round trip) and a night in a yurt camp by the monument (1,200–2,000 som with dinner and breakfast; Ak-Sai — from $65). No permit is needed for Tash-Rabat itself, but in 2026 restoration is under way: in August 2026 the Ministry of Culture asked people to refrain from visiting, Google marks the site as “temporarily closed” — check access through the camp or CBT Naryn before you go. Cash is essential: no ATMs, fuel stations or phone coverage in the valley, fill up in Naryn.

kg-0099.p.iti.1.title: 2 days with a night in a yurt
kg-0099.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Naryn → Koshoy-Korgon → Tash-Rabat by lunchtime, a walk/horse ride around the valley, dinner and a night in a yurt, stars. Day 2: dawn at the caravanserai, a side trip onto the slope, by evening Naryn or on to Bishkek/Song-Kol.

kg-0099.p.iti.2.plan: Day 1: Naryn → Tash-Rabat, night. Day 2: on horseback/on foot 21.6 km over the pass ≈3,996 m to the camp above Chatyr-Kol. Day 3: back to Tash-Rabat and Naryn. Arrange the permit 1–2 weeks ahead (tour.too.kg 3,000 som or CBT Naryn).
kg-0099.p.iti.3.title: Logical combinations along the route

kg-0099.p.season: May: snow on the slopes, camps not yet open, nights −5…0 °C. Mid-June — mid-September: yurt season, +15…20 °C in the day, frosts at night; July–August — peak of tourist groups. Restoration work — June–August (2025–2027). Late September — October: camps wind down, first snow. November — April: the valley is snowed in, access is difficult or impossible.
kg-0099.p.budget.economy: ≈6,500–8,000 som per person for 2 days from Bishkek: marshrutka Bishkek — Naryn round trip 1,200; taxi Naryn — Tash-Rabat round trip 4,000–6,000 per car (≈1,500–2,000 per person in a group of 3–4); a yurt with half board 1,200–2,000; entry 100–150; a night in Naryn 1,500–2,500.
kg-0099.p.budget.comfort: ≈25,000–45,000 som per person: Asman flight 2×2,100, car with driver/tour (Eurasia Travel from $500 for 2 days), Ak-Sai $75–85 with full board, horse 1,500 + guide 2,500 som/day.
kg-0099.p.permits: No border permit is needed for the caravanserai itself. It is needed for Chatyr-Kol, Kel-Suu, Ak-Say and Arpa (the border zone of the At-Bashy district): tour.too.kg — 3,000 som, 5–7 working days, office at 105/3 Isanov St., Bishkek; or via CBT Naryn (€30, urgent €50 in 2 days). It is checked at military posts; the original + passport are needed. Entry to the monument — 100–150 som to the caretaker (in 2026 access is restricted by the restoration).
kg-0099.p.access: With children — yes, if the child tolerates the altitude of ~3,100 m and cold nights; for older people — a short visit is possible (a few minutes over uneven ground from the parking), but altitude and cold are a risk factor. Stroller — no (gravel, steps, uneven floor). With a dog — animals are allowed at the Omurbek camps per the description; inside the monument — no.

kg-altyn-arashan.name: Altyn-Arashan
kg-altyn-arashan.near: Ak-Suu (formerly Teplokluchenka), ≈10–12 km east of Karakol; from Ak-Suu to the springs it is ≈15 km up the gorge
kg-altyn-arashan.elev: ≈2,435–2,600 m: trekking platforms (loc.wiki/AllTrails) give 2,350–2,435 m at the guesthouses, Too.kg and Visit Kyrgyzstan give 2,600 m at the springs; Nomad's Land gives 2,580 m. The “3,000 m” figure on some sites is overstated.
kg-altyn-arashan.short: A high-mountain valley with radon and hydrogen sulfide hot springs (35–41 °C), a relict spruce forest and a view of the trapezoid of Palatka Peak (4,260 m). From Ak-Suu it is 15 km on foot (3–5 h) or 1.5–2.5 h by UAZ over one of the roughest roads in the Issyk-Kul region.
kg-altyn-arashan.desc: Altyn-Arashan (“golden spring”) is the valley of the Arashan river above the village of Ak-Suu, a nature reserve (zakaznik) since 1963. At the confluence of the rivers stand a handful of guesthouses and yurt camps, each with its own bathhouse: radon water at 35 °C and hydrogen sulfide water at 41 °C year-round; there are also “wild” stone tubs by the river. The valley is dominated by Palatka Peak (the Aksuu Wall, 4,260 m). The road from Ak-Suu is 15 km of rocky climbing with fords: ordinary cars and rental cars are not allowed here, and the traffic is UAZ-469s/“bukhankas”, GAZ-66s and Nissan Patrols with local drivers; on foot it is 3–5 h with a gain of ≈600 m, and the trail is simple and obvious. This is where the classic trek over the Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) into the Karakol gorge starts or ends, and 5 km above the resort a side valley leads off toward the lake. Electricity comes from generators and solar, payment is cash only, and there is practically no mobile signal. At night, even in summer, it can drop to −2…−5 °C.
kg-altyn-arashan.guide: Walk up and take a “bukhanka” down — that way you see the gorge and also get a dose of adventure on the rocks and fords that make rental companies forbid driving here. The bathhouses belong to different guesthouses: some have a wooden log cabin with 41 °C hydrogen sulfide water, others a free stone tub right by the river — walk around and choose. In the evening, when the day-tour tourists leave, the valley belongs to the few who stay overnight: watch Palatka Peak in the sunset light and the stars without city light pollution. Bring cash som and a warm sleeping bag: cards are not accepted, and it is cold at night even in July. If you plan Ala-Kul, don’t do it “in a day from the bathhouse”: the 3,900 m pass needs acclimatization and a separate day.
kg-altyn-arashan.see: Hot bathhouses at the guesthouses (radon 35 °C, hydrogen sulfide 41 °C) and “wild” tubs by the river; Palatka Peak / the Aksuu Wall (4,260 m); a relict Tien Shan spruce forest; the upper Arashan valley and the side valley toward Ala-Kul; yurt camps; in winter — a snow-covered valley (access only by UAZ or on foot).
kg-altyn-arashan.skip: If you have one day and a bad back, 2.5 h of jolting in a UAZ each way will not make you happy. If you expect a spa resort with infrastructure — here you get log cabins, generators and outdoor toilets. If you are traveling in a rental sedan — entering the gorge is usually forbidden by the rental contract.
kg-altyn-arashan.diff: On foot: moderate — 15 km, gain ≈600 m, 3–5 h, the trail is obvious, safe for solo travelers. By vehicle: rough off-road for a prepared 4×4 with a local driver only. The Ala-Kul trek over the 3,900 m pass is hard and should be assessed separately.
kg-altyn-arashan.when: June–September is the main season; October brings golden larches and fewer people (Backpack Adventures). In winter the valley is accessible (UAZ/on foot) and the bathhouses work, but there can be avalanches on the road (video, 2023). In May–June the fords may be higher than normal.
kg-altyn-arashan.hours: The valley is open 24 hours; the bathhouses at the guesthouses operate by arrangement with the owners, usually until evening; there is no official schedule. Google Maps: 24 hours.
kg-altyn-arashan.daytime: Leave Karakol in the morning (transfers start at 8:00–9:00); bathe in the evening after the day groups leave or early in the morning; if you stay overnight — the stars.
kg-altyn-arashan.how: 1) Karakol → Ak-Suu: marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 from the market/center of Karakol (formerly ≈15 som, 2017; the current price is not confirmed), then 15 km on foot up the valley (3–5 h) or in a local UAZ. 2) A direct 4×4 transfer from Karakol (35 km, ≈2–2.5 h): Arashan Transfer, MYWAY, CBT Karakol, GetYourGuide. 3) On foot from the Ala-Kul Pass (the second part of the loop trek).
kg-altyn-arashan.needcar: No, if you are ready to walk 15 km uphill; yes — only a prepared 4×4 (UAZ, GAZ-66, Patrol) with a local driver. An ordinary car or rental car — no.
kg-altyn-arashan.self: Yes: on foot the trail is simple and safe for solo travelers (Backpack Adventures); book a place to stay in advance in season. For the Ala-Kul Pass you need experience and acclimatization; a guide is optional.
kg-altyn-arashan.roadtype: From Karakol to Ak-Suu — paved road; then 15 km of rocky dirt road with steep sections, boulders and fords; according to reviews, vehicles have to be “jacked up” on the rocks; “rental companies forbid this road” (TripAdvisor 2024–2025). In winter avalanche debris is possible.
kg-altyn-arashan.traveltime: Karakol → Ak-Suu 20–30 min; Ak-Suu → springs: on foot 3–5 h (15 km, gain ≈600 m), by UAZ 1.5–2.5 h; a direct transfer from Karakol is ≈2–2.5 h one way.
kg-altyn-arashan.stay: Elsa guesthouse — 1,700 som/person with breakfast (2025 review) or 4,000 som for two with lunch and dinner (Oct. 2022, T—Zh); yurt camps ≈3,600 som/night with breakfast and dinner (TripAdvisor 2025); Eco Yurtcamp Arashan, Arashan Hotel (bathhouse free for guests, 2025); Ala-Kul Guesthouse Altyn-Arashan; a tent pitch — ≈100 som (2017). Visit Kyrgyzstan: simple guesthouses $10–15/night. A bed in a guesthouse 300 som + dinner 250 + breakfast 150 (2017, outdated).
kg-altyn-arashan.net: There is practically no mobile signal in the valley (Too.kg: “no signal”; TripAdvisor: limited electricity and internet). According to NomadCar, a weak O!/MegaCom signal is possible near the cabins. Beeline strengthened its network in Karakol and the Ak-Suu District in 2026, but not in the gorge. Maps — offline, money — cash.
kg-altyn-arashan.entry: Entry to the Arashan gorge is through a paid barrier of the Karakol forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): per person — citizens of Kyrgyzstan 20 som, citizens of former USSR countries 100, foreigners 220 som; per vehicle — car 80, large vehicles 170, buses/trucks 300 som. Bathhouses: wild tubs by the river — free; a guesthouse bathhouse ≈250 som/person (Arashan Transfer, 2026) or 200–500 som (SaryTours 03.2026); a private cabin — ≈$12/person/h; for overnight guests it is often free. Karakol National Park from the Karakol gorge side — 300 som/person (2025).
kg-altyn-arashan.transfer: From Karakol, 2026: MYWAY — Patrol 9,200 som, UAZ 13,200, GAZ-66 17,600 per vehicle (not final); Arashan Transfer — $85/seat (day tour), $55–85 shuttle, $290–360 private UAZ; GetYourGuide — $90/person; per 2024–2025 reviews — 5,000–11,000 som per jeep; SaryTours 03.2026 — 3,000–5,000 som one way in a local UAZ. Marshrutka No. 350 — pennies (15 som in 2017).
kg-altyn-arashan.bring: Cash som (no cards), trekking shoes, a warm layer and a hat (down to −5 °C at night), a rain jacket, water/a filter (boil river water), swimwear and a towel, a snack, a power bank, a headlamp, an offline map, a sleeping bag if you camp.
kg-altyn-arashan.warn: The road is extreme: 4×4 with a local driver only, and rental cars are not allowed here under the rental contract. The altitude is 2.4–2.6 km and nights are cold even in summer; the weather changes abruptly (snow in August happens). Boil river water. There is no signal — tell someone your route. In winter — avalanches on the road. The Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) is a separate hard day, not a “walk from the bathhouse”. Radon baths — 15–20 minutes at a time, there are medical contraindications. Since 2025 there has been a forestry barrier at the gorge entrance with an entry fee (foreigners 220 som/person + 80 for a car); demand a receipt.
kg-altyn-arashan.food: Food is available only at guesthouses by arrangement: home-cooked dinners (lagman, plov, soup, flatbreads), breakfasts; 2017 guideline — dinner 250, breakfast 150 som, 2022 — half board included in 4,000 som for two. There is no café or shop in the valley — bring groceries and snacks from Karakol.
kg-altyn-arashan.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 706 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 219 reviews, No. 2 of 40 in Karakol, Travelers' Choice (07.10.2026). Pros: the scenery, the springs, the atmosphere, the hospitality. Cons: a very rough road, cold at night, weak electricity and signal, basic conditions.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.sum: The best option is to walk up from Ak-Suu (15–16 km, +600–700 m, 3–5 h) and come down by UAZ, or to make Altyn-Arashan the finale of the loop Karakol gorge → Ala-Kul → Altyn-Arashan. You cannot bring your own or a rental sedan here: the 16 km of riverbed with boulders and two fords is passable only by local UAZs and GAZ-66s (Arashan Transfer from $55/seat, private UAZ from $290; MYWAY from 9,200 som for a Patrol). It is worth staying at least one night in a guesthouse with a bathhouse (≈$20–59), bringing cash and a warm sleeping bag.

kg-altyn-arashan.p.apps.0.season: On foot — year-round; main season June–September, high fords in May–June; avalanche debris possible in winter

kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.0.plan: 08:00 transfer from Giraffe Coffee → 10:30 Altyn-Arashan, bathhouse, a walk up the valley → 17:30 descent → 19:00 Karakol. Or: marshrutka No. 350 at 07:30 to Ak-Suu, hike up 4–5 h, bathe and descend by UAZ.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.1.title: 2 days
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: marshrutka to Ak-Suu, hike up 15 km, bathhouse, a night in a guesthouse. Day 2: out-and-back up the valley toward Palatka, descend on foot or by UAZ, in the evening — the Ak-Suu Kench springs.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.2.title: 4 days — the Ala-Kul loop
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.2.plan: Karakol → national park (marshrutka No. 101, 30 som) → Sirota → Ala-Kul → pass → Altyn-Arashan → Ak-Suu (the reverse direction is also popular, but from the Altyn-Arashan side the climb to the pass is longer).
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.3.title: What to combine it with
kg-altyn-arashan.p.iti.3.plan: Karakol (cathedral, mosque) → Altyn-Arashan → Ala-Kul → Karakol gorge; the next day — Jeti-Oguz and Kok-Jaiyk along the southern shore.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.season: June–September is the main season (July–August is crowded); late September–October — golden larches, down to −5 °C at night; winter — access by UAZ/on foot, bathhouses work, avalanches on the road; May–June — high fords. Snow in August is possible.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.budget.economy: ≈4,000–6,000 som for 2 days: marshrutka 40×2, forestry fee 220, night + meals at a guesthouse ≈1,700–3,000, bathhouse 0–250, food for the road 500
kg-altyn-arashan.p.budget.comfort: ≈15,000–25,000 som/person for 2 days: Arashan Transfer $85 or a private UAZ $290 per vehicle, guesthouse $59–91, horse $25
kg-altyn-arashan.p.permits: No permit is needed. The Karakol forestry barrier at the gorge entrance (since 2025): foreigners 220 som, CIS citizens 100, Kyrgyz 20 som/person; car 80, large vehicles 170 som — demand a receipt. When trekking via Ala-Kul there is an additional Karakol National Park fee of 300 som/person at the suspension bridge.
kg-altyn-arashan.p.access: With children — possible by UAZ, but the jolting lasts 2–2.5 h; on foot for teenagers. For older people — only by vehicle, mind the altitude of 2.5 km. With a stroller — no. With a dog — possible on foot (livestock and shepherd dogs).

kg-skazka.name: Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon
kg-skazka.full: Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon (Skazka / Fairy Tale Canyon)
kg-skazka.near: Tosor (≈8 km east of the turnoff, 10–15 min by car). The turnoff to the canyon is about 4 km west of Tosor on the Balykchy–Karakol highway (south shore), around km 120 from Balykchy.
kg-skazka.elev: ≈1650–1700 m (estimate: Issyk-Kul's level is 1607 m, the canyon is on the first terrace above the south shore; the exact elevation of the entrance is not published in the sources)
kg-skazka.short: A small canyon of multicolored clays and sandstones on the south shore of Issyk-Kul between Tosor and Kaji-Sai. Red, orange, yellow and gray ridges; a visit takes 1–2 hours, with views of the lake and the Terskey Ala-Too range from the high points.
kg-skazka.desc: Skazka is a compact erosion canyon on the first terrace above the south shore of Issyk-Kul, ≈2 km from the Balykchy–Karakol highway (the turnoff is at about km 120 from Balykchy, with a big sign; next to it is a second sign “Jeti-Oguz”, and a fee is collected at the barrier). Wind and rain have carved walls, towers and Cappadocia-style “chimneys” in the red and ochre clays; the best-known ridge is called the “Great Wall of China”. A network of paths spreads through the canyon: a short loop takes about an hour, an extended route with viewpoints about two; the elevation gain is small. From the ridges there is a view of the lake. There is almost no snow here, so the canyon is accessible year-round, but at midday in summer it is very hot, and after rain the clay becomes slippery. Infrastructure is minimal: the cashier's booth at the barrier, a parking area, a simple toilet.
kg-skazka.guide: Don't stick to a single path, climb up onto a ridge: from above the “Great Wall of China” turns into a jagged line, and behind it the blue strip of Issyk-Kul opens up. Look for shapes yourself — travelers see a dragon, a penguin, castles and a sleeping giant here, and everyone ends up with their own fairy tale; there are no official signs. The best light is at sunrise and the hour before sunset, when the red layers glow and the gray ones fall into shadow; at midday the colors wash out and there is no shade at all. Wear shoes with a tread: loose sandstone is slippery even in dry weather, and after rain it is best not to go into the canyon. If you have time left, go down to the shore — the beach at Tosor is considered one of the most beautiful on the south shore.
kg-skazka.see: The “Great Wall of China” ridge; the “painted mountains” with yellow-orange-pink layers; “chimneys” and towers; viewpoints on the ridges with a view of Issyk-Kul and Terskey Ala-Too; “windows” in the rocks. The shapes of a dragon, a penguin and castles are informal tourist names, there are no signs.
kg-skazka.skip: If you have already been to Charyn Canyon or the “Mars” canyons at Kaji-Sai and expect scale, Skazka is noticeably smaller. If it is pouring rain or a thunderstorm — the clay is slippery and the dry riverbeds are dangerous. If you are coming at midday in July without a hat and water — there is no shade here at all.
kg-skazka.diff: Easy: a 1–2 h walk, small elevation gain. Be careful on loose ridges and steep descents; don't go after rain.
kg-skazka.when: Year-round (there is almost no snow). Most comfortable in May–June and September–October; in summer only early in the morning or in the evening. In October 2022 no fee was charged (the ticket booth is seasonal). In winter the days are short and ice is possible.
kg-skazka.hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): daily 24 hours; TripAdvisor: 00:00–23:59. In practice the cashier at the barrier works in daylight during the season (May–September); out of season entry is free.
kg-skazka.daytime: Sunrise (4:00–6:00 in summer, per TripAdvisor reviews) or the last 1–2 hours before sunset — side light and coolness. Avoid midday.
kg-skazka.how: From Bishkek: the highway through Balykchy along the south shore, ≈120 km from Balykchy, turn right at the “Skazka” sign about 4 km west of Tosor; 2 km of dirt road to the barrier/parking. From Karakol along the southern road ≈100 km (1.5–2 h). By public transport: a marshrutka (minibus) Karakol → Bishkek along the south shore (No. 310/315 from Karakol's southern bus station) — ask to be dropped at the turnoff, then 2 km on foot; from Bishkek, marshrutkas (minibuses) to Bokonbaevo/Kaji-Sai from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1; the Western station has been closed since 10.2024) (schedule and price not confirmed for 2025–2026).
kg-skazka.needcar: A car or taxi is preferable; any ordinary car can get through in dry weather. 4×4 is not needed. 2 km on foot from the highway is realistic if you travel by marshrutka (minibus).
kg-skazka.self: Yes. The paths are intuitive but branch a lot — remember your way back; a guide is not required.
kg-skazka.roadtype: Paved road on the Balykchy–Karakol highway; the last 2 km are dirt/gravel to the barrier and parking, an ordinary car can get through in dry weather; after rain it turns soft, and low cars are parked earlier. TripAdvisor: “a sandy unpaved road”.
kg-skazka.traveltime: From Tosor 10–15 min, from Bokonbaevo 35–45 min, from Karakol 1.5–2 h, from Balykchy 2–2.5 h, from Bishkek ≈4–4.5 h by car. Visit: 40 min – 2 h (up to 4 h with a full circuit).
kg-skazka.stay: None in the canyon itself (in 2022 there was an unfinished glamping site). Nearest: Yurt Camp Tosor (Tosor, 10 min), Guesthouse Gulmira and Guesthouse Aziza (Tosor), Yurt Camp Meiman Ordo; on the south shore — Lake Glamping IK, Ak-Tengir Yurt Resort; in Bokonbaevo — CBT guesthouses (a benchmark for south-shore yurt camps from 1600 ₽/person in 2024). Prices for 2026 are not confirmed.
kg-skazka.net: There is a signal along the highway and in Tosor/Tamga; in April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Tamga, Barskoon and Bokonbaevo (economist.kg). Inside the canyon a stable signal is not confirmed by any measurement; Yandex reviews do not mention problems. Download an offline map.
kg-skazka.entry: 50 som per person — consistent across reports from 2015, 2018, 2020 and 2024 (zigzagonearth, travel-tramp, The Planet Edit, eurasia.travel forum) and in Yandex/TripAdvisor reviews; Kaktus.media (06.2021): 50 som per person by car / 30 som on foot, the fee is collected by private individuals at the barrier without documents; Too.kg (old data) — 40 som. Out of season (October 2022) no fee was charged. There is no official rate — it is a local fee.
kg-skazka.transfer: 2024 benchmarks (eurasia.travel forum): a taxi from Tosor/Tamga to Skazka with a 2-hour wait — 1500 som per car (3 people); a private car Karakol → Tosor with stops — 5000 som. MYWAY (2026) publishes a Karakol–Skazka–Karakol route, prices on the page on request. An excursion from Bishkek (Sputnik8, 2026) — $430 per group of up to several people, 10 h.
kg-skazka.bring: 1–1.5 L of water per person, closed shoes with a tread, a hat, sunscreen, a windbreaker (wind on the ridges), cash in som for the entry fee, a charged phone/camera.
kg-skazka.warn: There is no shade or water inside — don't go at midday in hot weather. The ridges are loose, after rain the clay is slippery; in a thunderstorm or downpour don't enter the dry riverbeds (mudflows). The fee at the barrier (≈50 som) is collected by private individuals — it is not a state fee, and no receipt is given (Kaktus.media 2021). Don't break fragile formations and don't carve inscriptions. The names “Great Wall of China” and “dragon” are tourist comparisons.
kg-skazka.food: There is no cafe at the canyon — only the seasonal booth. The nearest cafes and canteens are in Tosor, Tamga, Kaji-Sai and Bokonbaevo (Issyk-Kul fish, lagman, shashlik); in the yurt camps of Tosor — home-cooked dinners. A specific establishment with a menu is not confirmed.
kg-skazka.reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 1682 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.7/5, 114 reviews (07.10.2026). Yandex Maps: 5.0, 69 reviews (07.10.2026). Pros: “Martian” colors, many trails for 30 min – 2 h, views of the lake, easy to reach from the highway. Cons: heat and no shade, slippery ground, crowds from buses in season, little parking, a primitive toilet, and for some “smaller than Charyn”.
kg-skazka.p.sum: The simplest way is your own car or a taxi: the turnoff from the Balykchy–Karakol highway (south shore) is ≈4 km west of Tosor, then 2 km of dirt road to the barrier and parking; 4×4 is not needed. Without a car — marshrutka (minibus) No. 315/310 from Karakol's southern bus station (≈2 h), getting off at the turnoff and walking 2 km. The most logical place to stay is Tosor or Tamga (yurts on the beach, guesthouses $30–50); arrive at sunrise or 2 hours before sunset, and always with water.

kg-skazka.p.season: Year-round (there is almost no snow). April–June and September–October are comfortable (15–25 °C); July–August >30 °C, only sunrise/evening, crowds from buses; the ticket booth works in season (≈May–September, 9:00–17:00), out of season entry is often free; winter is cold, ice is possible, short days. Don't go after rains.
kg-skazka.p.budget.economy: ≈1500–2500 som/day: marshrutka (minibus) Karakol ⇄ Skazka 300–800, entry 50, a guesthouse in Tosor ≈3000 som/room (≈1500 for two), food 500–800
kg-skazka.p.budget.comfort: ≈8000–15,000 som/day per person in a couple: a car with driver from Karakol 5000 (per car), a yurt camp/glamping $40–100, cafes
kg-skazka.p.permits: Not needed. A local fee at the barrier of ≈50 som/person (collected by private individuals, no receipt), often not charged out of season.
kg-skazka.p.access: With children — yes (short trails, but loose slopes, supervision needed); for older people — the short lower loop; with a stroller — no (dirt, slopes); with a dog — possible, but heat and no water.

kg-son-kul.name: Song-Kol
kg-son-kul.dist: A single administrative affiliation is not given in the sources…
kg-son-kul.near: There are no permanent villages on the shore. Bases: Kochkor (via Kalmak-Ashuu, ~3 h), Kyzart village (start of the horse routes), Sary-Bulak, Naryn (~90 km southeast as the crow flies, via Terskey-Torpok), and from the southwest Ak-Talaa/Baetov (Moldo-Ashuu) and Chayek/Kyzyl-Kiya (Kara-Keche).
kg-son-kul.elev: 3,016 m above sea level (map.kg, asiamountains.net, Ak-Sai, Caravanistan); Too.kg rounds it to 3,000 m.
kg-son-kul.short: Kyrgyzstan's second-largest lake, at 3,016 m amid endless jailoo (summer pasture): in summer there are yurt camps, herds of horses and flocks of sheep; in winter it is an empty, icy plain.
kg-son-kul.desc: Song-Kol is a freshwater high-mountain lake in the Inner Tian Shan between the Songkol-Too (north) and Moldo-Too (south) ranges: about 29 km long and 17–18 km wide, area ~278 km², depth up to 13–14 m (up to 22 m according to map.kg). 18 streams flow into the lake and one river, the Song-Kol, flows out. It is frozen from the second half of October–November until the end of April. There were no fish in the lake until 1959; now it has whitefish, peled and naked osman. Part of the water area belongs to the Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve (1994), and the lake is a Ramsar wetland site (2011): up to 66 species of waterfowl nest here in summer, including the Red Book bar-headed goose. The surrounding pastures (~108,000 ha) are among the country's main summer jailoos; there are no permanent settlements, and about 15 yurt camps operate from June to September. On the northern shore stands the stone mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr from the late 19th century.
kg-son-kul.guide: Stay at least one night: the highlights of Song-Kol are the sunset over the water, a starry sky without light pollution and the morning mist over the jailoo. Rent a horse from the camp hosts (about 700 som per day) and ride along the shore to the herds, try fresh kumys and watch the mares being milked. If you have 2–3 days, ride in from Kyzart via Kilemche and the Jalgyz-Karagay Pass (3,400 m) — this way the lake opens up from above, as the nomads saw it. On the northern shore, look for the mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr. Even in July there can be frost at night, so a sleeping bag and a down jacket are a must.
kg-son-kul.see: Sunset and starry sky over the lake; herds and shepherds' yurts on the jailoo; mare milking and kumys making; nesting waterfowl (bar-headed goose, cranes, swans) — a Ramsar site; the mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr on the northern shore; the switchbacks of the Kalmak-Ashuu and Moldo-Ashuu passes (“33 Parrots” — Terskey-Torpok); the Kok-Jerty cascade on the Song-Kol River (4 km below its source); in winter — the frozen lake (a winter yurt camp is set up every year — Caravanistan).
kg-son-kul.skip: You only have one day — the round trip from Kochkor takes 6–7 hours, and the whole point of the place is to spend the night. You don't tolerate an altitude of 3,000 m and night frosts well and aren't ready for outdoor facilities. You are going between October and May without winter expedition preparation — there are no camps and the passes are under snow.
kg-son-kul.diff: Medium in terms of logistics: walks around the lake are easy, but the approach is 3–4 h over high-mountain dirt roads and passes up to 3,400+ m. Horse/foot treks from Kyzart are medium (2 passes above 3,000–3,400 m, 4–6 h a day; CBT Kochkor). At 3,016 m, you need to acclimatize.
kg-son-kul.when: June–September (yurt camps operate from about late May–early June until mid-September/early October); peak season, with camps guaranteed to be open, is July–August; for peace and quiet, June and September. CBT Kochkor runs horse tours from mid-June to the end of September. The lake is frozen from the second half of October until the end of April; the passes are closed by snow in winter.
kg-son-kul.hours: An open natural area with no ticket office. Yurt camps are seasonal (Ak-Sai: June–September); in the off-season there is nobody on the shore except the winter camp (on request).
kg-son-kul.daytime: Sunset and night (stars) are the main thing; early in the morning — mist over the water and mare milking. It is best to cross the passes during the day: frost and ice are possible in the morning, thunderstorms in the evening.
kg-son-kul.how: By car: 1) Kochkor → Sary-Bulak → Kalmak-Ashuu (~3,400 m) → northeast shore — the most popular, ~3 h from Kochkor; 2) Naryn → Terskey-Torpok (“33 Parrots”) → southeast shore; 3) Ak-Talaa/Baetov → Moldo-Ashuu → southern shore; 4) Jumgal Valley/Kyzyl-Kiya → Kara-Keche → southwest. From Bishkek ~280 km (Too.kg) via Balykchy and Kochkor. On foot and horseback: Kyzart → Kilemche → Jalgyz-Karagay (3,400 m) → Song-Kol (2–3 days, CBT Kochkor), also the Tuz-Ashuu, Chil-Bel and Uzbek passes.
kg-son-kul.needcar: Yes: there is no public transport to the lake. You need an SUV/jeep with a driver from Kochkor or Naryn, your own 4×4, or a horse/hike. Do not go in a sedan (visitkyrgyzstan.org).
kg-son-kul.self: Yes, in your own 4×4 or by hiring a driver in Kochkor; no permits are needed. In summer you can find a yurt on the spot, but in July–August it is better to book through CBT/the camps 1–2 weeks ahead. Cash is a must (no ATMs or card terminals).
kg-son-kul.roadtype: Paved road to Kochkor; after that dirt and gravel over passes with switchbacks (Kalmak-Ashuu, Moldo-Ashuu, Kara-Keche); on the shore — tracks across the jailoo. High ground clearance is needed; you can puncture a tire on some sections. Check the condition of each pass for the date of your trip.
kg-son-kul.traveltime: Bishkek — Kochkor 3–4 h (marshrutka (minibus)); Kochkor — Song-Kol 3–4 h by jeep (CBT Kochkor: return transfer from Batay-Aral — 3 h); Bishkek — Song-Kol by car ~6–7 h; horse trek from Kyzart — 2 days of 4–6 h each.
kg-son-kul.stay: About 15 yurt camps around the lake (Caravanistan). Budget: $10–15 per person with breakfast and dinner (Backpack Adventures 2026; Caravanistan); mid-range $25–45 with meals (visitkyrgyzstan.org). Premium: Ak-Sai Travel Son-Kul Yurt Camp — 44 yurts for up to 90 guests, shower, electricity in every yurt, Starlink Wi-Fi; $65 (breakfast) / $75 (half board) / $85 (full board) per person in a double, single $100–115 (ak-sai.com, season June–September; booking@ak-sai.com, WhatsApp +996 770 901 616). Booking camps run by shepherds — through CBT Kochkor, CBT Naryn. Tent — free camping on the shore (there are camping spots).
kg-son-kul.net: Coverage only in places (Too.kg). The Ak-Sai camp advertises MegaCom coverage and Wi-Fi via Starlink; most shepherd camps have no connection (Caravanistan, visitkyrgyzstan.org). Beeline and O! are not confirmed at the lake. A signal can sometimes be caught on the passes.
kg-son-kul.entry: Free: no entrance ticket or eco fee for Song-Kol was found in any 2019–2026 source. You only pay for the camp, horses and transport.
kg-son-kul.transfer: Kochkor — Song-Kol by jeep: 2,500–3,500 som per car (visitkyrgyzstan.org); ~$20 per seat round trip (Caravanistan); Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka 350 som, Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (CBT Naryn, May 2026); a 2-day tour from Bishkek — $650 for 1–2 people (Tripster).
kg-son-kul.bring: A warm sleeping bag or a fleece/down jacket (frost at night even in summer), hat and gloves, rain jacket, sun protection (UV at 3,000 m), headlamp, power bank (electricity isn't available everywhere), cash in som, altitude sickness pills/first-aid kit, shoes for wet grass, offline maps. Drink water from the lake only after boiling it.
kg-son-kul.warn: At 3,016 m altitude sickness is possible, especially if you go up from Bishkek in one day. The weather changes quickly; night frosts even in July–August; thunderstorms on the open jailoo — don't stand on high ground. The roads over the passes are dirt, with a risk of puncturing a tire, and snow at the beginning/end of the season. There is almost no mobile coverage, and no ATMs or shops. There were complaints about taxi drivers in Kyzart overcharging (TripAdvisor, May 2025) — agree on the price in advance. Dogs at shepherds' camps.
kg-son-kul.food: Kumys (fresh, straight from the shepherds in summer), beshbarmak and kuurdak made from lamb, boorsoki, kaymak (cream) and homemade jam in the yurts; at the Ak-Sai camp — national and European cuisine as a buffet. Local fish (whitefish, peled) — occasionally from fishermen.
kg-son-kul.reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 382 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (“Song Kol Lake”, Kochkor): 4.8/5, 13 reviews (2018 — May 2025; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: incredible scenery, sunsets and stars, hospitable nomads, horse rides. Cons: a hard road, varying quality of yurts, cold nights, isolated complaints about taxi drivers in Kyzart overcharging.
kg-son-kul.p.sum: The easiest way is Bishkek → Kochkor (marshrutka 350 som, 3–4 h), then through CBT Kochkor or a private driver take a jeep to the lake via Sary-Bulak and Kalmak-Ashuu (≈85 km from the highway, 3–3.5 h; guide price ≈5,200 som per car for 4–6 people, 2026). The best experience is a 2–3-day horse trek from Kyzart village via Kilemche (from ≈15–20 thousand som per person with local guides, tours $280–440 / €). Spend the nights in yurt camps on the northern or southern shore (1,000–2,000 som with dinner and breakfast at the shepherds', $35–115 at Ak-Sai), and bring cash in advance — there are no ATMs or shops at the lake. Since September 2026 there has been a fence at Batay-Aral (southwest, Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve) — do not drive in there.

In June 2026 the owners of illegal glamping sites (A-frames) were fined 200,000 som — building on the jailoo requires permits.

kg-son-kul.p.svc.shop: None; the last shop is in Kochkor / Sary-Bulak / Chayek / Naryn
kg-son-kul.p.svc.atm: None; the nearest are in Kochkor, Naryn
kg-son-kul.p.svc.fuel: None; the last fuel stations are in Kochkor, Naryn, Chayek
kg-son-kul.p.svc.mobile: Mostly none; MegaCom at Ak-Sai, Starlink Wi-Fi at some camps for an extra fee; signal in places on the passes (Moldo-Ashuu)
kg-son-kul.p.svc.medical: The nearest hospitals are in Kochkor (district) and Naryn (regional)
kg-son-kul.p.svc.rescue: Ministry of Emergency Situations of Kyrgyzstan 112; at the lake help only comes via the camp/Starlink
kg-son-kul.p.iti.0.title: Minimum: 2 days from Bishkek
kg-son-kul.p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: 7:00 leave Bishkek → 10:30 Kochkor (lunch, cash) → 11:30 jeep via Sary-Bulak and Kalmak-Ashuu → 15:00 camp, a walk/horse ride for 1–2 h, sunset. Day 2: sunrise, breakfast, 10:00 departure → 13:00 Kochkor → 17:00 Bishkek.
kg-son-kul.p.iti.1.title: Classic: 3 days on horseback from Kyzart
kg-son-kul.p.iti.1.plan: Night in Kochkor → in the morning a taxi to Kyzart (1 h) → day 1: 18 km to the Kilemche yurts; day 2: Jalgyz-Karagay Pass, 14 km to the lake; day 3: via Tuz-Ashuu 23 km to Kyzart → taxi to Kochkor/Bishkek.
kg-son-kul.p.iti.2.title: Loop through the lake (with a 4×4)
kg-son-kul.p.iti.2.plan: Kochkor → Kalmak-Ashuu → night on the northern shore → south along the shore → Moldo-Ashuu → Kurtka/Ak-Tal → Naryn (Salkyn-Tor, Tash-Rabat) or Kara-Keche → Jumgal → Kyzyl-Korgon → Suusamyr → Bishkek.
kg-son-kul.p.iti.3.title: What to combine it with
kg-son-kul.p.iti.3.plan: Kochkor (“Altyn Kol” felt), Kol-Ukok (from Kochkor), Sarala-Saz and Kilemche (horse “jailoo hopping”), Naryn and Salkyn-Tor, the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons via Kara-Keche.
kg-son-kul.p.season: May — until mid-June: snow on the passes, camps open from late May (some from 15 May). Mid-June — August: all approaches are open, the camps are working, peak in July–August, daytime up to +20…+25, around 0 at night; thunderstorms. August — festivals of national games on the jailoo. September: quieter, colder, camps close between mid-September and 20 October. October — April: the lake is under ice (~200 days), the passes are closed by snow (Kalmak-Ashuu and Moldo-Ashuu were closed as early as 2 November).
kg-son-kul.p.budget.economy: ≈4,500–6,500 som/person for 2 days: Bishkek—Kochkor marshrutka 2×350; a seat in a jeep ≈1,000–1,500 (5,200 som/car for 4–6); yurt with meals 1,000–2,000; horse for 1–2 h 250–500.
kg-son-kul.p.budget.comfort: ≈20,000–40,000 som/person: a 3-day horse tour $280–440 or a 2-day tour from Bishkek €120–$650; Ak-Sai $75–115/night with meals.
kg-son-kul.p.permits: No permit needed; no entrance tickets or eco fees. The southwestern part (Batay-Aral) is the Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve: fenced off since 09.2026, vehicle access closed.
kg-son-kul.p.access: With kids — yes, with acclimatization (3,016 m) and warm clothes; it is better to spend a night in Kochkor on the way. For older people — by jeep via Kalmak-Ashuu, comfortable camps (Ak-Sai). With a wheelchair — practically not (grass, bumps, pit toilets). With a dog it is possible, but there are aggressive dogs at shepherds' camps.
